TL;DR

The person files carry a birthplace as text (birth_municipality) and a resolved 1910 okres (birth_okres_id, utils.parsing.records_geo). records_geo.add_settlement_attrs already picks a lexicon row per (municipality, okres_id) but exports only its attributes, never the settlement_id, and its homonym rule compares attributes (two different hamlets with equal attributes collapse to the first) rather than the D-144 obec-first rule on the set of ids. This module links each birth to a settlement_id (data/final/geo/settlements_1910, key slug:ordinal, D-148) and to the 1910 municipality whose institutions the corrected register holds (data/final/register_rechecked/register_municipalities, keyed on settlement_id).

How it works

The author's rulings it implements (2026-11-16):

  • the register first, the lexicon second. The 1910 register prints every municipality and part (register_places, Czech and German form in one cell); its settlement_id comes from the frozen anchoring plus utils.recheck.anchor_overrides.apply (Aš, the healed names).
  • D-144 on the set of ids. A key several settlements answer to: one id → take it; several, of which exactly one is an obec (for the register: exactly one is a municipality row) → that one; otherwise refused, the candidates kept for the rulings sheet. An ambiguous tier stops the search — a later, looser tier must not break a tie the stricter one could not.
  • the settlement's 1910 okres wins over the record's stated okres when the stated okres is in the settlement's okres timeline (okres_all) — P4, flagged birth_okres_corrected with the stated id kept. Greater Prague (P3) moves a suburb to its own 1910 okres the same way; since 0.3.0 a P3 move that passes only on a post-1910 Praha-venkov/-západ/… token, or on the agglomeration pool alone, is refused (prague_later_okres_only / prague_pool_only; the first can be accepted as a block with accept_prague_later_okres=True).
  • rulings the author has not confirmed do not drive the links (0.3.0): load_gazetteer applies only ruled_by = author rulings unless include_unconfirmed=True; build writes the confirmed-only links and reports the with evidence rulings counts beside them.
  • institutions join at the municipality total, the exact part is kept (birth_settlement_id is the part, birth_municipality_settlement_id the municipality).
  • the register's court is the 1910 court; the polygon court of settlements_1910 only as a flagged fallback (birth_court_source).
  • Aš: a two-letter name; matched like any other here (no length guard), and the register anchors it through anchor_overrides (as:1).

Passes, each inside the record's 1910 okres, first match wins, the tier recorded (birth_settlement_match):

====== ================================================================================= P0 clean the string: placeholders → missing; též alternates, orphan ), díl, parentheticals and ? split off as alternates P1 p1_register (printed names of the primary edition: cz for Bohemia, de-moravia, de-silesia), then p1_lexikon (headword / 1910 name / German name, healed forms included — utils.parsing.place_names.name_index) P3 Prague (run before P2, so Praha-Smíchov is never split to Praha): Praha &lt;Roman&gt;.-X; quarters I–VIII → their praha:1 part; post-1949 Praha 1–10 refused; a 1910 suburb (Nusle, Vršovice, …) → its own municipality and okres; the Libeň trap (liben:3 is a village of okres Vinohrady, Praha VIII Libeň is liben:2, a part of praha:1); a name two ring settlements share goes to the one that joined Prague in 1922 (the clerk who wrote "Praha" wrote the 1922 city); a 1923 district number with a name is read by the name (Praha VIII.-Troja is Troja) P2 variants: alternates and the VÚA German exonym through P1; p2_register_alt (the de-bohemia printed forms); p2_nospace; p2_alias (ČSÚ viz alias, the target's 1910 okres must equal the record's — viz_okres is modern); p2_split (parent-part: right piece first, the left must be its parent, its municipality or the okres seat; else the left piece alone); p2_qualifier (u/nad/pod/na/v/ve/při tails stripped on both sides) P4 p4_okres_timeline: the name is nowhere in the okres, and exactly one settlement of that name has the record's stated okres in okres_all P5 roll-up: register part → its municipality row (edition, court_key, muni_seq); not in the register → the lexicon parent_1910 resolved in the okres; statutory city → birth_link_unit = statutory_okres; a settlement two register municipalities hold (outside cross-references) is refused ====== =================================================================================

Columns added (prefix birth_): settlement_clean, settlement_id, settlement_id_refused, settlement_status, settlement_match, settlement_candidates, municipality_settlement_id, municipality_source (self / register_part / lexikon_parent / statutory_okres), register_row_key, register_key, register_owner_differs, in_register_municipalities, court_id_1910, court_source (register / polygon), link_unit (municipality / statutory_okres / none), link_refusal, okres_id_1910, okres_id_stated, okres_corrected, okres_correction_rule (p4_timeline / p3_prague_1910_okres / p3_prague_later_okres, the block accepted since 0.4.0), prague_quarter, greater_prague_1922, settlement_is_okres_name, settlement_qmark, settlement_piece_tier, vua_uncertain, vua_raw_qmark, settlement_owner_mismatch, okres_inferred, obec_over_part (0.4.0), pool_tie_break (0.5.0), settlement_uncertain.

Checks added in 0.2.0:

  • owner sanity (P5): the register row that owns the matched settlement must print the name the record was matched on (settlement_owner_mismatch otherwise); when the settlement's own lexicon names and the owner row's printed forms share no form and the row prints the name of another settlement of its okres, the anchor is wrong and the roll-up is refused owner_name_conflict (the settlement id is kept, the municipality is not). Disjoint names alone only set the mismatch flag: they are mostly German-only cells, 1910 spellings and OCR damage (owner_check).
  • Greater Prague 1922 from the settlement only: a hamlet joins only when its parent, resolved inside the hamlet's own 1910 okres, is a joiner; the flag reads the settlement, never its municipality, so GREATER_PRAGUE_EXCLUDED (Háje, Milíčov of Hostivař) stays out.
  • okres corrections carry their rule (okres_correction_rule): p4_timeline; a P3 move to a settlement with a Prague-named okres (Praha …) or the stated okres in its okres_all timeline is p3_prague_1910_okres; one without is p3_prague_pool_only (the record writer's generic Praha for the agglomeration; flagged for the author, never dropped here).
  • stated okres outside the agglomeration: P1 runs there before P3 (Kyje, Praha with okres Lomnice nad Popelkou is that okres's Kyje, not Prague's); a P3 reading that would move such a record to a ring okres not in the settlement's timeline is refused prague_okres_conflict; a Prague city reading with alternates (Praha? Hrubý Jeseník) is refused praha_city_with_alternate.
  • timeline keys space-free (the lexicon's okres_all carries OCR splits: usti nad orl ici).
  • settlement_uncertain: the raw string has a ?, the match came off an alternate, split or qualifier tier, or the VÚA reading was uncertain.

Changes in 0.3.0 (three independent reviews):

  • the register join compares keys, not set membership. register_rechecked/register_municipalities still carries the frozen anchoring, while the gazetteer carries the overrides (and, on request, the rulings). in_register_municipalities is True only where the municipality's row in that table has the same register key (edition|court_key|muni_seq, register_key) as the row that owns the link in the gazetteer; register_owner_differs marks a row that exists under another key (0.2.0 counted Kostomlaty's births as reachable through the frozen Kostomlátky row). A register_key or court_key column in the table, once the register hook adds one, is used as is (municipality_keys).
  • P3 okres moves split (above); the refused candidate is kept in settlement_id_refused.
  • qualifiers: za / před / mezi added; a qualified name whose okres holds the same head under a different qualifier is refused qualifier_conflict (unless P4 finds the name exactly as written), and P4 never strips a qualifier when the stated okres holds that bare head (Lhota u Červeného Kostelce, okres Náchod, was Lhota of okres Nové Město).
  • numbered siblings: a form without the Roman numeral the register prints for its settlement (Großaupa I, Velká Úpa) is ambiguous across the numbered siblings the register prints, never the first of them (the ČSÚ lexicon's own numerals, NOVÁ VES I, do not count).
  • owner check pools the printed forms of every register row holding the settlement (both editions, municipality and part rows; Novosady Blatiny split into its two names).
  • contradicted rows: so that pooling does not hide a wrong frozen anchor in one edition, a municipality whose rows print none of the settlement's names while another municipality row holding it prints one and gives another 1910 population no longer holds the settlement in the gazetteer (contradicted_keys: only the Czech Kostomlátky row for kostomlaty-nad-labem:1 today); the register join then reports the table's row as differing.
  • Prague pool tie-breaks (Sedlec, Lipany, Libeň) keep the ids chosen among in settlement_candidates and are listed in the rulings queue at any count.
  • Praha, X with okres Praha, Y is a parallel two-value list: X is matched in Y as p2_alternate and flagged uncertain, never silently.
  • every refusal empties settlement_id (the candidate goes to settlement_id_refused) and leaves the stated okres in place.
  • settlement_uncertain = settlement_qmark | settlement_piece_tier | vua_uncertain, each also its own column; vua_uncertain reads locations 1.2.2 candidates_agree_place (candidates naming different places in one okres are uncertain); the VÚA raw cell's ? (vua_raw_qmark) is reported but no longer counted.

Changes in 0.4.0 (the author's decisions of 2026-11-16 and the third review):

  • the later-okres Prague block is accepted (ACCEPT_PRAGUE_LATER_OKRES = True): such a record links with its okres moved to the 1910 ring okres and okres_correction_rule = p3_prague_later_okres, so the analysis can drop the block; a pool tie-break inside it (Čakovice, Lipany) stays refused prague_later_okres_tie_break and in the queue; prague_pool_only stays refused.
  • the seat rule: a name that is the stated okres's own name town, answered by several settlements, goes to the one in the okres's seat court (Podbořany: podborany:1, not podboranky:1); tier p1_okres_seat.
  • an okres inferred from the name ({prefix}_okres_match = muni with no okres string) links only when the name has exactly one settlement in the whole gazetteer or is that okres's seat; otherwise okres_from_name_ambiguous; when linked, the component okres_inferred.
  • owner check: the conflict test reads the split printed forms (Neustift, Novosady Blatiny holds blatiny:1: lhota:36 on that row is owner_name_conflict), and a part of such a municipality row is refused the same way (Samotín would roll up to lhota:36); the contradicted-row rule never frees a settlement from two_owners (Gazetteer.contradicted_freed).
  • Praha-X: an unknown X never falls back to praha:1 (praha_name_unknown), and a piece of a string (alternate, German form, split piece) never resolves to praha:1 unless the whole string is the city; hl. město Praha is the capital's title.
  • the VÚA readings: vua_uncertain reads locations 1.2.3 n_readings (the written head counted); a German cell of 2+ forms is decided on the union of their settlements — ambiguous when they give two, never D-144's one obec among them (german_verdict) — and the numbered-sibling guard runs on p2_german; a reading taken from VÚA's first candidate links only when every candidate gives the same settlement (ambiguous:vua_candidates).
  • P4 in the other direction: a name the stated okres holds inside a longer name (Lhota | Tábor: Balkova Lhota …; Ouběnice 1. díl) is not sent elsewhere (ambiguous:p4_in_okres); P4's bare-head refusal is qualifier_conflict on a qualified form, head_in_okres on the bare head.
  • cross-references on both rows: when every row holding a settlement is a viz row, the municipality row owns it and a part row of 10 % or less of its population is dropped (Pivoň).
  • refused rows carry no row key, owner flag, piece tier or uncertainty component; rulings_dependence counts linked rows only; the component obec_over_part marks a D-144 choice of a register municipality over a register part printing the same name (no link change).

Changes in 0.5.0 (the author's decisions of 2026-11-16, D1–D4):

  • D1, the first-candidate rule: a reading taken from VÚA's first candidate is refused (ambiguous:vua_candidates) only when another candidate gives a different settlement, or is itself ambiguous (candidate_verdicts). A candidate that gives nothing — its okres does not resolve (Kralupy, Hlučín, a Slovak or Subcarpathian okres), it names no okres or no municipality, or it matches nothing in its okres — is no evidence against the main reading; such a link keeps vua_uncertain = True. A candidate okres string naming a statutory city and its rural okres (Opava, Liberec) is read as the rural member unless the municipality is the city itself (records_geo's twin rule, D-17): the city okres answers any name with the city, which made 0.4.1 count Tábor, okres Opava (tabor:1, an osada of Loděnice) as giving nothing.
  • D2, an okres inferred from the name: linked when D-144 across all okresy (global_any; one id, else the one obec or town — a register municipality row, a lexikon obec, or a namesake whose 1910 status the lexikon does not give) is exactly the settlement the match found in the inferred okres, or (0.4.0) the name is that okres's own; refused okres_from_name_conflict when that one lies in another okres, else okres_from_name_ambiguous (okres_inferred_refusal).
  • D3: locations 1.2.x is accepted for data/final (nothing to code here).
  • D4a, head_in_okres: a qualified name whose stated okres holds exactly one settlement with the bare key and no qualified form of it links to that settlement, tier p2_qualifier (Klášter nad Jizerou | Mnichovo Hradiště, Novosedla nad Nežárkou | Třeboň).
  • D4b: locations 1.2.4 counts a parenthetical holding only an okres and a ? as a second reading (Bakov, okr. Náchod? (okr. Slaný?)): vua_uncertain.
  • D4c, Prague pool tie-breaks outside the later-okres block — the okres moves of rule p3_prague_1910_okres a pool preference picked (Záběhlice, Podbaba, Sedlec) — link as before and carry the new component pool_tie_break; inside the block they stay refused. A quarter read in okres Praha itself (Libeň → quarter VIII, the Libeň trap) moves nothing and is not flagged.
  • D4d: the VÚA German form breaks a P1 D-144 status tie it can decide: Oldřichov (Ulgersdorf), okres Děčín is oldrichov:1 (1910 Ulgersdorf, part 5 of Franzenthal-Ulgersdorf), not the obec oldrichov:2 (printed Ullgersdorf, court Děčín) — tier p2_german (german_tie_break). Záblatí and Ulgersdorf get evidence rulings in anchor_rulings.csv.

Changes in 0.6.0 (the author's decisions of 2026-11-16, T1–T4, after the 0.5.0 checkers found about 10–20 % wrong links among what D1 and D2 restored):

  • T1, D1 tightened — a VÚA candidate that "gives nothing" must not hide a real conflict (candidate_verdicts). Its okres is read off the candidate's own text with the typos normalised (okrese/okrs/okes/ores/okrr … → okres, na Nisou → nad Nisou, /…/ tails dropped, the last okres X taken: candidate_okres), then resolved (resolve_okres): a backbone name; a post-1910 okres onto its 1910 okres (LATER_OKRES_1910: Český Těšín → Těšín, Frýdek-Místek → Frýdek/Místek, Kralupy → the town's 1910 okres) and any other later okres through the lexikon timeline (P4 on the token); a Slovak, Hungarian, Subcarpathian or Hlučín okres is foreign (no evidence); else a close match (difflib >= 0.85) to one Czech-lands okres name (Nové Město na Morava). A candidate whose item names a land or country outside the Czech lands (Zwickau, Sasko; Vídeň, Dolní Rakousy) is foreign too. Global-name fallback: a candidate that still matches nothing — no okres, an okres that does not resolve, or nothing of the name in its okres — counts as a conflict when its name (as written, qualifier kept, or the right piece of a compound) answers in global_any to a Czech-lands 1910 settlement other than the link (kind global; LATER_TOWN_1910: Český Těšín is tesin:2, Teschen), or, in the okres it names, is a close spelling (difflib >= 0.9) of another settlement (Weisbach, okres Frýdland = Weissbach, close_names). The candidate that is the record's own reading is not checked against itself. An ambiguous candidate still refuses (the 0.4.0 extension, conservative: 11 records in 0.5.0).
  • T2, D2 tightened (okres_inferred_refusal): a link whose okres records_geo inferred from the name is refused okres_from_name_foreign when the raw cell names a land, country or district outside the Czech lands (foreign_token: Jaroslav, Halič; Steinbach, Gmünd), okres_from_name_conflict when an okres token of the cell (okr/okres/okes/ores …), or a bare Czech okres or court name after a comma, names an okres that is neither the settlement's nor in its timeline (raw_okres_refusal), and okres_from_name_home_conflict when the soldier's home okres or home municipality (home_okres_id / home_municipality) holds another namesake (home_conflict: legion Bukovka, Střížkov, Hodkov). D-144 across okresy (d2_decide): a namesake of unknown 1910 status may refuse but never wins (legion Dolní Lhotka), and an unanchored register municipality row printing the name counts as one more possible obec (Chudeřice, Milíčov).
  • T3, the census key follows the corrected okres (correct_census_okres_id, notebook 02 §4a): where birth_okres_corrected, birth_census_okres_id is the pooled census unit (utils.parsing.census.okres_census_crosswalk, D-17/D-18) of birth_okres_id_1910; the stated one is kept in birth_census_okres_id_stated.
  • T4: pool_tie_break is set wherever P3 broke a pool tie at p3_prague_suburb outside the later-okres block, okres moved or not; coverage's first-candidate counts are on the scope, as the headline; locations 1.2.5 (an okres-only parenthetical naming the head's own okres is no second reading).

Changes in 0.7.0 (the 0.6.0 checkers' findings and the author's answers A1–A3, 2026-11-16; each rule can be switched off for measurement, rules_off, RULES_070):

  • F1, a silent candidate the gazetteer holds under a later name (global_names, candidate_verdicts): a lexikon row with no 1910 okres whose earliest okres_all okres is a Czech-lands one (not Hlučín, Valticko, Vitorazsko: unplaced_czech) counts in the global-name fallback (Nový Bohumín, Ruda nad Moravou); in the okres a candidate names, such a row of the name or of its qualifier-stripped head counts when its timeline holds that okres (Louky nad Dřevnicí → louky:2); an unanchored register municipality printing the name counts (kind unanchored: Horní Líštná, de-silesia|303009022|28); LATER_TOWN_1910 adds Nový Bohumín → sunychl:1 (Šunychl, 1910). When the candidates disagree (a link standing beside silent candidates) the record's own head — the written text before the first parenthesis — goes through the same global check when it is not the linked candidate's own name (Eisenberg → ruda:4 beside jezeri:1; kind head_global).
  • F2, the head contradicts the link (head_verdict, same scope): it names a land, country or district outside the Czech lands (foreign_token, a Hungarian okres: Jeníkov, Nitra), a Czech land the link is not in (Bohemia against Moravia/Silesia; Moravia against Silesia tolerated: Markovice, Morava → Chrudim), it is the name of a candidate VÚA placed outside the Czech lands and not the linked one's (Inzersdorf, Hietzing), or it carries a distinguishing word (Něm., Horní, Nový …) that only another namesake's 1910 / German names carry (Něm. Kravaře = Deutsch Krawarn, kravare:2) — kinds head_foreign / head_land / head_namesake.
  • F3, D2's home and the post-1910 name (okres_inferred_refusal): a home outside the Czech lands (home_land other than Czech lands, home_megye_id / home_jaras_id set, a home municipality that only a Hungarian name answers to; and, where the name answers to more than one Czech-lands settlement and is not the okres's own, a home whose municipality and okres strings both resolve to nothing in the Czech lands: Bielik, Bielik) refuses an inferred okres, okres_from_name_home_foreign; a match that came only through a post-1910 lexikon name — the register holds the settlement but prints no such form, nor does the lexikon's 1910 name — may not win an inferred okres where D-144 had to choose among namesakes, okres_from_name_later_name (Dvorek, printed only Höflas; a unique modern name such as Český Krumlov still links).
  • F4, a land word in the cell (lands_named): the raw cell outside parentheses names Čechy against a Moravian or Silesian link, or Morava / Slezsko against a Bohemian one → okres_from_name_land_conflict; Horní / Pruské Slezsko (Upper, Prussian Silesia) is foreign.
  • F5, okres alternatives in parentheses (paren_okres_alternatives): an okres named inside a parenthesis after an okres word (Domoradice, okr. Vysoké Mýto? (Český Krumlov?)) is an alternative; when one alternative holds another namesake of the key the link is refused okres_from_name_ambiguous; when the link fits one alternative and no other alternative holds the name it stands (Javornice, Jiřetín the same way).
  • F6, an okres string that resolves to nothing is no evidence (_okres_fits → unknown, the link kept, flagged by okres_inferred); the close match takes the single best okres when its ratio beats the runner-up's by OKRES_FUZZY_MARGIN (Valšské Meziříčí) and never reaches or starts from a key of 4 letters or fewer (Plzań is not Plan); later okres and court forms (OKRES_NAME_ALIASES: Zábřeh na Moravě, Rokytnice, Horní Litvínov, Vrbno) and the Austrian districts of FOREIGN_DISTRICTS resolve.
  • A1 (the author): a home okres equal to the link's own okres is no conflict — kept from 0.6.0.
  • A2 (the author): where birth_okres_id is missing but the link supplies birth_okres_id_1910, birth_census_okres_id is that okres's census unit (the stated key stays missing); correct_census_okres_id is idempotent (F7: the stated key always from birth_okres_id).
  • A3 (the author): a written okres conflicting with a key that answers to exactly one Czech-lands settlement is refused okres_from_name_conflict_unique; such refusals are their own block of the rulings queue with whether the written okres borders the settlement's (MPIDR outlines), and the conservative refusals Rudolice and Kienberg are listed as the block conservative.

Changes in 0.8.0 (the author's answers A4–A6 of 2026-11-16 and the 0.7.0 checkers' defects D-a…D-h; each switchable, RULES_080):

  • A4, a foreign home narrowed: a home refuses an inferred okres only when it lies in Hungary / Slovakia, Galicia or Bukovina (home_land Slovakia, Hungary, Galicia — the records file Bukovina under Galicia — a Hungarian county or járás, a home only a Hungarian name answers to); a home in Austria (Vienna), overseas or Russia, or in any other land, never refuses; home_unresolved keeps its contested-name restriction and does not fire on a home recognisably elsewhere (HOME_ELSEWHERE_WORDS: Chicago, Illinois); and no home refuses when the raw cell writes the link's own okres (Habry, okr. Čáslav).
  • A6, the Habsburg regiment as refuse-only evidence (regiment_region): the soldier's infantry regiment (VÚA ah_unit_*; csol.cz habsburg_unit_peacetime / _capture) is looked up in Ehnl's Tabelle I (reference/units/ehnl_tabelle1_{infantry,landwehr,honved}.csv) and its recruiting district placed in a region (regiment_regions). A regiment raised outside the Czech lands refuses a link that VÚA read off its first candidate when another candidate lies in that region (vua_regiment_conflict: Žabokriek, IR 71 Trenčín; Prislop, IR 85 Máramaros), and an inferred okres when the name is a Slovak obec's and the regiment Hungarian (okres_from_name_regiment_conflict). The regiment never picks or creates a link.
  • D-a: F5 reaches a stated okres (an okres word followed by okres alternatives in parentheses: a namesake in another alternative refuses okres_from_name_ambiguous), and F6 reaches an okres string records_geo left unresolved: resolve_okres first, then — for a Czech-looking string — the okres inferred from the name as the as-is run does, the string no evidence (unresolved_okres_link).
  • D-b: close_okres scores the foreign district names too, and a foreign name at least as close wins (Turňa, Senice, Sečany).
  • D-c: the later-name rule does not fire on a cell whose parenthesis prints a 1910 form of the link (Prameny (Sangaberg)) nor where the home okres is the link's (Ludvíkov, home Einsidl).
  • D-d: head_global takes only namesakes in the land the head names (Benešov, Slezsko).
  • D-e: okres_from_name_conflict_unique counts the unplaced Czech namesakes (F1's _czech_1910), and a written okres holding a near spelling of the name or of the link is a plain okres_from_name_conflict (Libavá, Lobeč, Dobrová, Bernatice).
  • D-f: a candidate link stands (flagged) when the head is a printed 1910 form of it and the only other candidates are unplaced Czech rows the register does not print (Modlan).
  • D-g: the head refusals (F2) are vua_head_conflict, not ambiguous:vua_candidates.
  • D-h: a link is refused home_name_conflict when the home municipality is a Czech-lands name of another okres and the written head matches it better than the link (Krupka, Kutná Hora); a home namesake in a land the head's own land word contradicts does not count (Držkov, Morava).

Changes in 0.9.0 (the 0.8.0 checkers' defects E1–E13, 2026-11-17; E1–E12 each switchable, RULES_090):

Changes in 0.10.0 (the 0.9.0 checkers' findings F1–F13, 2026-11-17; the behavioural ones switchable as G1–G7, RULES_100 — G<n> is the checkers' F<n>, renamed because F1–F6 name the 0.7.0 switches):

  • G2 (F2): E6 does not refuse when exactly one settlement is held by every okres piece that holds the name (it links, moved as P4 moves where the stated okres is in its timeline, okres_common_switch), nor when the home municipality is the link or the link's 1910 parent (home_names_link_or_parent).

Changes in 0.11.0 (the 0.10.0 checkers' findings, 2026-11-17; switchable as RULES_110):

  • H1: where no namesake of the right piece lies under the left by 1910 parent, register owner or sibling, the modern municipality decides (Gazetteer.modern_obec, from settlements_1910_geo): a namesake whose modern obec is the left piece is under it (right_under_left; Jesenice-Martinice → martinice:6, osada of Nedrahovice in 1910, part of Jesenice today — not D-144's martinice:1, part of Votice); in the E4 shape a left piece whose modern obec is the right piece, and which is not the right piece's own settlement, is the place (left_in_right_modern; Mezná-Hřensko → mezna:1, Polanka-Chotoviny → polanka:6); and D-144's obec pick no longer stands where modern evidence names another namesake. VÚA's candidate readings go through the same split (Martinice ? (Martinice …; Jesenice-Martinice …) no longer agrees).

  • H2 is records_geo 1.11.0 (the Praha-countryside veto reads the other pieces of the string); H4 (a fresh VÚA re-parse in the build) and H5 (measurement hygiene) change no rule here.

Changes in 0.12.0 (the 0.11.0 checkers' findings, 2026-11-17; switchable as RULES_120):

  • I1: in a VÚA cell a ? between pieces separates alternatives (Podbořany ? Mukoděly, Kamenice nad Lipou ? Žďár, Benešov) ?Divišov: VÚA's reading after a lost (). A piece that is the record's own okres or its seat or a big city (G3's okres_locator) locates the place and is dropped; one piece left is matched alone, several that give different settlements (or an ambiguous one) are refused ambiguous:qmark_readings (qmark_readings, match_birthplace). Only with a stated okres, and only in a VÚA cell: a csol.cz clerk's Vrchlabí? Háje nad Jizerou? is two doubted birthplaces, not a locator and a reading.
  • I2: p2_qualifier's stripped head links only where the name as written is no other 1910 settlement outside the record's okres (qualified_elsewhere: Lipník nad Bečvou (čp. 286) | Moravský Krumlov is not the 95-house lipnik:2); else qualifier_conflict — unless the soldier's home municipality lies in the okres (home_muni_in_okres: Police nad Metují | Zábřeh, home Drozdov, stays police:1).

Changes in 0.13.0 (the 0.12.0 checkers' findings, 2026-11-17; switchable as RULES_130):

  • J1: a bare name that P1 does not find (Lhota, Újezd, Hradiště, Rybná) is no longer sent to the one qualified namesake D-144 picks (Lhota u Dubu) when the okres holds other settlements with the name as a word of their head — adjective forms (Horažďovická Lhota, Svijanský Újezd, Stará Lysá) and qualified ones alike (bare_namesakes). Where those namesakes hold more than one obec, or an obec besides the settlement the qualifier tier would take, the record is refused ambiguous:p2_bare_namesakes — unless the soldier's home municipality names, parents, owns or shares a modern municipality with exactly one of them (or, failing that, lies next to exactly one: RÚIAN adjacency of the modern municipalities), home_namesake. A home that repeats the written name is no evidence; one that repeats it and then names a municipality (Újezd, Dubí) is read at that municipality.
  • J2: qualified_elsewhere also matches the written name abbreviated — each written word equal to, or a shorter beginning of, the name's word, the qualifier's preposition equal (Újezd u Sv. Kříže is Újezd u Svatého Kříže): I2 then refuses the stripped head (ujezd:14 of okres Kralovice).
  • J3: a qualifier_conflict refusal (P2's or P4's) whose written name is within Levenshtein distance 2 of exactly one qualified settlement of the record's okres with the same head, and is no settlement elsewhere as written (exactly or abbreviated), links that settlement at tier p2_qualifier_fuzzy, flagged by its own uncertainty component qualifier_fuzzy (qualifier_fuzzy: Bystřice nad Perštejnem → bystrice-nad-pernstejnem:1, Ronov na Doubravou → ronov-nad-doubravou:1).

Changes in 0.14.0 (the 0.13.0 checkers' findings, 2026-11-17; switchable as RULES_140):

  • K1: J1's guard reaches the variant tiers. A bare name that an alternate, the VÚA German form or a ČSÚ viz alias sends to a settlement none of whose names is the written one (p2_alternate, p2_german, p2_alias) passes bare_namesake_verdict as p2_qualifier's bare branch does (bare_variant_verdict): Lhota | Náchod is no longer lhotky:4 (1910 Lhotka) while the okres holds Lhota pod Hořičkami, Lhota za Červeným Kostelcem and Řešetova Lhota. The alias table keeps each row's modern okres (Gazetteer.alias_okres), and an alias target is taken only where that okres is in the settlement's okres_all timeline or is its modern okres (Gazetteer.modern_okres), where the row names no okres, or where the okres holds no other namesake of the name (alias_in_okres: LHOTA viz Lhotka (Benešov / Ústí n. O.) is not Náchod's Lhotka). A bare name's parenthesised alternate that says where it lies is read so (locator_alternates): a preposition and its object is the name's qualifier (Lhota (u Č.Kostelce) is Lhota u Č.Kostelce), and the record's own okres or court, where the okres holds a namesake of the name, is dropped (Jeseník (Nymburk) | Poděbrady is not the court town Nymburk). Those records read the home column too.
  • K2: a qualified name written abbreviated (each word equal to the name's or a shorter beginning of it, as abbreviated_names) that holds exactly one settlement of the record's okres links it at tier p2_qualifier (flagged uncertain through settlement_piece_tier) instead of being refused (qualifier_abbreviated: Újezd u Sv. Kříže | Rokycany → ujezd-u-svateho-krize:1, Týniště n.Orl | Rychnov → tyniste-nad-orlici:1); inside the okres a written u (near) also meets another preposition (Lhota u Č.Kostelce → lhota-za-cervenym-kostelcem:1). The unresolved-okres path (D-a) reads a name the 1910 settlements do not hold through the same abbreviation, where it names exactly one (Brandýs n. L.).
  • K3: J3's bound is relative to the qualifier: a misspelt qualifier may be up to a quarter of the written qualifier's length away (never less than QUALIFIER_FUZZY_DISTANCE), still to exactly one settlement of the okres and only where the written name is no settlement anywhere (qualifier_fuzzy_bound: Veselí na Moravě → veseli-nad-moravou:1, Bystřice nad Perštýnem → bystrice-nad-pernstejnem:1).
  • K4: home_namesake also reads the home without its qualifier (its hyphen pieces too): home Trojanovice pod Radhoštěm is Trojanovice, whose modern municipality borders Kunčice pod Ondřejníkem.

Changes in 0.15.0 (the 0.14.0 checkers' findings, 2026-11-17; switchable as RULES_150):

  • L1: K1's exact-name test compares the written name with the target's full names only — its lexicon names, its 1910 name and the printed forms of its owner row — not the single words Gazetteer.pool_forms splits a two-word printed form into (Chocenická Lhota carries lhota there): Lhota ? | Plzeň is no longer chocenicka-lhota:1 through the alias while Hradišťská Lhotka is an obec of the okres too, Málkovice | Vyškov no longer moravske-malkovice:1 beside Bohaté (1910 Německé) Málkovice. A 1910 town whose name is the written one plus Město / Městys / Městečko (or Stadt / Markt), or a statutory city, still stands over the namesake villages (town_over_village: Libavá | Moravský Beroun stays mesto-libava:1).
  • L2: the alias's "no other namesake in the okres" fallback (alias_in_okres) holds only where the alias row's okres agrees, or the written name is a spelling of one of the target's own names (best difflib.SequenceMatcher ratio at least ALIAS_SPELLING_RATIO, alias_spelling), or a qualified name whose head is the target's. A renaming tied to another okres (ŠUMVALD viz Podlesí (Opava)) is set aside; if no later tier matches, the record is refused alias_other_okres (alias_other_okres), not linked to a settlement that merely shares the target's name (Šumvald | Šumperk is not 1910 Krumperky).
  • L3: the alias's namesakes (alias_rivals) leave out those in the target's own 1910 municipality (its register parts, or the other parts of the municipality it is a part of), so only obce and the parts of other municipalities stand against it: Bezděkov | Kladno is horni-bezdekov:2 again (Dolní Bezděkov is its part), read as J1 reads one candidate, tier p2_qualifier, flagged uncertain; Oujezd | Mladá Boleslav is ujezd:9 (Velký Oujezd) beside Malý Oujezd, both parts of Bratronice, flagged so. A part of another municipality still counts (Hutě | Kutná Hora: Stará Huť 1. and 2. díl lie in Lošiny and Sudějov; Lhotka | Čáslav: Žlebská Lhotka against Sovoluská Lhota) — narrower than "only obce", which would turn those into municipal coin flips.
  • L4: a bare name's locator alternate that resolves to nothing joined (Lhota (u Nákla)), while the bare name is a P1 settlement, is read by its object: the settlements of the okres whose name the object writes in another case (stem_agrees) are read as home_namesake reads a home, over P1's ids and the name's namesakes (locator_object_verdict). One pick other than P1's links at p2_qualifier (flagged uncertain): lhota-nad-moravou:1, whose modern municipality is Náklo. None, while P1's pick has a qualified name of another object (Lhota u Konice): refused ambiguous:p2_bare_namesakes.
  • L5: a qualifier written in another grammatical case or with another preposition reaches the one settlement of the okres with the head whose qualifier's object words agree by stem (qualifier_stem, stem_agrees: Czech case endings dropped, a common beginning of at least the shorter stem's length less three and never under four letters), where the written name is no settlement anywhere: Lhota u Červeného Kostelce | Náchod → lhota-za-cervenym-kostelcem:1, Ostrov n. Macochou | Boskovice → ostrov-u-macochy:1; tier p2_qualifier_fuzzy, component qualifier_fuzzy.
  • L6: alias_namesake_refusal's ambiguous:p2_bare_namesakes lists the alias target(s) it set aside beside the namesakes, so the refusal names both readings (Lhotka | Čáslav: sovoluska-lhota:1 and zlebska-lhotka:1).
  • L7: K2's qualifier_abbreviated takes K3's guard: nothing where the written name is a settlement anywhere (Gazetteer.global_name, Gazetteer.global_any) or its abbreviated reading names a settlement outside the okres.

Nothing here writes data/final: build writes output/places/birth_settlement_* and output/places/birthplace_rulings_queue.csv.

Usage

from utils.parsing import birth_settlement as bs
gaz = bs.load_gazetteer()                       # register + lexikon + overrides + rulings + heals
legion = bs.add_birth_settlement_columns(legion, gaz)   # the one notebook-02 entry point
legion = bs.correct_census_okres_id(legion, districts)  # 0.6.0 (T3): the census key, before §4b
result = bs.build()                             # both datasets, report, rulings queue

def rules_off(rules=RULES):
    """Inside the block the given *rules* (of :data:`RULES_070`, :data:`RULES_080`, :data:`RULES_090`,
    :data:`RULES_100`, :data:`RULES_110`, :data:`RULES_120`, :data:`RULES_130`, :data:`RULES_140` or
    :data:`RULES_150`) do not apply (measurement only; with every 0.15.0 rule off the module gives the 0.14.0 links,
    with the 0.14.0 ones off as well the 0.13.0 links, and so on)."""
    unknown = (set(rules) - set(RULES_070) - set(RULES_080) - set(RULES_090) - set(RULES_100)
               - set(RULES_110) - set(RULES_120) - set(RULES_130) - set(RULES_140) - set(RULES_150))
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"no such rule: {sorted(unknown)}")
    before = set(_RULES_OFF)
    _RULES_OFF.update(rules)
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        _RULES_OFF.clear()
        _RULES_OFF.update(before)

def key(text) -> str:
    """Match key: :func:`records_geo._norm` (unaccented, lower, ``-`` → space, ``n.`` → ``nad``),
    then every other punctuation mark dropped.

    0.9.0 (E8): an interior ``n.`` / ``p.`` right before a capital letter is ``nad`` / ``pod`` also when
    no space follows it (*Ústí n.Orlicí* → ``usti nad orlici``, *Frenštát p.Radhoštěm* → ``frenstat pod
    radhostem``); :func:`records_geo._norm` expands only a free-standing ``n.``. No gazetteer name carries
    the shape (checked 2026-11-17), so the indexes are unchanged."""
    if _on("E8") and isinstance(text, str) and ("n." in text or "p." in text):
        text = _ABBREV_NP_RE.sub(lambda m: " nad " if m.group(1) == "n" else " pod ", text)
    k = _norm(text)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", re.sub(r"[^\w\s]", " ", k)).strip()

def form_set(keys) -> set[str]:
    """Comparison forms of name keys: each space-free, as written and without its qualifier, ``ß``
    folded to ``ss`` (the register prints *Roßbach*, the lexicon *Rossbach*)."""
    out = set()
    for k in keys:
        if k:
            k = k.replace("ß", "ss")
            out |= {nospace(k), nospace(strip_qualifier(k))}
    out.discard("")
    return out

def clean_birthplace(raw) -> tuple[str | None, tuple[str, ...]]:
    """``(name, alternates)`` from a birthplace cell; ``(None, ())`` for a placeholder.

    ``též Ronšperk`` → ``Ronšperk``; ``Mirošov (též Nedašov)`` → ``Mirošov`` + ``Nedašov``;
    ``Vrajt)`` → ``Vrajt``; ``Lučice-Janovec 1. díl`` → ``Lučice-Janovec``;
    ``Krásná Lípa ? Krásná Lípa`` → ``Krásná Lípa``; ``(Velké) Jirny`` → ``Velké Jirny`` + ``Jirny``.
    """
    if raw is None or (isinstance(raw, float) and pd.isna(raw)) or raw is pd.NA:
        return None, ()
    s = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", str(raw)).replace("+", " ")
    s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()
    if _PLACEHOLDER_RE.match(s):
        return None, ()
    alts: list[str] = []
    lead = re.match(r"^\(([^()]+)\)\s*(\S.*)$", s)              # "(Velké) Jirny"
    if lead:
        alts.append(lead.group(2))
        s = f"{lead.group(1)} {lead.group(2)}"
    alts += [a for a in re.findall(r"\(([^()]*)\)", s)]
    s = re.sub(r"\([^()]*\)", " ", s)
    s = s.replace("(", " ").replace(")", " ")
    s = _DIL_RE.sub(" ", s)
    pieces = [p for p in re.split(r"\s+\?\s*|\?\s+|,\s*též\b|\btéž\b", s) if p and p.strip()]
    pieces = [_TEZ_RE.sub("", p).strip(" ?,.;:-–") for p in pieces]
    pieces = [re.sub(r"\s+", " ", p.replace("?", " ")).strip() for p in pieces]
    pieces = [p for p in pieces if p and not _PLACEHOLDER_RE.match(p)]
    alts = [re.sub(r"\s+", " ", _TEZ_RE.sub("", a).replace("?", " ")).strip(" ,.;:-–")
            for a in alts]
    alts = [a for a in alts if a and not _PLACEHOLDER_RE.match(a)]
    if not pieces:
        return (alts[0], tuple(alts[1:])) if alts else (None, ())
    out = list(dict.fromkeys([*pieces[1:], *alts]))
    return pieces[0], tuple(a for a in out if key(a) != key(pieces[0]))

def german_form(value) -> str | None:
    """The VÚA German exonym's first usable form (``-; Biela-Tscheche`` debris skipped)."""
    if value is None or (isinstance(value, float) and pd.isna(value)) or value is pd.NA:
        return None
    for item in str(value).split(";"):
        item = re.sub(r"[-–]\s*\?\s*$", "", item).strip(" -–?()")
        if item and not _PLACEHOLDER_RE.match(item):
            return item
    return None

class Gazetteer:
    """Every index the passes read, built once by :func:`build_gazetteer`."""
    reg: dict = field(default_factory=dict)          # (key, okres) -> {sid}   primary editions
    reg_alt: dict = field(default_factory=dict)      # (key, okres) -> {sid}   de-bohemia forms
    lex: dict = field(default_factory=dict)          # (key, okres) -> {sid}
    nospace: dict = field(default_factory=dict)      # (nospace key, okres) -> {sid}

def xref_both_owner(use: list) -> tuple[object, list]:
    """``(kept row, dropped rows)`` when every row holding a settlement in one edition prints the
    ``viz`` / ``siehe`` marker (0.4.0): the text sits on both the real row and the cross-reference
    (*Pivoň, Stockau . odd. viz*: municipality 345, part 1), so :data:`_XREF_RE` cannot tell them
    apart. The one municipality-level row is kept when it is the most populous; a part row whose
    population is :data:`XREF_PART_SHARE` (10 %) of it or less is dropped. ``(None, [])`` when
    that does not leave one municipality (two municipality rows, a population missing, a part row
    above 10 %: *Záblatí* part 64 of 312 stays two owners)."""
    munis = [r for r in use if r.place_level == "municipality"]
    if len(munis) != 1 or _row_pop(munis[0]) is None:
        return None, []
    keep = munis[0]
    others = [r for r in use if (str(r.court_key), int(r.muni_seq)) != (str(keep.court_key), int(keep.muni_seq))]
    if any(_row_pop(r) is None or r.place_level != "part"
           or _row_pop(r) > XREF_PART_SHARE * _row_pop(keep) for r in others):
        return None, []
    return keep, others

def register_owners(places: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[dict, set, list]:
    """``({sid: owner}, {sids two municipalities hold}, [viz-on-every-row decisions])`` from the
    land's first edition holding it.

    A cross-reference row (``… odd. viz X``) names a detached piece filed elsewhere and owns nothing
    unless it is the only row holding the settlement; when **every** row is one, see
    :func:`xref_both_owner`. ``owner`` carries the row's register key, level, court, okres and the
    settlement_id of its municipality row (``None`` if unanchored).
    """
    muni_sid = {(e, str(c), int(m)): s for e, c, m, q, s in
                zip(places["edition"], places["court_key"], places["muni_seq"],
                    places["settlement_seq"], places["settlement_id"]) if q == 0 and pd.notna(s)}
    rows_by_sid: dict[str, list] = {}
    for r in places[places["settlement_id"].notna() & places["okres_id"].notna()].itertuples(index=False):
        xref = bool(_XREF_RE.search(str(r.printed_name)))
        rows_by_sid.setdefault(r.settlement_id, []).append((r, xref))
    owners, two, xref_both = {}, set(), []
    for sid, rows in rows_by_sid.items():
        land = int(rows[0][0].okres_id) // 1000
        for ed in EDITION_ORDER.get(land, ()):
            ed_rows = [(r, x) for r, x in rows if r.edition == ed]
            if not ed_rows:
                continue
            use = [r for r, x in ed_rows if not x] or [r for r, _x in ed_rows]
            if len({(str(r.court_key), int(r.muni_seq)) for r in use}) > 1:
                keep, dropped = (xref_both_owner(use) if all(x for _r, x in ed_rows) else (None, []))
                if keep is None:
                    two.add(sid)
                    break
                xref_both.append({"settlement_id": sid, "edition": ed,
                                  "kept": f"{ed}|{keep.court_key}|{int(keep.muni_seq)}|{int(keep.settlement_seq)}",
                                  "kept_pop": _row_pop(keep),
                                  "dropped": [f"{ed}|{r.court_key}|{int(r.muni_seq)}|{int(r.settlement_seq)}"
                                              f" ({_row_pop(r):g})" for r in dropped]})
                use = [keep]
            r = min(use, key=lambda r: int(r.settlement_seq))
            owners[sid] = {"edition": ed, "court_key": str(r.court_key), "muni_seq": int(r.muni_seq),
                           "settlement_seq": int(r.settlement_seq), "level": r.place_level,
                           "court_id": int(r.court_id) if pd.notna(r.court_id) else None,
                           "okres_id": int(r.okres_id),
                           "muni_sid": muni_sid.get((ed, str(r.court_key), int(r.muni_seq))),
                           "printed_name": str(r.printed_name),
                           "printed_keys": tuple(dict.fromkeys(
                               k for f in pn.cell_forms(r.printed_name)
                               for k in (key(f), key(f).replace("ß", "ss")))),
                           "printed_forms": form_set(key(f) for f in pn.cell_forms(r.printed_name))}
            break
    return owners, two, xref_both

def printed_split(form: str) -> list[str]:
    """A printed form and, when it is two capitalised names run together without a comma
    (``Novosady Blatiny``: the Moravian edition's *Novosady t. Blatiny*), each name as well.
    Each name must be 3+ letters (``Velká Úpa I`` and ``Lhota u Brna`` stay whole)."""
    form = str(form).strip()
    words = form.split()
    if (len(words) == 2 and all(len(w) >= 3 and w[0].isupper() and w.isalpha() for w in words)):
        return [form, *words]
    return [form]

def pooled_forms(places: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[str, set]:
    """``{sid: form_set}`` of the printed forms of **every** register row holding the settlement —
    both editions, municipality and part rows, cross-references included (0.3.0). The owner check
    refuses only when none of them shares a form with the settlement's own names: the Czech cell
    of *Doubravička* prints *Doubravice, Kleindoubra- witz*, the German cell *Doubravička*."""
    out: dict[str, set] = {}
    has = places[places["settlement_id"].notna()]
    for sid, cell in zip(has["settlement_id"], has["printed_name"]):
        out.setdefault(sid, set()).update(
            form_set(key(p) for f in pn.cell_forms(cell) for p in printed_split(f)))
    return out

def greater_prague_sids(g: Gazetteer) -> tuple[set, dict]

(sids inside the 1922 annexation, {law name: sid or None}).

Each name of GREATER_PRAGUE_1922 is resolved inside the okres the law files it under (D-144: one id, else the one obec); a part or hamlet joins too (Pankrác of Nusle) when its parent, resolved inside the hamlet's own 1910 okres (register, then lexikon), is a joined obec — never by the parent's name alone across the five agglomeration okresy (0.1.0 put Bořanovice and Pakoměřice, hamlets of Karlín's Sedlec, under Smíchov's joined Sedlec, and Žabovřesky, of Smíchov's Záběhlice, under Vinohrady's). So does every register part of a joined municipality row. GREATER_PRAGUE_EXCLUDED stays out either way.

def greater_prague_sids(g: Gazetteer) -> tuple[set, dict]:
    """``(sids inside the 1922 annexation, {law name: sid or None})``.

    Each name of :data:`GREATER_PRAGUE_1922` is resolved inside the okres the law files it under
    (D-144: one id, else the one obec); a part or hamlet joins too (Pankrác of Nusle) when its
    parent, resolved **inside the hamlet's own 1910 okres** (register, then lexikon), is a joined
    obec — never by the parent's name alone across the five agglomeration okresy (0.1.0 put
    Bořanovice and Pakoměřice, hamlets of Karlín's Sedlec, under Smíchov's joined Sedlec, and
    Žabovřesky, of Smíchov's Záběhlice, under Vinohrady's). So does every register part of a joined
    municipality row. :data:`GREATER_PRAGUE_EXCLUDED` stays out either way.
    """
    resolved = {}
    for oid, names in GREATER_PRAGUE_1922.items():
        for name in names:
            ids = {s for s in g.prague.get(key(name), set())
                   if g.okres_of.get(s) == oid and s not in g.quarter_sids}
            v, val = decide(ids, _lex_status(g))
            resolved[name] = val if v == "ok" else None
    excluded = {key(n) for n in GREATER_PRAGUE_EXCLUDED}
    joiners = {s for n, s in resolved.items() if s and n not in GREATER_PRAGUE_PARTS_ONLY}
    out = {s for s in resolved.values() if s}
    for sid, pk in g.parent_key.items():
        oid = g.okres_of.get(sid)
        if not pk or oid not in PRAGUE_AGGLOMERATION or sid in out:
            continue
        if key(g.cs_name.get(sid)) in excluded:
            continue
        v, _t, parent = _lookup(pk, oid, g)
        if v == "ok" and parent != sid and parent in joiners:
            out.add(sid)
    out |= {sid for sid, o in g.owner.items() if o.get("muni_sid") in joiners
            and key(g.cs_name.get(sid)) not in excluded}
    return out, resolved

def greater_prague_check(g: Gazetteer) -> dict:
    """The lexikon's own view: ring obce whose timeline names no okres after the ring okresy."""
    lex = {sid for sid, oid in g.okres_of.items()
           if oid in PRAGUE_AGGLOMERATION - {PRAHA_OKRES_ID} and g.status.get(sid) == "obec"
           and g.timeline.get(sid) and g.timeline[sid] <= _RING_OKRES_NAMES}
    law, resolved = greater_prague_sids(g)
    law_obce = {s for s in resolved.values() if s}
    law_okres = {n: oid for oid, names in GREATER_PRAGUE_1922.items() for n in names}
    unresolved = sorted(n for n, s in resolved.items() if s is None)
    # documented exclusions (0.3.0): a law name with no settlements_1910 row in its okres is left
    # out of the resolution, with every settlement of that name elsewhere (Zátiší of Modřany)
    detail = {n: {"okres_id": law_okres[n],
                  "settlements_of_the_name": [f"{s} {g.cs_name.get(s)} (okres {g.okres_of.get(s)})"
                                              for s in sorted(g.global_name.get(key(n), set()))],
                  "note": "no settlements_1910 row of this name in the okres the law names: "
                          "excluded from the 1922 resolution"} for n in unresolved}
    return {"law_names": sum(len(v) for v in GREATER_PRAGUE_1922.values()),
            "law_resolved": len(law_obce),
            "law_unresolved": unresolved,
            "law_unresolved_detail": detail,
            "lexikon_timeline_obce": len(lex),
            "in_law_not_timeline": sorted(g.cs_name[s] for s in law_obce - lex),
            "in_timeline_not_law": sorted(g.cs_name[s] for s in lex - law_obce),
            "settlements_flagged": len(law)}

def build_gazetteer(settlements: pd.DataFrame, places: pd.DataFrame, districts: pd.DataFrame, aliases: pd.DataFrame | None, municipalities: pd.DataFrame, heals: pd.DataFrame | None=None, foreign_names=None) -> Gazetteer

All indexes from the frames (places already carrying the anchor overrides).

Since 0.3.0 the rows of a municipality that contradicted_keys finds contradicted for a settlement do not hold that settlement in the gazetteer (they are neither indexed nor an owner): an automatic refusal of a frozen anchor, never a new one (the cz row Kostomlátky no longer answers to kostomlaty-nad-labem:1; the register join then reports the table's row as differing).

foreign_names (0.6.0): okres and district names outside the Czech lands — a set, or foreign_name_keys's {"districts", "obce"} (an obec name a Czech-lands settlement also carries is dropped); FOREIGN_OKRES is always added, a Czech okres or court name never.

def build_gazetteer(settlements: pd.DataFrame, places: pd.DataFrame, districts: pd.DataFrame,
                    aliases: pd.DataFrame | None, municipalities: pd.DataFrame,
                    heals: pd.DataFrame | None = None, foreign_names=None) -> Gazetteer:
    """All indexes from the frames (``places`` already carrying the anchor overrides).

    Since 0.3.0 the rows of a municipality that :func:`contradicted_keys` finds contradicted for a
    settlement do not hold that settlement in the gazetteer (they are neither indexed nor an owner):
    an automatic *refusal* of a frozen anchor, never a new one (the cz row *Kostomlátky* no longer
    answers to ``kostomlaty-nad-labem:1``; the register join then reports the table's row as
    differing).

    *foreign_names* (0.6.0): okres and district names outside the Czech lands — a set, or
    :func:`foreign_name_keys`'s ``{"districts", "obce"}`` (an obec name a Czech-lands settlement also
    carries is dropped); :data:`FOREIGN_OKRES` is always added, a Czech okres or court name never."""
    heals = heals if heals is not None else pn.heal_frame(settlements)
    attrs = pn.healed_attributes(settlements, heals)
    forms = pn.name_index(settlements, heals)
    g = Gazetteer(okres_names=_okres_names(districts), seat_court=_seat_courts(districts))
    _lexikon_indexes(g, attrs, forms)
    g.muni_keys_contradicted = contradicted_keys(places, g.forms_of)
    _owners_before, two_before, _x = register_owners(places)
    places = drop_contradicted(places, g.muni_keys_contradicted)
    _register_indexes(g, places)
    g.owner, g.two_owners, g.xref_both = register_owners(places)
    # 0.4.0: dropping a contradicted row is a refusal, never a new link — a settlement it would take
    # out of two_owners stays there (reported in contradicted_freed)
    g.contradicted_freed = sorted(two_before - g.two_owners)
    g.two_owners |= set(g.contradicted_freed)
    _global_indexes(g)
    for r in districts.itertuples(index=False):          # court names name their okres too
        for v in (getattr(r, "gerichtsbezirk_cs", None), getattr(r, "gerichtsbezirk_de", None)):
            if isinstance(v, str) and key(v):
                for kk in (key(v), nospace(key(v))):
                    g.okres_by_name.setdefault(kk, set()).add(_okres_id(r.okres_code))
    _prague_indexes(g, attrs, forms, places)
    _statutory(g, districts, attrs)
    g.greater_prague, _ = greater_prague_sids(g)
    g.pool_forms = pooled_forms(places)
    g.muni_keys = municipality_row_keys(places)
    g.register_munis = set(municipalities["settlement_id"].dropna())
    g.register_muni_key = municipality_keys(municipalities)
    if g.register_munis and not g.register_muni_key:
        raise ValueError("register_municipalities carries no key columns (edition, court_key or "
                         "court_id, muni_seq; or register_key): the join compares keys since 0.3.0")
    g.register_key_sid = {k: s for s, k in g.register_muni_key.items()}
    if aliases is not None:
        viz_okres = aliases["viz_okres"] if "viz_okres" in aliases.columns else [None] * len(aliases)
        for a, t, o in zip(aliases["cs_name"], aliases["viz_target"], viz_okres):
            if isinstance(a, str) and isinstance(t, str):
                _add(g.alias, key(a), key(t))
                # 0.14.0 (K1): the row's modern okres with it ("" where the row names none)
                _add(g.alias_okres, key(a), (key(t), okres_token(o) if isinstance(o, str) else ""))
    _later_indexes(g, places, foreign_names)
    return g

def foreign_name_keys(districts_hu: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
                      settlements_hu: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
    """Keys of the Hungarian frame's names (0.6.0): ``districts`` — every district and county name
    (``districts_hu_1910``: Slovak, Magyar and modern names of each járás and vármegye;
    ``settlements_hu_1910``: each obec's 1910 okres) — and ``obce`` — every Slovak obec name (an
    interwar okres was named after its seat: *Modrý Kameň*, *Bánovce nad Bebravou*). What a VÚA okres
    string names when it is not a Czech-lands okres; an obec name some Czech-lands settlement also
    carries (*Vysočany*) is left out by :func:`build_gazetteer`."""
    out: dict[str, set[str]] = {"districts": set(), "obce": set()}
    for part, frame, cols in (("districts", districts_hu, ("name_sk", "name_sk_alt", "name_sk_modern", "name_hu",
                                                           "jaras_hu", "megye_sk", "megye_hu")),
                              ("districts", settlements_hu, ("okres_sk",)),
                              ("obce", settlements_hu, ("obec_sk",))):
        if frame is None:
            continue
        for c in cols:
            if c in frame.columns:
                out[part] |= {key(v) for v in frame[c].dropna().astype(str)}
        out[part].discard("")
    return out

def municipality_keys(municipalities: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[str, str]:
    """``{settlement_id: "edition|court_key|muni_seq"}`` of ``register_municipalities``.

    A ``register_key`` column (``edition|court_key|muni_seq``) is used as is; else ``court_key``;
    else the court id as text, which is the register's ``court_key`` (they differ on one unresolved
    de-bohemia row of ``register_places``, which holds no municipality). Rows without a
    ``settlement_id`` key nothing. Raises if a settlement holds two keys."""
    m = municipalities[municipalities["settlement_id"].notna()]
    if not len(m):
        return {}
    if "register_key" in m.columns:
        keys = m["register_key"].astype(str).map(lambda k: "|".join(k.split("|")[:3]))
    elif {"edition", "muni_seq"} <= set(m.columns) and ("court_key" in m.columns or "court_id" in m.columns):
        court = m["court_key"] if "court_key" in m.columns else m["court_id"]
        court = court.astype(object).map(lambda c: c if isinstance(c, str) else
                                         "" if pd.isna(c) else str(int(c)))
        keys = m["edition"].astype(str) + "|" + court + "|" + m["muni_seq"].astype("int64").astype(str)
    else:
        return {}
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    for sid, k in zip(m["settlement_id"].astype(str), keys):
        if out.setdefault(sid, k) != k:
            raise ValueError(f"register_municipalities: {sid} under two keys {out[sid]} / {k}")
    return out

def load_gazetteer(final_dir: Path = FINAL, overrides: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
                   heals: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
                   rulings: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
                   include_unconfirmed: bool = False) -> Gazetteer:
    """The gazetteer from ``data/final`` (read only), the anchor overrides **and** the anchor rulings
    (``reference/places/anchor_rulings.csv``: anchor / replace / unanchor) applied in memory through
    :func:`utils.recheck.anchor_overrides.apply`. Only the rulings the author confirmed
    (``ruled_by = author``) apply unless ``include_unconfirmed=True``, which adds the ``evidence``
    ones (passed through to :func:`anchor_overrides.apply`). Pass ``rulings=`` an empty frame to
    measure the state before the rulings.

    *heals* (:func:`place_names.heal_frame`) may be passed in; building it takes about a minute.
    It reads the register's names, so it should come from the same rulings mode.
    """
    from utils.recheck import anchor_overrides as ao
    final_dir = Path(final_dir)
    settlements = pd.read_parquet(final_dir / "geo" / "settlements_1910.parquet")
    places = pd.read_parquet(final_dir / "register_rechecked" / "register_places.parquet")
    overrides = ao.load_overrides() if overrides is None else overrides
    rulings = ao.load_rulings() if rulings is None else rulings
    places = ao.apply(places, overrides, rulings, include_unconfirmed=include_unconfirmed)
    if heals is None:
        heals = pn.heal_frame(settlements, pn.official_names(final_dir / "geo"),
                              pn.register_names(places))
    muni_path = final_dir / "register_rechecked" / "register_municipalities.parquet"
    hu = [final_dir / "geo" / f for f in ("districts_hu_1910.parquet", "settlements_hu_1910.parquet")]
    hu_frames = [pd.read_parquet(f) if f.exists() else None for f in hu]
    foreign = foreign_name_keys(*hu_frames)                                                    # 0.6.0
    g = build_gazetteer(
        settlements, places, pd.read_parquet(final_dir / "geo" / "districts_1910.parquet"),
        pd.read_csv(final_dir / "geo" / "settlement_aliases_1910.csv"),
        pd.read_parquet(muni_path, columns=_municipality_columns(muni_path)), heals,
        foreign_names=foreign)
    _hu_indexes(g, hu_frames[1], hu_frames[0])                                    # 0.8.0 (A6), 0.9.0 (E2)
    geo = final_dir / "geo" / "settlements_1910_geo.parquet"                       # 0.11.0 (H1)
    if not geo.exists():           # 0.12.0 (I5): a required input, as the others — H1 must not turn off silently
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"birth_settlement needs {geo} (data/final/geo/settlements_1910_geo.parquet: "
                                "each 1910 settlement's modern municipality, H1's evidence)")
    import pyarrow.parquet as pq
    geo_cols = [c for c in ("settlement_id", "obec_name", "obec_kod", "okres_name")          # okres_name: 0.14.0 (K1)
                if c in set(pq.read_schema(geo).names)]
    modern_obec_index(g, pd.read_parquet(geo, columns=geo_cols))
    adjacency = final_dir / "geo" / "ruian_obce_adjacency.parquet"                # 0.13.0 (J1)
    if not adjacency.exists():     # as I5: J1's home evidence must not turn off silently
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"birth_settlement needs {adjacency} (data/final/geo/ruian_obce_adjacency.parquet: "
                                "which modern municipalities border, J1's home evidence)")
    obec_neighbours_index(g, pd.read_parquet(adjacency, columns=["obec_kod", "neighbour_kod"]))
    g.rulings_refused = [str(x) for x in places.attrs.get("anchor_rulings_refused", [])]
    g.rulings_unconfirmed = list(places.attrs.get("anchor_rulings_unconfirmed", []))
    g.rulings_applied = [tuple(k) for k in places.attrs.get("anchor_rulings_applied", [])]
    g.include_unconfirmed = bool(include_unconfirmed)
    return g

def modern_obec_index(g: Gazetteer, geo: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    """H1 (0.11.0): :attr:`Gazetteer.modern_obec` — each 1910 settlement's modern municipality (RÚIAN
    ``obec_name`` of ``data/final/geo/settlements_1910_geo.parquet``, keyed by ``settlement_id``) as a :func:`key`;
    a settlement with no RÚIAN match is left out. Read only as G1's last evidence (:func:`right_under_left`,
    :func:`left_in_right_modern`)."""
    for sid, name in zip(geo["settlement_id"], geo["obec_name"]):
        if isinstance(sid, str) and isinstance(name, str) and key(name):
            g.modern_obec[sid] = key(name)
    if "obec_kod" in geo.columns:         # 0.13.0 (J1): the modern obec's RÚIAN code, for adjacency
        for sid, kod in zip(geo["settlement_id"], geo["obec_kod"]):
            if isinstance(sid, str) and kod is not None and not pd.isna(kod):
                g.modern_obec_kod[sid] = int(kod)
    if "okres_name" in geo.columns:       # 0.14.0 (K1): the modern okres, for a ČSÚ alias row's viz_okres
        for sid, name in zip(geo["settlement_id"], geo["okres_name"]):
            if isinstance(sid, str) and isinstance(name, str) and okres_token(name):
                g.modern_okres[sid] = okres_token(name)

def decide(ids, status_of) -> tuple[str, object]:
    """D-144 on a set of ids: ``("ok", sid)`` / ``("ambiguous", sorted ids)`` / ``("none", None)``.

    *status_of* maps a sid to its status; ``"obec"`` is the independent municipality.
    """
    ids = set(ids or ())
    if not ids:
        return "none", None
    if len(ids) == 1:
        return "ok", next(iter(ids))
    obce = [s for s in ids if status_of(s) == "obec"]
    if len(obce) == 1:
        return "ok", obce[0]
    return "ambiguous", tuple(sorted(ids))

def numbered_guard(k: str, oid, verdict: str, val, g: Gazetteer) -> tuple[str, object]:
    """A key without a Roman numeral that reached a settlement the register prints with one, while
    the register prints 2+ numbered siblings of that base in the okres, is ambiguous across them
    (0.3.0): the German cell *Großaupa I, Velká Úpa* prints the bare *Velká Úpa* beside the
    numbered name, and 0.2.0 sent every bare *Velká Úpa* to ``velka-upa-i:1``."""
    if verdict != "ok" or _KEY_NUMERAL_RE.match(k):
        return verdict, val
    sibs = g.numbered.get((k, oid)) or g.numbered.get((nospace(k), oid)) or {}
    if val in sibs and len(sibs) > 1:
        return "ambiguous", tuple(sorted(sibs))
    return verdict, val

def seat_rule(k: str, oid, ids, g: Gazetteer)

The seat rule (0.4.0, the author): a name that is the okres's own name town (k among the okres's names), answered by several settlements, is the one in the okres's seat court — and, if the seat court holds several, the one whose headword is the name. None when that does not leave exactly one (Podbořany, okres Podbořany: podborany:1 of court Podbořany, not podboranky:1 of court Jesenice, whose 1910 name was also Podbořany).

def seat_rule(k: str, oid, ids, g: Gazetteer):
    """The seat rule (0.4.0, the author): a name that is the okres's own name town (*k* among the
    okres's names), answered by several settlements, is the one in the okres's **seat court** —
    and, if the seat court holds several, the one whose headword is the name. ``None`` when that
    does not leave exactly one (*Podbořany*, okres Podbořany: ``podborany:1`` of court Podbořany,
    not ``podboranky:1`` of court Jesenice, whose 1910 name was also *Podbořany*)."""
    if oid is None or k not in g.okres_names.get(oid, set()) or oid not in g.seat_court:
        return None
    seat = [s for s in ids if _court_of(s, g) == g.seat_court[oid]]
    if len(seat) > 1:
        seat = [s for s in seat if key(g.cs_name.get(s)) == k]
    if len(seat) != 1:
        return None
    # 0.4.1: the seat answers only through another of its names (German *Plan* for Planá) while a
    # non-seat candidate's own Czech headword is the written key (*Pláň*, plan:3): refuse
    if key(g.cs_name.get(seat[0])) != k and any(key(g.cs_name.get(s)) == k
                                                for s in ids if s != seat[0]):
        return None
    return seat[0]

def prague_shape(text: str) -> tuple[str, object, str] | None:
    """``(kind, number, name)`` for a Prague-shaped string, else ``None``.

    ``kind``: ``roman`` (``Praha XI.-Žižkov`` → 11, ``Žižkov``), ``arabic`` (``Praha 2``, post-1949),
    ``named`` (``Praha-Smíchov``, ``Smíchov, Praha``), ``city`` (``Praha``, ``Hlavní město Praha``).
    """
    if _NEAR_PRAHA_RE.search(text):
        return None
    text = _CAPITAL_RE.sub("", text)
    m = _PRAHA_RE.match(text)
    if not m:
        tail = _PRAHA_TAIL_RE.match(text)
        return ("named", None, tail.group(1).strip(" ,-–")) if tail and tail.group(1).strip() else None
    rest = m.group(1).strip(" ,-–.")
    if not rest:
        return "city", None, ""
    a = _ARABIC_RE.match(rest)
    if a:
        return "arabic", int(a.group(1)), ""
    r = _ROMAN_RE.match(rest)
    if r and r.group(1) in _ROMAN and (not r.group(2) or rest[len(r.group(1)):][:1] in ".-–, "):
        return "roman", _ROMAN[r.group(1)], r.group(2).strip(" ,-–.")
    return "named", None, rest

def p3_prague(text: str, oid, g: Gazetteer, alts=()) -> tuple[str, str, object, object, tuple]:
    """``(verdict, tier, value, quarter number, tie)`` for the Prague forms; verdict ``none`` = not
    Prague; *tie* = the ids a pool preference chose among (:func:`_prague_pool`).

    A 1923 district number with a name (``Praha VIII.-Troja``) is read by the name: post-1922
    Praha VIII was Libeň *and* the joined Troja, Kobylisy, Bohnice, Střížkov. The number alone
    (``Praha II.``) names a 1910 quarter only for I–VIII. A bare city reading with an alternate
    that is not itself a Prague form (``Praha? Hrubý Jeseník``) is refused
    ``praha_city_with_alternate``: the clerk did not know which. A bare name in an agglomeration
    okres that resolves to a quarter (*Libeň*, okres Praha) is ``p3_prague_quarter`` (0.3.0).
    """
    shape = prague_shape(text)
    if shape is None:
        if oid is not None and oid in PRAGUE_AGGLOMERATION:
            v, val, tie = _prague_pool(text, g)
            return v, _p3_tier(val, g), val, None, tie
        return "none", "", None, None, ()
    kind, num, name = shape
    if kind == "city":
        if any(prague_shape(a) is None for a in alts):
            return "refused", "p3_prague", "praha_city_with_alternate", None, ()
        return "ok", "p3_prague_city", PRAHA_SID, None, ()
    if kind == "arabic":
        return "refused", "p3_prague", "praha_post1949_number", num, ()
    v, val, tie = _prague_pool(name, g) if name else ("none", None, ())
    if v == "none" and kind == "named":
        v, val, tie = _prague_pool(text, g)
    if v == "ok":
        return v, _p3_tier(val, g), val, num, tie
    if v == "ambiguous":
        return v, "p3_prague_suburb", val, num, ()
    if kind == "roman" and num in g.quarters:
        return "ok", "p3_prague_quarter", g.quarters[num], num, ()
    if not name:
        return "refused", "p3_prague", "praha_district_unnamed", num, ()
    return "none", "p3_prague_suburb", None, num, ()

def alias_in_okres(k: str, sid: str, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """K1 (0.14.0): settlement *sid* of okres *oid*, reached through a ČSÚ ``viz`` alias of the key *k*, is the
    alias's target — a row of the alias names a modern okres (``viz_okres``) that is in *sid*'s ``okres_all``
    timeline or is its modern okres (:attr:`Gazetteer.modern_okres`), or names none; or else the okres holds no
    other namesake of *k* (:func:`bare_namesakes`). *LHOTA viz Lhotka (Benešov / Ústí n. O.)* does not reach
    ``lhotky:4`` of okres Náchod (1910 *Lhotka*, timeline Nové Město|Náchod), where Lhota pod Hořičkami, Lhota za
    Červeným Kostelcem and Řešetova Lhota lie; *TĚŠICE viz Tršice (Olomouc)* reaches ``trsice:2`` (timeline
    Hranice|Olomouc).

    0.15.0 (L2): where the row's okres disagrees, the fallback holds only where the written name is a spelling of one
    of the target's own names (:func:`alias_spelling`): *ŠUMVALD viz Podlesí (Opava)* does not reach ``podlesi:14`` of
    okres Šumperk (1910 Krumperky). L3: the namesakes counted are :func:`alias_rivals`'s."""
    if alias_okres_agrees(k, sid, oid, g):
        return True
    if alias_rivals(k, sid, oid, g):
        return False
    return not _on("L2") or alias_spelling(k, sid, g)

def alias_rivals(k: str, sid: str, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> set:
    """K1 (0.14.0): the namesakes of *k* in okres *oid* (:func:`bare_namesakes`) other than the alias target *sid* that
    stand against it. 0.15.0 (L3): not a namesake in the target's own 1910 municipality (:func:`_muni_of`: a register
    part of *sid*, or a part of the municipality *sid* is a part of) — the municipality is certain whichever of them
    the record meant: Dolní Bezděkov is a part of Horní Bezděkov; Malý Oujezd and Velký Oujezd (okres Mladá Boleslav)
    are both parts of Bratronice. So only obce, and the parts of **other** municipalities, are rivals: Stará Huť 2. díl
    (a part of Sudějov) stands against the alias's Stará Huť (a part of Lošiny), and the osada Žlebská Lhotka against
    *LHOTKA viz Lhota (Blansko)*'s Sovoluská Lhota (okres Čáslav). A namesake whose municipality is unknown is a
    rival."""
    names = bare_namesakes(k, oid, g) - {sid}
    if not _on("L3"):
        return names
    own = _muni_of(sid, g)
    return {s for s in names if own is None or _muni_of(s, g) != own}

def alias_spelling(k: str, sid: str, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """L2 (0.15.0): the written key *k* is a spelling of one of settlement *sid*'s own names — its lexicon names, the
    forms of every register row holding it, its 1910 name and its owner row's printed forms — at a
    :class:`difflib.SequenceMatcher` ratio of at least :data:`ALIAS_SPELLING_RATIO` (*Bezděkov* / Horní Bezděkov
    0.76), or *k* is qualified and its head is one of them (*Újezd u Průhonic* / Újezd). *Šumvald* / Podlesí,
    Krumperky, Grumberg (0.27) is not."""
    own = (g.forms_of.get(sid, set()) | g.pool_forms.get(sid, set()) | g.forms_1910.get(sid, set())
           | ((g.owner.get(sid) or {}).get("printed_forms") or set()))
    if not own or not k:
        return False
    head = strip_qualifier(k)
    if head != k and nospace(head) in own:
        return True
    nk = nospace(k)
    return any(difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, nk, f).ratio() >= ALIAS_SPELLING_RATIO for f in own)

def alias_other_okres(k: str, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """L2 (0.15.0): a ``viz`` alias of the bare key *k* reached settlements of okres *oid*, and every one of them was set
    aside only because its row names another okres and *k* spells none of its names (:func:`alias_in_okres`,
    :func:`alias_spelling`) — no namesake stood against it. Where no later tier matched, :func:`_first_verdict`
    refuses the record ``alias_other_okres`` instead of ``unmatched``."""
    if oid is None or not k or strip_qualifier(k) != k:
        return False
    reached = {s for t in g.alias.get(k, set()) for s in g.lex.get((t, oid), set())}
    return bool(reached) and all(not alias_okres_agrees(k, s, oid, g) and not alias_rivals(k, s, oid, g)
                                 and not alias_spelling(k, s, g) for s in reached)

def alias_okres_agrees(k: str, sid: str, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """K1 (0.14.0): a ``viz`` row of the alias key *k* that reaches settlement *sid* of okres *oid* names a modern okres
    in *sid*'s ``okres_all`` timeline or *sid*'s modern okres (:attr:`Gazetteer.modern_okres`), or names none."""

def alias_namesake_refusal(k: str, oid, g: Gazetteer, home=None):
    """K1 (0.14.0): where every settlement a ``viz`` alias of the bare key *k* reached in okres *oid* was set aside
    (:func:`alias_in_okres`) and no later tier matched, the namesakes of *k* in the okres (:func:`bare_namesakes`)
    answer as J1's do: the one the home picks (:func:`home_namesake`), tier ``p2_qualifier``, else the refusal
    ``ambiguous:p2_bare_namesakes`` listing them (up to 12, as P4's ``ambiguous:p4_in_okres``) — not ``unmatched``.
    ``None`` when the alias reached nothing or kept something, or *k* has no namesake there.

    0.15.0 (L3): the namesakes leave out those in a set-aside target's own 1910 municipality (:func:`_muni_of`), the
    target itself kept; which namesakes stand against a target at all is :func:`alias_rivals`'s count, through
    :func:`alias_in_okres`. L6:
    the refusal lists the set-aside target(s) beside the namesakes, so it names both readings — *Lhotka* | Čáslav
    lists ``sovoluska-lhota:1`` (the alias's *Lhota*) and ``zlebska-lhotka:1``, not a single candidate."""
    if oid is None or not k or strip_qualifier(k) != k:
        return None
    reached = {s for t in g.alias.get(k, set()) for s in g.lex.get((t, oid), set())}
    if not reached or any(alias_in_okres(k, s, oid, g) for s in reached):
        return None
    names = bare_namesakes(k, oid, g)
    if _on("L3"):
        munis = {_muni_of(s, g) for s in reached} - {None}
        names = {s for s in names if s in reached or _muni_of(s, g) not in munis}
    if not names:
        return None
    pick = home_namesake(home, k, names, oid, g)
    if pick is not None:
        return "ok", "p2_qualifier", pick
    listed = names | reached if _on("L6") else names
    return "ambiguous", "p2_bare_namesakes", tuple(sorted(listed)[:12])

def p2_split(text: str, oid: int, g: Gazetteer, uncertain: bool, vua: bool=False) -> tuple[str, str, object]

parent-part: the right piece if the left is its parent; else the left piece alone.

A VÚA reading off an uncertain candidate list whose piece is a big city or a land (Bratrouchov-Brno, Bělá-Čechy) is refused city_on_hamlet. No piece resolves to praha:1 (0.4.0, _piece_lookup).

0.9.0: E4 — in VÚA's Obec-Část form (vua: a VÚA cell or candidate; _obec_cast; csol.cz's Zaháj -Litomyšl and Rájec-Jestřebí name a place and its town, or a town) whose two pieces are distinct 1910 settlements of the okres, the left not the right's parent and the right no okres name, the right piece is taken: the part VÚA names was its own 1910 obec (Kralupy nad Vltavou-Míkovice → mikovice:1; Nelahozeves-Hleďsebe, which the register prints Hleďsebe … viz Kralupy, so that Hleďsebe answers only through Kralupy: refused ambiguous); where the register files the right piece under the left, the left is its parent and the right is taken as before. E11 — a comma piece after the first that is an okres name or a big city (Gazetteer.city_pieces) locates the place and is no piece of it (Stupno - Břasy, Plzeň is not plzen:1; Svatobořice, Kyjov is Svatobořice; a court name stays a piece: Litoměřice, Úštěk is Úštěk).

0.10.0: G1 — in a VÚA string (vua), of the right piece's namesakes in the okres the one under the left piece (right_under_left) is taken, also where D-144 picked another or none (Střechov-Dubovka → dubovka:2); in the E4 shape with 2+ namesakes, none under the left, a D-144 pick that is a part of another municipality is refused ambiguous. G3 — only a big city or the record's own okres is a locator (okres_locator).

0.11.0: H1 — where no namesake lies under the left piece in 1910, the modern municipality decides (right_under_left: Jesenice-Martinice → martinice:6; left_in_right_modern, the reversed order: Mezná-Hřensko → mezna:1), and D-144's obec pick no longer stands against it.
