def p2_split(text: str, oid: int, g: Gazetteer, uncertain: bool, vua: bool = False) -> tuple[str, str, object]:
    """``parent-part``: the right piece if the left is its parent; else the left piece alone.

    A VÚA reading off an uncertain candidate list whose piece is a big city or a land
    (``Bratrouchov-Brno``, ``Bělá-Čechy``) is refused ``city_on_hamlet``. No piece resolves to
    ``praha:1`` (0.4.0, :func:`_piece_lookup`).

    0.9.0: E4 — in VÚA's ``Obec-Část`` form (*vua*: a VÚA cell or candidate; :func:`_obec_cast`;
    csol.cz's *Zaháj -Litomyšl* and *Rájec-Jestřebí* name a place and its town, or a town) whose two pieces are **distinct** 1910 settlements of the
    okres, the left not the right's parent and the right no okres name, the right piece is taken: the part VÚA names was its own
    1910 obec (*Kralupy nad Vltavou-Míkovice* → ``mikovice:1``; *Nelahozeves-Hleďsebe*, which the register
    prints *Hleďsebe … viz Kralupy*, so that Hleďsebe answers only through Kralupy: refused ambiguous); where the
    register files the right piece
    under the left, the left is its parent and the right is taken as before. E11 — a comma piece after
    the first that is an okres name or a big city (:attr:`Gazetteer.city_pieces`) locates the place and is
    no piece of it (*Stupno - Břasy, Plzeň* is not ``plzen:1``; *Svatobořice, Kyjov* is Svatobořice; a
    court name stays a piece: *Litoměřice, Úštěk* is Úštěk).

    0.10.0: G1 — in a VÚA string (*vua*), of the right piece's namesakes in the okres the one under the left piece
    (:func:`right_under_left`) is taken, also where D-144 picked another or none (*Střechov-Dubovka* →
    ``dubovka:2``); in the E4 shape with 2+ namesakes, none under the left, a D-144 pick that is a part of another
    municipality is refused ambiguous. G3 — only a big city or the record's own okres is a locator
    (:func:`okres_locator`).

    0.11.0: H1 — where no namesake lies under the left piece in 1910, the modern municipality decides
    (:func:`right_under_left`: *Jesenice-Martinice* → ``martinice:6``; :func:`left_in_right_modern`, the reversed
    order: *Mezná-Hřensko* → ``mezna:1``), and D-144's obec pick no longer stands against it.
    """
    pieces = [p for p in re.split(r"\s*[-–/]\s*|\s*,\s*", text) if p.strip()]
    if len(pieces) < 2:
        return "none", "", None
    if uncertain and any(key(p) in g.city_pieces for p in pieces):
        return "refused", "p2_split", "city_on_hamlet"
    if _on("E11") and "," in text:
        first, *rest = [p for p in re.split(r"\s*,\s*", text) if p.strip()] or [text]
        if _on("G3"):        # 0.10.0: only the record's own okres (its town) or a big city locates the place
            rest = [p for p in rest if not okres_locator(p, oid, g)]
        else:
            rest = [p for p in rest if not (key(p) in _okres_name_keys(g) or key(p) in g.city_pieces)]
        pieces = [p for p in re.split(r"\s*[-–/]\s*|\s*,\s*", ", ".join([first, *rest])) if p.strip()]
        if len(pieces) == 1:                    # the place and its okres: the place alone
            v, _t, sid = _piece_lookup(key(pieces[0]), oid, g)
            return (v, "p2_split_left", sid) if v != "none" else ("none", "", None)
        if len(pieces) < 2:
            return "none", "", None
    keys = [key(p) for p in pieces]
    if len(pieces) == 2:
        left, right = keys
        v, _t, sid = _piece_lookup(right, oid, g)
        if v == "ok" and _parent_ok(left, sid, oid, g):
            return "ok", "p2_split_right", sid
        lv, _t, lsid = _piece_lookup(left, oid, g)
        if _on("G1") and vua and v in ("ok", "ambiguous"):
            # 0.10.0 (G1): VÚA's Obec-Část names the part *under* the obec — of the right piece's namesakes
            # in the okres, the one whose 1910 parent (or register owner) is the left piece
            under = right_under_left(left, right, oid, g, lsid if lv == "ok" else None)
            if len(under) == 1:
                return "ok", "p2_split_right", next(iter(under))
            if _on("H1") and v == "ok" and not under and _obec_cast_shape(text, right, g):
                # 0.11.0 (H1): the part first, its modern municipality second — no namesake of either piece lies
                # under the other in 1910, and the left piece names a settlement of the okres whose modern obec is
                # the right piece (Mezná-Hřensko: mezna:1)
                lefts = obec_cast_namesakes(left, oid, g) - {sid}
                rev = (set() if any(under_left(s, right, sid, g) for s in lefts)
                       else left_in_right_modern(left, right, oid, g, sid))
                if len(rev) == 1:
                    return "ok", "p2_split_left", next(iter(rev))
        if v == "ambiguous":
            return v, "p2_split_right", sid
        if _on("E4") and vua and v == "ok" and lv == "ok" and lsid != sid and _obec_cast(text, left, right, lsid, sid, g):
            namesakes = obec_cast_namesakes(right, oid, g) - {lsid}
            modern_other = {s for s in namesakes - {sid} if _modern_is(s, left, g)} if _on("H1") else set()
            if _on("G1") and len(namesakes) >= 2 and (g.status.get(sid) != "obec" or modern_other):
                # G1: the right piece has namesakes in the okres, none lies under the left, and D-144's pick is a
                # part of another municipality: which part VÚA meant is open (0.9.0 took the pick). A pick that was
                # its own 1910 obec stands — 0.11.0 (H1) only where no modern municipality names another namesake
                # under the left piece (Jesenice-Martinice: martinice:6 by H1, not D-144's martinice:1)
                return "ambiguous", "p2_split_right", tuple(sorted(namesakes))
            names = _name_forms(sid, g) | g.forms_1910.get(sid, set())
            if not any(difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, f, n).ratio() >= OBEC_CAST_NAME_RATIO
                       for f in form_set([right]) for n in names):
                # the part VÚA names answers only through another settlement (a 'viz' row, an alias): neither
                # piece is preferable (Nelahozeves-Hleďsebe, which the register prints 'viz Kralupy')
                return "ambiguous", "p2_split_right", tuple(sorted({lsid, sid}))
            return "ok", "p2_split_right", sid
        return (lv, "p2_split_left", lsid) if lv != "none" else ("none", "", None)
    found = [_piece_lookup(k, oid, g) for k in keys]
    oks = {val for v, _t, val in found if v == "ok"}
    return ("ok", "p2_split_pieces", next(iter(oks))) if len(oks) == 1 else ("none", "", None)

def okres_locator(piece: str, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """G3 (0.10.0): a comma piece after the first is the place's okres locator, not a piece of it, when it is a
    big city (:attr:`Gazetteer.city_pieces`) or names the record's **own** okres *oid* and does not resolve to a
    settlement of that okres other than its town (one in the okres's seat court): *Stupno - Břasy, Plzeň* is not
    ``plzen:1``; *Jablunkov, Piosek, Písek* | Český Těšín keeps *Písek* (``pisek:2``, Piosek of okres Těšín —
    0.9.0 dropped any piece naming any okres, here the Bohemian okres Písek)."""
    k = key(piece)
    if k in g.city_pieces:
        return True
    if oid is None or k not in g.okres_names.get(oid, set()):
        return False
    v, _t, sid = _piece_lookup(k, oid, g)
    return v == "none" or (v == "ok" and _court_of(sid, g) == g.seat_court.get(oid))

def obec_cast_namesakes(right: str, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> set:
    """G1 (0.10.0): every settlement of okres *oid* answering to the key *right* — a lexikon or register name
    (:attr:`Gazetteer.okres_keys`), also space-free — never ``praha:1``."""
    if oid is None or not right:
        return set()
    ids = set(g.okres_keys.get(oid, {}).get(right, ())) | set(g.nospace.get((nospace(right), oid), ()))
    return ids - {PRAHA_SID}

def under_left(sid: str, left: str, lsid, g: Gazetteer) -> bool

def under_left(sid: str, left: str, lsid, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """G1 (0.10.0): settlement *sid* lies under the left piece of ``left-right`` — its register owner is the
    left piece's settlement *lsid*, or its 1910 parent (:func:`_parent_forms`) is the left key or a name of *lsid*
    (*Frymburk-Damětice*: ``dametice:1``, parent *Frimburk* = the 1910 name of ``frymburk:2``), or it shares
    *lsid*'s 1910 parent (two osady of one obec: *Travná-Kameničky*, both of Rohozná)."""
    if lsid is not None and sid != lsid and (g.owner.get(sid) or {}).get("muni_sid") == lsid:
        return True
    pk = g.parent_key.get(sid) or ""
    if not pk:
        return False
    parents = _parent_forms(pk)
    lefts = {nospace(left)} | ((_name_forms(lsid, g) | g.forms_1910.get(lsid, set())) if lsid else set())
    if parents & lefts:
        return True
    return bool(lsid) and bool(g.parent_key.get(lsid)) and _parent_forms(g.parent_key.get(lsid)) == parents

0.11.0 (H1): where none lies under it in 1910, those whose modern municipality is the left piece (Gazetteer.modern_obec; modern = False skips this): Jesenice-Martinice → {martinice:6}, osada of Nedrahovice in 1910 and a part of Jesenice today, not D-144's martinice:1 (a part of Votice).

def right_under_left(left: str, right: str, oid, g: Gazetteer, lsid=None, modern: bool = True) -> set:
    """G1 (0.10.0): the namesakes of the right piece in the okres (:func:`obec_cast_namesakes`) that lie under
    the left piece (:func:`under_left`): *Střechov-Dubovka* → {``dubovka:2``} (osada of Střechov), not D-144's
    ``dubovka:1`` (a part of Neveklov).

    0.11.0 (H1): where none lies under it in 1910, those whose **modern** municipality is the left piece
    (:attr:`Gazetteer.modern_obec`; *modern* = False skips this): *Jesenice-Martinice* → {``martinice:6``}, osada
    of Nedrahovice in 1910 and a part of Jesenice today, not D-144's ``martinice:1`` (a part of Votice)."""
    names = obec_cast_namesakes(right, oid, g) - {lsid}
    under = {s for s in names if under_left(s, left, lsid, g)}
    if not under and modern and _on("H1"):
        under = {s for s in names if _modern_is(s, left, g)}
    return under

def left_in_right_modern(left: str, right: str, oid, g: Gazetteer, sid=None) -> set:

def p2_qualifier(k: str, oid: int, g: Gazetteer, home=None) -> tuple[str, str, object]

A u/nad/pod/na/v/ve/při qualifier on one side only: the record's stripped against the exact names, or the bare record against the stripped qualified names. Two different qualifiers (Oldřichov v Hájích vs Oldřichov na Hranicích) never meet — also when the register prints the candidate bare but its headword carries another qualifier (Kostomlaty pod Milešovkou is not Kostomlaty = Kostomlaty pod Řípem).

Since 0.3.0 such a meeting is a refusal, ("refused", "p2_qualifier", "qualifier_conflict"), not none: the okres holds the same head under another qualifier, so a later tier (P4's qualifier strip) must not hand the record to a namesake elsewhere — Lhota u Červeného Kostelce, okres Náchod, holds Lhota za Červeným Kostelcem and is not lhota:15 of okres Nové Město. _first_verdict still lets P4 take the name exactly as written.

0.5.0 (D4a): head_in_okres links when the okres holds exactly one settlement with the bare key and no qualified form of it — Klášter nad Jizerou | Mnichovo Hradiště is klaster-hradiste-nad-jizerou:1 (1910 Klášter), the record's qualifier being the modern one; tier p2_qualifier, so the link is flagged through settlement_piece_tier.

0.12.0 (I2): the stripped head links only where the name as written is no other 1910 settlement outside the okres (qualified_elsewhere) — else qualifier_conflict, unless the soldier's home municipality lies in the okres (home_muni_in_okres): Lipník nad Bečvou (čp. 286) | Moravský Krumlov is refused (the okres's lipnik:2 had 95 houses; lipnik-nad-becvou:1 is okres Hranice), Police nad Metují | Zábřeh with home Drozdov (okres Zábřeh) keeps police:1.

0.13.0 (J1): the bare record's pick stands only where it is the okres's one candidate among all the name's namesakes there (bare_namesake_verdict); else ambiguous:p2_bare_namesakes, unless the home picks.

0.14.0 (K2): first, a qualified record written abbreviated in the okres (qualifier_abbreviated). 0.14.0 (K1): where D-144 cannot decide among the qualified forms of the bare record, the home may pick one of the name's namesakes (home_namesake), as J1 lets it where D-144 could.

def p2_qualifier(k: str, oid: int, g: Gazetteer, home=None) -> tuple[str, str, object]:
    """A ``u/nad/pod/na/v/ve/při`` qualifier on **one** side only: the record's stripped against the
    exact names, or the bare record against the stripped *qualified* names. Two different
    qualifiers (``Oldřichov v Hájích`` vs ``Oldřichov na Hranicích``) never meet — also when the
    register prints the candidate bare but its headword carries another qualifier
    (``Kostomlaty pod Milešovkou`` is not ``Kostomlaty`` = *Kostomlaty pod Řípem*).

    Since 0.3.0 such a meeting is a refusal, ``("refused", "p2_qualifier", "qualifier_conflict")``,
    not ``none``: the okres holds the same head under another qualifier, so a later tier (P4's
    qualifier strip) must not hand the record to a namesake elsewhere — *Lhota u Červeného
    Kostelce*, okres Náchod, holds *Lhota za Červeným Kostelcem* and is not ``lhota:15`` of
    okres Nové Město. :func:`_first_verdict` still lets P4 take the name **exactly as written**.

    0.5.0 (D4a): ``head_in_okres`` links when the okres holds **exactly one** settlement with the
    bare key and no qualified form of it — *Klášter nad Jizerou* | Mnichovo Hradiště is
    ``klaster-hradiste-nad-jizerou:1`` (1910 *Klášter*), the record's qualifier being the modern
    one; tier ``p2_qualifier``, so the link is flagged through ``settlement_piece_tier``.

    0.12.0 (I2): the stripped head links only where the name **as written** is no other 1910 settlement outside the
    okres (:func:`qualified_elsewhere`) — else ``qualifier_conflict``, unless the soldier's *home* municipality lies in
    the okres (:func:`home_muni_in_okres`): *Lipník nad Bečvou (čp. 286)* | Moravský Krumlov is refused (the okres's
    ``lipnik:2`` had 95 houses; ``lipnik-nad-becvou:1`` is okres Hranice), *Police nad Metují* | Zábřeh with home
    Drozdov (okres Zábřeh) keeps ``police:1``.

    0.13.0 (J1): the bare record's pick stands only where it is the okres's one candidate among **all** the name's
    namesakes there (:func:`bare_namesake_verdict`); else ``ambiguous:p2_bare_namesakes``, unless the home picks.

    0.14.0 (K2): first, a qualified record written abbreviated in the okres (:func:`qualifier_abbreviated`). 0.14.0
    (K1): where D-144 cannot decide among the qualified forms of the bare record, the home may pick one of the name's
    namesakes (:func:`home_namesake`), as J1 lets it where D-144 could."""
    stripped = strip_qualifier(k)
    if stripped != k and _on("K2"):      # 0.14.0 (K2): an abbreviated name of one settlement of the okres
        abbreviated = qualifier_abbreviated(k, oid, g)
        if abbreviated is not None:
            return "ok", "p2_qualifier", abbreviated
    if stripped != k:
        v, _t, val = _lookup(stripped, oid, g)
        if v == "ok":
            head = key(g.cs_name.get(val))
            if strip_qualifier(head) != head and head != k:
                # 0.4.0: a qualified form of the head in the okres, or only the bare head printed
                if g.qualifier.get((stripped, oid)):
                    return "refused", "p2_qualifier", "qualifier_conflict"
                if bare_ids(stripped, oid, g) != {val}:
                    return "refused", "p2_qualifier", "head_in_okres"
            if (_on("I2") and head != k and qualified_elsewhere(k, oid, g, val)
                    and not home_muni_in_okres(home, oid, g)):
                return "refused", "p2_qualifier", "qualifier_conflict"
    else:
        v, val = decide(g.qualifier.get((k, oid)), _reg_status(g))
        if v == "ok" and _on("J1"):
            return bare_namesake_verdict(k, oid, val, g, home)
        if v == "ambiguous" and _on("K1"):       # 0.14.0 (K1): the home may pick among the namesakes here too
            pick = home_namesake(home, k, bare_namesakes(k, oid, g) | set(val), oid, g)
            if pick is not None:
                return "ok", "p2_qualifier", pick
    return (v, "p2_qualifier", val) if v != "none" else ("none", "", None)

def bare_namesakes(k: str, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> set

J1 (0.13.0): every settlement of okres oid with a name (lexikon or register, either edition: Gazetteer.okres_keys) whose head — the name without its u/nad/pod qualifier — holds the bare key k as a whole word: for Lhota in okres Strakonice Lhota u Dubu and Lhota pod Kůstrým, and as well Horažďovická Lhota, Střelskohoštická Lhota and Kapsova Lhota; not Loukov u Bystřice pod Hostýnem for Bystřice (the word is in its qualifier). Never praha:1.

def bare_namesakes(k: str, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> set:
    """J1 (0.13.0): every settlement of okres *oid* with a name (lexikon or register, either edition:
    :attr:`Gazetteer.okres_keys`) whose **head** — the name without its ``u/nad/pod`` qualifier — holds the bare key
    *k* as a whole word: for *Lhota* in okres Strakonice *Lhota u Dubu* and *Lhota pod Kůstrým*, and as well
    *Horažďovická Lhota*, *Střelskohoštická Lhota* and *Kapsova Lhota*; not *Loukov u Bystřice pod Hostýnem* for
    *Bystřice* (the word is in its qualifier). Never ``praha:1``."""
    if oid is None or not k:
        return set()
    pat = re.compile(rf"(?<!\S){re.escape(k)}(?!\S)")
    out: set = set()
    for kk, sids in g.okres_keys.get(oid, {}).items():
        if pat.search(strip_qualifier(kk)):
            out |= set(sids)
    return out - {PRAHA_SID}

    """J1 (0.13.0): the bare record's qualifier-tier pick *val* (D-144 on the qualified forms of *k* in okres *oid*)
    against every namesake of *k* there (:func:`bare_namesakes`). The candidates are *val* and every obec among
    them; one candidate keeps ``("ok", "p2_qualifier", val)``. Several: the settlement the soldier's home picks
    among the namesakes (:func:`home_namesake`), tier ``p2_qualifier``; else ``("ambiguous", "p2_bare_namesakes",
    candidates)``. *Lhota* | Strakonice was ``dubska-lhota:1`` (*Lhota u Dubu*, the one qualified obec) although
    *Horažďovická Lhota* and *Střelskohoštická Lhota* are obce of the okres too: refused, or with home *Horažďovice*
    ``horazdovicka-lhota:1``."""
    names = bare_namesakes(k, oid, g)
    status = _reg_status(g)
    cands = {s for s in names if status(s) == "obec"} | {val}
    if len(cands) <= 1:
        return "ok", "p2_qualifier", val
    pick = home_namesake(home, k, names | {val}, oid, g)
    if pick is not None:
        return "ok", "p2_qualifier", pick
    return "ambiguous", "p2_bare_namesakes", tuple(sorted(cands))

    """K1 (0.14.0): J1 on the variant tiers. A **bare** written key *k* that ``p2_alternate``, ``p2_german`` or
    ``p2_alias`` sent to a settlement *val* none of whose names is *k* goes through :func:`bare_namesake_verdict`:

    home may pick one of them, the pick included (tier ``p2_qualifier``, flagged uncertain), or the record is refused
    ``ambiguous:p2_bare_namesakes``. *Lhota* | Náchod is not

    that names one of those namesakes itself (*Lhota (Lhota pod Hořičkami)*) is the record's own answer and stands;
    an alias is the authority's general pointer, so even one whose row agrees with the okres meets the namesakes
    (*Těšice* | Hranice: *TĚŠICE viz Tršice (Olomouc)*, while Dolní and Horní Těšice are obce of the okres) — unless
    every candidate obec is a 1910 piece of the alias settlement's own modern municipality (:func:`_one_modern_obec`:
    *Javorník* | Frývaldov, *JAVORNÍK viz Město Javorník (Šumperk)*, beside Ves Javorník: both today's Javorník).
    Anything else is returned unchanged.

    :attr:`Gazetteer.pool_forms` holds (*Lhota* is no name of Chocenická Lhota); a 1910 town of the written name stands
    over its namesake villages (:func:`town_over_village`: *Libavá* → ``mesto-libava:1``). L3: an alias target taken
    where its row names another okres while the okres holds namesakes :func:`alias_rivals` does not count (those in
    the target's own 1910 municipality) is J1's one candidate — tier ``p2_qualifier``, flagged uncertain (*Bezděkov* | Kladno →
    ``horni-bezdekov:2``, beside its part Dolní Bezděkov)."""
    if v != "ok" or not _on("K1") or not k or strip_qualifier(k) != k or val is None:
        return v, tier, val
    names = full_name_forms(val, g) if _on("L1") else _name_forms(val, g) | g.forms_1910.get(val, set())
    if form_set({k}) & names:
        return v, tier, val
    if tier in ("p2_alternate", "p2_german") and val in bare_namesakes(k, oid, g):
        return v, tier, val
    if _on("L1") and town_over_village(k, oid, val, g):
        return v, tier, val
    if tier == "p2_alias" and alias_okres_agrees(k, val, oid, g) and _one_modern_obec(k, oid, val, g):
        return v, tier, val
    status = _reg_status(g)
    if len({s for s in bare_namesakes(k, oid, g) if status(s) == "obec"} | {val}) <= 1:
        if (_on("L3") and tier == "p2_alias" and not alias_okres_agrees(k, val, oid, g)
                and bare_namesakes(k, oid, g) - {val}):
            return "ok", "p2_qualifier", val     # 0.15.0 (L3): J1's one candidate among namesakes it does not count
        return v, tier, val                  # the okres's one candidate: the pick stands at its own tier
    return bare_namesake_verdict(k, oid, val, g, home)

def town_over_village(k: str, oid, val, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """L1 (0.15.0): the pick *val* is a 1910 town whose name is the written bare key *k* with a town word
    (:func:`_town_heads`), and no other obec of *k*'s namesakes in okres *oid* is a town (:func:`is_town`): the town
    is the natural reading of the bare name (*Libavá* | Moravský Beroun → ``mesto-libava:1``, Město Libavá, over Stará
    Libavá). A statutory city of the name itself never gets here: its own name is the written one."""
    if nospace(k) not in _town_heads(val, g):
        return False
    status = _reg_status(g)
    return not any(is_town(s, g) for s in bare_namesakes(k, oid, g) - {val} if status(s) == "obec")

def locator_alternates(clean: str, alts, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> tuple[str, tuple]:
    """K1 (0.14.0): a bare name's parenthesised alternates that say **where** it lies rather than give another name
    of it. The first that is a qualifier — a preposition and its object (:data:`_LOCATOR_ALT_RE`; one, with no comma,
    dash or slash: *(nad Vltavou - u Borovan???)* and *(u Litomyšle?, u Jarošova?)* name two places) — becomes the
    name's qualifier where the bare name is no settlement of the okres (P1), or the located name is another one than
    the bare name's (exactly, or abbreviated: :func:`qualifier_abbreviated`): *Lhota (u Č.Kostelce)* is read *Lhota u
    Č.Kostelce*; *Kámen (u Habrů)* stays *Kámen*, whose P1 settlement it is. Else one that names the record's own
    okres or one of its courts (:attr:`Gazetteer.okres_by_name`) is dropped where the okres holds a namesake of the
    name (:func:`bare_namesakes`): *Jeseník (Nymburk)* | Poděbrady (court Nymburk) is a Jeseník of the okres, not
    the court town. A qualified name, or a record with no okres, is returned unchanged."""
    k = key(clean) if clean else ""
    if not alts or not k or oid is None or strip_qualifier(k) != k:
        return clean, tuple(alts)
    for a in alts:
        if _LOCATOR_ALT_RE.match(key(a)) and not re.search(r"[,;/–-]", a):
            joined, rest = f"{clean} {a}", tuple(x for x in alts if x is not a)
            v1, _t, s1 = _lookup(k, oid, g)
            if v1 == "none":                     # the bare name is no settlement of the okres: the locator's reading
                return joined, rest
            vj, _t, sj = _lookup(key(joined), oid, g)
            sj = sj if vj == "ok" else (qualifier_abbreviated(key(joined), oid, g) if _on("K2") else None)
            if sj is not None and sj != s1:      # the bare name is one settlement, the located name another
                return joined, rest
            return clean, tuple(alts)
    if not bare_namesakes(k, oid, g):
        return clean, tuple(alts)
    return clean, tuple(a for a in alts if oid not in (g.okres_by_name.get(key(a), set())
                                                       | g.okres_by_name.get(nospace(key(a)), set())))

def home_namesake(home, k: str, ids, oid, g: Gazetteer)

J1 (0.13.0): the one settlement of ids (namesakes of the written bare key k in okres oid) the soldier's home municipality (the first of home's values, its first comma piece and each hyphen piece of it) points to, else None. A home key equal to k is a copy of the birthplace, no evidence. First, those the home names (a name of the settlement or its 1910 name), parents (its 1910 parent), owns (its register municipality is the home's settlement in the okres) or shares a modern municipality with (its modern obec is the home, or the modern obec of the home's settlement): exactly one is the pick, several none. Where none, those whose modern municipality is the home settlement's or borders it (RÚIAN adjacency, Gazetteer.obec_neighbours): exactly one is the pick. Lhota | Strakonice, home Horažďovice → horazdovicka-lhota:1 (modern obec Horažďovice); home Sedlo → strelskohosticka-lhota:1 (Sedlo and it are both of modern Střelské Hoštice); home Úlehle-Švejcarova Lhota → svejcarova-lhota:1; home Lhota → nothing. A home whose first comma piece copies the written name is read at its second piece, the municipality the part lies in: Újezd | Kladno, home Újezd, Dubí → ujezd-pod-kladnem:1 (its 1910 parent Dubí). 0.14.0 (K4): the home is also read without its qualifier, and its hyphen pieces so: home Trojanovice pod Radhoštěm is Trojanovice (trojanovice:1), whose modern municipality borders Kunčice pod Ondřejníkem and not Baška.

def home_namesake(home, k: str, ids, oid, g: Gazetteer):
    """J1 (0.13.0): the one settlement of *ids* (namesakes of the written bare key *k* in okres *oid*) the soldier's
    home municipality (the first of *home*'s values, its first comma piece and each hyphen piece of it) points to,
    else ``None``. A home key equal to *k* is a copy of the birthplace, no evidence. First, those the home **names**
    (a name of the settlement or its 1910 name), **parents** (its 1910 parent), **owns** (its register municipality
    is the home's settlement in the okres) or **shares a modern municipality** with (its modern obec is the home, or
    the modern obec of the home's settlement): exactly one is the pick, several none. Where none, those whose modern
    municipality is the home settlement's or **borders** it (RÚIAN adjacency, :attr:`Gazetteer.obec_neighbours`):
    exactly one is the pick. *Lhota* | Strakonice, home *Horažďovice* → ``horazdovicka-lhota:1`` (modern obec
    Horažďovice); home *Sedlo* → ``strelskohosticka-lhota:1`` (Sedlo and it are both of modern Střelské Hoštice);
    home *Úlehle-Švejcarova Lhota* → ``svejcarova-lhota:1``; home *Lhota* → nothing. A home whose first comma piece
    copies the written name is read at its **second** piece, the municipality the part lies in: *Újezd* | Kladno,
    home *Újezd, Dubí* → ``ujezd-pod-kladnem:1`` (its 1910 parent Dubí). 0.14.0 (K4): the home is also read without
    its qualifier, and its hyphen pieces so: home *Trojanovice pod Radhoštěm* is *Trojanovice* (``trojanovice:1``),
    whose modern municipality borders Kunčice pod Ondřejníkem and not Baška."""
    hm = (tuple(home or ()) + (None,))[0]
    if oid is None or not isinstance(hm, str) or not ids:
        return None
    pieces = hm.split(",")
    hname = clean_birthplace(pieces[0])[0]
    if hname and key(hname) == k and len(pieces) > 1:      # 'Újezd, Dubí': the part, then its municipality
        hname = clean_birthplace(pieces[1])[0]
    if not hname:
        return None
    hkeys = {key(hname)} | {key(x) for x in re.split(r"\s*[-–]\s*", hname) if x.strip()}
    if _on("K4"):                    # 0.14.0 (K4): the home without its qualifier ('Trojanovice pod Radhoštěm')
        hkeys |= {strip_qualifier(h) for h in hkeys}
    hkeys = {h for h in hkeys if h and h != k}
    if not hkeys:
        return None
    hsids = set()
    for h in hkeys:
        v, _t, hs = _lookup_any(h, oid, g)
        if v == "ok":
            hsids.add(hs)
    hforms = {nospace(h) for h in hkeys}
    home_modern = {g.modern_obec.get(s) for s in hsids} - {None, ""}
    strong = set()
    for s in ids:
        own = (g.owner.get(s) or {}).get("muni_sid")
        if (s in hsids or hforms & (_name_forms(s, g) | g.forms_1910.get(s, set()))
                or hforms & _parent_forms(g.parent_key.get(s) or "") or (own is not None and own in hsids)
                or any(_modern_is(s, h, g) for h in hkeys) or g.modern_obec.get(s) in home_modern):
            strong.add(s)
    if strong:
        return next(iter(strong)) if len(strong) == 1 else None
    home_kod = {g.modern_obec_kod.get(s) for s in hsids} - {None}
    near = {s for s in ids if g.modern_obec_kod.get(s) is not None
            and any(g.modern_obec_kod[s] == h or g.modern_obec_kod[s] in g.obec_neighbours.get(h, ()) for h in home_kod)}
    return next(iter(near)) if len(near) == 1 else None

def qualified_elsewhere(k: str, oid, g: Gazetteer, val=None) -> bool:
    """I2 (0.12.0): the qualified key *k* exactly as written names a 1910 settlement outside okres *oid* — a lexikon
    name (:attr:`Gazetteer.global_name`; *val*, the stripped head's settlement, left out) or a register name. Then
    the qualifier is the record's evidence of **which** place, and stripping it to a namesake in *oid* is a guess.

    0.13.0 (J2): also the name **abbreviated** (:func:`abbreviated_names`: *ujezd u sv krize* is *Újezd u Svatého
    Kříže*, okres Rokycany)."""
    if oid is None or not k:
        return False
    for kk in [k] + (sorted(abbreviated_names(k, g)) if _on("J2") else []):
        if any(s != val and _okres_any(s, g) not in (None, oid) for s in g.global_name.get(kk, ())):
            return True
        if _register_okresy(kk, g) - {oid}:
            return True

    (the key has lost the abbreviation's dot; the rule ``records_geo.praha_rural_all_czech`` applies to *Král.

def qualifier_abbreviated(k: str, oid, g: Gazetteer):
    """K2 (0.14.0): the one settlement of okres *oid* with a qualified name (lexikon or register, either edition:
    :attr:`Gazetteer.okres_keys`) the qualified key *k* writes abbreviated — the same head and number of words,
    every word after the preposition equal to the name's or a shorter beginning of it — and either some word
    shorter or the prepositions different where *k* writes ``u`` (*near*, which locates by any of them):
    *ujezd u sv krize* | Rokycany → ``ujezd-u-svateho-krize:1``, *tyniste nad orl* | Rychnov →
    ``tyniste-nad-orlici:1``, *lhota u c kostelce* | Náchod → ``lhota-za-cervenym-kostelcem:1``. ``None`` when *k*
    has no qualifier, is itself a name of the okres, or no settlement or several answer.

    0.15.0 (L7): K3's guard — also ``None`` where *k* as written is a settlement anywhere
    (:attr:`Gazetteer.global_name`, :attr:`Gazetteer.global_any`) or its abbreviated reading
    (:func:`abbreviated_names`) names a settlement outside the okres: a name the record wrote exactly, or the
    shortening of another okres's place, is not read into this okres."""
    head = strip_qualifier(k)
    if oid is None or not k or head == k:
        return None
    names = g.okres_keys.get(oid, {})
    if names.get(k):
        return None
    if _on("L7") and (g.global_name.get(k) or g.global_any.get(k)
                      or any(_okres_any(s, g) not in (None, oid) for kk in abbreviated_names(k, g)
                             for s in g.global_any.get(kk, ()))):
        return None
    words = k.split()
    n_head = len(head.split())
    found: set = set()
    for kk, sids in names.items():
        name = kk.split()
        if len(name) != len(words) or name[:n_head] != words[:n_head] or strip_qualifier(kk) != head:
            continue
        same_prep = name[n_head] == words[n_head]
        if not same_prep and words[n_head] != "u":
            continue
        pairs = list(zip(words[n_head + 1:], name[n_head + 1:]))
        if not pairs or not all(a == b or (len(a) < len(b) and b.startswith(a)) for a, b in pairs):
            continue
        if same_prep and all(a == b for a, b in pairs):
            continue
        found |= set(sids)
    found.discard(PRAHA_SID)
    return next(iter(found)) if len(found) == 1 else None

def qualifier_fuzzy_bound(k: str, head: str) -> int:
    """K3 (0.14.0): how far a misspelt qualified key *k* (of head *head*) may be from its namesake —
    :data:`QUALIFIER_FUZZY_DISTANCE`, or a quarter (:data:`QUALIFIER_FUZZY_SHARE`) of the written qualifier's length
    (the preposition and its object, spaces included), rounded up, if that is more: *na morave* (9) → 3, *nad
    perstynem* (13) → 4, *pod lipcany* (11) → 3. With K3 off, :data:`QUALIFIER_FUZZY_DISTANCE` (0.13.0)."""
    if not _on("K3"):
        return QUALIFIER_FUZZY_DISTANCE
    qualifier = k[len(head):].strip()
    return max(QUALIFIER_FUZZY_DISTANCE, math.ceil(QUALIFIER_FUZZY_SHARE * len(qualifier)))

    :attr:`Gazetteer.okres_keys`) of the same head as the qualified key *k* and within
    :func:`qualifier_fuzzy_bound` of it (0.13.0: :data:`QUALIFIER_FUZZY_DISTANCE`) — a misspelt qualifier (*bystrice nad perstejnem* →
    ``bystrice-nad-pernstejnem:1``, *ronov na doubravou* → ``ronov-nad-doubravou:1``, *frydlant nad ostarvici* →

    head = strip_qualifier(k)
    if oid is None or not k or head == k or g.global_name.get(k) or _register_okresy(k, g):
        return None
    if _on("J2") and abbreviated_names(k, g):
        return None
    close: set = set()

    for kk, sids in g.okres_keys.get(oid, {}).items():

                and _levenshtein(k, kk) <= bound:
            close |= set(sids)
    close.discard(PRAHA_SID)
    return next(iter(close)) if len(close) == 1 else None

def word_stem(word: str) -> str:
    """L5 (0.15.0): *word* without one Czech case ending (:data:`_CASE_ENDINGS`), keeping at least three letters."""
    for e in _CASE_ENDINGS:
        if word.endswith(e) and len(word) - len(e) >= 3:
            return word[:-len(e)]
    return word

def stem_agrees(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
    """L5 (0.15.0): two object words (keys) name the same thing in different grammatical cases — equal, or their stems
    (:func:`word_stem`) equal, or sharing a beginning at least the shorter stem's length less three and at least
    :data:`STEM_MIN_PREFIX` letters: *cerveneho* / *cervenym*, *kostelce* / *kostelcem*, *macochou* / *macochy*,
    *nakla* / *naklo*; not *brodem* / *brnem*, *c* / *cervenym* (an abbreviation is K2's)."""
    if a == b:
        return True
    sa, sb = word_stem(a), word_stem(b)
    if sa == sb:
        return True
    common = next((i for i, (x, y) in enumerate(zip(sa, sb)) if x != y), min(len(sa), len(sb)))
    return common >= max(STEM_MIN_PREFIX, min(len(sa), len(sb)) - 3)

def object_settlement_keys(obj: str, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> set:
    """L4 (0.15.0): the name keys of okres *oid* (:attr:`Gazetteer.okres_keys`) whose head the locator object *obj*

def locator_object_verdict(clean: str, alts, oid, g: Gazetteer):
    """L4 (0.15.0): a bare name with a locator alternate (:data:`_LOCATOR_ALT_RE`, one, no comma, dash or slash) that
    :func:`locator_alternates` left unjoined because the joined name is no settlement (exactly or abbreviated) while
    the bare name is a P1 settlement of okres *oid*. The locator's object (*u Nákla* → *Nákla*) names the settlements
    of the okres it writes in another case (:func:`object_settlement_keys`), each read as :func:`home_namesake` reads
    a home over P1's ids and the name's namesakes (:func:`bare_ids`, :func:`bare_namesakes`). One pick other than
    P1's: ``("ok", "p2_qualifier", pick)`` (flagged uncertain) — *Lhota (u Nákla)* | Litovel →
    ``lhota-nad-moravou:1`` (modern municipality Náklo), not P1's ``lhota-u-konice:1``. No single pick, while P1's
    pick has a qualified name and none of them has the written object (:func:`stem_agrees`): ``("ambiguous",
    "p2_bare_namesakes", ids)``. Else ``None`` (P1 stands)."""
    k = key(clean) if clean else ""
    if not alts or not k or oid is None or strip_qualifier(k) != k:
        return None
    loc = next((a for a in alts if _LOCATOR_ALT_RE.match(key(a)) and not re.search(r"[,;/–-]", a)), None)
    if loc is None:
        return None
    v1, _t, s1 = _lookup(k, oid, g)
    if v1 != "ok":
        return None
    joined = key(f"{clean} {loc}")
    vj, _t, _sj = _lookup(joined, oid, g)
    if vj != "none" or (_on("K2") and qualifier_abbreviated(joined, oid, g) is not None):
        return None
    obj = " ".join(key(loc).split()[1:])
    ids = bare_ids(k, oid, g) | bare_namesakes(k, oid, g) | {s1}
    picks = {home_namesake((h,), k, ids, oid, g) for h in {obj} | object_settlement_keys(obj, oid, g)} - {None}
    if len(picks) == 1:
        pick = next(iter(picks))
        return None if pick == s1 else ("ok", "p2_qualifier", pick)
    own = _qualified_names_of(s1, g)
    if own and not any(len(_object_words(n, strip_qualifier(n))) == len(obj.split())
                       and all(stem_agrees(a, b) for a, b in zip(obj.split(), _object_words(n, strip_qualifier(n))))
                       for n in own):
        return "ambiguous", "p2_bare_namesakes", tuple(sorted(ids)[:12])
    return None

def p4_timeline(k: str, stated: str, oid, g: Gazetteer, exact_only: bool=False) -> tuple[str, str, object]

Exactly one settlement of the name, elsewhere, whose okres_all holds the stated okres.

The name is tried as written, then — only when no settlement anywhere carries the qualified name — without its u/nad/pod qualifier (Kamýk nad Vltavou exists, so it never becomes Kamýk) — and, since 0.3.0, never when the record's own okres holds a settlement of that bare head (qualifier_conflict: Lhota pod Lipčany, okres Hradec Králové, holds Lhota pod Libčany; the record is not lhota:6 of okres Dvůr Králové). exact_only skips the strip.

def p4_timeline(k: str, stated: str, oid, g: Gazetteer, exact_only: bool = False) -> tuple[str, str, object]:
    """Exactly one settlement of the name, elsewhere, whose ``okres_all`` holds the stated okres.

    Also for a record with no 1910 okres at all (``Kunratice u Prahy``, okres ``Praha venkov``, a
    1928 unit): the stated okres in the timeline is the gate that keeps a foreign homonym out. The
    name is tried as written, then — only when no settlement anywhere carries the qualified name —
    without its ``u/nad/pod`` qualifier (``Kamýk nad Vltavou`` exists, so it never becomes *Kamýk*)
    — and, since 0.3.0, never when the record's own okres holds a settlement of that bare head
    (``qualifier_conflict``: *Lhota pod Lipčany*, okres Hradec Králové, holds *Lhota pod Libčany*;
    the record is not ``lhota:6`` of okres Dvůr Králové). *exact_only* skips the strip.
    """
    stated = nospace(stated or "")              # timeline tokens are space-free (0.2.0)
    if not stated:
        return "none", "", None
    forms = [k] if (g.global_name.get(k) or exact_only) else list(dict.fromkeys([k, strip_qualifier(k)]))
    for kk in forms:
        if kk != k and _okres_holds_head(kk, oid, g):
            # 0.4.0: a qualified form of the head in the okres, or the bare head itself
            why = "qualifier_conflict" if g.qualifier.get((kk, oid)) else "head_in_okres"
            return "refused", "p4_okres_timeline", why
        ids = {s for s in g.global_name.get(kk, set())
               if stated in g.timeline.get(s, set()) and g.okres_of.get(s) not in (None, oid)}
        if len(ids) == 1:
            inside = names_inside(k, oid, g)
            if inside:                          # 0.4.0: the okres holds the name in a longer one
                return "ambiguous", "p4_in_okres", tuple(sorted(inside))
            return "ok", "p4_okres_timeline", next(iter(ids))
        if ids:
            return "ambiguous", "p4_okres_timeline", tuple(sorted(ids))
    return "none", "", None

P4 must not send such a bare name to a namesake elsewhere. At most limit ids are returned (the refusal's candidate list).

def names_inside(k: str, oid, g: Gazetteer, limit: int = 12) -> set:
    """Settlements of okres *oid* whose name holds *k* as a whole word inside a longer name (0.4.0):
    *Lhota* in okres Tábor (*Balkova Lhota*, *Dlouhá Lhota* …), *Ouběnice* in okres Benešov
    (*Ouběnice 1. díl*). P4 must not send such a bare name to a namesake elsewhere. At most
    *limit* ids are returned (the refusal's candidate list)."""
    if oid is None or not k:
        return set()
    pat = re.compile(rf"(?<!\S){re.escape(k)}(?!\S)")
    out: set = set()
    for kk, sids in g.okres_keys.get(oid, {}).items():
        if kk != k and pat.search(kk):
            out |= sids
    return set(sorted(out)[:limit])

def german_verdict(forms, clean: str, oid, g: Gazetteer, okres_named: bool=False, keep_okres_town: bool=False) -> tuple[str, object]

The VÚA German cell (0.4.0): every form looked up in the okres and the union of their settlements taken, so Nieder-Ebersdorf; Ober-Ebersdorf (Dolní and Horní Habartice) or Königreich I.; II.; III. come out ambiguous instead of the first form's settlement; then the numbered-sibling guard on the record's own name (Království is not kralovstvi-i:1).

On the union the obec-first rule of D-144 is not applied: it settles one name several settlements answer to, while the forms of VÚA's list name the places of its candidate list, so two settlements are ambiguous (Lochčitz-Hottowitz; Hottowies: Otovice and Hostovice). One settlement is taken only when every form gives it; when some forms give nothing and the rest one settlement, the cell decides nothing (("partial", ids)): the later P2 tiers and P4 run as before 0.4.0, and only if none of them matches is the record refused ambiguous:p2_german with those ids (Hradiště, okres Znojmo, Znaim-Pöltenberg; Erdberg: only Erdberg = Hrádek resolves, and Hrádek is VÚA's second candidate; Albeřice (Nieder-Albendorf; Ober-Albendorf): only Dolní Albeřice resolves). A form naming the record's own okres (Javorník, okres Frývaldov (Jauernig; Freiwaldau)) is dropped unless the record's name is the okres's (a cell of 2+ forms only; one form is read as before 0.4.0).

0.9.0 (E5): where the cell names the okres (okres_named), a single German form that is a name of that okres's town (okres_names: Starkenbach for okres Jilemnice) is VÚA's German name of the okres, not of the place, and is dropped too — unless the Czech head is a spelling of the town (difflib ratio >= GERMAN_OKRES_TOWN_RATIO): Rochlice, okres Jilemncie (Starkenbach) is not Jilemnice, Pessinkau ?, okres Domažlice (Taus) not Domažlice.

0.10.0 (G6): not when VÚA's own candidate reading of the cell is the okres town itself (keep_okres_town, okres_town_read: Aisič, okres Ústí nad Labem ? (Ústí nad Labem, okres Ústí nad Labem ?) (Aussig - ?) — Aussig is the German of that reading, the head a garbled Aussig).

def german_verdict(forms, clean: str, oid, g: Gazetteer, okres_named: bool = False,
                   keep_okres_town: bool = False) -> tuple[str, object]:
    """The VÚA German cell (0.4.0): every form looked up in the okres and the **union** of their
    settlements taken, so *Nieder-Ebersdorf; Ober-Ebersdorf* (Dolní and Horní Habartice) or
    *Königreich I.; II.; III.* come out ambiguous instead of the first form's settlement; then the
    numbered-sibling guard on the record's own name (*Království* is not ``kralovstvi-i:1``).

    On the union the obec-first rule of D-144 is **not** applied: it settles one name several
    settlements answer to, while the forms of VÚA's list name the places of its candidate list, so
    two settlements are ambiguous (*Lochčitz-Hottowitz; Hottowies*: Otovice and Hostovice). One
    settlement is taken only when **every** form gives it; when some forms give nothing and the rest
    one settlement, the cell decides nothing (``("partial", ids)``): the later P2 tiers and P4 run as
    before 0.4.0, and only if none of them matches is the record refused ``ambiguous:p2_german`` with
    those ids (*Hradiště*, okres Znojmo, *Znaim-Pöltenberg; Erdberg*: only *Erdberg* = Hrádek
    resolves, and Hrádek is VÚA's second candidate; *Albeřice* (*Nieder-Albendorf; Ober-Albendorf*):
    only Dolní Albeřice resolves). A form naming the record's own okres (*Javorník, okres Frývaldov
    (Jauernig; Freiwaldau)*) is dropped unless the record's name is the okres's (a cell of 2+ forms
    only; one form is read as before 0.4.0).

    0.9.0 (E5): where the cell names the okres (*okres_named*), a single German form that is a name of
    that okres's town (``okres_names``: *Starkenbach* for okres Jilemnice) is VÚA's German name of the
    okres, not of the place, and is dropped too — unless the Czech head is a spelling of the town
    (difflib ratio >= :data:`GERMAN_OKRES_TOWN_RATIO`): *Rochlice, okres Jilemncie (Starkenbach)* is not
    Jilemnice, *Pessinkau ?, okres Domažlice (Taus)* not Domažlice.

    0.10.0 (G6): not when VÚA's own candidate reading of the cell is the okres town itself
    (*keep_okres_town*, :func:`okres_town_read`: *Aisič, okres Ústí nad Labem ? (Ústí nad Labem, okres Ústí nad
    Labem ?) (Aussig - ?)* — *Aussig* is the German of that reading, the head a garbled *Aussig*)."""
    k = key(clean)
    if len(forms) >= 2 and oid is not None and k not in g.okres_names.get(oid, set()):
        forms = tuple(f for f in forms if key(f) not in g.okres_names.get(oid, set()))
    if (_on("E5") and okres_named and len(forms) == 1 and oid is not None and not keep_okres_town
            and key(forms[0]) in g.okres_names.get(oid, set())
            and not any(difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, k, n).ratio() >= GERMAN_OKRES_TOWN_RATIO
                        for n in g.okres_names.get(oid, set()))):
        forms = ()
    if not forms:
        return "none", None
    if len(forms) == 1:                          # one form: as before 0.4.0
        v, _t, val = _lookup(key(forms[0]), oid, g, alt=True)
    else:
        ids: set = set()
        silent = False
        for f in forms:
            fv, _t, fval = _lookup(key(f), oid, g, alt=True)
            if fv == "ok":
                ids.add(fval)
            elif fv == "ambiguous":
                ids |= set(fval)
            else:
                silent = True
        v, val = (("ambiguous", tuple(sorted(ids))) if len(ids) > 1
                  else ("ok", next(iter(ids))) if ids and not silent
                  else ("partial", tuple(sorted(ids))) if ids else ("none", None))
        if v == "partial":                  # decided by the caller after the later tiers
            return v, val
    if v == "none":
        return v, val
    return numbered_guard(k, oid, v, val, g)

def qmark_readings(text, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> tuple[str, ...] | None:
    """I1 (0.12.0): the pieces of a VÚA cell written around a ``?`` (a ``?`` with a space on either side, as
    :func:`clean_birthplace` splits) that remain once a piece naming the record's own okres *oid*, its seat or a big
    city (:func:`okres_locator`) is dropped — *Podbořany ? Mukoděly* | Podbořany → ``("Mukoděly",)``, *Benešov)
    ?Divišov* → ``("Divišov",)``, the cell having lost the ``(`` of VÚA's ``(? Reading, okres X ?)``. ``None`` when
    the cell has no such ``?``, no piece is a locator or every piece is one, or the record has no okres."""
    if oid is None or not isinstance(text, str) or "?" not in text:
        return None
    pieces = [p for p in re.split(r"\s+\?\s*|\?\s+", unicodedata.normalize("NFC", text))
              if clean_birthplace(p)[0]]
    if len(pieces) < 2:
        return None
    locator = [okres_locator(clean_birthplace(p)[0], oid, g) for p in pieces]
    if not any(locator) or all(locator):
        return None
    return tuple(p for p, loc in zip(pieces, locator) if not loc)

def match_birthplace(text, okres_id, stated_okres=None, german=None, uncertain=False,
                     g: Gazetteer | None = None, german_forms=None, vua: bool = False,
                     keep_okres_town: bool = False, home=None, stated: bool | None = None) -> dict:
    """One birthplace → ``{clean, sid, tier, refusal, candidates, okres_1910, quarter}``.
    *german_forms* (0.4.0): every form of the VÚA German cell (:func:`_german_tuple`); *keep_okres_town*
    (0.10.0, G6): :func:`german_verdict` keeps a German form naming the okres town. *home* (0.12.0, I2): the
    soldier's home values (:func:`home_muni_in_okres`). 0.12.0 (I1): a VÚA cell (*vua*) whose ``?`` pieces include an
    okres locator is matched on the other pieces (:func:`qmark_readings`, :func:`_qmark_match`). 0.13.0 (J4): only
    where *okres_id* is the okres the record **stated** — *stated* ``True`` (:func:`link_one`'s stated-okres path);
    ``False`` from the D-a, timeline and candidate paths, which match in an okres the string, the name or a
    candidate supplied; ``None`` (a direct call) reads *okres_id* as stated, as 0.12.0 did."""
    oid = int(okres_id) if okres_id is not None and pd.notna(okres_id) else None
    if vua and _on("I1") and not (stated is False and _on("J4")):
        readings = qmark_readings(text, oid, g)
        if readings is not None:
            return _qmark_match(readings, okres_id, stated_okres, german, uncertain, g, german_forms, vua,
                                keep_okres_town, home)
    clean, alts = clean_birthplace(text)
    if _on("K1") and clean is not None:             # 0.14.0 (K1): an alternate saying where the place lies
        clean, alts = locator_alternates(clean, alts, oid, g)
    gforms = _german_tuple(german, german_forms)
    out = {"clean": clean, "sid": None, "tier": None, "refusal": None, "candidates": None,
           "okres_1910": oid, "quarter": None, "alternates": bool(alts), "tie": None,
           "name_keys": None if clean is None else name_keys(clean, alts, gforms, g)}
    if clean is None:
        out["refusal"] = "no_municipality"
        return out
    if oid is not None and oid in g.statutory and oid != PRAHA_OKRES_ID:
        return {**out, "sid": g.statutory[oid], "tier": "statutory_city"}
    parallel = praha_parallel(text, stated_okres)
    located = (locator_object_verdict(clean, alts, oid, g) if parallel is None and _on("K1") and _on("L4")
               else None)          # 0.15.0 (L4): an unjoined locator read by its object
    if parallel is not None:
        x_clean, x_alts = clean_birthplace(parallel)
        out["name_keys"] = name_keys(x_clean, x_alts, gforms, g) if x_clean else out["name_keys"]
        res = _parallel_verdict(x_clean, oid, g)
    elif located is not None:
        res = (*located, None, ())
    else:
        res = _first_verdict(clean, alts, oid, stated_okres, gforms, uncertain, g, vua, keep_okres_town, home)
    v, tier, val, quarter, tie = res
    out.update(tier=tier or None, quarter=quarter, tie=tie or None)
    if v == "ok":
        out["sid"] = val
        out["okres_1910"] = _okres_1910(val, oid, tier, g)
    elif v == "ambiguous":
        out["refusal"], out["candidates"] = f"ambiguous:{tier}", val
    elif v == "refused":
        out["refusal"] = val
    else:
        out["refusal"] = "no_okres_1910" if oid is None else "unmatched"
    return out

def name_keys(clean: str, alts=(), german=None, g: Gazetteer | None = None) -> frozenset:
    """Every name the record could have been matched on, as :func:`form_set` forms: the string, its
    alternates, the VÚA German form, its split pieces, the name a Prague form carries, and the
    ``viz`` alias targets of each. P5 compares these with the owner row's printed forms. *german*
    is the German column's value or (0.4.0) a tuple of its forms."""
    ks = {key(clean), *(key(a) for a in alts)}
    gfs = german if isinstance(german, tuple) else ((german_form(german),) if german_form(german) else ())
    ks |= {key(f) for f in gfs if f}
    ks |= {key(p) for p in re.split(r"\s*[-–/]\s*|\s*,\s*", clean) if p.strip()}
    shape = prague_shape(clean)
    if shape is not None and shape[2]:
        ks.add(key(shape[2]))
    if g is not None:
        ks |= {t for k in list(ks) for t in g.alias.get(k, ())}
    return frozenset(form_set(ks))

def german_tie_break(k: str, oid, tier: str, val, german, clean, g: Gazetteer):
    """0.5.0 (D4d): the settlement the record's VÚA German form names, when P1's D-144 chose *val*
    among several settlements of the name *k* by status alone and the German form resolves in the
    okres to exactly one **other** of them; else ``None``. *Oldřichov (Ulgersdorf), okres Děčín*:
    ``oldrichov`` answers to the obec ``oldrichov:2`` (printed *Ullgersdorf*, court Děčín, 2,188)
    and the osada ``oldrichov:1`` (1910 *Ulgersdorf*, part 5 of *Franzenthal-Ulgersdorf*, 456);
    the German form is the osada's 1910 name, the register's spelling of it and its lexikon German
    name, and nothing else in the okres. D-144's obec preference settles a name with nothing else
    to go on; here the record says more. One VÚA record in 0.4.1."""
    table = {"p1_register": g.reg, "p1_lexikon": g.lex}.get(tier or "")
    forms = german if isinstance(german, tuple) else _german_tuple(german)
    if table is None or not forms:
        return None
    ids = set(table.get((k, oid)) or ())
    if len(ids) < 2 or val not in ids:
        return None
    gv, gval = german_verdict(forms, clean, oid, g)
    return gval if gv == "ok" and gval in ids and gval != val else None

def praha_parallel(text, stated) -> str | None:
    """*X* of ``Praha, X`` when the stated okres is ``Praha, Y`` / ``Praha; Y``: two parallel
    two-value lists (Praha in Praha, or X in Y), so X is only an alternate (0.3.0)."""
    if not isinstance(text, str) or not isinstance(stated, str):
        return None
    m, s = _PRAHA_LIST_RE.match(text), _PRAHA_LIST_RE.match(stated)
    if not (m and s) or prague_shape(text) is None:
        return None
    return m.group(1).strip()

def owner_check(sid: str, keys, g: Gazetteer) -> tuple[object, bool, bool]

(mismatch, disjoint, conflict) for a settlement's register owner row.

mismatch: none of the record's name keys (name_keys) is a form the owner row prints (None when no keys are given or the row prints nothing). disjoint: the settlement's own lexicon names and the owner row's printed forms share no form. conflict: disjoint, and a form the row prints is the lexicon name of another settlement of the row's okres — the anchor puts the settlement on a row that prints a different place (0.1.0's Kostomlaty: kostomlaty-nad-labem:1 on the row printing Kostomlátky, which is kostomlatky:2).

Disjoint alone is not evidence of a wrong anchor (the build reports the births it covers as owner_disjoint_unrefused); nearly all are genuine — the Czech edition printing only the German name (Tannwald, Gabel), a 1910 spelling (Horní Cerekew, Labská Týnice), OCR damage (Černoš n), two forms without a comma. P5 refuses on conflict only and flags the rest through mismatch.

Since 0.3.0 mismatch and disjoint read the printed forms of every register row holding the settlement (pooled_forms): the Czech row of Hněvětice is OCR-damaged (Rvasice, Rwasitz, pop. 19) while the German row and the Czech part row print Hněvětice.

def owner_check(sid: str, keys, g: Gazetteer) -> tuple[object, bool, bool]:
    """``(mismatch, disjoint, conflict)`` for a settlement's register owner row.

    *mismatch*: none of the record's name *keys* (:func:`name_keys`) is a form the owner row prints
    (``None`` when no keys are given or the row prints nothing). *disjoint*: the settlement's own
    lexicon names and the owner row's printed forms share no form. *conflict*: disjoint, **and** a
    form the row prints is the lexicon name of another settlement of the row's okres — the anchor
    puts the settlement on a row that prints a different place (0.1.0's Kostomlaty:
    ``kostomlaty-nad-labem:1`` on the row printing *Kostomlátky*, which is ``kostomlatky:2``).

    Disjoint alone is not evidence of a wrong anchor (the build reports the births it covers as
    ``owner_disjoint_unrefused``); nearly all are genuine — the Czech edition printing only the German name
    (*Tannwald*, *Gabel*), a 1910 spelling (*Horní Cerekew*, *Labská Týnice*), OCR damage
    (*Černoš n*), two forms without a comma. P5 refuses on *conflict* only and flags the rest
    through *mismatch*.

    Since 0.3.0 *mismatch* and *disjoint* read the printed forms of **every** register row holding
    the settlement (:func:`pooled_forms`): the Czech row of *Hněvětice* is OCR-damaged (*Rvasice,
    Rwasitz*, pop. 19) while the German row and the Czech part row print *Hněvětice*.
    """
    own = g.owner.get(sid) or {}
    printed = (own.get("printed_forms") or set()) | (g.pool_forms.get(sid) or set())
    if not printed:
        return None, False, False
    mismatch = None if keys is None else not (set(keys) & printed)
    own_forms = g.forms_of.get(sid) or set()
    disjoint = bool(own_forms) and not (own_forms & printed)
    conflict = disjoint and any(s != sid for k in conflict_keys(own)
                                for s in g.lex.get((k, own.get("okres_id")), ()))
    return mismatch, disjoint, conflict

def roll_up(sid: str | None, okres_1910, g: Gazetteer, keys=None) -> dict:
    """The municipality, court and link unit of a matched settlement; *keys* (:func:`name_keys`)
    feed the owner check (:func:`owner_check`)."""
    out = {"municipality_settlement_id": None, "municipality_source": None, "register_row_key": None,
           "register_key": None, "court_id_1910": None, "court_source": None, "link_unit": "none",
           "rollup_refusal": None, "owner_mismatch": None}
    if sid is None:
        return out
    if sid in g.statutory_sids or sid in g.quarter_sids:
        city = PRAHA_SID if sid in g.quarter_sids else sid
        court = g.court_polygon.get(city)
        return {**out, "municipality_settlement_id": city, "municipality_source": "statutory_okres",
                "register_key": owner_muni_key(city, g),
                "court_id_1910": court, "court_source": "polygon" if court else None,
                "link_unit": "statutory_okres"}
    if sid in g.two_owners:
        return {**out, "rollup_refusal": "two_owners"}
    own = g.owner.get(sid)
    if own:
        mismatch, disjoint, conflict = owner_check(sid, keys, g)
        out.update(register_row_key=f"{own['edition']}|{own['court_key']}|{own['muni_seq']}|{own['settlement_seq']}",
                   owner_mismatch=True if disjoint else mismatch)
        if conflict:
            return {**out, "rollup_refusal": "owner_name_conflict"}
        out.update(court_id_1910=own["court_id"], court_source="register")
        if own["level"] == "municipality":
            out.update(municipality_settlement_id=sid, municipality_source="self",
                       register_key=f"{own['edition']}|{own['court_key']}|{own['muni_seq']}")
        elif own["muni_sid"]:
            # 0.4.0: a part of a municipality row whose own anchor conflicts with its printed name
            # (Samotín, a part of the Neustift/Novosady Blatiny row anchored to lhota:36) is refused
            if owner_check(own["muni_sid"], None, g)[2]:
                return {**out, "rollup_refusal": "owner_name_conflict"}
            out.update(municipality_settlement_id=own["muni_sid"], municipality_source="register_part",
                       register_key=f"{own['edition']}|{own['court_key']}|{own['muni_seq']}")
    if out["municipality_settlement_id"] is None:
        muni, source = _lexikon_municipality(sid, okres_1910, g)
        out.update(municipality_settlement_id=muni, municipality_source=source,
                   register_key=owner_muni_key(muni, g) if muni else None)
    if out["court_id_1910"] is None and g.court_polygon.get(sid):
        out.update(court_id_1910=g.court_polygon[sid], court_source="polygon")
    if out["municipality_settlement_id"] is None:
        out["rollup_refusal"] = "no_municipality_1910"
    else:
        out["link_unit"] = "municipality"
    return out

def municipality_row_keys(places: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[str, set]:
    """``{sid: {"edition|court_key|muni_seq", …}}`` of every register **municipality** row holding
    the settlement in the gazetteer's register (overrides and applied rulings included), in either
    Bohemian edition: the Czech and German rows of one municipality carry different ``muni_seq``
    (*Dolní Kralovice* is cz 10 and de-bohemia 40), and ``register_municipalities`` keys Bohemia on
    the Czech row except where only the German edition prints a municipality."""
    m = places[(places["place_level"] == "municipality") & places["settlement_id"].notna()]

        out.setdefault(str(sid), set()).add(f"{ed}|{ck}|{int(ms)}")
    return out

def contradicted_keys(places: pd.DataFrame, forms_of: dict) -> dict[str, set]:
    """``{sid: {keys}}`` of municipality rows holding a settlement that the other rows holding it
    contradict on **both** name and population (0.3.0): the row's municipality (the row and every
    part row of it holding the settlement) prints none of the settlement's names, while another
    municipality row holding it prints one and gives another 1910 population.

    This keeps the 0.2.0 Kostomlaty refusal alive after the owner check started pooling the forms of
    both editions: ``kostomlaty-nad-labem:1`` is held by the Czech row *Kostomlátky* (pop. 566) and
    the German row *Großkostomlat, Kostomlaty* (816), so the Czech row is not its municipality — while
    *Doubravička* (Czech *Doubravice, Kleindoubra- witz* 270, German *… Doubravička …* 270) and
    *Hněvětice* (the Czech municipality prints the name on its part row) are not contradicted."""
    held = places[places["settlement_id"].notna()]
    forms_at: dict[tuple, set] = {}
    for sid, ed, ck, ms, cell in zip(held["settlement_id"], held["edition"], held["court_key"],
                                     held["muni_seq"], held["printed_name"]):
        forms_at.setdefault((str(sid), f"{ed}|{ck}|{int(ms)}"), set()).update(
            form_set(key(p) for f in pn.cell_forms(cell) for p in printed_split(f)))
    m = held[held["place_level"] == "municipality"]
    pop = {(str(s), f"{e}|{c}|{int(q)}"): (int(v) if pd.notna(v) else None)
           for s, e, c, q, v in zip(m["settlement_id"], m["edition"], m["court_key"], m["muni_seq"],
                                    m["pop_total"] if "pop_total" in m.columns else [None] * len(m))}
    by_sid: dict[str, list] = {}
    for (sid, k) in pop:
        by_sid.setdefault(sid, []).append(k)
    out: dict[str, set] = {}
    for sid, keys in by_sid.items():
        if len(keys) < 2:
            continue
        own = forms_of.get(sid) or set()
        named = {k for k in keys if forms_at.get((sid, k), set()) & own}
        for k in set(keys) - named:
            pk = pop[(sid, k)]
            if pk is not None and any(pop[(sid, n)] is not None and pop[(sid, n)] != pk for n in named):
                out.setdefault(sid, set()).add(k)
    return out

def drop_contradicted(places: pd.DataFrame, contradicted: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """*places* with the settlement emptied on every row (municipality and part) of a municipality
    :func:`contradicted_keys` found contradicted for that settlement; a copy, input untouched."""
    if not contradicted:
        return places
    bad = {(s, k) for s, ks in contradicted.items() for k in ks}
    hit = [(str(s), f"{e}|{c}|{int(m)}") in bad if pd.notna(s) else False
           for s, e, c, m in zip(places["settlement_id"], places["edition"], places["court_key"],
                                 places["muni_seq"])]
    out = places.copy()
    sid = out["settlement_id"].astype("string")
    out["settlement_id"] = sid.mask(pd.Series(hit, index=out.index))
    return out

def register_join(muni_sid, owner_key, g: Gazetteer) -> tuple[bool, object, object]:
    """``(in_register_municipalities, register_owner_differs, register_key)`` for one link (0.3.0).

    The link reaches the municipality's institutions only when ``register_municipalities`` holds
    *muni_sid* on a key at which the gazetteer's register (overrides and applied rulings) also
    holds it as a municipality (:func:`municipality_row_keys`), a row the other edition does not
    contradict on name and population (:func:`contradicted_keys`) — never on membership alone.
    *differs* is True where the table holds it on a key the gazetteer does not (the frozen anchoring
    an override or ruling moved, e.g. Kostomlaty on the *Kostomlátky* row), False where they agree,
    ``pd.NA`` where the table lacks the settlement (Aš until the register hook) or there is no
    municipality. *register_key* is the table's key where they agree, else the owner row's
    (*owner_key*)."""
    if not muni_sid:
        return False, pd.NA, owner_key
    table_key = g.register_muni_key.get(muni_sid)
    if table_key is None:
        return False, pd.NA, owner_key
    if table_key in g.muni_keys.get(muni_sid, set()):
        return True, False, table_key
    return False, True, owner_key

def vua_uncertain(df: pd.DataFrame, prefix: str = "birth") -> pd.Series:
    """A VÚA place read off 2+ readings that do not name one place: ``locations`` 1.2.2
    ``candidates_agree_place`` (same okres **and** same place; 0.3.0 — *Velká Úpa I./II./III.*
    agree on the okres only), counted on ``locations`` 1.2.3 ``n_readings`` (0.4.0: the written head
    counts, so *Dražov, okres Karlovy Vary ? (Dražov, okres Teplá ?)* is two readings that differ)
    and, without it, on ``n_candidates``; without ``candidates_agree_place`` the 1.2.x
    ``candidates_agree`` (okres only); without either, the v1.1 ``loc_uncertain`` flag; without any
    (the legionnaire frame), False."""
    n = pd.to_numeric(_col(df, f"{prefix}_n_readings"), errors="coerce")
    if n.isna().all():
        n = pd.to_numeric(_col(df, f"{prefix}_n_candidates"), errors="coerce")
    for col in (f"{prefix}_candidates_agree_place", f"{prefix}_candidates_agree"):
        agree = _col(df, col)
        if agree.notna().any():
            return (agree.eq(False) & n.ge(2)).fillna(False).astype(bool)
    return _col(df, f"{prefix}_loc_uncertain").fillna(False).astype(bool)

def correction_rule(sid, tier, stated, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> str | None:
    """The rule a corrected okres moved under (``okres_correction_rule``).

    ``p4_timeline`` for P4. For P3 (0.3.0):

    * ``p3_prague_1910_okres`` — the settlement joined Prague in 1922 (it or its parent: every
      joined part), is the 1910 city or a quarter, or has the stated okres **literally** in its
      ``okres_all`` timeline: within the standing decision;
    * ``p3_prague_later_okres`` — none of that, and only a post-1910 ``Praha-venkov`` /
      ``-západ`` / ``-sever`` / ``-východ`` / ``-jih`` token in the timeline lets it pass (0.2.0
      counted these as ``p3_prague_1910_okres``): **not** within the decision, refused
      ``prague_later_okres_only`` unless accepted as a block;
    * ``p3_prague_pool_only`` — nothing in the timeline: the move rests on the record writer's
      generic *Praha* for the agglomeration alone; refused ``prague_pool_only``.
    """
    tier = tier or ""
    if tier.startswith("p4"):
        return "p4_timeline"
    if not tier.startswith("p3"):
        return None
    timeline = g.timeline.get(sid, set())
    if (sid in g.greater_prague or sid == PRAHA_SID or sid in g.quarter_sids
            or move_allowed(sid, stated, oid, g)):
        return "p3_prague_1910_okres"
    if any(t.startswith("praha") and t != "praha" for t in timeline):
        return "p3_prague_later_okres"
    return "p3_prague_pool_only"

def okres_from_name(df: pd.DataFrame, prefix: str = "birth") -> pd.Series:

def german_forms_column(df: pd.DataFrame, prefix: str = "birth") -> pd.Series:
    """Every form of the VÚA German cell where it holds 2+ (``locations.german_forms`` on the raw
    cell, 0.4.0), else ``None``. Built as a list, not ``Series.map``: on a ``string``-dtype raw
    column (notebook 02 §4 attaches the cell that way) ``map`` turns each tuple into an array and
    ``None`` into ``<NA>``, which the matcher cannot hash."""
    from utils.parsing import locations as loc
    raw = _raw_cells(df, prefix)
    if raw is None:
        return pd.Series([None] * len(df), index=df.index, dtype=object)
    forms = {v: loc.german_forms(v) for v in raw.dropna().unique()}
    return pd.Series([forms[v] if isinstance(v, str) and v in forms and len(forms[v]) >= 2 else None
                      for v in raw], index=df.index, dtype=object)

def candidates_column(df: pd.DataFrame, prefix: str = "birth") -> pd.Series:
    """VÚA's candidate readings ``((municipality, okres, text), …)`` where the place was read off the
    first of 2+ candidates (``{prefix}_loc_reading = candidate``, 0.4.0; the reading's own text since
    0.6.0, :func:`locations.candidate_readings`), else ``None``."""
    from utils.parsing import locations as loc
    raw = _raw_cells(df, prefix)
    use = first_candidate_mask(df, prefix)
    if raw is None:
        return pd.Series([None] * len(df), index=df.index, dtype=object)
    cells = {v: loc.candidate_readings(v, with_text=True) for v in raw[use].dropna().unique()}
    out = [cells.get(v) if u else None for v, u in zip(raw, use)]
    if _on("E11"):       # 0.9.0: readings in separate parentheses (Stodůlky … Praha venkov / … Sušice)

        sep = {v: separate_paren_candidates(v) for v in raw[~use].dropna().unique() if v.count("(") >= 2}

               for c, v, mm in zip(out, raw, muni)]
    return pd.Series(out, index=df.index, dtype=object)

def top_level_groups(raw) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """G4 (0.10.0): the depth-1 parentheses of *raw*, each as ``(whole content, own text)`` — the own text
    with every nested parenthesis removed — scanned with a depth counter (an unclosed group runs to the end)."""
    if not isinstance(raw, str):
        return []
    out, depth, start = [], 0, None
    for i, ch in enumerate(raw):
        if ch == "(":
            depth += 1
            if depth == 1:
                start = i + 1
        elif ch == ")" and depth:
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0 and start is not None:
                out.append(raw[start:i])
                start = None
    if depth and start is not None:
        out.append(raw[start:])
    own = []
    for x in out:
        prev = None
        while prev != x:
            prev, x2 = x, re.sub(r"\([^()]*\)", " ", x)
            x = x2
        own.append(re.sub(r"[()]", " ", x))
    return list(zip(out, own))

0.10.0 (G4): only depth-1 parentheses (top_level_groups), the okres word and the ? in the group's own text, nested groups set aside — 0.9.0's innermost-group regex took (Hamry, okres Klatovy ?) from inside a second segment of the cell (as-is 124183) as a top-level reading.

def separate_paren_candidates(raw) -> tuple | None:
    """E11 (0.9.0): VÚA's candidate readings when the cell gives each in its **own** parenthesis — two or
    more top-level parentheses that each hold an okres word and a ``?`` (*Stodůlky ?, (Stodůlky, okres
    Praha venkov - ?), (Stodůlky, okres Sušice - ?)*), which :func:`locations.candidate_readings` reads as
    one reading; ``((municipality, okres, text), …)`` from each parenthesis's first reading, else ``None``.

    0.10.0 (G4): only **depth-1** parentheses (:func:`top_level_groups`), the okres word and the ``?`` in the
    group's own text, nested groups set aside — 0.9.0's innermost-group regex took *(Hamry, okres Klatovy ?)*
    from inside a second segment of the cell (as-is 124183) as a top-level reading."""
    from utils.parsing import locations as loc
    if not isinstance(raw, str):
        return None
    if _on("G4"):
        groups = [own for _whole, own in top_level_groups(raw)]
    else:
        groups = [m.group(1) for m in re.finditer(r"\(([^()]*)\)", raw)]
    groups = [x for x in groups if _OKRES_WORD_RE.search(x) and "?" in x]
    if len(groups) < 2:
        return None
    out = []
    for x in groups:
        rd = loc.candidate_readings(f"x ({x})", with_text=True) or ()
        if rd and isinstance(rd[0][0], str):
            out.append(rd[0])
    return tuple(out) if len(out) >= 2 else None

def okres_string_unresolved(df: pd.DataFrame, prefix: str = "birth") -> pd.Series:
    """D-a (0.8.0): True where the record writes an okres string records_geo left unresolved (no
    ``{prefix}_okres_id``) beside a municipality, and its land is the Czech lands or unknown (a
    ``{prefix}_land`` outside them — *Vídeň*, *Slovensko* — is never read as a Czech okres)."""
    s = _col(df, f"{prefix}_okres").astype("string").str.strip()
    m = _col(df, f"{prefix}_municipality").astype("string").str.strip()
    land = _col(df, f"{prefix}_land").astype("string")
    ok_land = land.isna() | land.eq("Czech lands")
    return (s.notna() & s.ne("") & m.notna() & m.ne("") & _col(df, f"{prefix}_okres_id").isna()
            & ok_land).fillna(False).astype(bool)

def okres_only_alternatives(raw, g: Gazetteer, sid=None) -> list[str]:
    """D-a (0.8.0): the okres alternatives of a cell that writes an okres word in its head and then, as its
    **first** parenthesis, one holding **only** okres names (*Domoradice, okr. Vysoké Mýto? (Český
    Krumlov?)*; *Javornice, okr. Lomnice nad Popelkou? (Rychnov nad Kněžnou?, Vodňany?)*): every piece, ``?``
    and ``+`` dropped, names a Czech-lands okres or court as written (no close spelling). A piece that is a
    name of the linked settlement *sid* itself — VÚA's German form after a verified okres, *Falknov, okres
    Česká Lípa+ (Falkenau)*, *Nejdek, okres Mikulov+ (Neudek)*, which happen to be okres or court names
    too — is no alternative; a parenthesis with an okres word inside is VÚA's candidate list (*Planá, Čechy ?
    (Planá, okres Planá ?; …)*), and a later parenthesis VÚA's German forms of the candidates."""
    if not has_paren_okres(raw):
        return []
    grp = re.search(r"\(([^()]*)\)", raw)
    if not grp or _OKRES_WORD_RE.search(grp.group(1)):
        return []
    own = (g.forms_of.get(sid, set()) | g.pool_forms.get(sid, set()) | g.forms_1910.get(sid, set())) if sid else set()
    pieces = [re.sub(r"\s+", " ", re.sub(r"[?+]", " ", x)).strip(" -–.") for x in re.split(r"[,;]", grp.group(1))]
    pieces = [x for x in pieces if x]
    if not pieces or not all(resolve_okres(x, None, None, g, fuzzy=False)[0] in ("czech", "later", "timeline")
                             for x in pieces):
        return []
    return list(dict.fromkeys(x for x in pieces if not (form_set([key(x)]) & own)))

def home_name_conflict(head, sid, home_m, home_o, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """D-h (0.8.0): the soldier's home municipality *home_m* is exactly the name of a Czech-lands
    settlement of his home okres *home_o* (``home_okres_id``; for VÚA records_geo infers it from the home
    name), another okres than the link's; the link itself does not answer to that name; and the written
    *head* is closer to it (difflib, space-free) than to any name of the link *sid*: VÚA 143950 *Krupka,
    Kutná Hora ?* → ``krupa:3`` (Krupá, Kutná Hora), home *Krupka*, okres Teplice — the town Krupka. No
    home okres, no conflict; :func:`home_name_pass` calls it only where VÚA read the place off another
    name than the one written. A home settlement in a land the head's own land word contradicts
    (:func:`lands_named`, :func:`land_conflict`) is no rival: *Držkov, Morava ?* → ``drzkova:1`` (Holešov)
    stands although a Bohemian Držkov (Semily) carries the home name (0.8.0 round, the reader's
    narrowing of D-h)."""
    name = clean_birthplace(re.split(r"[,;]", head)[0])[0] if isinstance(head, str) else None
    hname = clean_birthplace(str(home_m).split(",")[0])[0] if isinstance(home_m, str) else None
    hk, mk = (nospace(key(name)) if name else ""), (key(hname) if hname else "")
    if not hk or not mk or sid is None or home_o is None:
        return False
    namesakes = set(g.global_any.get(mk, ()))
    if sid in namesakes:
        return False
    link_okres = _okres_any(sid, g)
    lands = lands_named(head)
    homes = [s for s in _czech(namesakes, g) if _okres_any(s, g) == home_o != link_okres
             and not land_conflict(lands, _land_of(s, g))]
    if not homes:
        return False
    link_forms = _name_forms(sid, g) | g.forms_1910.get(sid, set())
    to_home = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, hk, nospace(mk)).ratio()
    to_link = max((difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, hk, f).ratio() for f in link_forms), default=0.0)
    return to_home > to_link

def home_name_pass(rows: list, raw_all: pd.Series, df: pd.DataFrame, g: Gazetteer, home_prefix: str='home', prefix: str='birth') -> list

D-h (0.8.0): every linked VÚA result (a record with the raw cell {prefix}_raw) whose written head (the raw cell's head_text, its first comma piece) is not the name VÚA read the place off ({prefix}_municipality: VÚA took a candidate or corrected the spelling — Krupka written, Krupá read) and is within HOME_HEAD_RATIO of the home municipality goes through home_name_conflict; a conflict refuses the link home_name_conflict (the row's result is copied, never the shared one). Where the head is the reading, the link was read off what was written and a home copied from it is no evidence against it (Vesec, okres Liberec+, home Vesec); csol.cz writes municipality and okres as fields, with no such reading.

0.9.0 (E12, a diagnostic; which rows are refused does not change): refusal_detail says whether the home okres was written (home_name:home_okres_written) or inferred by records_geo from the home name (home_name:home_okres_inferred — then a home cell that copies the head is no independent evidence: the coin flips the rulings queue lists as the block home_name_conflict).
