def home_name_pass(rows: list, raw_all: pd.Series, df: pd.DataFrame, g: Gazetteer,
                   home_prefix: str = "home", prefix: str = "birth") -> list:
    """D-h (0.8.0): every linked VÚA result (a record with the raw cell ``{prefix}_raw``) whose written
    head (the raw cell's :func:`head_text`, its first comma piece) is **not** the name VÚA read the place
    off (``{prefix}_municipality``: VÚA took a candidate or corrected the spelling — *Krupka* written,
    *Krupá* read) and is within :data:`HOME_HEAD_RATIO` of the home municipality goes through
    :func:`home_name_conflict`; a conflict refuses the link ``home_name_conflict`` (the row's result is
    copied, never the shared one). Where the head is the reading, the link was read off what was
    written and a home copied from it is no evidence against it (*Vesec, okres Liberec+*, home *Vesec*);
    csol.cz writes municipality and okres as fields, with no such reading.

    0.9.0 (E12, a diagnostic; which rows are refused does not change): ``refusal_detail`` says whether the
    home okres was written (``home_name:home_okres_written``) or inferred by records_geo from the home name
    (``home_name:home_okres_inferred`` — then a home cell that copies the head is no independent
    evidence: the coin flips the rulings queue lists as the block ``home_name_conflict``)."""
    if f"{prefix}_raw" not in df.columns:
        return list(rows)
    hm = _col(df, f"{home_prefix}_municipality").astype(object).tolist()
    ho = _col(df, f"{home_prefix}_okres_id").astype(object).tolist()
    hok = _col(df, f"{home_prefix}_okres").astype(object).tolist()
    hmatch = _col(df, f"{home_prefix}_okres_match").astype(object).tolist()
    reading = _col(df, f"{prefix}_municipality").astype(object).tolist()
    out, seen = list(rows), {}
    for i, (res, raw, m, o, rd) in enumerate(zip(rows, raw_all, hm, ho, reading)):
        if res["sid"] is None or not isinstance(m, str) or not isinstance(raw, str) or not isinstance(rd, str):
            continue
        head = head_text(raw)
        if not head:
            continue
        o = int(o) if o is not None and not pd.isna(o) else None
        k = (head, m, o, rd, res["sid"])
        if k not in seen:
            hname = clean_birthplace(re.split(r"[,;]", head)[0])[0]
            mname = clean_birthplace(m.split(",")[0])[0]
            rname = clean_birthplace(rd)[0]
            close = (bool(hname) and bool(mname) and bool(rname) and key(hname) != key(rname)
                     and difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, key(hname), key(mname)).ratio() >= HOME_HEAD_RATIO)
            seen[k] = close and home_name_conflict(head, res["sid"], m, o, g)
        if seen[k]:
            r = _refuse(res, "home_name_conflict", res.get("stated_id"))
            in_reg, differs, reg_key = register_join(None, None, g)
            detail = "home_name"
            if _on("E12"):
                detail += ":home_okres_written" if home_okres_written(hok[i], hmatch[i]) else ":home_okres_inferred"
            r.update(refusal_detail=detail, refusal_okres_ids=(), in_register=in_reg, owner_differs=differs,
                     register_key=reg_key)
            out[i] = r
    return out

def home_okres_written(okres, match) -> bool:

def add_birth_settlement_columns(df: pd.DataFrame, g: Gazetteer, prefix: str='birth', dataset: str | None=None, accept_prague_later_okres: bool | None=None, home_prefix: str='home', diagnostics: bool=False) -> pd.DataFrame

The {prefix}_* settlement columns on a copy of df (see the module docstring) — the one entry point notebook 02 calls, for either dataset.

Reads {prefix}_municipality, {prefix}_okres, {prefix}_okres_id and, where present, {prefix}_okres_match, {prefix}_german, {prefix}_raw, the VÚA candidate columns (n_candidates, n_readings, loc_reading, candidates_agree_place) and {prefix}_quarter_no. Each distinct input is matched once. dataset is accepted for backward compatibility and ignored: every flag reads the columns present. accept_prague_later_okres (default ACCEPT_PRAGUE_LATER_OKRES, True since 0.4.0) is the author's single switch for the p3_prague_later_okres block. Since 0.6.0 (T2) a record whose okres was inferred from the name also passes its raw text (raw_text_column) and its home place ({home_prefix}_municipality, {home_prefix}_okres_id) to okres_inferred_refusal; since 0.7.0 also {home_prefix}_land, _megye_id, _jaras_id and _okres (F3), and a record read off VÚA's first candidate passes its raw text too (the head, F1/F2). Since 0.8.0 the soldier's regiment region (regiment_region_column, A6) reaches those records and the ones whose okres string records_geo left unresolved (okres_string_unresolved, D-a), and a linked record is checked against its home municipality (home_name_pass, D-h). diagnostics (0.7.0, build only — notebook 02 leaves it off, so data/final carries no such column) adds {prefix}_refusal_detail (the kinds or sub-rule behind a refusal) and {prefix}_refusal_okres_ids (the okresy a written okres named, A3).

def add_birth_settlement_columns(df: pd.DataFrame, g: Gazetteer, prefix: str = "birth",
                                 dataset: str | None = None,
                                 accept_prague_later_okres: bool | None = None,
                                 home_prefix: str = "home", diagnostics: bool = False) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The ``{prefix}_*`` settlement columns on a copy of *df* (see the module docstring) — the one
    entry point notebook 02 calls, for either dataset.

    Reads ``{prefix}_municipality``, ``{prefix}_okres``, ``{prefix}_okres_id`` and, where present,
    ``{prefix}_okres_match``, ``{prefix}_german``, ``{prefix}_raw``, the VÚA candidate columns
    (``n_candidates``, ``n_readings``, ``loc_reading``, ``candidates_agree_place``) and
    ``{prefix}_quarter_no``. Each distinct input is matched once. *dataset* is accepted for
    backward compatibility and ignored: every flag reads the columns present.
    *accept_prague_later_okres* (default :data:`ACCEPT_PRAGUE_LATER_OKRES`, True since 0.4.0) is the
    author's single switch for the ``p3_prague_later_okres`` block. Since 0.6.0 (T2) a record whose
    okres was inferred from the name also passes its raw text (:func:`raw_text_column`) and its home
    place (``{home_prefix}_municipality``, ``{home_prefix}_okres_id``) to :func:`okres_inferred_refusal`;
    since 0.7.0 also ``{home_prefix}_land``, ``_megye_id``, ``_jaras_id`` and ``_okres`` (F3), and a
    record read off VÚA's first candidate passes its raw text too (the head, F1/F2). Since 0.8.0 the
    soldier's regiment region (:func:`regiment_region_column`, A6) reaches those records and the ones
    whose okres string records_geo left unresolved (:func:`okres_string_unresolved`, D-a), and a linked
    record is checked against its home municipality (:func:`home_name_pass`, D-h).
    *diagnostics* (0.7.0, :func:`build` only — notebook 02 leaves it off, so ``data/final`` carries
    no such column) adds ``{prefix}_refusal_detail`` (the kinds or sub-rule behind a refusal) and
    ``{prefix}_refusal_okres_ids`` (the okresy a written okres named, A3).
    """
    accept = ACCEPT_PRAGUE_LATER_OKRES if accept_prague_later_okres is None else accept_prague_later_okres
    out = df.copy()
    unc = vua_uncertain(out, prefix)
    inputs = pd.DataFrame({"m": _col(out, f"{prefix}_municipality"), "o": _col(out, f"{prefix}_okres_id"),
                           "s": _col(out, f"{prefix}_okres"), "g": _col(out, f"{prefix}_german"),
                           "u": unc}).astype(object).where(lambda x: x.notna(), None)
    inputs["i"] = okres_from_name(out, prefix).to_numpy()
    inputs["gf"] = german_forms_column(out, prefix).to_numpy()
    inputs["c"] = candidates_column(out, prefix).to_numpy()
    # 0.6.0 (T2): the raw text and the home place, only where the okres was inferred (keeps the
    # distinct inputs few); 0.7.0: the raw text also where the reading came off VÚA's candidates;
    # 0.8.0: the raw text, home and regiment also where the okres string is unresolved (D-a, F6), the
    # raw text where it gives okres alternatives in parentheses (D-a, F5)
    inf = inputs["i"].astype(bool)
    unresolved = okres_string_unresolved(out, prefix).to_numpy()
    raw_all = raw_text_column(out, prefix)
    alternatives = pd.Series([has_paren_okres(v) for v in raw_all], index=out.index, dtype=bool).to_numpy()
    regiment = regiment_region_column(out)                                  # 0.8.0 (A6)
    with_home = inf.to_numpy() | unresolved
    if _on("E2"):        # 0.9.0: a candidate reading whose regiment may refuse it reads the home cell (E2)
        with_home = with_home | (inputs["c"].notna().to_numpy()
                                 & regiment.isin(list(REGIMENT_EVIDENCE_REGIONS)).to_numpy())
    if _on("E6"):        # 0.9.0: an alternate under a doubted okres string reads the home okres (E6)
        doubted = inputs["s"].map(lambda v: isinstance(v, str) and "?" in v).astype(bool).to_numpy()
        with_home = with_home | doubted
    with_raw = with_home | inputs["c"].notna().to_numpy() | alternatives
    # 0.10.0 (G4): the candidates read off E11's separate parentheses (not VÚA's own first-candidate reading)
    separate = (inputs["c"].notna() & ~first_candidate_mask(out, prefix).to_numpy()).to_numpy() if _on("E11") \
        else np.zeros(len(out), dtype=bool)
    if (_on("G7") or _on("G6")) and f"{prefix}_raw" in out.columns:
        # 0.10.0 (G7): a VÚA cell listing 2+ candidates with a '?' reaches the stated-okres E3 test (and G6)
        with_raw = with_raw | np.array([isinstance(v, str) and "(" in v and v.count("?") >= 2 for v in raw_all])
    inputs["r"] = raw_all.where(with_raw, None).to_numpy()
    # the home columns: where the rules above read them, and (0.10.0) for an okres string naming several okresy
    # (G2: the home settles E6's coin flip) and for E11's separate-parenthesis candidates (G4)
    home_rows = with_home.copy()
    if _on("G2"):
        home_rows = home_rows | inputs["s"].map(lambda v: isinstance(v, str) and bool(re.search(r"[/?,;()]", v))
                                                ).astype(bool).to_numpy()
    if _on("G4"):
        home_rows = home_rows | separate
    if _on("G7") and f"{prefix}_raw" in out.columns:     # G7: VÚA's pick off the head reads the home (as G4)
        home_rows = home_rows | np.array([isinstance(v, str) and "(" in v and v.count("?") >= 2 for v in raw_all])
    for col, src in (("hm", f"{home_prefix}_municipality"), ("ho", f"{home_prefix}_okres_id"),
                     ("hl", f"{home_prefix}_land"), ("hmg", f"{home_prefix}_megye_id"),
                     ("hj", f"{home_prefix}_jaras_id"), ("hok", f"{home_prefix}_okres")):
        vals = [v if (f and v is not None and not (not isinstance(v, str) and pd.isna(v))) else None
                for v, f in zip(_col(out, src).astype(object), home_rows)]
        if col == "ho":
            vals = [int(v) if v is not None else None for v in vals]
        elif col != "hm":
            vals = [str(v) if v is not None else None for v in vals]
        inputs[col] = pd.Series(vals, index=inputs.index, dtype=object)
    with_regiment = with_home | inputs["c"].notna().to_numpy()
    inputs["rg"] = pd.Series([v if f else None for v, f in zip(regiment, with_regiment)], index=inputs.index,
                             dtype=object)
    # 1: an unresolved okres field (csol.cz), 2: the same in a VÚA cell (D-a's repeated-name reading)
    inputs["un"] = [(2 if f"{prefix}_raw" in out.columns else 1) if u else 0 for u in unresolved]
    # 0.9.0 (E2): the regiment's recruiting area, where the regiment reaches the rules
    area = regiment_area_column(out) if _on("E2") else pd.Series([None] * len(out), index=out.index, dtype=object)
    inputs["ra"] = pd.Series([v if f and r in REGIMENT_EVIDENCE_REGIONS else None
                              for v, f, r in zip(area, with_regiment, regiment)], index=inputs.index, dtype=object)
    inputs["vc"] = 1 if f"{prefix}_raw" in out.columns else 0                # 0.9.0 (E4): a VÚA cell
    inputs["sp"] = [1 if f and _on("G4") else 0 for f in separate]           # 0.10.0 (G4)
    # 0.12.0 (I2): a qualified name's home municipality, read only by p2_qualifier (its own column, so the other
    # home rules see exactly the rows they saw before)
    qualified = inputs["m"].map(lambda v: isinstance(v, str) and bool(_QUALIFIER_RE.search(key(v)))).astype(bool)
    qualified = qualified & _on("I2")
    if _on("J1"):        # 0.13.0 (J1): also a bare name some qualified settlement carries as its head (home_namesake)
        heads = _qualified_heads(g)
        qualified = qualified | inputs["m"].map(
            lambda v: isinstance(v, str) and bool(clean_birthplace(v)[0])
            and key(clean_birthplace(v)[0]) in heads).astype(bool)
    if _on("J4"):        # 0.13.0 (J4): a VÚA candidate list, matched with the home (candidate_verdicts)
        qualified = qualified | inputs["c"].notna()
    if _on("K1"):        # 0.14.0 (K1): a bare name an alias, an alternate or a German form may send elsewhere
        qualified = qualified | pd.Series([_variant_home_needed(m, ger, g) for m, ger in zip(inputs["m"], inputs["g"])],
                                          index=inputs.index, dtype=bool)
    inputs["hq"] = pd.Series([v if f and isinstance(v, str) else None
                              for v, f in zip(_col(out, f"{home_prefix}_municipality").astype(object), qualified)],
                             index=inputs.index, dtype=object)
    tuples = [tuple(t) for t in inputs.itertuples(index=False, name=None)]
    results = {tup: link_one(tup, g, accept) for tup in set(tuples)}
    rows = [results[t] for t in tuples]
    if _on("Dh"):                                                           # 0.8.0 (D-h)
        rows = home_name_pass(rows, raw_all, out, g, home_prefix, prefix)
    res = pd.DataFrame(rows, index=out.index)
    out.attrs["accept_prague_later_okres"] = bool(accept)
    out = _assemble(out, res, inputs, unc, g, prefix)
    # 0.8.0 (D-a): links through an okres string records_geo left unresolved, by reading
    linked_rule = res["okres_string_rule"].where(res["link_unit"].ne("none"))
    out.attrs["okres_string_rule"] = {str(k): int(v) for k, v in linked_rule.value_counts().items()}
    if diagnostics:
        out[f"{prefix}_refusal_detail"] = pd.array([d or pd.NA for d in res["refusal_detail"]], dtype="string")
        out[f"{prefix}_refusal_okres_ids"] = pd.array(["|".join(str(o) for o in sorted(x)) if x else pd.NA
                                                      for x in res["refusal_okres_ids"]], dtype="string")
        if _on("E10"):   # 0.9.0 (E10): where the okres the match ran in came from (okres_source)
            out[f"{prefix}_okres_source"] = pd.array([v or pd.NA for v in res["okres_source"]], dtype="string")
    return out

def okres_inferred_verdict(clean, sid, oid, g: Gazetteer, raw=None, home=None, tier=None, regiment=None, area=None) -> tuple[str | None, str | None, tuple]

(refusal, detail, written okres ids); (None, None, ()) when a name whose okres records_geo inferred from the name (no okres string) may link to sid, the settlement the match found in that okres oid; else the refusal.

0.4.0: the name is the inferred okres's own (its seat or okres name) → link. 0.5.0 (D2): D-144 across all okresy on every name the gazetteer knows (global_any: lexikon names and register forms) — one id, else the one obec or town (_obec_or_unknown: a register municipality row, a lexikon obec, or a namesake whose 1910 status the lexikon does not give) — and that one is sid → link (Brtnice, Netolice, Choltice, Loket: one obec among hamlets of the name); that one lies in another okres → okres_from_name_conflict; no one (Nové Město: one obec, four namesakes of unknown status among the 13; Nový Dvůr; Pečky: the register prints the Kolín obec Červené Pečky as Pečky too) or one in this okres that the match did not find → okres_from_name_ambiguous.

0.6.0 (T2), in this order: the record's raw text names a land, country or district outside the Czech lands → okres_from_name_foreign (foreign_token), or an okres the settlement does not lie in → okres_from_name_conflict (raw_okres_refusal); the okres's own name links as before; D-144 across okresy is d2_decide (a namesake of unknown 1910 status refuses but never wins; an unanchored register municipality printing the name is one more possible obec); a link the soldier's home (municipality, okres_id) contradicts → okres_from_name_home_conflict (home_conflict).

0.7.0: the raw cell's land word (F4, okres_from_name_land_conflict), okres alternatives in parentheses (F5), an unresolved okres string as no evidence (F6) and the unique name's own conflict (A3, okres_from_name_conflict_unique), all in raw_okres_verdict; after D-144 across okresy, a match through a post-1910 name only (F3, later_name_only, tier the match tier: okres_from_name_later_name) and a home outside the Czech lands (F3, home_foreign: okres_from_name_home_foreign), before the home namesake test. The detail names the sub-rule; the okres ids are those a conflicting written okres names (A3).

0.8.0: A4 narrows the foreign home (home_refuses); A6 refuses okres_from_name_regiment_conflict where the soldier's regiment (regiment_region) recruited in Hungary and a Slovak obec carries the name (Gazetteer.hu_obce); D-c reaches later_name_only through raw and home.

def okres_inferred_verdict(clean, sid, oid, g: Gazetteer, raw=None, home=None,
                           tier=None, regiment=None, area=None) -> tuple[str | None, str | None, tuple]:
    """``(refusal, detail, written okres ids)``; ``(None, None, ())`` when a name whose okres
    :mod:`records_geo` inferred from the name (no okres string)
    may link to *sid*, the settlement the match found in that okres *oid*; else the refusal.

    0.4.0: the name is the inferred okres's own (its seat or okres name) → link. 0.5.0 (D2): D-144
    across **all** okresy on every name the gazetteer knows (``global_any``: lexikon names and
    register forms) — one id, else the one obec or town (:func:`_obec_or_unknown`: a register
    municipality row, a lexikon obec, or a namesake whose 1910 status the lexikon does not give) —
    and that one is *sid* → link (*Brtnice*, *Netolice*, *Choltice*, *Loket*: one obec among hamlets
    of the name); that one lies in **another** okres → ``okres_from_name_conflict``; no one (*Nové
    Město*: one obec, four namesakes of unknown status among the 13; *Nový Dvůr*; *Pečky*: the
    register prints the Kolín obec Červené Pečky as *Pečky* too) or one in this okres that the match
    did not find → ``okres_from_name_ambiguous``.

    0.6.0 (T2), in this order: the record's *raw* text names a land, country or district outside the
    Czech lands → ``okres_from_name_foreign`` (:func:`foreign_token`), or an okres the settlement does
    not lie in → ``okres_from_name_conflict`` (:func:`raw_okres_refusal`); the okres's own name links
    as before; D-144 across okresy is :func:`d2_decide` (a namesake of unknown 1910 status refuses
    but never wins; an unanchored register municipality printing the name is one more possible
    obec); a link the soldier's *home* ``(municipality, okres_id)`` contradicts →
    ``okres_from_name_home_conflict`` (:func:`home_conflict`).

    0.7.0: the raw cell's land word (F4, ``okres_from_name_land_conflict``), okres alternatives in
    parentheses (F5), an unresolved okres string as no evidence (F6) and the unique name's own
    conflict (A3, ``okres_from_name_conflict_unique``), all in :func:`raw_okres_verdict`; after D-144
    across okresy, a match through a post-1910 name only (F3, :func:`later_name_only`, *tier* the
    match tier: ``okres_from_name_later_name``) and a home outside the Czech lands (F3,
    :func:`home_foreign`: ``okres_from_name_home_foreign``), before the home namesake test. The
    *detail* names the sub-rule; the okres ids are those a conflicting written okres names (A3).

    0.8.0: A4 narrows the foreign home (:func:`home_refuses`); A6 refuses
    ``okres_from_name_regiment_conflict`` where the soldier's *regiment* (:func:`regiment_region`)
    recruited in Hungary and a Slovak obec carries the name (:attr:`Gazetteer.hu_obce`); D-c reaches
    :func:`later_name_only` through *raw* and *home*."""
    k = key(clean) if clean else ""
    if not k:
        return "okres_from_name_ambiguous", "no_name", ()
    if raw:
        why, detail, ids = raw_okres_verdict(raw, clean, sid, g)
        if why:
            return why, detail, ids
    if not (oid is not None and k in g.okres_names.get(oid, set())):
        v, one = d2_decide(k, g)
        if v != "ok":
            return "okres_from_name_ambiguous", "d2_no_single_settlement", ()
        if one != sid:
            if _okres_any(one, g) != oid:
                return "okres_from_name_conflict", "d2_other_okres", ()
            return "okres_from_name_ambiguous", "d2_other_settlement", ()
    # F3's later-name rule and its home_unresolved reading apply only where the name answers to more
    # than one Czech-lands settlement and is not the okres's own — where D-144 had to choose, which is
    # what "may not win" means: VÚA and csol.cz write today's names (Český Krumlov, Bruntál, Jeseník),
    # and a unique name or the okres town (Brno, home Brixton) is the place
    own_name = oid is not None and k in g.okres_names.get(oid, set())
    contested = not own_name and len(_czech_1910(g.global_any.get(k, ()), g)) > 1
    if _on("F3") and contested and later_name_only(k, sid, tier, g, raw=raw, home=home):
        return "okres_from_name_later_name", "later_name", ()
    # 0.8.0 (A6): a Hungarian regiment and a Slovak obec of the name — refuse only, never a link; not on
    # the okres's own name town (Praha: a Slovak village Praha is no rival to the capital)
    if (_on("A6") and regiment == "hungary" and k in g.hu_obce and not own_name
            and not (_on("E2") and not in_area(g.hu_county.get(k, ()), area))):   # 0.9.0 (E2): its county
        return "okres_from_name_regiment_conflict", "regiment_hu_obec", ()
    if home is not None:
        if _on("F3"):
            why = home_foreign(home, g)
            if why == "home_unresolved" and not contested:
                why = None
            if why and _on("A4") and not home_refuses(why, home, raw, sid, g):
                why = None
            if why:
                return "okres_from_name_home_foreign", why, ()
        # A1 (the author, 2026-11-16): a home okres equal to the link's own okres is no conflict —
        # it corroborates the inferred okres (0.6.0's reading, kept; see home_conflict)
        if home_conflict(k, sid, home, g):
            return "okres_from_name_home_conflict", "home_namesake", ()
    return None, None, ()

def later_name_only(k: str, sid, tier, g: Gazetteer, raw=None, home=None) -> bool

F3 (0.7.0): the match reached sid only through a post-1910 lexikon name — tier p1_lexikon, the register holds the settlement (pool_forms) but prints no form of the name k nor one within LATER_NAME_PRINTED_RATIO of it, and the lexikon's 1910 name is not k either: legion 86003 Dvorek → dvorek:1, which the register prints only as Höflas (the Czech name is post-1945). Such a match may not win an inferred okres — applied by okres_inferred_verdict only where the name answers to more than one Czech-lands settlement and is not the okres's own (a unique modern name, Český Krumlov, is the place).

0.8.0 (D-c): not when a form the raw cell prints in parentheses is a printed 1910 form of the link (key, or within LATER_NAME_PRINTED_RATIO of a register or 1910 lexikon form: VÚA 91000 Prameny (Sangaberg), printed Sangerberg), nor when the soldier's home lies in the link's okres (home_in_okres: 171464 Ludvíkov, home Einsidl = Einsiedel of Bruntál).

def later_name_only(k: str, sid, tier, g: Gazetteer, raw=None, home=None) -> bool:
    """F3 (0.7.0): the match reached *sid* only through a post-1910 lexikon name — tier
    ``p1_lexikon``, the register holds the settlement (``pool_forms``) but prints no form of the
    name *k* nor one within :data:`LATER_NAME_PRINTED_RATIO` of it, and the lexikon's 1910 name is
    not *k* either: legion 86003 *Dvorek* → ``dvorek:1``, which the register prints only as
    *Höflas* (the Czech name is post-1945). Such a match may not win an inferred okres — applied by
    :func:`okres_inferred_verdict` only where the name answers to more than one Czech-lands
    settlement and is not the okres's own (a unique modern name, *Český Krumlov*, is the place).

    0.8.0 (D-c): not when a form the raw cell prints in parentheses is a printed 1910 form of the link
    (key, or within :data:`LATER_NAME_PRINTED_RATIO` of a register or 1910 lexikon form: VÚA 91000
    *Prameny (Sangaberg)*, printed *Sangerberg*), nor when the soldier's home lies in the link's okres
    (:func:`home_in_okres`: 171464 *Ludvíkov*, home *Einsidl* = Einsiedel of Bruntál)."""
    if tier != "p1_lexikon" or not k or sid is None:
        return False
    printed = g.pool_forms.get(sid) or set()
    if not printed:
        return False
    mine = form_set([k])
    if mine & (printed | g.forms_1910.get(sid, set())):
        return False
    if any(difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, a, b).ratio() >= LATER_NAME_PRINTED_RATIO
           for a in mine for b in printed):
        return False
    if _on("Dc"):
        forms_1910 = printed | g.forms_1910.get(sid, set())
        parens = [p for grp in re.findall(r"\(([^()]*)\)", raw) for p in re.split(r"[,;]", grp)] \
            if isinstance(raw, str) else []
        for p in parens:
            pc = clean_birthplace(p)[0]
            pf = form_set([key(pc)]) if pc else set()
            if pf & forms_1910 or any(difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, a, b).ratio() >= LATER_NAME_PRINTED_RATIO
                                      for a in pf for b in forms_1910):
                return False
        if home is not None and home_in_okres(home, _okres_any(sid, g), g):
            return False
    return True

def home_in_okres(home, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """D-c (0.8.0): the soldier's home lies in okres *oid*: its stated okres (``home_okres_id``) is
    *oid*, or — with none stated — its municipality answers (D-144 across the Czech-lands namesakes) to
    a settlement of *oid*, or is a close spelling (:data:`HOME_OKRES_NAME_RATIO`) of a settlement name
    of *oid* (*Einsidl* / *Einsiedel*)."""
    if oid is None:
        return False
    hm, ho = (tuple(home) + (None, None))[:2]
    if ho is not None:
        return int(ho) == int(oid)
    first = str(hm).split(",")[0] if isinstance(hm, str) else None
    hclean = clean_birthplace(first)[0] if first else None
    hk = key(hclean) if hclean else ""
    if not hk:
        return False
    v, s = decide(_czech(g.global_any.get(hk, ()), g), _reg_status(g))
    if v == "ok" and _okres_any(s, g) == oid:
        return True
    names = [nospace(n) for n in g.okres_keys.get(oid, {})]
    return bool(difflib.get_close_matches(nospace(hk), names, n=1, cutoff=HOME_OKRES_NAME_RATIO))

def home_foreign(home, g: Gazetteer) -> str | None:
    """F3 (0.7.0): why the soldier's home lies outside the Czech lands, else ``None``. *home* is
    ``(municipality, okres_id, land, megye_id, jaras_id, okres)``: ``home_land`` set and not *Czech
    lands* (``home_land``; legion 54336's is empty), a Hungarian county or járás (``home_hungary``:
    legion 26367, home Ipolské Šiahy, Hont), and — only where no Czech okres was resolved — a home
    municipality that only a Hungarian okres or obec name answers to (``home_name_foreign``), or one no
    Czech-lands settlement answers to whose okres string names no Czech-lands okres either
    (``home_unresolved``: legion 54336 *Bielik, Bielik*; *Chicago, Illinois* — a reading beyond the
    author's text, so :func:`okres_inferred_verdict` applies it only to a contested name)."""
    hm, ho, hl, hmg, hj, hok = (tuple(home) + (None,) * 6)[:6]
    if isinstance(hl, str) and hl.strip() and hl.strip() != "Czech lands":
        return "home_land"
    if (isinstance(hmg, str) and hmg.strip()) or (isinstance(hj, str) and hj.strip()):
        return "home_hungary"
    if ho is not None:
        return None
    first = str(hm).split(",")[0] if isinstance(hm, str) else None
    hclean = clean_birthplace(first)[0] if first else None
    hk = key(hclean) if hclean else ""
    if not hk or _czech_1910(g.global_any.get(hk, ()), g) or hk in g.later_town:
        return None
    if hk in g.foreign_okres:
        return "home_name_foreign"
    ok_first = str(hok).split(",")[0] if isinstance(hok, str) else ""
    if key(ok_first) and resolve_okres(ok_first, None, None, g)[0] in ("none", "foreign"):
        return "home_unresolved"
    return None

def home_elsewhere(home) -> bool:
    """A4 (0.8.0): the home cell (municipality and okres strings) places the home outside the refusing
    lands although ``home_land`` is empty — a word of :func:`_elsewhere_words` (*Chicago*, *Illinois*,
    *Ohio*, *Peking*) or a :mod:`records_geo` land marker of another land (*Vídeň*, *Rusko*, *USA*)."""
    from utils.parsing import records_geo as rg
    hm, _ho, _hl, _hmg, _hj, hok = (tuple(home) + (None,) * 6)[:6]
    text = " ".join(str(x) for x in (hm, hok) if isinstance(x, str))
    k = key(text)
    if not k:
        return False
    words = _elsewhere_words()
    padded = f" {k} "
    if any(f" {w} " in padded for w in words):
        return True
    return any(pat.search(k) and land not in HOME_REFUSING_LANDS for pat, land in rg._LAND_MARKER_RES)

def raw_names_link_okres(raw, sid, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """A4 (0.8.0): the raw cell writes the link's own okres — an okres word's name, a bare comma piece
    naming exactly an okres or court, or VÚA's capital-city okres (*Hlavní město Praha*, *Zemské hlavní
    město Brno*: the title dropped) — that fits the settlement (:func:`_okres_fits`: *Habry, okr.
    Čáslav*; *Praha, Hlavní město Praha+*)."""
    if not isinstance(raw, str):
        return False
    named = [(n, False) for n in okres_names_in(raw)] + [(n, True) for n in _bare_qualifiers(raw)]
    top = re.sub(r"\([^()]*\)", " ", raw)
    for piece in re.split(r"[,;]", top)[1:]:
        piece = re.sub(r"[?+]", " ", piece).strip(" -–.")
        if _CAPITAL_RE.match(piece):
            named.append((_CAPITAL_RE.sub("", piece).strip(), True))
    return any(okres_token(n) and _okres_fits(n, sid, g, exact_only=e) is None for n, e in named)

def home_refuses(why: str, home, raw, sid, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """A4 (the author, 2026-11-16): whether the F3 home reason *why* (:func:`home_foreign`) refuses. A
    home refuses only where a same-named foreign birthplace is plausible — ``home_land`` one of
    :data:`HOME_REFUSING_LANDS`, a Hungarian county or járás (``home_hungary``), a home only a Hungarian
    name answers to (``home_name_foreign``) — or (``home_unresolved``, kept for a contested name) a home
    no Czech-lands name answers to that is not recognisably elsewhere (:func:`home_elsewhere`: legion
    54336 *Bielik*, not *Chicago, Illinois*); never when the raw cell writes the link's own okres
    (:func:`raw_names_link_okres`)."""
    if raw_names_link_okres(raw, sid, g):
        return False
    if why == "home_land":
        hl = (tuple(home) + (None,) * 6)[2]
        return isinstance(hl, str) and hl.strip() in HOME_REFUSING_LANDS
    if why == "home_unresolved":
        return not home_elsewhere(home)
    return why in ("home_hungary", "home_name_foreign")

def unplaced_czech(sid, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """F1 (0.7.0): a lexikon row with no 1910 okres (neither the lexikon's nor a register row's)
    whose **earliest** ``okres_all`` okres is not one of :data:`_FOREIGN_FIRST_OKRES`: a 1910
    settlement of the Czech lands the lexikon knows only under a later name or without its 1910
    clause (*Nový Bohumín*, Fryštát; *Ruda nad Moravou*, Šumperk; *Louky nad Dřevnicí*, Uherské
    Hradiště; *Domoradice*, Krumlov). The lexikon covers today's Czech Republic, so the earliest okres
    outside it is what separates the Hlučín villages, Valticko and Vitorazsko. A row with no timeline
    at all is not counted."""
    if _okres_any(sid, g) is not None:
        return False
    first = g.first_okres.get(sid)
    if not first:
        return False
    k = key(first)
    return k not in _FOREIGN_FIRST_OKRES and _RURAL_WORD_RE.sub("", k).strip() not in _FOREIGN_FIRST_OKRES

def lands_named(text) -> set:
    """F2/F4 (0.7.0): the lands a text names outside parentheses, in the comma pieces after the
    name (:data:`LAND_PIECES`: ``Morava`` → 302, ``Čechy`` → 301, ``Rakouské Slezsko`` → 303,
    ``Horní Slezsko`` → ``"foreign"``); an okres name holding a land word (*Moravská Třebová*,
    *Nové Město na Moravě*) is no land."""
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        return set()
    top = re.sub(r"\([^()]*\)", " ", text)
    out: set = set()
    for piece in re.split(r"[,;]", top)[1:]:
        k = re.sub(r"^(?:okres|okr|o)\s+", "", key(re.sub(r"[?+]", " ", piece)))
        for phrase, land in LAND_PIECES:
            if k == phrase or k.startswith(phrase + " "):
                out.add(land)
                break
    return out

def land_conflict(lands, land) -> bool:
    """F2/F4 (0.7.0): the named *lands* contradict a settlement's *land*: Bohemia against Moravia or
    Silesia; Moravia and Silesia, which the records confuse, never contradict each other."""
    named = {x for x in lands if x != "foreign"}
    if not named or land not in (301, 302, 303):
        return False
    return not any(x == land or {x, land} <= {302, 303} for x in named)

def d2_decide(k: str, g: Gazetteer) -> tuple[str, object]:
    """D-144 across all okresy for an inferred okres (0.6.0, T2): ``("ok", sid)`` or
    ``("ambiguous", ids)``. One settlement of the name (``global_any``) and no unanchored register
    municipality printing it → that one. Else exactly one namesake may be an obec (a register
    municipality row, a lexikon obec, or — for refusing only — a namesake of unknown 1910 status),
    and it wins only when it **is** an obec (register municipality or lexikon obec: legion *Dolní
    Lhotka*, whose one possible obec has no 1910 status, is refused) and no unanchored municipality
    row printing the name lies elsewhere (*Chudeřice*, *Milíčov*: the register prints a second 1910
    municipality it did not anchor; a row in the winner's own okres, where the winner has no anchored
    municipality row, is taken to be the winner's)."""
    ids = set(g.global_any.get(k, ()))         # every namesake, as 0.5.0 (Prague's Nové Město included)
    ph = set(g.unanchored_munis.get(k, ()))
    if len(ids) == 1 and not ph:
        return "ok", next(iter(ids))
    maybe = [s for s in ids if s in g.reg_municipal or g.status.get(s, "") in ("obec", "")]
    if len(maybe) != 1:
        return "ambiguous", tuple(sorted(ids))
    one = maybe[0]
    known = one in g.reg_municipal or g.status.get(one) == "obec"
    others = {o for o in ph if not (o == _okres_any(one, g) and one not in g.reg_municipal)}
    if not known or others:
        return "ambiguous", tuple(sorted(ids))
    return "ok", one

def foreign_token(text, exclude=()) -> str | None:
    """The first word or piece of *text* naming a land, country or district outside the Czech lands
    (:data:`FOREIGN_WORDS`, :data:`FOREIGN_DISTRICTS`), else ``None`` (0.6.0, T1/T2). The text is cut
    at ``, ; ( ) /``; the first piece (the place name as written) and every piece whose key is one of
    *exclude* (the record's own name: the Pardubice village *Uhersko*) are skipped."""
    if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
        return None
    skip = {key(e) for e in exclude if isinstance(e, str)}
    pieces = [key(x) for x in re.split(r"[,;()/]+", text)]
    for k in pieces[1:]:
        if not k or k in skip:
            continue
        if k in FOREIGN_DISTRICTS:
            return k
        hit = next((w for w in k.split() if w in FOREIGN_WORDS), None)
        if hit:
            return hit
    return None

    district outside the Czech lands (*Jaroslav, Halič*; *Ludwigsthal, Regen, Bavorsko*; *Steinbach,
    Gmünd*) or an okres of the Hungarian frame (*Súlovice, orkes Topoľčany*); ``okres_from_name_conflict``
    when an okres word (``okres``, ``okr``, ``okes``, ``ores``, ``okrr`` …) names an okres that is not
    the settlement's 1910 okres nor in its timeline, or a bare comma piece resolves **exactly** to a
    Czech-lands okres or court that is not the settlement's (*X, Kolín*).

    0.7.0: F4 a land word against the settlement's land (:func:`lands_named`, :func:`land_conflict`:
    ``okres_from_name_land_conflict``; Upper / Prussian Silesia foreign); F6 an okres string that
    resolves to nothing is no evidence; A3 a conflict on a key that answers to exactly one Czech-lands
    settlement (and no unanchored register municipality elsewhere) is ``okres_from_name_conflict_unique``;
    F5 when the cell gives okres **alternatives** in parentheses (:func:`paren_okres_alternatives`),
    every okres it names is an alternative: one that does not fit the settlement and holds another
    namesake of the key (:func:`holds_namesake`) → ``okres_from_name_ambiguous``; else the link stands
    when one alternative fits it, and is a conflict when none does."""
    if foreign_token(raw, exclude=(clean,)):
        return "okres_from_name_foreign", "foreign_word", ()
    if _on("F4"):
        lands = lands_named(raw)
        if "foreign" in lands:
            return "okres_from_name_foreign", "land_foreign", ()
        if land_conflict(lands, _land_of(sid, g)):
            return "okres_from_name_land_conflict", "land_word", ()
    k = key(clean) if clean else ""
    alts = paren_okres_alternatives(raw, g) if _on("F5") else []
    named = [(n, False) for n in okres_names_in(raw)] + [(n, True) for n in _bare_qualifiers(raw)]
    fits, conflicts = [], []
    for name, exact in named:
        fit = _okres_fits(name, sid, g, exact_only=exact)
        if fit == "foreign":
            return "okres_from_name_foreign", "okres_foreign", ()
        if fit == "conflict":
            if not alts:
                return _written_conflict(k, sid, g, name, exact)
            conflicts.append((name, exact))
        elif fit is None and okres_token(name):
            fits.append(name)
    if not alts:
        return None, None, ()
    for name, exact in [*conflicts, *((a, False) for a in alts)]:
        if _okres_fits(name, sid, g, exact_only=exact) == "conflict" and holds_namesake(name, k, sid, g):
            return "okres_from_name_ambiguous", "okres_alternative", tuple(sorted(_written_ids(name, g, exact)))
    fits += [a for a in alts if _okres_fits(a, sid, g) is None]
    if conflicts and not fits:
        return _written_conflict(k, sid, g, *conflicts[0])
    return None, None, ()

def written_holds_near(k: str, sid, okresy, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """D-e (0.8.0): one of the written *okresy* holds a settlement whose name is within
    :data:`UNIQUE_NEAR_RATIO` (space-free) of the key *k* or of a name of the link *sid* (*Bernatice,
    okr. Frývaldov*: Bernartice; *Dobrová, okr. Fryštát*: Doubrava, the link's own name)."""
    mine = {nospace(k)} | {f for f in g.forms_of.get(sid, set()) | g.pool_forms.get(sid, set()) if f}
    sm = difflib.SequenceMatcher()
    for o in okresy or ():
        for name in g.okres_keys.get(o, {}):
            sm.set_seq2(nospace(name))
            for m in mine:
                sm.set_seq1(m)
                if sm.real_quick_ratio() >= UNIQUE_NEAR_RATIO and sm.ratio() >= UNIQUE_NEAR_RATIO:
                    return True
    return False

def paren_okres_alternatives(raw, g: Gazetteer) -> list[str]:
    """F5 (0.7.0): the okres names inside a top-level parenthesis that follows an okres word —
    VÚA's alternatives (*Domoradice, okr. Vysoké Mýto? (Český Krumlov?)* → ``Český Krumlov``;
    *Javornice, okr. Lomnice nad Popelkou? (Rychnov nad Kněžnou?, Vodňany?)*) — each piece with its
    okres word, ``?`` and ``+`` dropped, kept when it names a Czech-lands okres, court or later okres
    (a German exonym in parentheses, *Zetschin*, is no alternative)."""
    if not isinstance(raw, str):
        return []
    m = _OKRES_WORD_RE.search(raw)
    if not m:
        return []
    out = []
    for grp in re.finditer(r"\(([^()]*)\)", raw):
        if grp.start() < m.start():
            continue
        for piece in re.split(r"[,;]", grp.group(1)):
            p = re.sub(r"[?+]", " ", _OKRES_WORD_RE.sub(" ", piece)).strip(" -–.")
            p = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", p)
            if p and resolve_okres(p, None, None, g)[0] in ("czech", "later", "timeline"):
                out.append(p)
    return list(dict.fromkeys(out))

def holds_namesake(name, k: str, sid, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """F5 (0.7.0): okres string *name* holds a Czech-lands settlement of the key *k* other than *sid*
    — in its 1910 okres, or with the okres in its ``okres_all`` timeline (*Český Krumlov* holds
    ``domoradice:1``; *Strakonice* ``krty:2``)."""
    kind, ids = resolve_okres(name, None, None, g)
    if kind not in ("czech", "later", "timeline") or not k:
        return False
    tok = okres_token(name)
    for s in _czech_1910(set(g.global_any.get(k, ())) - {sid}, g):
        tl = g.timeline.get(s, set())
        if (kind in ("czech", "later") and _okres_any(s, g) in ids) or tok in tl or (kind == "timeline" and ids in tl):
            return True
    return False

def home_conflict(k: str, sid, home, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """T2 (0.6.0): the soldier's home place holds **another** settlement of the name *k*: a namesake
    other than *sid* lies in the home okres (``home_okres_id``, or the okres of the home municipality
    where D-144 across okresy settles it) or is a part of the home municipality (its 1910 parent) —
    legion 105562 *Bukovka* (home *Starý Bozděchov*, the parent of ``bukovka:1``), 130497 *Střížkov*
    (home okres Benešov holds ``strizkov:1``), 130334 *Hodkov* (home okres Sedlčany). A home okres
    that holds only the linked settlement is no conflict, nor is the linked settlement's own okres:
    there the home **corroborates** the inferred okres, and the choice inside it stays D-144's or the
    seat rule's (*Podbořany*, home Podbořany: ``podborany:1``, not ``podboranky:1`` of the same okres)."""
    hm, ho = (tuple(home) + (None, None))[:2]
    okresy = {int(ho)} if ho is not None else set()
    hclean = clean_birthplace(hm)[0] if isinstance(hm, str) else None
    hk = key(hclean) if hclean else ""
    if hk and hk != k:
        v, s = decide(_czech(g.global_any.get(hk, ()), g), _reg_status(g))
        if v == "ok" and _okres_any(s, g) is not None:
            okresy.add(_okres_any(s, g))
    okresy.discard(_okres_any(sid, g))
    part_of_home = bool(hk) and hk != k and g.parent_key.get(sid) == hk
    for s in set(g.global_any.get(k, ())) - {sid}:
        if _okres_any(s, g) in okresy or (hk and hk != k and not part_of_home and g.parent_key.get(s) == hk):
            return True
    return False

def candidate_okres(okres, text=None, g: Gazetteer | None = None) -> str | None:
    """The okres a candidate reading names (0.6.0, T1): the **last** ``okres X`` of its own *text*
    after the okres word's typos are normalised (``okrese``/``okrs``/``okes``/``ores``/``okrr`` …:
    *Rokytnice nad Jizerou-Horní Rokytnice, okrese Jilemnice*; *Bedřichovice, okres
    Čestín-Bedřichovice, okres Sedlčany*), else the parsed *okres*, else (with *g*) the first bare
    comma piece that is exactly a Czech-lands okres or court name (*Loket, Ledeč nad Sázavou*;
    *Nučice, Český Brod*); ``na Nisou`` → ``nad Nisou`` and a ``/…/`` tail dropped (*Planá
    /Karolinenhof/*)."""
    names = okres_names_in(re.sub(r"/[^/]*/", " ", text)) if isinstance(text, str) else []
    out = names[-1] if names else okres
    if not isinstance(out, str) and g is not None and isinstance(text, str):
        out = next((q for q in _bare_qualifiers(text)
                    if resolve_okres(q, None, None, g, fuzzy=False, timeline=False)[0] == "czech"), None)
    if not isinstance(out, str):
        return None
    out = re.sub(r"/[^/]*/", " ", out)
    out = re.sub(r"(?<![^\W\d_])na(\s+Nisou)(?![^\W\d_])", r"nad\1", out, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    out = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", out).strip(" -–.?+")
    return out or None

def timeline_okresy(tok, g: Gazetteer) -> set:
    """E9 (0.9.0): the 1910 okresy of the settlements whose ``okres_all`` timeline holds the token *tok*
    (*kralupynadvltavou*: Slaný, Smíchov, Mělník); memoised on the gazetteer."""
    cache = g.__dict__.setdefault("_timeline_okresy_cache", {})
    if tok not in cache:

def resolve_okres(okres, stated, oid, g: Gazetteer, fuzzy: bool=True, timeline: bool=True) -> tuple[str, object]

What an okres string names (0.6.0, T1): ("czech", ids) — the record's own okres string, or a backbone okres or court name (a city/rural twin gives both members) as written or without venkov/okolí; ("later", ids) — a post-1910 okres of LATER_OKRES_1910; ("timeline", token) — any other later okres the lexikon timeline carries; ("czech", ids) — the first hyphen piece (Teplice-Šanov); ("foreign", set()) — a Slovak, Hungarian, Subcarpathian or Hlučín name (Gazetteer.foreign_okres); ("czech", ids) — a close match (difflib >= OKRES_FUZZY_CUTOFF) to backbone names of one okres (Nové Město na Morava); else ("none", set()).

0.9.0: E7 — a Prussian-Silesian town (FOREIGN_DISTRICTS_PRUSSIA: Ratibor), a name of the Hungarian frame written as such (Holíč) and Uherská X where X close-spells a foreign name (Uherská Skalice = Skalica) are foreign before any later-okres timeline prefix or close Czech spelling (Holíč is not Holice, Uherská Skalice not Česká Skalice); E9 — a later okres of LATER_OKRES_1910 whose settlements the lexikon timeline puts in several 1910 okresy (Kralupy: Slaný, Smíchov, Mělník) and the capital's countryside (Praha-venkov, Praha-západ) are ("timeline", token), never one okres and never the city okres Praha. okres_resolution also says how the string resolved (E10).

def resolve_okres(okres, stated, oid, g: Gazetteer, fuzzy: bool = True,
                  timeline: bool = True) -> tuple[str, object]:
    """What an okres string names (0.6.0, T1): ``("czech", ids)`` — the record's own okres string, or
    a backbone okres or court name (a city/rural twin gives both members) as written or without
    ``venkov``/``okolí``; ``("later", ids)`` — a post-1910 okres of :data:`LATER_OKRES_1910`;
    ``("timeline", token)`` — any other later okres the lexikon timeline carries; ``("czech", ids)``
    — the first hyphen piece (*Teplice-Šanov*); ``("foreign", set())`` — a Slovak, Hungarian,
    Subcarpathian or Hlučín name (:attr:`Gazetteer.foreign_okres`); ``("czech", ids)`` — a close
    match (difflib >= :data:`OKRES_FUZZY_CUTOFF`) to backbone names of one okres (*Nové Město na
    Morava*); else ``("none", set())``.

    0.7.0 (F6): a form of :data:`OKRES_NAME_ALIASES` resolves (*Zábřeh na Moravě*, *Rokytnice*), a
    Lower Austrian district (:data:`FOREIGN_DISTRICTS_LOWER_AUSTRIA`) is foreign, and the close match
    is :func:`close_okres` (the best okres when it clearly beats the runner-up; no key of 4 letters or
    fewer).

    0.9.0: E7 — a Prussian-Silesian town (:data:`FOREIGN_DISTRICTS_PRUSSIA`: *Ratibor*), a name of the
    Hungarian frame written as such (*Holíč*) and *Uherská X* where *X* close-spells a foreign name
    (*Uherská Skalice* = Skalica) are foreign before any later-okres timeline prefix or close Czech spelling
    (*Holíč* is not Holice, *Uherská Skalice* not Česká Skalice); E9 — a later okres of
    :data:`LATER_OKRES_1910` whose settlements the lexikon timeline puts in several 1910 okresy (*Kralupy*:
    Slaný, Smíchov, Mělník) and the capital's countryside (*Praha-venkov*, *Praha-západ*) are
    ``("timeline", token)``, never one okres and never the city okres Praha. :func:`okres_resolution` also
    says how the string resolved (E10)."""
    return okres_resolution(okres, stated, oid, g, fuzzy=fuzzy, timeline=timeline)[:2]

def okres_resolution(okres, stated, oid, g: Gazetteer, fuzzy: bool = True,
                     timeline: bool = True) -> tuple[str, object, str | None]:
    """:func:`resolve_okres` with how the string resolved (0.9.0, E10): ``stated`` (the record's own
    okres), ``exact`` (a backbone okres or court name, ``venkov``/``okolí`` dropped), ``later``, ``alias``,
    ``hyphen`` (the first hyphen piece), ``fuzzy`` (:func:`close_okres` or 0.6.0's close match), or the
    kind itself for ``foreign`` / ``timeline`` / ``none``."""
    if not isinstance(okres, str) or not key(okres):
        return "none", set(), "none"
    if stated is not None and oid is not None and okres_token(okres) == okres_token(stated):
        return "czech", {oid}, "stated"
    k = key(okres)
    rural = _RURAL_WORD_RE.sub("", k).strip()
    if _on("E9") and _PRAHA_RURAL_RE.match(k):               # Praha-venkov is no city okres
        tok = _timeline_token(k, g) if timeline else None
        return ("timeline", tok, "timeline") if tok else ("none", set(), "none")
    for kk in dict.fromkeys([k, rural]):
        ids = g.okres_by_name.get(kk) or g.okres_by_name.get(nospace(kk))
        if ids:
            return "czech", set(ids), "exact"
        if g.later_okres.get(kk):
            tok = g.later_token.get(kk) if _on("E9") else None
            if tok and timeline:                             # E9: a later okres over several 1910 okresy
                return "timeline", tok, "timeline"
            return "later", set(g.later_okres[kk]), "later"
        if _on("F6") and g.okres_alias.get(kk):
            return "czech", set(g.okres_alias[kk]), "alias"
    if k in _FOREIGN_OKRES_KEYS or rural in _FOREIGN_OKRES_KEYS:   # Hlučín before its later timeline
        return "foreign", set(), "foreign"
    if _on("F6") and (k in FOREIGN_DISTRICTS_LOWER_AUSTRIA or rural in FOREIGN_DISTRICTS_LOWER_AUSTRIA):
        return "foreign", set(), "foreign"
    if _on("E7") and _foreign_by_name(k, rural, g, okres):
        return "foreign", set(), "foreign"
    if timeline:
        tok = _timeline_token(rural, g)
        if tok:
            return "timeline", tok, "timeline"
    first = key(re.split(r"\s*[-–]\s*", str(okres))[0])
    ids = g.okres_by_name.get(first) or g.okres_by_name.get(nospace(first))
    if ids:
        return "czech", set(ids), "hyphen"
    if k in g.foreign_okres or rural in g.foreign_okres:
        return "foreign", set(), "foreign"
    if fuzzy and rural and _on("F6"):
        kind, ids = close_okres(rural, g)
        return kind, ids, ("fuzzy" if kind == "czech" else kind)
    if fuzzy and rural:
        close = difflib.get_close_matches(rural, [n for n in g.okres_by_name if " " in n or len(n) > 3],
                                          n=5, cutoff=OKRES_FUZZY_CUTOFF)
        ids = {o for n in close for o in g.okres_by_name[n]}
        if close and len({frozenset(g.okres_by_name[n]) for n in close}) == 1:
            return "czech", ids, "fuzzy"
    return "none", set(), "none"

def uhersky_rest(k: str, g: Gazetteer, okres=None) -> str | None:
    """The *X* of an okres string *Uherská X* that may name Hungary (E7), else ``None``.

    0.9.0 tested the whole key, *Uh.* included, against the Moravian *Uhersk…* okres names. 0.10.0 (G5): only the
    **first** comma piece of the string (*okres*), only written out — *Uh.* abbreviates the Moravian forms
    (*Uh. Brod* is Uherský Brod) — and only when that piece's first two words are not within
    :data:`UHERSKY_REST_RATIO` of a Moravian *Uhersk…* okres name (*Uherský Brod, Bratislava*, *Uherský Brod Nové
    Mesto nad Váhom* are Uherský Brod; *Uherské Headiště* a typo of Uherské Hradiště)."""
    moravian = [n for n in g.okres_by_name if n.startswith("uhersk")]
    if not _on("G5"):
        m = _UHERSKY_RE.match(k)
        if m and not any(difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, k, n).ratio() >= UHERSKY_REST_RATIO for n in moravian):
            return m.group(1)
        return None
    first = key(re.split(r"[,;]", okres)[0]) if isinstance(okres, str) else k
    m = _UHERSKY_FULL_RE.match(first)
    if not m:
        return None
    lead = " ".join(first.split()[:2])
    if any(difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, x, n).ratio() >= UHERSKY_REST_RATIO for x in (lead, first) for n in moravian):
        return None
    return m.group(1)

def close_okres(k: str, g: Gazetteer) -> tuple[str, set]

F6 (0.7.0): ("czech", ids) of the okres whose backbone name is closest to k (difflib ratio >= OKRES_FUZZY_CUTOFF) when it beats the next okres's best by OKRES_FUZZY_MARGIN (Valšské Meziříčí: Valašské Meziříčí 0.97 against Velké Meziříčí 0.87), else ("none", set()). Neither k nor the name it reaches may be shorter than OKRES_FUZZY_MIN_LEN letters (Plzań must not become Plan, Planá; Brmo stays unresolved).

0.8.0 (D-b): the foreign district names are scored too (Gazetteer.foreign_okres and FOREIGN_DISTRICTS_LOWER_AUSTRIA, each also without its qualifier: Turňa nad Bodvou → turna); when the best foreign ratio is at least the best Czech one the string is ("foreign", set()) (Turňa is not Turnau, Senice not Jesenice, Sečany not Sedlčany).

def close_okres(k: str, g: Gazetteer) -> tuple[str, set]:
    """F6 (0.7.0): ``("czech", ids)`` of the okres whose backbone name is closest to *k* (difflib
    ratio >= :data:`OKRES_FUZZY_CUTOFF`) when it beats the next okres's best by
    :data:`OKRES_FUZZY_MARGIN` (*Valšské Meziříčí*: Valašské Meziříčí 0.97 against Velké Meziříčí
    0.87), else ``("none", set())``. Neither *k* nor the name it reaches may be shorter than
    :data:`OKRES_FUZZY_MIN_LEN` letters (*Plzań* must not become *Plan*, Planá; *Brmo* stays
    unresolved).

    0.8.0 (D-b): the foreign district names are scored too (:attr:`Gazetteer.foreign_okres` and
    :data:`FOREIGN_DISTRICTS_LOWER_AUSTRIA`, each also without its qualifier: *Turňa nad Bodvou* →
    *turna*); when the best foreign ratio is at least the best Czech one the string is ``("foreign",
    set())`` (*Turňa* is not Turnau, *Senice* not Jesenice, *Sečany* not Sedlčany)."""
    if len(nospace(k)) < OKRES_FUZZY_MIN_LEN:
        return "none", set()
    best: dict[frozenset, float] = {}
    sm = difflib.SequenceMatcher()
    sm.set_seq2(k)
    for n, ids in g.okres_by_name.items():
        if len(nospace(n)) < OKRES_FUZZY_MIN_LEN:
            continue
        sm.set_seq1(n)
        if (sm.real_quick_ratio() >= OKRES_FUZZY_CUTOFF and sm.quick_ratio() >= OKRES_FUZZY_CUTOFF
                and sm.ratio() >= OKRES_FUZZY_CUTOFF):
            fs = frozenset(ids)
            best[fs] = max(best.get(fs, 0.0), sm.ratio())
    if not best:
        return "none", set()
    ranked = sorted(best.values(), reverse=True)
    top = max(best, key=best.get)
    if _on("Db"):
        near = _closest_foreign(k, g)
        if near and near[0] >= ranked[0]:
            return "foreign", set()
    if len(ranked) == 1 or ranked[0] - ranked[1] >= OKRES_FUZZY_MARGIN:
        return "czech", set(top)
    return "none", set()

def twin_member(okresy: set, muni, g: Gazetteer) -> set:
    """The okres ids a candidate reading means when its okres string names a statutory city **and**
    its rural okres (*Opava* → 303011 city, 303010 rural): the city when the municipality is the
    city itself, else the rural member — records_geo's twin rule (D-17), 0.5.0. Without it the city
    okres answers any name with the city (:func:`match_birthplace`'s statutory short-cut), so
    *Tábor, okres Opava* gave {opava:1, tabor:1} and counted as giving nothing."""
    city = {o for o in okresy if o in g.statutory and o != PRAHA_OKRES_ID}
    if not city or len(okresy) < 2:
        return set(okresy)
    k = key(muni) if muni else ""
    own = {o for o in city if k in g.okres_names.get(o, set())}
    return own or set(okresy) - city

def global_names(muni, g: Gazetteer) -> set:
    """Every Czech-lands 1910 settlement the name answers to across all okresy (``global_any``): the
    name as written (a qualifier kept: *Lhota u Police nad Metují*), the right piece of a compound
    (*Vráto Brod-Hlinsko* → *Hlinsko*) and :data:`LATER_TOWN_1910` (*Český Těšín* → ``tesin:2``)
    (0.6.0, T1's global-name fallback). 0.7.0 (F1): a Czech-lands settlement with no 1910 okres
    counts too (:func:`unplaced_czech`: *Ruda nad Moravou*), except where :data:`LATER_TOWN_1910`
    names the 1910 settlement the later name stands for (*Nový Bohumín* → ``sunychl:1``)."""
    clean = clean_birthplace(muni)[0] if isinstance(muni, str) else None
    if not clean:
        return set()
    ks = {key(clean)}
    pieces = [p for p in re.split(r"\s*[-–]\s*", clean) if p.strip()]
    if len(pieces) > 1:
        ks.add(key(pieces[-1]))
    pick = _czech_1910 if _on("F1") else _czech
    later = _later_towns(g)
    out = set()
    for k in ks:
        ids = pick(g.global_any.get(k, ()), g)
        if k in later:          # the later name's own row stands for the 1910 settlement
            ids = {s for s in ids if _okres_any(s, g) is not None} | {later[k]}
        out |= ids
    return out

    """F1 (0.7.0): the Czech-lands settlements with no 1910 okres (:func:`unplaced_czech`) named *k*,

    (*okres_s* or a name of one of *okresy*): *Louky nad Dřevnicí, okres Uherské Hradiště* →
    ``louky:2`` (LOUKY, timeline Uherské Hradiště|…|Zlín)."""

def candidate_verdicts(cands, stated, oid, g: Gazetteer, main=None, main_sid=None, home=None) -> list[tuple[str, object]]

What each VÚA candidate reading gives on its own: ("ok", sid), ("ambiguous", ids) (several settlements, in one okres or across the okresy its string may name), ("global", ids) (0.6.0: it matched nothing in an okres, but its name answers elsewhere in the Czech lands to settlements other than main_sid), or ("none", why) with why one of SILENT_CANDIDATE.

0.5.0 (D1) counted every candidate that gave nothing as no evidence. 0.6.0 (T1): a candidate is (municipality, okres[, text]); no_municipality (no name, or a placeholder such as 1. díl); foreign (its text names a land outside the Czech lands, foreign_token); its okres is candidate_okres of the text, resolved by resolve_okres — okres_foreign for a Slovak / Hungarian / Subcarpathian / Hlučín okres, else matched through P1–P4 in the okresy it names (twin_member), a later okres also through its timeline token; a candidate that matches nothing there (unmatched), names no okres (no_okres) or an unresolvable one (okres_unresolved) takes the global-name fallback (global_names, and in a resolved okres close_names). The candidate that is the record's own reading (main = (municipality, okres) of the record) is never checked against the link by name alone.

0.7.0 (F1): the fallback also counts Czech-lands settlements with no 1910 okres (global_names, unplaced_in_okres), and a candidate whose name only an unanchored register municipality prints gives ("unanchored", okres ids) (unanchored_named).

0.13.0 (J4): a candidate is matched as not stated (no I1 reading of its okres) and with the soldier's home values, so I2's and J1's home exceptions read the same home as the record's own match.

def candidate_verdicts(cands, stated, oid, g: Gazetteer, main=None, main_sid=None,
                       home=None) -> list[tuple[str, object]]:
    """What each VÚA candidate reading gives on its own: ``("ok", sid)``, ``("ambiguous", ids)``
    (several settlements, in one okres or across the okresy its string may name), ``("global", ids)``
    (0.6.0: it matched nothing in an okres, but its name answers elsewhere in the Czech lands to
    settlements other than *main_sid*), or ``("none", why)`` with *why* one of
    :data:`SILENT_CANDIDATE`.

    0.5.0 (D1) counted every candidate that gave nothing as no evidence. 0.6.0 (T1): a candidate is
    ``(municipality, okres[, text])``; ``no_municipality`` (no name, or a placeholder such as *1.
    díl*); ``foreign`` (its text names a land outside the Czech lands, :func:`foreign_token`); its
    okres is :func:`candidate_okres` of the text, resolved by :func:`resolve_okres` —
    ``okres_foreign`` for a Slovak / Hungarian / Subcarpathian / Hlučín okres, else matched through
    P1–P4 in the okresy it names (:func:`twin_member`), a later okres also through its timeline
    token; a candidate that matches nothing there (``unmatched``), names no okres (``no_okres``) or an
    unresolvable one (``okres_unresolved``) takes the global-name fallback (:func:`global_names`, and
    in a resolved okres :func:`close_names`). The
    candidate that is the record's own reading (*main* = ``(municipality, okres)`` of the record) is
    never checked against the link by name alone.

    0.7.0 (F1): the fallback also counts Czech-lands settlements with no 1910 okres
    (:func:`global_names`, :func:`unplaced_in_okres`), and a candidate whose name only an
    **unanchored** register municipality prints gives ``("unanchored", okres ids)``
    (:func:`unanchored_named`).

    0.13.0 (J4): a candidate is matched as not stated (no I1 reading of its okres) and with the soldier's *home*
    values, so I2's and J1's home exceptions read the same home as the record's own match."""
    out: list[tuple[str, object]] = []
    mhome = home if _on("J4") else None              # 0.13.0 (J4)
    main_key = (key(main[0]) if main and isinstance(main[0], str) else None,
                okres_token(main[1]) if main and isinstance(main[1], str) else "")
    for c in cands:
        muni, okres, text = (tuple(c) + (None, None))[:3]
        if not isinstance(muni, str) or clean_birthplace(muni)[0] is None:
            out.append(("none", "no_municipality"))
            continue
        if isinstance(text, str) and foreign_token(text, exclude=(muni,)):
            out.append(("none", "foreign"))
            continue
        okres_s = candidate_okres(okres, text, g)
        kind, ids = resolve_okres(okres_s, stated, oid, g)
        if kind == "foreign":
            out.append(("none", "okres_foreign"))
            continue
        found = None
        if kind in ("czech", "later"):
            found = _matches([match_birthplace(muni, o, okres_s, None, False, g, vua=True, home=mhome, stated=False)
                              for o in sorted(twin_member(ids, muni, g))])
        if kind == "timeline" or (kind == "later" and found is None):
            found = _matches([match_birthplace(muni, None, okres_s, None, False, g, vua=True, home=mhome,
                                               stated=False)])
        k = key(clean_birthplace(muni)[0])
        if found is None and k in _later_towns(g):
            found = ("ok", _later_towns(g)[k])
        if found is not None:
            out.append(found)
            continue
        why = "no_okres" if not okres_s else "okres_unresolved" if kind == "none" else "unmatched"
        own = (k == main_key[0] or key(muni) == main_key[0]) and (okres_token(okres or "") == main_key[1])
        other, unanchored = set(), set()
        if not own:
            other = global_names(muni, g) - {main_sid}
            if kind in ("czech", "later"):          # a spelling of a settlement of its own okres (Weisbach)
                other |= close_names(k, twin_member(ids, muni, g), g) - {main_sid}
                if _on("F1"):                       # 0.7.0: a later name in the okres it names (Louky)
                    other |= unplaced_in_okres(k, twin_member(ids, muni, g), okres_s, g) - {main_sid}
            if _on("F1"):                           # 0.7.0: a 1910 municipality the register prints unanchored
                unanchored = unanchored_named(k, main_sid, g)
        out.append(("global", tuple(sorted(other))) if other
                   else ("unanchored", tuple(sorted(unanchored))) if unanchored else ("none", why))
    return out

def close_names(k: str, okresy, g: Gazetteer) -> set:
    """The settlements of *okresy* whose name is a close spelling of *k* (difflib ratio >=
    :data:`NAME_FUZZY_CUTOFF`): a candidate that matched nothing in the okres it names but is one
    letter off a settlement there names that settlement, not nothing (0.6.0, T1: vua 136140
    *Weisbach, okres Frýdland* is *Weissbach* of okres Frýdlant, ``bily-potok:3``)."""
    out: set = set()
    for o in okresy or ():
        names = g.okres_keys.get(o, {})
        for n in difflib.get_close_matches(k, list(names), n=3, cutoff=NAME_FUZZY_CUTOFF):
            out |= set(names[n])
    return out

def regiment_regions(units_dir: str = str(UNITS_DIR)) -> dict:
    """``{(army, reg_no): region}`` for the 1914 infantry of Ehnl's Tabelle I (A6): ``army`` is
    ``common`` (k.u.k., ``ehnl_tabelle1_infantry.csv``), ``landwehr`` (k.k.) or ``honved`` (k.u.); the
    region is ``czech`` where the table resolves the recruiting district to a Czech-lands okres
    (``land``), else the corps area's (:data:`CORPS_REGION`, :data:`LANDWEHR_REGION`); every Honvéd
    regiment ``hungary`` (the Hungarian crown's own army), the Croatian-Slavonian district ``croatia``.
    A regiment the tables do not resolve is absent: no evidence."""
    u, out = Path(units_dir), {}
    for army, name in (("common", "infantry"), ("landwehr", "landwehr"), ("honved", "honved")):
        path = u / f"ehnl_tabelle1_{name}.csv"
        if not path.exists():
            continue
        for r in pd.read_csv(path).itertuples(index=False):
            corps = str(r.corps_territorial) if isinstance(r.corps_territorial, str) else ""
            if isinstance(r.land, str) and r.land.strip():
                region = "czech"
            elif army == "common":
                region = CORPS_REGION.get(corps.strip())
            elif army == "landwehr":
                region = LANDWEHR_REGION.get(key(corps.split(";")[0]))
            else:
                region = "croatia" if corps.lower().startswith("kroat") else "hungary"
            if region:
                out[(army, int(r.reg_no))] = region
    return out

def legion_regiment(unit) -> tuple[str, int] | None:
    """``(army, number)`` of a csol.cz Habsburg infantry unit (``45.p.pl.`` → common 45, ``10.zem.p.pl.``
    → Landwehr 10, ``honv.p.pl.`` → Honvéd; the abbreviations of
    ``utils.docs.build_docs._legion_ah_matched``), else ``None`` (Landsturm ``dom.``, Schützen, other arms,
    a unit written with a ``?``)."""
    m = _LEGION_UNIT_RE.match(unit) if isinstance(unit, str) and "?" not in unit else None
    if not m:
        return None
    n, rest = int(m.group(1)), m.group(2).strip().lower()
    if rest.startswith(("p.pl.", "pp")):
        return "common", n
    if rest.startswith(("zem.p.pl.", "zem.pl.")):
        return "landwehr", n
    if rest.startswith("honv.p.pl."):
        return "honved", n
    return None

def regiment_region(units) -> str | None:
    """The one recruiting region of a soldier's regiments (A6): each ``(army, number)`` of *units*
    (``None`` skipped) looked up in :func:`regiment_regions`; ``None`` when none resolves or two
    resolve to different regions (the peacetime and the capture regiment disagree: no evidence)."""
    table = regiment_regions()
    regions = {table.get(u) for u in units if u is not None} - {None}
    return next(iter(regions)) if len(regions) == 1 else None

def regiment_region_column(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """The recruiting region (:func:`regiment_region`) of every row: VÚA from ``ah_unit_org`` /
    ``ah_unit_type`` / ``ah_regiment_no``, csol.cz from ``habsburg_unit_peacetime`` and
    ``habsburg_unit_capture`` (recruitment ≠ field unit: both must agree, ERGAENZUNG.md); ``None`` without
    the columns, and for a VÚA unit written with a ``?`` (*pěší pluk 48 ?*: no evidence) (0.8.0, A6)."""
    units = regiment_units(df)
    if units is None:
        return pd.Series([None] * len(df), index=df.index, dtype=object)
    cache: dict = {}
    vals = [cache.setdefault(u, regiment_region(u)) for u in units]
    return pd.Series(vals, index=df.index, dtype=object)

def regiment_units(df: pd.DataFrame) -> list | None:
    """The ``(army, number)`` units of every row (VÚA one, csol.cz the peacetime and the capture
    regiment), ``None`` without the columns (0.9.0: shared by :func:`regiment_region_column` and
    :func:`regiment_area_column`)."""
    if {"ah_unit_org", "ah_unit_type", "ah_regiment_no"} <= set(df.columns):
        doubt = [isinstance(u, str) and "?" in u for u in _col(df, "ah_unit_primary").astype(object)]
        return [(None if d else vua_regiment(o, t, n),) for o, t, n, d in zip(df["ah_unit_org"].astype(object),
                                                                               df["ah_unit_type"].astype(object),
                                                                               df["ah_regiment_no"].astype(object),
                                                                               doubt)]
    if {"habsburg_unit_peacetime", "habsburg_unit_capture"} & set(df.columns):
        cols = [_col(df, c).astype(object) for c in ("habsburg_unit_peacetime", "habsburg_unit_capture")]
        return [(legion_regiment(a), legion_regiment(b)) for a, b in zip(*cols)]
    return None

def foreign_okres_region(okres_s, g: Gazetteer) -> str | None:
    """The region (A6) of an okres string :func:`resolve_okres` reads as foreign: ``austria`` for a
    Lower Austrian district (or, D-b, a close spelling of one), ``prussia`` for Hlučín, else
    ``hungary`` (the Hungarian frame's district and obec names, the Subcarpathian okresy); ``None``
    when the string is not foreign."""
    if not isinstance(okres_s, str) or not key(okres_s):
        return None
    if resolve_okres(okres_s, None, None, g)[0] != "foreign":
        return None
    k = key(okres_s)
    rural = _RURAL_WORD_RE.sub("", k).strip()
    if "hlucin" in (k, rural):
        return "prussia"
    if _on("E7") and (k in FOREIGN_DISTRICTS_PRUSSIA or rural in FOREIGN_DISTRICTS_PRUSSIA):
        return "prussia"
    if k in FOREIGN_DISTRICTS_LOWER_AUSTRIA or rural in FOREIGN_DISTRICTS_LOWER_AUSTRIA:
        return "austria"
    near = _closest_foreign(rural or k, g)
    if near and near[1] in FOREIGN_DISTRICTS_PRUSSIA:
        return "prussia"

def regiment_candidates(cands, region, g: Gazetteer, area=None) -> list:
    """A6: the candidates of *cands* placed in the regiment's *region* (one of
    :data:`REGIMENT_EVIDENCE_REGIONS`).

    0.9.0 (E2): only a candidate in the regiment's own recruiting county or a county next to it
    (*area*, :func:`regiment_area`; :func:`in_area`), and never one that is only a ``dříve:`` former-name
    list (:func:`former_name_only`): IR 34 Kassa (Abaúj-Torna) is no evidence for *Opava, okres Modrý
    Kameň* (Nógrád); IR 67 Eperjes (Sáros) is for *Tvarožná, okres Kežmarok* (Szepes, next to Sáros). With
    E2 on, a regiment without a known area is no evidence."""
    if region not in REGIMENT_EVIDENCE_REGIONS:
        return []
    out = [c for c in cands if candidate_region(c, g) == region]
    if _on("E2"):
        out = [c for c in out if not former_name_only(c) and in_area(candidate_counties(c, g), area)]
    return out

def regiment_areas(units_dir: str = str(UNITS_DIR)) -> dict:
    """E2 (0.9.0): ``{(army, reg_no): frozenset}`` — the recruiting area of each regiment outside the
    Czech lands: the 1910 counties of its Ergänzungsbezirk seats (Ehnl ``ergbez``, every ``;`` piece,
    :data:`ERGBEZ_COUNTY`) for a Hungarian regiment, ``seat:<key>`` of each seat for a Galician, Austrian or
    Croatian one (compared with :data:`DISTRICT_ERGBEZ`); a regiment none of whose seats is known is absent."""
    regions = regiment_regions(units_dir)
    u, out = Path(units_dir), {}
    for army, name in (("common", "infantry"), ("landwehr", "landwehr"), ("honved", "honved")):
        path = u / f"ehnl_tabelle1_{name}.csv"
        if not path.exists():
            continue
        for r in pd.read_csv(path).itertuples(index=False):
            region = regions.get((army, int(r.reg_no)))
            if region not in REGIMENT_EVIDENCE_REGIONS or not isinstance(r.ergbez, str):
                continue
            seats = [s for s in (_seat_key(x) for x in r.ergbez.split(";")) if s]
            area = ({ERGBEZ_COUNTY[s] for s in seats if s in ERGBEZ_COUNTY} if region == "hungary"
                    else {f"seat:{s}" for s in seats})
            if area:
                out[(army, int(r.reg_no))] = frozenset(area)
    return out

def regiment_area(units) -> frozenset | None:
    """E2 (0.9.0): the union of the recruiting areas (:func:`regiment_areas`) of a soldier's regiments,
    ``None`` where none is known."""
    table = regiment_areas()
    out = frozenset().union(*(table.get(u, frozenset()) for u in units if u is not None))
    return out or None

def candidate_counties(cand, g: Gazetteer) -> set:
    """E2 (0.9.0): where one VÚA candidate reading lies, county by county: its okres string's 1910 counties
    (:attr:`Gazetteer.hu_county`: a Slovak or Subcarpathian okres, a járás or its seat), or ``seat:<key>``
    for a foreign district word that is a recruiting seat (:data:`DISTRICT_ERGBEZ`: *Krakov*); empty where
    the candidate names only a land (*Halič*, *Slovensko*)."""

        for piece in re.split(r"[,;()/]+", text)[1:]:
            if key(piece) in DISTRICT_ERGBEZ:
                return {f"seat:{DISTRICT_ERGBEZ[key(piece)]}"}

    rural = _RURAL_WORD_RE.sub("", k).strip()
    return set(g.hu_county.get(k) or g.hu_county.get(rural) or ())

def former_name_only(cand) -> bool:
    """E2 (0.9.0): a candidate reading that is only VÚA's ``dříve:`` former-name list — the parenthesis
    of German or former names read as a reading (*(Vezekény - ?; dříve: Végvezekény - ?)*, no name of its

def home_names_link(home, head, sid, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """E2 (0.9.0): the soldier's VÚA home cell names the link — its municipality (or a hyphen piece of it:
    *Sedlišťka-Nová Sídla*) is a name of the linked settlement, or its **written** okres string fits the
    link's okres — and is not merely a copy of the written *head* (*Opava*, home *Opava*: no evidence)."""
    hm, _ho, _hl, _hmg, _hj, hok = (tuple(home or ()) + (None,) * 6)[:6]
    hname = clean_birthplace(str(hm).split(",")[0])[0] if isinstance(hm, str) else None
    name = clean_birthplace(re.split(r"[,;]", head)[0])[0] if isinstance(head, str) else None
    if not hname or sid is None or (name and key(hname) == key(name)):
        return False
    keys = {key(hname)} | {key(x) for x in re.split(r"\s*[-–]\s*", hname) if x.strip()}
    if form_set(keys) & (_name_forms(sid, g) | g.forms_1910.get(sid, set())):
        return True
    okr = re.sub(r"[?+]", " ", str(hok).split(",")[0]).strip(" -–.") if isinstance(hok, str) else ""
    return bool(okres_token(okr)) and _okres_fits(okr, sid, g, exact_only=True) is None

def modlan_keeps(head, main_sid, glob, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """D-f (0.8.0): a link read off VÚA's first candidate stands beside ``global`` candidates when the
    written *head* (exact key, space-free) is a printed 1910 form of the link — a register form or the
    lexikon's 1910 name — and every other id is an unplaced Czech-lands row (:func:`unplaced_czech`) the
    register does not print and the lexikon gives no 1910 name (*Modlan* = ``modlany:1``, printed
    *Modlan, Modlany*, beside *Nové Modlany*, ``nove-modlany:1``). *Nový Bohumín* (``sunychl:1``, a
    register row) stays refused."""
    if not isinstance(head, str) or not glob:
        return False
    name = clean_birthplace(re.split(r"[,;]", head)[0])[0]
    hk = nospace(key(name)) if name else ""
    printed = g.pool_forms.get(main_sid, set()) | g.forms_1910.get(main_sid, set())
    if not hk or hk not in printed:
        return False
    return all(unplaced_czech(s, g) and not g.pool_forms.get(s) and s not in g.owner and not g.forms_1910.get(s)
               for s in glob)

def vua_candidate_rule(main_sid, cands, stated, oid, g: Gazetteer, main=None, head=None, regiment=None, area=None, home=None, match_home=None) -> tuple[object, tuple, tuple]

D1 (0.5.0, tightened in 0.6.0 by T1): (refusal candidates or None, silent reasons, against kinds) for a reading taken from VÚA's first candidate and matched to main_sid.

Refused when any candidate gives a different settlement, is itself ambiguous (an ambiguous candidate may name another place: refused even when its ids hold main_sid — conservative, the 0.4.0 extension the author kept), or (0.6.0) names, by the global-name fallback, Czech-lands settlements other than main_sid (global); the refusal candidates are main_sid and every id the candidates give (at most GLOBAL_CANDIDATES_SHOWN from the fallback). A candidate giving nothing is no evidence: its reason goes to silent (the caller keeps such a link vua_uncertain). main is the record's own (municipality, okres).

0.7.0: a candidate naming a 1910 municipality the register prints unanchored refuses too (unanchored, F1); and where the link would stand beside silent candidates — the candidates disagree — the record's written head (head_text) is read against it (head_verdict: head_global F1; head_foreign / head_land / head_namesake F2).

0.8.0: D-f — global candidates that are only unplaced rows the register does not print stand aside when the head is a printed 1910 form of the link (modlan_keeps; the link keeps vua_uncertain through the silent reason global_unplaced); A6 — where the link would stand, a candidate in the recruiting region of the soldier's regiment (regiment_candidates) refuses it (kind regiment); the regiment never picks a candidate. match_home (0.13.0, J4): the home values the candidates are matched with (candidate_verdicts; the record's own match reads the same).
