def vua_candidate_rule(main_sid, cands, stated, oid, g: Gazetteer, main=None,
                       head=None, regiment=None, area=None, home=None, match_home=None) -> tuple[object, tuple, tuple]:
    """D1 (0.5.0, tightened in 0.6.0 by T1): ``(refusal candidates or None, silent reasons, against
    kinds)`` for a reading taken from VÚA's first candidate and matched to *main_sid*.

    Refused when any candidate gives a **different** settlement, is itself ambiguous (an ambiguous
    candidate may name another place: refused even when its ids hold *main_sid* — conservative, the
    0.4.0 extension the author kept), or (0.6.0) names, by the global-name fallback, Czech-lands
    settlements other than *main_sid* (``global``); the refusal candidates are *main_sid* and every
    id the candidates give (at most :data:`GLOBAL_CANDIDATES_SHOWN` from the fallback). A candidate
    giving nothing is no evidence: its reason goes to *silent* (the caller keeps such a link
    ``vua_uncertain``). *main* is the record's own ``(municipality, okres)``.

    0.7.0: a candidate naming a 1910 municipality the register prints unanchored refuses too
    (``unanchored``, F1); and where the link would stand beside silent candidates — the candidates
    disagree — the record's written *head* (:func:`head_text`) is read against it
    (:func:`head_verdict`: ``head_global`` F1; ``head_foreign`` / ``head_land`` / ``head_namesake``
    F2).

    0.8.0: D-f — ``global`` candidates that are only unplaced rows the register does not print stand
    aside when the head is a printed 1910 form of the link (:func:`modlan_keeps`; the link keeps
    ``vua_uncertain`` through the silent reason ``global_unplaced``); A6 — where the link would stand,
    a candidate in the recruiting region of the soldier's *regiment* (:func:`regiment_candidates`)
    refuses it (kind ``regiment``); the regiment never picks a candidate. *match_home* (0.13.0, J4): the home values
    the candidates are matched with (:func:`candidate_verdicts`; the record's own match reads the same)."""
    verdicts = candidate_verdicts(cands, stated, oid, g, main=main, main_sid=main_sid, home=match_home)
    other = {v for kind, v in verdicts if kind == "ok" and v != main_sid}
    amb = {x for kind, v in verdicts if kind == "ambiguous" for x in v}
    glob = {x for kind, v in verdicts if kind == "global" for x in v} - {main_sid}
    unanch = any(kind == "unanchored" for kind, _v in verdicts)
    silent = tuple(v for kind, v in verdicts if kind == "none")
    if glob and not (other or amb or unanch) and _on("Df") and modlan_keeps(head, main_sid, glob, g):
        silent, glob = silent + ("global_unplaced",), set()
    if other or amb or glob or unanch:
        against = tuple(k for k, flag in (("settlement", other), ("ambiguous", amb), ("global", glob),
                                          ("unanchored", unanch)) if flag)
        shown = set(sorted(glob)[:GLOBAL_CANDIDATES_SHOWN])
        return tuple(sorted(other | amb | shown | {main_sid})), silent, against
    if silent and head:
        kind, ids = head_verdict(head, cands, verdicts, main, main_sid, g)
        if kind:
            shown = set(sorted(ids)[:GLOBAL_CANDIDATES_SHOWN])
            return tuple(sorted(shown | {main_sid})), silent, (kind,)
    if silent and regiment and _on("A6") and regiment_candidates(cands, regiment, g, area=area):
        # 0.9.0 (E2): a home cell that names the link (not a copy of the head) outweighs the regiment
        if not (_on("E2") and home_names_link(home, head, main_sid, g)):
            return (main_sid,), silent, ("regiment",)
    return None, silent, ()

def head_text(raw) -> str | None:
    """The record's written head: the raw cell before its first parenthesis (``Eisenberg ?``;
    ``Jeníkov, Nitra ?``), ``None`` where empty (0.7.0)."""
    if not isinstance(raw, str):
        return None
    h = raw.split("(", 1)[0].strip(" ?;,")
    return h or None

(kind, ids) where the written head contradicts a link read off VÚA's first candidate, else (None, set()) (0.7.0). In order:

  • F2 head_foreign — the head names a land, country or district outside the Czech lands (foreign_token, a Hungarian or other foreign okres among its comma pieces: Jeníkov, Nitra; Upper Silesia), or the head's name is a candidate VÚA placed outside the Czech lands and not the linked candidate's name nor any name of the link (Inzersdorf = Inzersdorf, Hietzing, Dolní Rakousy, not Tolštejn-Innozenzidorf);
  • F2 head_land — a land word against the link's land (land_conflict: Markovice, Morava → Chrudim);
  • F2 head_namesake — a distinguishing word of the head (MARKER_WORDS: Něm., Horní, Nový …) that the names of another namesake carry and the link's do not (Něm. Kravaře → kravare:2, Deutsch Krawarn), marker_namesakes;
  • F1 head_global — the head's name is not the linked candidate's own (nor a piece of it, nor a spelling of it within HEAD_SAME_NAME_RATIO) and answers elsewhere to Czech-lands settlements other than the link (global_names; within the okres and the land the head names, when it names them): Eisenberg → ruda:4 beside jezeri:1. 0.8.0 (D-d): a named land keeps only the namesakes in exactly that land — the Moravia/Silesia tolerance of land_conflict refuses a link but creates no competing namesake (Benešov, Slezsko: not benesov:2 of Boskovice).

A head naming the link's own okres is no foreign candidate's name (Dolní Štěpánov, Šternberk beside Dolní Štepanov, okres Trstená).

def head_verdict(head, cands, verdicts, main, main_sid, g: Gazetteer) -> tuple[str | None, set]:
    """``(kind, ids)`` where the written *head* contradicts a link read off VÚA's first candidate,
    else ``(None, set())`` (0.7.0). In order:

    * F2 ``head_foreign`` — the head names a land, country or district outside the Czech lands
      (:func:`foreign_token`, a Hungarian or other foreign okres among its comma pieces: *Jeníkov,
      Nitra*; Upper Silesia), or the head's name **is** a candidate VÚA placed outside the Czech
      lands and not the linked candidate's name nor any name of the link (*Inzersdorf* = *Inzersdorf,
      Hietzing, Dolní Rakousy*, not *Tolštejn-Innozenzidorf*);
    * F2 ``head_land`` — a land word against the link's land (:func:`land_conflict`: *Markovice,
      Morava* → Chrudim);
    * F2 ``head_namesake`` — a distinguishing word of the head (:data:`MARKER_WORDS`: *Něm.*,
      *Horní*, *Nový* …) that the names of another namesake carry and the link's do not (*Něm.
      Kravaře* → ``kravare:2``, *Deutsch Krawarn*), :func:`marker_namesakes`;
    * F1 ``head_global`` — the head's name is not the linked candidate's own (nor a piece of it, nor a
      spelling of it within :data:`HEAD_SAME_NAME_RATIO`) and answers elsewhere to Czech-lands
      settlements other than the link (:func:`global_names`; within the okres and the land the head
      names, when it names them): *Eisenberg* → ``ruda:4`` beside ``jezeri:1``. 0.8.0 (D-d): a named
      land keeps only the namesakes in exactly that land — the Moravia/Silesia tolerance of
      :func:`land_conflict` refuses a link but creates no competing namesake (*Benešov, Slezsko*: not
      ``benesov:2`` of Boskovice).

    A head naming the link's own okres is no foreign candidate's name (*Dolní Štěpánov, Šternberk*
    beside *Dolní Štepanov, okres Trstená*)."""
    pieces = [p.strip() for p in re.split(r"[,;]", head)]
    name = clean_birthplace(pieces[0])[0] if pieces and pieces[0] else None
    if not name:
        return None, set()
    hk = key(name)
    main_muni = main[0] if main and isinstance(main[0], str) else None
    main_clean = clean_birthplace(main_muni)[0] if main_muni else None
    main_keys = {key(main_clean)} if main_clean else set()
    if main_clean:
        main_keys |= {key(p) for p in re.split(r"\s*[-–]\s*", main_clean) if p.strip()}
    okresy = set().union(*(_written_ids(p, g, exact=True) for p in pieces[1:] if key(p))) if len(pieces) > 1 else set()
    lands = lands_named(head)
    if _on("F2"):
        if foreign_token(head, exclude=(main_muni,) if main_muni else ()) or any(
                key(p) and resolve_okres(p, None, None, g, fuzzy=False, timeline=False)[0] == "foreign"
                for p in pieces[1:]):
            return "head_foreign", set()
        if "foreign" in lands:
            return "head_foreign", set()
        if land_conflict(lands, _land_of(main_sid, g)):
            return "head_land", set()
        mine = form_set([hk])
        names_link_okres = _okres_any(main_sid, g) in okresy      # "Dolní Štěpánov, Šternberk": the link's okres
        for c, (kind, why) in zip(cands, verdicts):
            cm = clean_birthplace(c[0])[0] if c and isinstance(c[0], str) else None
            if (kind == "none" and why in ("foreign", "okres_foreign") and cm and key(cm) == hk
                    and hk not in main_keys and not (mine & _name_forms(main_sid, g)) and not names_link_okres):
                return "head_foreign", set()
        ids = marker_namesakes(hk, main_sid, g)
        if ids:
            return "head_namesake", ids
    # the head's own spelling of the linked candidate's name is that name (Kunova / Kunov)
    near = any(difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, hk, m).ratio() >= HEAD_SAME_NAME_RATIO for m in main_keys)
    if _on("F1") and hk not in main_keys and not near:
        ids = global_names(name, g) - {main_sid}
        if okresy:                                   # the okres the head names (Třítěz, Pelhřimov)
            ids = {s for s in ids if _okres_any(s, g) in okresy}
        numbered = {x for x in lands if x != "foreign"}
        if numbered and _on("Dd"):                   # 0.8.0 (D-d): exactly the land the head names
            ids = {s for s in ids if _land_of(s, g) in numbered}
        elif numbered:                               # the land the head names (Benešov, Slezsko)
            ids = {s for s in ids if not land_conflict(numbered, _land_of(s, g))}
        if ids:
            return "head_global", ids
    return None, set()

def marker_namesakes(hk: str, main_sid, g: Gazetteer) -> set

F2 (0.7.0): the namesakes a distinguishing word of the head points to. For each word of the head key hk in MARKER_WORDS (nem in nem kravare), the settlements of the rest of the name (kravare, every okres and land: the head may name a place outside the Czech lands) whose names — lexikon (1910 and German included) or register — start with one of the word's stems (deutschkrawarn); returned only when the link's own names carry none of them.

def marker_namesakes(hk: str, main_sid, g: Gazetteer) -> set:
    """F2 (0.7.0): the namesakes a distinguishing word of the head points to. For each word of the
    head key *hk* in :data:`MARKER_WORDS` (*nem* in ``nem kravare``), the settlements of the rest of
    the name (``kravare``, every okres and land: the head may name a place outside the Czech lands)
    whose names — lexikon (1910 and German included) or register — start with one of the word's stems
    (``deutschkrawarn``); returned only when the link's own names carry none of them."""
    words = hk.split()
    out: set = set()
    for i, w in enumerate(words):
        for heads, stems in MARKER_WORDS:
            if w not in heads:
                continue
            base = " ".join(words[:i] + words[i + 1:])
            if not base:
                continue
            carry = lambda s: any(f.startswith(stems) for f in _name_forms(s, g))    # noqa: E731
            if carry(main_sid):
                return set()
            out |= {s for s in g.global_any.get(base, ()) if s != main_sid and carry(s)}
    return out

def obec_over_part(sid, tier, clean, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """D-144 chose a register municipality over a register **part** printing the same name (0.4.0, no
    link change): *Nová Ves* | Kolín → ``nova-ves-i:1`` (cz 301040087/20, 1,375) while the register
    also prints the part *Nová Ves, Neudorf* of Svojšice."""
    table = {"p1_register": g.reg, "p2_register_alt": g.reg_alt}.get(tier or "")
    if table is None or sid is None or oid is None or not clean:
        return False
    ids = table.get((key(clean), oid)) or set()
    # 0.4.1: a competing part the chosen municipality itself owns is no rival (Osek → novy-osek:1,
    # whose own part hrad-osek:1 prints the same name)
    return (len(ids) > 1 and sid in ids and sid in g.reg_municipal
            and any(s not in g.reg_municipal and (g.owner.get(s) or {}).get("muni_sid") != sid
                    for s in ids if s != sid))

def candidate_refusal(against) -> str:
    """The refusal of the first-candidate rule for the kinds that refused it: ``vua_regiment_conflict``
    (A6, the regiment), ``vua_head_conflict`` (0.8.0, D-g: the written head against the link — F2's
    ``head_foreign`` / ``head_land`` / ``head_namesake``), else ``ambiguous:vua_candidates``."""
    if "regiment" in against:
        return "vua_regiment_conflict"
    if _on("Dg") and set(against) & _HEAD_KINDS:
        return "vua_head_conflict"
    return "ambiguous:vua_candidates"

def stated_okres_alternatives(raw, clean, sid, g: Gazetteer) -> tuple[str | None, str | None, tuple]:
    """D-a (0.8.0, F5 for a stated okres): where the cell gives okres alternatives in parentheses after an
    okres word of the head (:func:`okres_only_alternatives`: *Domoradice, okr. Vysoké Mýto? (Český Krumlov?)*), an
    okres the cell names that the link does not lie in and that holds another namesake of the key
    (:func:`holds_namesake`) refuses the link ``okres_from_name_ambiguous`` — as F5 does for an okres
    inferred from the name; ``(None, None, ())`` otherwise."""
    alts = okres_only_alternatives(raw, g, sid)
    k = key(clean) if clean else ""
    if not alts or not k:
        return None, None, ()
    for name in dict.fromkeys([*okres_names_in(raw), *alts]):
        if _okres_fits(name, sid, g) == "conflict" and holds_namesake(name, k, sid, g):
            return "okres_from_name_ambiguous", "okres_alternative_stated", tuple(sorted(_written_ids(name, g)))
    return None, None, ()

def czech_looking_okres(okres, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """D-a (0.8.0): an unresolved okres string is a misspelt Czech-lands okres — some backbone okres or
    court name within :data:`OKRES_LOOSE_CUTOFF` of it (``venkov`` / ``okolí`` dropped) and no foreign
    district name at least as close (:func:`_closest_foreign`)."""
    k = key(okres) if isinstance(okres, str) else ""
    rural = _RURAL_WORD_RE.sub("", k).strip() or k
    if not rural:
        return False
    close = difflib.get_close_matches(rural, [n for n in g.okres_by_name if len(nospace(n)) >= 3], n=1,
                                      cutoff=OKRES_LOOSE_CUTOFF)
    if not close:
        return False
    best = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, rural, close[0]).ratio()
    near = _closest_foreign(rural, g)
    return not (near and near[0] >= best)

def okres_string_consistent(s, sid, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """D-a (0.8.0): the unresolved okres string *s* is a spelling of the okres the name inference reached
    — within :data:`OKRES_LOOSE_CUTOFF` (space-free, ``venkov`` dropped) of a name of the settlement's 1910
    okres or of a token of its ``okres_all`` timeline (*Preha venkov* / Praha-venkov for Točná, 1910
    Smíchov)."""
    k = key(s) if isinstance(s, str) else ""
    forms = {nospace(_RURAL_WORD_RE.sub("", k).strip() or k), nospace(k)} - {""}
    targets = {nospace(n) for n in g.okres_names.get(_okres_any(sid, g), ())} | set(g.timeline.get(sid, ()))
    return any(difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, f, t).ratio() >= OKRES_LOOSE_CUTOFF for f in forms for t in targets if t)

  • "string" — resolve_okres reads the string as one Czech-lands okres (a backbone, court or later name, an alias, a close spelling: Kroměíž venkov, Žlužice; city/rural twins by twin_member) and the name is matched there, as under a stated okres;

  • (None, None) — a foreign cell or string (a land word, a foreign district, the string itself: Lvov; D-b, no fuzzy reading of Senica, Slovensko), a later-okres timeline token (P4 already reads it), no single okres or settlement.

      then no evidence, F6; the link carries ``okres_inferred``) — never for a home outside the Czech lands
      (*home_land*: legion *Dubno, okres Dubno*, home in Volhynia);
    * ``(None, None)`` — a foreign cell or string (a land word, a foreign district, the string itself:
      *Lvov*; D-b, no fuzzy reading of *Senica, Slovensko*), a later-okres timeline token (P4 already reads
      it), no single okres or settlement.

    0.13.0 (J4): every match here runs in an okres the string or the name supplied, not a stated one — no I1 reading
    (``stated=False``) — and with the soldier's *home* values (I2's and J1's home exceptions).

    0.14.0 (K2): a name no 1910 settlement carries as written but exactly one carries abbreviated
    (:func:`abbreviated_settlement`) is read in that settlement's okres where the string is a later-okres token of its
    timeline (``"string"``: the string named the okres, *Brandýs n. L.* | *Brandýs n. L.*) or, as any name (``"name"``),
    a spelling of its okres."""
    mhome = home if _on("J4") else None
    text = ", ".join(x for x in ("x", s, raw if isinstance(raw, str) else None) if isinstance(x, str))
    if (foreign_token(text, exclude=(m,) if isinstance(m, str) else ()) or "foreign" in lands_named(text)
            or _foreign_string(s, g)):
        return None, None
    kind, ids, how = okres_resolution(s, None, None, g)
    if kind == "timeline" and _on("E9") and ids in multi_okres_tokens(g):
        res = timeline_okres_link(m, s, ids, ger, unc, g, gforms, vua=vua_cell, home=mhome)
        return (res, "timeline") if res is not None else (None, None)
    if kind == "timeline" and _on("K2"):
        # 0.14.0 (K2): a name the 1910 settlements hold only abbreviated (*Brandýs n. L.*), under a later-okres token
        # its one settlement's timeline carries (*Brandýs n. L.* read as the okres Brandýs nad Labem)
        clean = clean_birthplace(m)[0] if isinstance(m, str) else None
        one = abbreviated_settlement(key(clean), g) if clean else None
        if one is not None and ids in g.timeline.get(one, set()) and _okres_any(one, g) is not None:
            return (match_birthplace(m, _okres_any(one, g), None, ger, unc, g, german_forms=gforms, vua=vua_cell,
                                     home=mhome, stated=False), "string")
    if kind in ("foreign", "timeline"):
        return None, None
    if kind in ("czech", "later"):
        found = [match_birthplace(m, o2, s, ger, unc, g, german_forms=gforms, vua=vua_cell, home=mhome, stated=False)
                 for o2 in sorted(twin_member(set(ids), m, g))]
        for r in found:
            r["okres_how"] = how                   # 0.9.0 (E10): exact / alias / later / hyphen / fuzzy
        if len(found) == 1:
            return found[0], "string"
        linked = [r for r in found if r["sid"] is not None]
        if len(linked) == 1 and not any(str(r["refusal"] or "").startswith("ambiguous") for r in found):
            return linked[0], "string"
        return None, None
    if isinstance(home_land, str) and home_land.strip() and home_land.strip() != "Czech lands":
        return None, None
    clean = clean_birthplace(m)[0] if isinstance(m, str) else None
    repeated = bool(clean) and vua_cell and key(s) == key(clean)
    if not clean or not (repeated or czech_looking_okres(s, g)):
        return None, None
    v, one = d2_decide(key(clean), g)
    if v == "ambiguous" and not one and _on("K2"):    # 0.14.0 (K2): no 1910 settlement as written; abbreviated?
        abbreviated = abbreviated_settlement(key(clean), g)
        if abbreviated is not None:
            v, one = "ok", abbreviated
            repeated = repeated or okres_token(s) == okres_token(clean)
    if v != "ok" or _okres_any(one, g) is None or not (repeated or okres_string_consistent(s, one, g)):
        return None, None
    return (match_birthplace(m, _okres_any(one, g), None, ger, unc, g, german_forms=gforms, vua=vua_cell, home=mhome,
                             stated=False), "name")

def multi_okres_tokens(g: Gazetteer) -> set:
    """E9 (0.9.0): the okres_all tokens of the later okresy that span several 1910 okresy — those of
    :data:`LATER_OKRES_1910` (:attr:`Gazetteer.later_token`) and the capital's countryside
    (*prahavenkov*, *prahazapad* …)."""
    out = set(g.later_token.values())
    out |= {t for t in g.timeline_tokens if _PRAHA_RURAL_RE.match(re.sub(r"^(praha)", r"\1 ", t))}
    return out

def timeline_okres_link(m, s, tok, ger, unc: bool, g: Gazetteer, gforms=None, vua: bool = False,
                        home=None) -> dict | None:
    """E9 (0.9.0): a name under a later okres that spans several 1910 okresy (*Kralupy*: Slaný, Smíchov,
    Mělník; *Praha-venkov*: Smíchov, Karlín, Královské Vinohrady), read as P4 reads a timeline okres but
    through every tier: the name matched in each 1910 okres that formed it (:func:`timeline_okresy`) and in
    its seat okresy (:func:`timeline_seat_okresy`) — one settlement across them links (in its own 1910
    okres), namesakes in several are refused ``ambiguous:p4_okres_timeline`` (no okres set), none gives
    ``None`` (P4 as before). In a seat okres the settlement need not carry the later okres in its own
    ``okres_all`` — the lexikon's timeline misses it on villages the records place there (*Koleč, okres
    Kralupy*: Slaný, Kladno; *Butovice, okres Praha venkov*: Smíchov) — elsewhere it must (*Vokovice* of
    Smíchov is no village of okres Kralupy, and nor are *Letky* and *Tursko* of Smíchov: their lexikon timeline is
    Smíchov|Praha-venkov|Praha-západ, without Kralupy — 0.9.0's docstring said they were; corrected in 0.10.0, F8,
    behaviour unchanged, so legion *Letky* | *Kralupy nad Vltavou* stays ``no_okres_1910``). As P4, a statutory city answers only to its own name and a qualifier is not stripped off a
    name that exists as written elsewhere (*Kamýk nad Vltavou*)."""
    clean = clean_birthplace(m)[0] if isinstance(m, str) else None
    k = key(clean) if clean else ""
    found = []
    seats = timeline_seat_okresy(tok, g)
    okresy = timeline_okresy(tok, g) | seats
    for o2 in sorted(okresy):
        r = match_birthplace(m, o2, s, ger, unc, g, german_forms=gforms, vua=vua, home=home,
                             stated=False)    # 0.13.0 (J4): not a stated okres (the flag is read only with J4 on)
        # as P4: no statutory city for a name that is not the city's, no qualifier stripped off a name that
        # exists as written elsewhere (Kamýk nad Vltavou is not Kamýk of Velké Přílepy), and no settlement
        # the Prague pool finds outside the okresy that formed the later okres
        if r["tier"] == "statutory_city" and k not in g.okres_names.get(o2, set()):
            continue
        if r["tier"] == "p2_qualifier" and g.global_name.get(k):
            continue
        # outside the seat okres the settlement must carry the later okres in its own timeline (Vokovice of
        # Smíchov is no village of okres Kralupy, nor are Letky and Tursko of Smíchov: no Kralupy in their timeline)
        if r["sid"] is not None and _okres_any(r["sid"], g) not in seats and tok not in g.timeline.get(r["sid"], set()):
            continue
        found.append(r)
    if not found:
        return None
    sids = {r["sid"] for r in found if r["sid"] is not None}
    amb = {c for r in found if r["sid"] is None and str(r["refusal"] or "").startswith("ambiguous")
           for c in (r["candidates"] or ())}
    if len(sids) == 1 and not amb:
        res = next(r for r in found if r["sid"] in sids)
        res["okres_how"] = "timeline"
        return res
    if sids or amb:
        base = found[0]
        return {**base, "sid": None, "tier": "p4_okres_timeline", "refusal": "ambiguous:p4_okres_timeline",
                "candidates": tuple(sorted(sids | amb)), "okres_1910": None, "tie": None,
                "okres_how": "timeline", "okres_ids": tuple(sorted(timeline_okresy(tok, g)))}
    return None

def reading_not_head(m, raw) -> bool:
    """E3 (0.9.0): VÚA's reading *m* is not the name the cell writes before its parenthesis (the
    :func:`head_text`'s first comma piece, :func:`clean_birthplace` and :func:`key` on both)."""

def raw_candidates(raw) -> tuple | None:

def okres_town_read(raw, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """G6 (0.10.0): a VÚA candidate reading of the cell (:func:`locations.candidate_readings`) is the town of
    okres *oid* itself — its name one of the okres's names (:attr:`Gazetteer.okres_names`) and its okres
    string resolving to *oid* (*Aisič, okres Ústí nad Labem ? (Ústí nad Labem, okres Ústí nad Labem ?)
    (Aussig - ?)*). A German-forms parenthesis (*(Taus)*, *(Starkenbach)*) names no okres and never counts."""
    from utils.parsing import locations as loc
    if not isinstance(raw, str) or "(" not in raw or oid is None or pd.isna(oid):
        return False
    names = g.okres_names.get(int(oid), set())
    for c in loc.candidate_readings(raw, with_text=True) or ():
        muni, okres, text = (tuple(c) + (None, None))[:3]
        name = clean_birthplace(muni)[0] if isinstance(muni, str) else None
        if not name or key(name) not in names:
            continue
        okres_s = candidate_okres(okres, text, g)
        kind, ids = resolve_okres(okres_s, None, None, g, fuzzy=False)
        if kind == "czech" and int(oid) in ids:
            return True
    return False

def okres_string_alternatives(m, s, clean, g: Gazetteer, common: bool = True) -> tuple[str | None, str | None, tuple]:
    """E6 (0.9.0): an okres string that names two or more okresy (*X/Y*, *X? Y?*, *? (A, B)*; each piece an
    okres, court or later okres as written) of which at least two hold a settlement of a name the record
    writes (the name, its alternates and its ``/`` / ``?`` pieces: *Stěžery? Žižkov?* under *Hradec
    Králové? Praha?*) is refused ``okres_from_name_ambiguous`` (detail ``okres_alternative_string``) — which
    okres the place lies in is a coin flip the record does not settle (legion *Krčín*, *? (Nové město nad
    Metují, Kaplice)*; *Měšice*, *Tábor? Brandýs nad Labem?*); ``(None, None, ())`` otherwise.

    0.10.0 (G2): ``(None, 'okres_alternative_common', (sid,))`` where the pieces agree on one settlement;
    *common* = False (0.11.0, H3) skips that branch and gives E6's refusal with the okres ids."""
    if not isinstance(s, str):
        return None, None, ()
    m, s = _drop_paired_parentheses(m, s)
    single = isinstance(m, str) and not re.search(r"[/?]", m)
    pieces = [re.sub(r"\s+", " ", _OKRES_WORD_RE.sub(" ", x)).strip(" -–.+") for x in re.split(r"[/?,;()]+", s)]
    if single and clean:                       # 'Nové Hrady, okres Nové Hrady, Vysoké Mýto': the place repeated
        pieces = [x for x in pieces if key(x) != key(clean)]
    okresy = []
    for x in dict.fromkeys(x for x in pieces if key(x)):
        kind, ids = resolve_okres(x, None, None, g, fuzzy=False)
        if kind in ("czech", "later"):
            ids = set(ids) | (set(PRAGUE_AGGLOMERATION) if PRAHA_OKRES_ID in ids else set())
            okresy.append((x, frozenset(ids), None))
        elif kind == "timeline":
            okresy.append((x, frozenset(), ids))
    if len({(o, t) for _x, o, t in okresy}) < 2:
        return None, None, ()
    names = written_names(m, clean)
    held = []
    for x, ids, tok in okresy:
        toks = {nospace(n) for o in ids for n in g.okres_names.get(o, ())} | ({tok} if tok else set())
        sids = {sid for k in names for sid in _czech_1910(g.global_any.get(k, ()), g)
                if _okres_any(sid, g) in ids or g.timeline.get(sid, set()) & toks}
        if sids:
            held.append((ids, frozenset(sids)))
    # two okresy holding **different** settlements: Vrané nad Vltavou under *Zbraslav, Praha-venkov* is one
    if len(held) < 2 or len({s for _ids, s in held}) < 2 or len(set().union(*(s for _i, s in held))) < 2:
        return None, None, ()
    if common and _on("G2") and not ({key(x) for x, _ids, _tok in okresy} & names):
        # 0.10.0 (G2): exactly one settlement every okres piece holding the name holds — the place the
        # pieces agree on (*Bohuslavice | Uherské Hradiště (Zlín)*: bohuslavice-u-zlina:1 lies in both); not
        # where an okres piece is itself a name written for the place (*Praha/Brandýs nad Labem* written as both
        # municipality and okres: two places, not two okresy)
        common = frozenset.intersection(*(s for _i, s in held))
        if len(common) == 1:
            return None, "okres_alternative_common", tuple(common)
    return "okres_from_name_ambiguous", "okres_alternative_string", tuple(sorted(set().union(*(i for i, _s in held))))

def okres_common_switch(r: dict, m, s, stated_id, g: Gazetteer) -> dict:
    """G2 (0.10.0): where the okres pieces of the string agree on one settlement (:func:`okres_string_alternatives`,
    ``okres_alternative_common``) other than the link, the link moves to it as P4 moves one — only when the
    stated okres lies in its ``okres_all`` timeline (:func:`move_allowed`), tier ``p4_okres_timeline``
    (legion *Žďár* | *Police nad Metují, Náchod*: ``zdar-nad-metuji:1`` of 1910 Broumov, which both pieces hold,
    not Náchod's ``zdar:9``); else *r* unchanged."""
    _ref, why, ids = okres_string_alternatives(m, s, r["clean"], g)
    if why != "okres_alternative_common" or not ids or ids[0] == r["sid"] or stated_id is None:
        return r
    common = ids[0]
    o2 = _okres_any(common, g)
    if o2 is None or o2 == stated_id or not move_allowed(common, s, stated_id, g):
        return r
    return {**r, "sid": common, "tier": "p4_okres_timeline", "okres_1910": o2, "tie": None, "candidates": None}

def written_names(m, clean) -> set:
    """E6 (0.9.0): the names a record writes for its birthplace — the matched name *clean*, the alternates and
    the ``/`` / ``?`` pieces of the municipality string *m* (keys)."""
    names = {key(clean)} if clean else set()
    if isinstance(m, str):
        c, alts = clean_birthplace(m)
        names |= {key(a) for a in (c, *alts) if a}
        names |= {key(x) for x in re.split(r"[/?]+", m) if key(x)}
    names.discard("")
    return names

def home_names_link_or_parent(home, m, clean, sid, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """G2 (0.10.0): the soldier's home municipality is the link *sid*'s 1910 parent (legion *Záluží* | *Český
    Krumlov, České Budějovice*, home *Slavče*: ``zaluzi:3``, osada of Slavče), or a name of the link that is not
    a name the record writes for the birthplace (:func:`written_names`) — a home that repeats the birthplace
    (*Stěžery? Žižkov?*, home *Stěžery*) is no evidence of which okres."""
    hm = (tuple(home or ()) + (None,))[0]
    hname = clean_birthplace(str(hm).split(",")[0])[0] if isinstance(hm, str) else None
    if not hname or sid is None:
        return False
    hk = nospace(key(hname))
    parents = {nospace(p) for p in re.split(r"\s+t\s+", g.parent_key.get(sid) or "") if p.strip()}
    if hk in parents:
        return True
    return (hk in (_name_forms(sid, g) | g.forms_1910.get(sid, set()))
            and hk not in {nospace(n) for n in written_names(m, clean)})

def alternate_home_head(r: dict, s, home, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """E6 (0.9.0): a link read off an alternate name (tier ``p2_alternate``) under a doubted okres string
    (a ``?``) while the soldier's home okres — another okres than the link's — holds the written name
    exactly (legion *Nové Dvory (Nový Dvůr?)*, okres *? Písek?* → ``novy-dvur:20``, home okres Kutná Hora
    holding ``nove-dvory:7``)."""
    if r.get("tier") != "p2_alternate" or not isinstance(s, str) or "?" not in s or not r.get("clean"):
        return False
    ho = (tuple(home or ()) + (None, None))[1]
    if ho is None or int(ho) == _okres_any(r["sid"], g):
        return False
    return bool(g.okres_keys.get(int(ho), {}).get(key(r["clean"])))

def okres_source(stated_id, inferred, string_rule, how) -> str | None:
    """E10 (0.9.0, a diagnostic): where the okres the match ran in came from — ``records_geo`` (a written
    okres records_geo resolved), ``records_geo_name`` (records_geo inferred it from the name), or for an
    okres string records_geo left unresolved ``string_<how>`` (``exact`` / ``alias`` / ``later`` /
    ``hyphen`` / ``fuzzy``), ``timeline`` (E9) or ``name`` (inferred from the name, D-a); ``None`` without
    an okres."""
    if stated_id is not None:
        return "records_geo_name" if inferred else "records_geo"
    if string_rule == "string":
        return f"string_{how or 'exact'}"
    return string_rule

def link_one(tup: tuple, g: Gazetteer, accept_prague_later_okres: bool=ACCEPT_PRAGUE_LATER_OKRES) -> dict

One distinct input (municipality, okres_id, okres, german, vua_uncertain[, okres_inferred, german_forms, candidates, raw, home × 6, regiment, okres_unresolved (0 / 1 field / 2 VÚA cell)]) → its result.

The match, the first-candidate rule (ambiguous:vua_candidates, vua_candidate_rule), the okres-correction rule, the P3 refusals (P3_REFUSED_RULES; a tie-break inside the accepted later-okres block: P3_LATER_TIE_REFUSAL), the okres-inferred rule (okres_from_name_ambiguous / okres_from_name_conflict, okres_inferred_refusal) and the roll-up. Every refusal (match, P3 rule, inferred okres or roll-up) empties the link: sid → None with the candidate in refused_sid, the okres back to the stated one, no correction rule, no register row key, no owner flag and no uncertainty component (0.4.0; 0.5.0 pool_tie_break and the silent candidates as well). 0.7.0: the tuple carries the raw text for a candidate reading too (its head, head_verdict) and the home's land, county, járás and okres string (home_foreign); refusal_detail / refusal_okres_ids say which sub-rule refused (diagnostics).

0.8.0: the soldier's regiment region (A6, regiment_region) reaches the candidate and the inferred-okres rules; a record whose okres string records_geo left unresolved (okres_unresolved) goes through unresolved_okres_link first (D-a, F6); a stated okres with parenthetical alternatives through stated_okres_alternatives (D-a, F5); the first-candidate refusal is named by candidate_refusal (D-g, A6).

0.9.0: the tuple ends with the regiment's recruiting area (E2, regiment_area). E1 — a match through an unresolved okres string that does not link returns no okres: the row keeps okres_1910 empty (so no census key from A2) and its refusal (unmatched, ambiguous:*, no_municipality_1910 … — or 0.7.0's when the plain match reads more), the okres the string gave only in refusal_okres_ids; E3 — in a VÚA cell, a reading that is not the written head under 2+ candidates with a ? is refused ambiguous:vua_candidates (the as-is twin of the first-candidate rule); E6 — an okres string naming 2+ okresy that each hold the name (okres_string_alternatives) or an alternate under a doubted okres the home okres contradicts (alternate_home_head) refuses okres_from_name_ambiguous; E10 — okres_fuzzy (a close-spelling okres string) and the diagnostic okres_source.

0.10.0: the tuple ends with the E11 flag (G4: the candidates are separate parentheses). G2 — E6's okres pieces agreeing on one settlement link it (okres_common_switch), and a home that is the link or its 1910 parent outweighs E6; G4 — a home cell naming the first separate-parenthesis reading keeps the link; G6 — E5 keeps the German okres town VÚA itself read (okres_town_read); G7 — on the stated-okres path a reading that is not the written head under 2+ ? candidates goes through the first-candidate rule with the cell's own candidates (raw_candidates; detail reading_not_head+…).

0.11.0: H3 — where E6's okres pieces agree on a settlement that is not the link (after okres_common_switch), E6's refusal okres_from_name_ambiguous stands (detail okres_alternative_string).

0.12.0: the tuple ends with a qualified name's home municipality (I2, read by p2_qualifier through home_muni_in_okres only); I1 is match_birthplace's (qmark_readings).

def link_one(tup: tuple, g: Gazetteer, accept_prague_later_okres: bool = ACCEPT_PRAGUE_LATER_OKRES) -> dict:
    """One distinct input ``(municipality, okres_id, okres, german, vua_uncertain[, okres_inferred,
    german_forms, candidates, raw, home × 6, regiment, okres_unresolved (0 / 1 field / 2 VÚA cell)])`` →
    its result.

    The match, the first-candidate rule (``ambiguous:vua_candidates``, :func:`vua_candidate_rule`),
    the okres-correction rule, the P3 refusals (:data:`P3_REFUSED_RULES`; a tie-break inside the
    accepted later-okres block: :data:`P3_LATER_TIE_REFUSAL`), the okres-inferred rule
    (``okres_from_name_ambiguous`` / ``okres_from_name_conflict``, :func:`okres_inferred_refusal`)
    and the roll-up. Every refusal (match, P3 rule, inferred okres or roll-up) empties the link:
    ``sid`` → ``None`` with the candidate in ``refused_sid``, the okres back to the stated one, no
    correction rule, no register row key, no owner flag and no uncertainty component (0.4.0; 0.5.0
    ``pool_tie_break`` and the silent candidates as well). 0.7.0: the tuple carries the raw text for
    a candidate reading too (its head, :func:`head_verdict`) and the home's land, county, járás and
    okres string (:func:`home_foreign`); ``refusal_detail`` / ``refusal_okres_ids`` say which
    sub-rule refused (``diagnostics``).

    0.8.0: the soldier's regiment region (A6, :func:`regiment_region`) reaches the candidate and the
    inferred-okres rules; a record whose okres string records_geo left unresolved (*okres_unresolved*)
    goes through :func:`unresolved_okres_link` first (D-a, F6); a stated okres with parenthetical
    alternatives through :func:`stated_okres_alternatives` (D-a, F5); the first-candidate refusal is
    named by :func:`candidate_refusal` (D-g, A6).

    0.9.0: the tuple ends with the regiment's recruiting area (E2, :func:`regiment_area`). E1 — a match
    through an unresolved okres string that does not link returns no okres: the row keeps
    ``okres_1910`` empty (so no census key from A2) and its refusal (``unmatched``, ``ambiguous:*``,
    ``no_municipality_1910`` … — or 0.7.0's when the plain match reads more), the okres the string gave
    only in ``refusal_okres_ids``; E3 — in a VÚA cell, a reading that is not the written head under 2+
    candidates with a ``?`` is refused ``ambiguous:vua_candidates`` (the as-is twin of the first-candidate
    rule); E6 — an okres string naming 2+ okresy that each hold the name (:func:`okres_string_alternatives`)
    or an alternate under a doubted okres the home okres contradicts (:func:`alternate_home_head`) refuses
    ``okres_from_name_ambiguous``; E10 — ``okres_fuzzy`` (a close-spelling okres string) and the
    diagnostic ``okres_source``.

    0.10.0: the tuple ends with the E11 flag (G4: the candidates are separate parentheses). G2 — E6's okres
    pieces agreeing on one settlement link it (:func:`okres_common_switch`), and a home that is the link or its
    1910 parent outweighs E6; G4 — a home cell naming the first separate-parenthesis reading keeps the link; G6 —
    E5 keeps the German okres town VÚA itself read (:func:`okres_town_read`); G7 — on the stated-okres path a
    reading that is not the written head under 2+ ``?`` candidates goes through the first-candidate rule with the
    cell's own candidates (:func:`raw_candidates`; detail ``reading_not_head+…``).

    0.11.0: H3 — where E6's okres pieces agree on a settlement that is not the link (after
    :func:`okres_common_switch`), E6's refusal ``okres_from_name_ambiguous`` stands (detail
    ``okres_alternative_string``).

    0.12.0: the tuple ends with a qualified name's home municipality (I2, read by :func:`p2_qualifier` through
    :func:`home_muni_in_okres` only); I1 is :func:`match_birthplace`'s (:func:`qmark_readings`)."""
    m, o, s, ger, unc, *rest = tup
    inferred, gforms, cands, raw, *more = (list(rest) + [False, None, None, None] + [None] * 12)[:16]
    home_vals, regiment, unresolved, area, vua = more[:6], more[6], more[7] or 0, more[8], bool(more[9])
    separate = bool(more[10])          # 0.10.0 (G4): the candidates are E11's separate parentheses
    home_q = more[11]                  # 0.12.0 (I2): a qualified name's home municipality (p2_qualifier only)
    stated_id = int(o) if o is not None else None
    match_home = (home_q,) if home_q else tuple(home_vals)    # what p2_qualifier's home exceptions read
    r, string_rule, failed, failed_why = None, None, None, None
    if unresolved and stated_id is None and _on("Da6"):
        r, string_rule = unresolved_okres_link(m, s, ger, bool(unc), raw, g, gforms, home_land=home_vals[2],
                                               vua_cell=unresolved == 2, home=match_home)
        if r is not None and r["sid"] is None and _on("E1"):
            failed, failed_why, r, string_rule = r, f"okres_{string_rule}_unlinked", None, None
        elif (r is not None and _on("E3") and unresolved == 2 and not cands and reading_not_head(m, raw)
              and qmark_candidates(raw) >= 2):
            failed = {**r, "sid": None, "tier": "vua_candidates", "refusal": "ambiguous:vua_candidates",
                      "candidates": (r["sid"],), "tie": None}
            failed_why, r, string_rule = "reading_not_head", None, None
        inferred = bool(inferred) or string_rule == "name"
    if r is None:
        keep_town = _on("G6") and vua and okres_town_read(raw, o, g)
        r = match_birthplace(m, o, s, ger, bool(unc), g, german_forms=gforms, vua=vua, keep_okres_town=keep_town,
                             home=match_home, stated=stated_id is not None)   # 0.13.0 (J4): I1 on a stated okres only
        if failed is not None and (r["sid"] is None or failed_why == "reading_not_head"):
            # E1/E3: the D-a refusal stands with no okres; the okres the string gave is a diagnostic
            failed_ids = failed.get("okres_ids") or ((failed["okres_1910"],) if failed["okres_1910"] else ())
            r = {**failed, "okres_1910": None, "okres_ids": tuple(failed_ids)}
    reading_off_head = False
    if (_on("G7") and vua and stated_id is not None and string_rule is None and failed is None and not cands
            and r["sid"] is not None and raw and reading_not_head(m, raw) and qmark_candidates(raw) >= 2):
        # 0.10.0 (G7): E3 on the stated-okres path — a reading that is not the written head, under 2+ candidates
        # with a '?', is VÚA's pick among them: the first-candidate rule reads the cell's candidates against it
        cands, reading_off_head = raw_candidates(raw), True
    # the okres the match ran in: the stated one, or (D-a) the one the string or the name gave
    match_oid = stated_id if stated_id is not None else (r["okres_1910"] if string_rule else None)
    r["parallel"] = praha_parallel(m, s) is not None
    silent, against = (), ()
    detail, written = (failed_why, r.get("okres_ids", ())) if failed is not None and r["sid"] is None else (None, ())
    if cands and r["sid"] is not None:
        # 0.5.0 (D1): refused only on a candidate giving another settlement (or ambiguous)
        refused_ids, silent, against = vua_candidate_rule(r["sid"], cands, s, stated_id, g, main=(m, s),
                                                          match_home=match_home,
                                                          head=head_text(raw), regiment=regiment, area=area,
                                                          home=tuple(home_vals))
        if (refused_ids is not None and ((separate and _on("G4")) or reading_off_head)
                and home_names_only_link(tuple(home_vals), head_text(raw), r["sid"], refused_ids, g)):
            # 0.10.0 (G4, G7): readings in separate parentheses, or VÚA's pick off the head, and the home cell (not a
            # copy of the head) names the first reading's settlement or okres and no other candidate's — E2's test
            refused_ids, against = None, ()
        if refused_ids is not None:
            r.update(sid=None, tier="vua_candidates", refusal=candidate_refusal(against),
                     candidates=refused_ids, okres_1910=stated_id, tie=None)
            silent = ()
            detail = "+".join(("reading_not_head",) * reading_off_head + tuple(against))
    if r["sid"] is not None and _on("E6") and _on("G2"):
        r = okres_common_switch(r, m, s, stated_id, g)
    moved = r["sid"] is not None and stated_id is not None and r["okres_1910"] not in (None, stated_id)
    rule = correction_rule(r["sid"], r["tier"], s, stated_id, g) if moved else None
    refusal = P3_REFUSED_RULES.get(rule)
    if rule == "p3_prague_later_okres" and accept_prague_later_okres:
        refusal = P3_LATER_TIE_REFUSAL if r["tie"] else None
    if refusal is None and not inferred and r["sid"] is not None and raw and _on("Da5"):
        refusal, why, written = stated_okres_alternatives(raw, r["clean"], r["sid"], g)
        detail = why if refusal else detail
    if refusal is None and r["sid"] is not None and _on("E6"):    # 0.9.0 (E6): any okres string, D-a's too
        refusal, why, ids6 = okres_string_alternatives(m, s, r["clean"], g)
        if _on("H3") and why == "okres_alternative_common" and ids6 and ids6[0] != r["sid"]:
            # 0.11.0 (H3): the pieces agree on a settlement okres_common_switch did not move the link to (the
            # stated okres holds another namesake, or is not in its timeline): E6's refusal stands
            refusal, why, ids6 = okres_string_alternatives(m, s, r["clean"], g, common=False)
        if refusal and _on("G2") and home_names_link_or_parent(home_vals, m, r["clean"], r["sid"], g):
            refusal = None             # 0.10.0 (G2): the home municipality is the link or its 1910 parent
        if refusal is None and alternate_home_head(r, s, home_vals, g):
            refusal, why, ids6 = "okres_from_name_ambiguous", "alternate_home_head", (int(home_vals[1]),)
        if refusal:
            detail, written = why, ids6
    if refusal is None and inferred and r["sid"] is not None:
        # 0.5.0 (D2); 0.6.0 (T2): the raw text and the home place; 0.7.0 (F3): the home's land
        home = tuple(home_vals) if any(v is not None for v in home_vals) else None
        refusal, why, written = okres_inferred_verdict(r["clean"], r["sid"], match_oid, g, raw=raw, home=home,
                                                       tier=r["tier"], regiment=regiment, area=area)
        detail = why if refusal else None
    roll = roll_up(None if refusal else r["sid"], r["okres_1910"], g, r["name_keys"])
    refusal = refusal or roll["rollup_refusal"]
    res = {**r, **roll, "correction_rule": rule, "refused_sid": None,
           "refusal_detail": detail, "refusal_okres_ids": tuple(written or ()),
           "okres_inferred": bool(inferred) and r["sid"] is not None,
           "obec_over_part": obec_over_part(r["sid"], r["tier"], r["clean"], match_oid, g),
           # 0.5.0 (D4c): a Prague pool preference chose among several ring settlements of the name
           # (Záběhlice, Podbaba, Sedlec); 0.6.0 (T4): at tier p3_prague_suburb whether or not the okres
           # moved (VÚA as-is writes no okres), outside the later-okres block (refused there); a quarter
           # (p3_prague_quarter: the Libeň trap, an earlier ruling) is not flagged
           "pool_tie_break": (r["sid"] is not None and bool(r["tie"]) and r["tier"] == "p3_prague_suburb"
                              and rule != "p3_prague_later_okres"),
           # 0.5.0 (D1): candidates that gave nothing (the link keeps vua_uncertain); the kinds that refused
           "vua_candidates_silent": silent if r["sid"] is not None else (),
           "vua_candidates_against": against, "stated_id": stated_id,
           # 0.8.0 (D-a): how an unresolved okres string was read (string / name), else None
           "okres_string_rule": string_rule,
           # 0.9.0 (E10): the link's okres came from an unresolved string by a close spelling
           "okres_fuzzy": (_on("E10") and r["sid"] is not None and string_rule == "string"
                           and r.get("okres_how") == "fuzzy"),
           "okres_source": okres_source(stated_id, inferred, string_rule, r.get("okres_how"))}
    if refusal:          # only reached with a matched sid: a match refusal has sid None already
        res = _refuse(res, refusal, stated_id)
    in_reg, differs, reg_key = register_join(res["municipality_settlement_id"], res["register_key"], g)
    res.update(in_register=in_reg, owner_differs=differs, register_key=reg_key)
    return res

def vua_candidate_counts(res: pd.DataFrame, linked: pd.Series, scope: pd.Series | None = None) -> dict:
    """D1's record counts (0.5.0): links read off VÚA's first candidate with silent candidates, by
    reason (a record counted once per reason it shows), and the ``ambiguous:vua_candidates``
    refusals by what refused them. Since 0.6.0 on *scope* (:func:`coverage`'s, so the refusal count
    equals the headline's), the refusals on every row in ``refused_all_rows``."""
    in_scope = scope.to_numpy() if scope is not None else [True] * len(res)
    lk = linked.to_numpy() & in_scope
    silent = [s for s, k in zip(res["vua_candidates_silent"], lk) if k and s]
    # 0.8.0: the first-candidate rule's own values too (D-g vua_head_conflict, A6 vua_regiment_conflict)
    refused_all = res["refusal"].isin(CANDIDATE_REFUSALS).fillna(False).to_numpy()
    refused = refused_all & in_scope
    against = ["+".join(a) or "?" for a, f in zip(res["vua_candidates_against"], refused) if f]
    by_reason: dict[str, int] = {}
    for s in silent:
        for why in set(s):
            by_reason[why] = by_reason.get(why, 0) + 1
    by_against: dict[str, int] = {}
    for a in against:
        by_against[a] = by_against.get(a, 0) + 1
    return {"linked_with_silent_candidates": len(silent), "silent_reason": dict(sorted(by_reason.items())),
            "refused": int(refused.sum()), "refused_by": dict(sorted(by_against.items())),
            "refused_all_rows": int(refused_all.sum())}

def today_keyed_pick(settlements: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
    """``{(norm name, okres_id): settlement_id}`` exactly as :func:`records_geo.add_settlement_attrs`
    picks it (attribute-collapsing :func:`records_geo._pick_homonym`), refused keys left out."""
    have = [c for c in _TODAY_FIELDS if c in settlements.columns]
    cands: dict = {}
    for r in settlements.itertuples(index=False):
        rd = r._asdict()
        if pd.isna(rd.get("okres_id")):
            continue
        rec = {c: rd.get(c) for c in have}
        for nm in (rd.get("cs_name"), rd.get("name_1910"), rd.get("de_name")):
            k = _norm(nm)
            if k:
                cands.setdefault((k, int(rd["okres_id"])), {})[rd["settlement_id"]] = (
                    rec, str(rd.get("status_1910") or ""))
    out = {}
    for k, found in cands.items():
        pairs = list(found.values())
        pick = _pick_homonym(pairs)
        if pick is not None:
            out[k] = next(sid for sid, (rec, _st) in found.items() if rec is pick)
    return out

def compare_with_today(df: pd.DataFrame, keyed: dict, g: Gazetteer, prefix: str = "birth") -> dict:
    """Agreement of ``{prefix}_settlement_id`` with today's ``(municipality, okres_id)`` pick."""
    today = pd.Series([keyed.get((_norm(m), int(o))) if isinstance(m, str) and pd.notna(o) else None
                       for m, o in zip(df[f"{prefix}_municipality"], df[f"{prefix}_okres_id"])],
                      index=df.index, dtype="object")
    mine = df[f"{prefix}_settlement_id"].astype(object).where(df[f"{prefix}_settlement_id"].notna(), None)
    both = today.notna() & mine.notna()
    agree = both & (today == mine)
    name_ok = None
    if f"{prefix}_municipality_cs" in df.columns:
        tn = today[today.notna()].map(lambda s: _titlecase_cs(g.cs_name.get(s)))
        name_ok = float((tn == df.loc[tn.index, f"{prefix}_municipality_cs"]).mean()) if len(tn) else None
    dis = df[both & ~agree]
    pairs = (pd.DataFrame({"municipality": dis[f"{prefix}_municipality"], "today": today[dis.index],
                           "now": mine[dis.index], "tier": dis[f"{prefix}_settlement_match"]})
             .value_counts().head(25))
    sub = lambda mask, col: {str(k): int(v) for k, v in df.loc[mask, col].value_counts().items()}
    return {"today_linked": int(today.notna().sum()), "now_linked": int(mine.notna().sum()),
            "both": int(both.sum()), "agree": int(agree.sum()), "disagree": int((both & ~agree).sum()),
            "today_only": int((today.notna() & mine.isna()).sum()),
            "today_only_by_refusal": sub(today.notna() & mine.isna(), f"{prefix}_link_refusal"),
            "now_only": int((today.isna() & mine.notna()).sum()),
            "now_only_by_tier": sub(today.isna() & mine.notna(), f"{prefix}_settlement_match"),
            "replication_name_agreement": name_ok,
            "disagreements_by_tier": sub(both & ~agree, f"{prefix}_settlement_match"),
            "top_disagreements": [{**dict(zip(pairs.index.names, k)), "n": int(n)} for k, n in pairs.items()]}

def parse_vua_raw(raw: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """``vua_id`` + the ``birth_*`` parse columns of :mod:`utils.parsing.locations` (1.2.x) from the
    raw ``Místo narození``, cleaned as notebook 02 cleans it (placeholders, ``+`` markers)."""

def reparse_vua_births(habs: pd.DataFrame, parsed: pd.DataFrame, districts: pd.DataFrame,
                       settlements: pd.DataFrame, exclude_names: set | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """``habsburg_clean`` with every ``birth_*`` place column rebuilt from *parsed* through
    :func:`records_geo.add_place_standardization` and :func:`records_geo.resolve_prague_suburbs`
    — notebook 02 §4 for the birth role, Czech lands only (the Slovak passes fill no Czech okres).

    Since 0.2.0 this runs on records_geo 1.9.1 as notebook 02 does: no ``to_numpy`` patch, and the
    suburb-moved rows are re-keyed against *settlements* (``birth_municipality_cs`` and the other
    attributes), which is what the replication check against today's pick reads."""
    from utils.parsing import records_geo as rg
    drop = [c for c in habs.columns if c.startswith("birth_") and c not in _VUA_KEEP]
    base = habs.drop(columns=drop)
    n = len(base)
    df = base.merge(parsed, on="vua_id", how="left", validate="1:1")
    assert len(df) == n, "re-parse merge changed the row count"
    df = rg.add_place_standardization(df, districts, settlements, prefix="birth",
                                      exclude_names=exclude_names)
    return rg.resolve_prague_suburbs(df, prefix="birth", districts=districts, settlements=settlements)

def p3_moves(moved: pd.DataFrame, g: Gazetteer, prefix: str = "birth") -> dict:
    """P3 okres moves that stand, split by whether the settlement joined Prague in 1922 and whether
    its timeline names a Prague okres, with the settlements of each cell."""
    p = f"{prefix}_"
    m = moved[moved[p + "settlement_match"].fillna("").str.startswith("p3")]
    sids = m[p + "settlement_id"].astype(object)
    gp = sids.isin(g.greater_prague | {PRAHA_SID} | g.quarter_sids)
    named = sids.map(lambda s: any(t.startswith("praha") for t in g.timeline.get(s, set())))
    cells = {}
    for gp_v, named_v in ((True, True), (True, False), (False, True), (False, False)):
        sel = m[(gp == gp_v) & (named == named_v)]
        top = sel[p + "settlement_id"].value_counts().head(25)
        # "gp" counts the 1910 city and its quarters with the 1922 joiners (a move into okres Praha)
        cells[f"gp1922_or_1910_city={gp_v}, prague_named_okres={named_v}"] = {
            "n": int(len(sel)), "settlements": int(sel[p + "settlement_id"].nunique()),
            "top": [f"{s} {g.cs_name.get(s)} ({int(n)})" for s, n in top.items()]}
    return {"p3_moves": int(len(m)), "to_greater_prague_1922": int(gp.sum()),
            "outside_1922_law": int((~gp).sum()), "cells": cells,
            "by_rule": _vc(m, p + "okres_correction_rule")}

def register_reach(scope: pd.DataFrame, g: Gazetteer, prefix: str = "birth", top_n: int = 15) -> dict:
    """Linked births by register reach (0.3.0): reachable (same key), the table holding the
    municipality under **another** key (``register_owner_differs``), the table lacking it (Aš until
    the register hook), no owner key in the gazetteer; and what 0.2.0's set membership said."""
    p = f"{prefix}_"
    linked = scope[scope[p + "link_unit"] != "none"]
    muni = linked[p + "municipality_settlement_id"].astype(object)
    reach = linked[p + "in_register_municipalities"].fillna(False).astype(bool)
    differs = linked[p + "register_owner_differs"].fillna(False).astype(bool)
    in_table = muni.isin(set(g.register_muni_key))
    no_key = linked[p + "register_key"].isna()
    member = muni.isin(g.register_munis)            # 0.2.0's test

    def top(mask):
        vc = muni[mask].value_counts().head(top_n)
        return [f"{s} {g.cs_name.get(s)} ({int(n)}; table {g.register_muni_key.get(s, '-')}, "
                f"owner {linked.loc[mask & (muni == s), p + 'register_key'].iloc[0]})" for s, n in vc.items()]
    return {"linked": int(len(linked)), "reachable": int(reach.sum()),
            "owner_differs": int(differs.sum()), "owner_differs_top": top(differs),
            "table_lacks_municipality": int((~in_table & ~no_key).sum()),
            "table_lacks_top": top(~in_table & ~no_key),
            "no_owner_key": int(no_key.sum()), "no_owner_key_in_table": int((no_key & in_table).sum()),
            "no_owner_key_top": top(no_key & in_table),
            "membership_0_2_0": int(member.sum()),
            "membership_but_not_reachable": int((member & ~reach).sum()),
            "membership_but_not_reachable_top": top(member & ~reach)}

def owner_disjoint_unrefused(scope: pd.DataFrame, g: Gazetteer, prefix: str = "birth") -> dict:
    """Linked births whose settlement shares no name with the register rows holding it but were not
    refused (no other settlement of the okres answers to the printed name): what the literal
    "share no form" refusal would have cost, with the owner rows behind it."""

def uncertainty(scope: pd.DataFrame, prefix: str = "birth") -> dict:
    """Each ``settlement_uncertain`` component apart (0.3.0) and the raw-cell ``?`` (VÚA only, not a
    component), all and linked."""
    p = f"{prefix}_"
    linked = scope[p + "link_unit"] != "none"
    b = lambda c: scope[p + c].fillna(False).astype(bool) if p + c in scope.columns else \
        pd.Series(False, index=scope.index)
    comp = {"settlement_qmark": b("settlement_qmark"),
            "settlement_piece_tier": scope[p + "settlement_piece_tier"].notna(),
            "vua_uncertain": b("vua_uncertain"), "okres_inferred": b("okres_inferred"),
            "obec_over_part": b("obec_over_part"), "pool_tie_break": b("pool_tie_break"),
            "qualifier_fuzzy": b("qualifier_fuzzy"),
            "settlement_uncertain": b("settlement_uncertain"),
            "vua_raw_qmark (not a component)": b("vua_raw_qmark")}
    return {"all": {k: int(v.sum()) for k, v in comp.items()},
            "linked": {k: int((v & linked).sum()) for k, v in comp.items()},
            "piece_tier": _vc(scope, p + "settlement_piece_tier"),
            "vua_raw_qmark_recorded": int(scope[p + "vua_raw_qmark"].notna().sum())}

def coverage(df: pd.DataFrame, okres_cs: dict, prefix: str = "birth", g: Gazetteer | None = None) -> dict:
    """Counts for one dataset/pass: tiers, link units, refusals, okres corrections, Prague, register
    reach, uncertainty.

    The scope is every record with a stated 1910 okres, a linked settlement (Prague strings with no
    okres reach a settlement through P3) or a refused candidate."""
    p = f"{prefix}_"
    scope = df[df[p + "okres_id_stated"].notna() | df[p + "settlement_id"].notna()
               | df[p + "settlement_id_refused"].notna()]
    linked = scope[p + "link_unit"] != "none"
    moved = scope[scope[p + "okres_corrected"].fillna(False).astype(bool)]
    pairs = (pd.DataFrame({"fr": moved[p + "okres_id_stated"].map(lambda o: okres_cs.get(o, str(o))),
                           "to": moved[p + "okres_id_1910"].map(lambda o: okres_cs.get(o, str(o))),
                           "tier": moved[p + "settlement_match"]})
             .value_counts().head(30))
    flag = lambda c: int(scope[p + c].fillna(False).astype(bool).sum())
    owner_mis = scope[p + "settlement_owner_mismatch"].fillna(False).astype(bool)
    ties = scope[linked & scope[p + "settlement_candidates"].notna()]
    return {"records": int(len(df)), "scope": int(len(scope)),
            "okres_corrected_by_rule": _vc(moved, p + "okres_correction_rule"),
            "p3_moves": p3_moves(moved, g, prefix) if g is not None else None,
            "p3_refused": ({r: refused_block(scope, r, g, prefix) for r in P3_REFUSED_RULES.values()}
                           if g is not None else None),
            "prague_pool_tie_breaks": _vc(ties, p + "settlement_id"),
            "owner_mismatch": int(owner_mis.sum()),
            "owner_mismatch_linked": int((owner_mis & linked).sum()),
            "owner_name_conflict": int((scope[p + "link_refusal"] == "owner_name_conflict").sum()),
            "owner_name_conflict_settlements": owner_conflicts(scope, g, prefix) if g is not None else None,
            "owner_disjoint_unrefused": owner_disjoint_unrefused(scope, g, prefix) if g is not None else None,
            "owner_mismatch_by_tier": _vc(scope[owner_mis], p + "settlement_match"),
            "uncertainty": uncertainty(scope, prefix),
            # 0.5.0 (D1): the first-candidate rule's counts (whole frame; the rule needs a VÚA list)
            "vua_candidate_rule": df.attrs.get("vua_candidate_rule"),
            "prague_quarter_filled_from_locations": int(df.attrs.get("prague_quarter_filled", 0)),
            "prague_quarter_disagree_with_locations": int(df.attrs.get("prague_quarter_disagree", 0)),
            "settlement_linked": int(scope[p + "settlement_id"].notna().sum()),
            "settlement_refused_with_candidate": int(scope[p + "settlement_id_refused"].notna().sum()),
            "linked_unit": int(linked.sum()), "link_unit": _vc(scope, p + "link_unit"),
            "tier": _vc(scope, p + "settlement_match", dropna=False),
            "linked_by_tier": _vc(scope[linked], p + "settlement_match", dropna=False),
            "municipality_source": _vc(scope, p + "municipality_source"),
            "court_source": _vc(scope, p + "court_source"),
            "in_register_municipalities": flag("in_register_municipalities"),
            "register_reach": register_reach(scope, g, prefix) if g is not None else None,
            "refusal": _vc(scope, p + "link_refusal"),

def rulings_queue(frames: dict, g: Gazetteer, okres_cs: dict, min_soldiers: int = 5,
                  prefix: str = "birth") -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Strings written the same way by ``>= min_soldiers`` soldiers that stay refused, ambiguous or
    unmatched: one row per ``(municipality, stated okres, okres_id)`` with counts and candidates.
    Since 0.3.0 also every Prague pool tie-break (``status = tie_break``, any count: Sedlec, Lipany)."""
    p = f"{prefix}_"
    parts = []
    for name, df in frames.items():
        ref = df[p + "link_refusal"].fillna("")
        refused = ((df[p + "link_unit"] == "none") & (ref != "")
                   & (df[p + "okres_id_stated"].notna() | ref.str.startswith("praha")))
        # a Prague pool tie-break, linked or refused later (Lipany, okres Praha: lipany:3 chosen
        # over lipany:2, then refused prague_later_okres_only) — listed at any count
        tie = (df[p + "settlement_candidates"].notna() & df[p + "settlement_match"].fillna("").str.startswith("p3")
               & ~ref.str.startswith("ambiguous"))
        sub = df[refused | tie]
        parts.append(pd.DataFrame({"dataset": name, "municipality": sub[p + "municipality"],
                                   "okres_stated": sub[p + "okres"], "okres_id": sub[p + "okres_id_stated"],
                                   "clean": sub[p + "settlement_clean"],
                                   "refusal": sub[p + "link_refusal"].fillna("tie_break"),
                                   "candidates": sub[p + "settlement_candidates"],
                                   "tie": tie[sub.index].to_numpy(),
                                   "settlement_id": sub[p + "settlement_id"].fillna(sub[p + "settlement_id_refused"])}))
    long = pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True)
    keys = ["municipality", "okres_stated", "okres_id"]
    long[keys] = long[keys].astype(object).where(long[keys].notna(), "")
    agg = (long.groupby(keys).agg(
        n=("dataset", "size"), n_legion=("dataset", lambda s: int((s == "legion").sum())),
        n_vua=("dataset", lambda s: int((s == "vua").sum())), clean=("clean", "first"),
        refusal=("refusal", lambda s: s.value_counts().index[0]),
        candidates=("candidates", "first"), settlement_id=("settlement_id", "first"),
        pool_tie_break=("tie", "any")).reset_index())
    agg = agg[(agg["n"] >= min_soldiers) | agg["pool_tie_break"]].sort_values("n", ascending=False)
    agg.insert(3, "okres_cs", agg["okres_id"].map(lambda o: okres_cs.get(o, "") if o != "" else ""))
    agg["status"] = agg["refusal"].map(lambda r: "ambiguous" if r.startswith("ambiguous")
                                       else "unmatched" if r == "unmatched"
                                       else "tie_break" if r == "tie_break" else "refused")
    agg["candidate_detail"] = [_queue_candidates(r, g, okres_cs) for r in agg.itertuples(index=False)]
    agg["register_rows"] = [_register_prefix_rows(r, g) for r in agg.itertuples(index=False)]
    agg["why"] = agg["refusal"].map(lambda r: _WHY.get(r, "D-144: several settlements, not exactly one "
                                                          "obec, answer to this name at tier "
                                                          + r.split(":")[-1]))
    return agg.reset_index(drop=True)

def queue_blocks(frames: dict, g: Gazetteer, okres_cs: dict, adjacency: dict | None = None,
                 prefix: str = "birth") -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The rulings queue's blocks (0.7.0, A3), at any count, each row a string with its record ids:

    * ``conflict_unique`` — every ``okres_from_name_conflict_unique`` refusal, one row per
      (municipality, written okres): the settlement's 1910 okres, the okres the cell names and
      ``okres_borders`` — True where the MPIDR outlines of the two okresy touch (*adjacency*,
      :meth:`utils.recheck.anchor_overrides.Courts.okres_adjacency`; a column for the author's
      decision, not a decision; ``<NA>`` without polygons);
    * (``conservative``, 0.7.0–0.9.0: a fixed id list; dropped in 0.10.0, F9 — a block lists only rows refused now);
    * ``home_name_conflict`` (0.9.0, E12) — every D-h refusal, one row per (raw cell, refused settlement),
      with its ``shape`` (:func:`home_name_shape`) for the author's ruling on the coin flips.

    Needs the frames built with ``diagnostics=True`` (``{prefix}_refusal_okres_ids``)."""
    p = f"{prefix}_"
    rows = []
    for name, df in frames.items():
        idc = "legion_id" if "legion_id" in df.columns else "vua_id"
        written = df[p + "refusal_okres_ids"] if p + "refusal_okres_ids" in df.columns else pd.Series(pd.NA, index=df.index)
        sel = df[df[p + "link_refusal"].eq("okres_from_name_conflict_unique").fillna(False)]
        for (muni, wr), grp in sel.groupby([sel[p + "municipality"].astype(str), written[sel.index].fillna("")]):
            sid = grp[p + "settlement_id_refused"].iloc[0]
            so = _okres_any(sid, g)
            w_ids = [int(x) for x in str(wr).split("|") if x]
            borders = (pd.NA if adjacency is None or so is None or not w_ids
                       else bool(any(w in adjacency.get(int(so), set()) for w in w_ids)))
            rows.append({"block": "conflict_unique", "dataset": name, "municipality": muni,
                         "clean": grp[p + "settlement_clean"].iloc[0], "refusal": "okres_from_name_conflict_unique",
                         "settlement_id": sid, "settlement_okres": okres_cs.get(so, ""),
                         "written_okres": "; ".join(okres_cs.get(w, str(w)) for w in w_ids),
                         "written_okres_ids": wr, "okres_borders": borders, "n": len(grp),
                         "raw": "; ".join(dict.fromkeys(str(x) for x in grp.get(p + "raw", grp[p + "municipality"]))),
                         "ids": "|".join(str(int(i)) for i in grp[idc]),
                         "why": _WHY["okres_from_name_conflict_unique"]})
        if idc == "vua_id" and _on("E12"):
            rows += home_name_block(df, name, okres_cs, prefix)
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    for c in ("settlement_id", "candidates"):
        if c in out.columns:
            out[c] = out[c].astype(object).where(out[c].notna(), "")
    return out

def home_name_shape(raw, home_m, detail, reading=None) -> str:
    """E12 (0.9.0): what kind of D-h refusal a row is — ``second_candidate`` (VÚA read the place off a
    later candidate than the first: *Smíchov ? (Praha XVI.-Smíchov …; Švihov, okres Podbořany ?)*),
    ``okres_guessed`` (the author's open question: the home okres inferred by records_geo from a home cell
    that copies the written head, and VÚA's reading marked ``?``: *Turov, Tábor ? (Turovec, okres Tábor
    ?)*, home *Turov*), else ``other`` (a written home okres, or a home that is not the head)."""
    from utils.parsing import locations as loc
    head = head_text(raw)
    hname = clean_birthplace(re.split(r"[,;]", head)[0])[0] if head else None
    mname = clean_birthplace(str(home_m).split(",")[0])[0] if isinstance(home_m, str) else None
    cands = loc.candidate_readings(raw, with_text=True) if isinstance(raw, str) and "(" in raw else None
    if (cands and len(cands) >= 2 and isinstance(reading, str) and isinstance(cands[0][0], str)
            and key(cands[0][0]) != key(reading)):
        return "second_candidate"
    if (hname and mname and key(hname) == key(mname) and str(detail).endswith("home_okres_inferred")
            and isinstance(raw, str) and "?" in raw):
        return "okres_guessed"
    return "other"

def home_name_block(df: pd.DataFrame, name: str, okres_cs: dict, prefix: str = "birth") -> list[dict]:
    """E12 (0.9.0): the rulings-queue block ``home_name_conflict`` — every D-h refusal of the frame, one

    rows = []
    for (raw, sid), grp in sel.groupby([sel[p + "raw"].astype(str), sel[p + "settlement_id_refused"].astype(str)]):
        d = str(detail[grp.index[0]])
        hm = grp["home_municipality"].iloc[0] if "home_municipality" in grp.columns else None
        rows.append({"block": "home_name_conflict", "dataset": name, "municipality": grp[p + "municipality"].iloc[0],
                     "clean": grp[p + "settlement_clean"].iloc[0], "refusal": "home_name_conflict",
                     "settlement_id": sid, "n": len(grp), "raw": raw,
                     "home_municipality": hm if isinstance(hm, str) else "",
                     "home_okres": "written" if d.endswith("written") else "inferred" if d.endswith("inferred") else "",
                     "shape": home_name_shape(raw, hm, d, grp[p + "municipality"].iloc[0]),
                     "ids": "|".join(str(int(i)) for i in grp["vua_id"]), "why": _WHY["home_name_conflict"]})
    return rows

def register_prefix_rows(k: str, oid, g: Gazetteer, limit: int = 8) -> list[tuple[str, str, object]]:
    """``[(row key, printed name, sid)]`` of the register rows of okres *oid* that print a form
    starting with the word(s) *k* (``Staňkov`` → *Staňkov Městys* ``stankov-i:1``, *Staňkov Ves*
    ``stankov-ii:1``), anchored or not, each row once (0.3.0)."""
    if not k or oid is None or oid == "":
        return []
    seen, out = set(), []
    for form, printed, sid, row_key in g.reg_rows.get(int(oid), ()):
        if (form == k or form.startswith(k + " ")) and row_key not in seen:
            seen.add(row_key)
            out.append((row_key, printed, sid))
    return out[:limit]

def schema_patch(schema_path: Path = ROOT / "utils" / "parsing" / "schema.py") -> str:
    """A unified diff (not applied) adding to ``schema.py``: the ``locations`` 1.2 columns to
    ``HABSBURG_RENAME`` / ``HABSBURG_FINAL`` / ``_DESCRIPTIONS`` (both place roles; the legionnaire
    frame has no ``locations`` columns — csol.cz gives obec and okres as two fields), and the
    birth-settlement columns as a ``_BIRTH_SETTLEMENT`` block documented by
    :func:`schema.write_data_dictionary` for both datasets — they are added in notebook 02 §4 after
    ``to_english`` (they need ``birth_okres_id``), like ``_GEO_DERIVED``, so no ``*_FINAL`` entry.

    Empty once ``schema.py`` carries the block (applied 2026-11-16, ``schema`` 1.14.0); the test then
    checks the applied schema against :data:`SETTLEMENT_DESCRIPTIONS` instead."""
    old = Path(schema_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if "_BIRTH_SETTLEMENT: dict[str, str] = {" in old:
        return ""
    new = old.replace(
        '__version__ = "1.13.0"  # date precision, death_date_raw, note_register_ref, §4 columns documented (audit 2026-09-22)',
        '__version__ = "1.14.0"  # locations 1.2 columns + birth_settlement columns documented (birth_settlement 0.5.0)')
    roles = {"birth": "birth", "home": "home (domicile)"}
    for role, anchor_rename, anchor_final in (
            ("birth", '    "birth_loc_uncertain": "birth_loc_uncertain",\n',
             '    "birth_land", "birth_cisleithanian", "birth_loc_uncertain",\n'),
            ("home", '    "home_cisleithanian": "home_cisleithanian",\n',
             '    "home_municipality", "home_okres", "home_land", "home_cisleithanian",\n')):
        cols = [f"{role}{s}" for s in LOCATIONS_12_DESCRIPTIONS]
        new = _insert_after(new, anchor_rename,
                            f"    # locations.py 1.2 (statutory-city quarter, the VÚA candidate list)\n"
                            + "".join(f'    "{c}": "{c}",\n' for c in cols))
        new = _insert_after(new, anchor_final, "    " + ", ".join(f'"{c}"' for c in cols) + ",\n")
        desc = "".join(f'    "{role}{s}": "{d.format(role=roles[role], prefix=role)}",\n'
                       for s, d in LOCATIONS_12_DESCRIPTIONS.items())
        new = _insert_after(new, '    "home_cisleithanian": "As birth_cisleithanian, for the home (domicile) '
                                 'place — derived from the corrected home_land",\n' if role == "home" else
                            '    "birth_loc_uncertain": "True if birthplace parse was uncertain",\n', desc)
    block = ("\n# Birth-settlement link columns added in notebook §4 by\n"
             "# utils.parsing.birth_settlement.add_birth_settlement_columns (birth role, both datasets),\n"
             "# after records_geo has set birth_okres_id. {role} is substituted per prefix.\n"
             "_BIRTH_SETTLEMENT: dict[str, str] = {\n"
             + "".join(f'    "{s}": "{d}",\n' for s, d in SETTLEMENT_DESCRIPTIONS.items()) + "}\n")
    new = _insert_after(new, '_GEO_PREFIXES = {"birth": "birth", "home": "home (domicile)"}\n', block)
    loop = ('        for suffix, desc in _BIRTH_SETTLEMENT.items():\n'
            '            rows.append({"dataset": ds, "final_name": f"birth{suffix}",\n'
            '                         "source_name": "birth_municipality / birth_okres_id (utils.parsing.birth_settlement)",\n'
            '                         "description": desc.format(role="birth")})\n')
    new = _insert_after(new, '                             "description": desc.format(role=role)})\n'
                             '\n    dd = pd.DataFrame', "")
    new = new.replace('                             "description": desc.format(role=role)})\n'
                      '\n    dd = pd.DataFrame',
                      '                             "description": desc.format(role=role)})\n' + loop
                      + '\n    dd = pd.DataFrame')
    return "".join(difflib.unified_diff(old.splitlines(keepends=True), new.splitlines(keepends=True),
                                        "a/utils/parsing/schema.py", "b/utils/parsing/schema.py"))

def correct_census_okres_id(df: pd.DataFrame, districts: pd.DataFrame, prefix: str='birth') -> pd.DataFrame

T3 (0.6.0): {prefix}_census_okres_id follows the corrected okres. Where {prefix}_okres_corrected is True the key becomes the census unit of {prefix}_okres_id_1910 through the same crosswalk notebook 02 §4 uses (utils.parsing.census.okres_census_crosswalk: the identity, except that both members of a city/rural twin pair point at the rural member, D-17/D-18; a P3 move into a ring okres is the identity, as any other okres); elsewhere it is unchanged. The written key is kept in {prefix}_census_okres_id_stated. {prefix}_okres_id is never changed. Counts go to attrs["census_key"].

0.7.0: A2 (the author) — where {prefix}_okres_id is missing but the link supplies {prefix}_okres_id_1910 (a Prague string with no okres, a later-okres string records_geo could not resolve), the key is that okres's census unit too; the stated key stays missing. F7 — idempotent: the stated key is always the census unit of {prefix}_okres_id (what utils.parsing.census.add_census_okres_id writes), never read back from a key this function may already have corrected, so running notebook 02 §4a twice changes nothing.
