"""birth_settlement.py — every Czech-lands birth to one ČSÚ-lexicon settlement, rolled up to its 1910 municipality
==============================================================================================================
The person files carry a birthplace as text (``birth_municipality``) and a resolved 1910 okres
(``birth_okres_id``, :mod:`utils.parsing.records_geo`). :func:`records_geo.add_settlement_attrs`
already picks a lexicon row per ``(municipality, okres_id)`` but exports only its attributes, never
the ``settlement_id``, and its homonym rule compares *attributes* (two different hamlets with equal
attributes collapse to the first) rather than the D-144 obec-first rule on the set of ids. This
module links each birth to a ``settlement_id`` (``data/final/geo/settlements_1910``, key
``slug:ordinal``, D-148) and to the **1910 municipality** whose institutions the corrected register
holds (``data/final/register_rechecked/register_municipalities``, keyed on ``settlement_id``).

The author's rulings it implements (2026-11-16):

* **the register first, the lexicon second.** The 1910 register prints every municipality and part
  (``register_places``, Czech *and* German form in one cell); its ``settlement_id`` comes from the
  frozen anchoring plus :func:`utils.recheck.anchor_overrides.apply` (Aš, the healed names).
* **D-144 on the set of ids.** A key several settlements answer to: one id → take it; several, of
  which exactly one is an obec (for the register: exactly one is a municipality row) → that one;
  otherwise refused, the candidates kept for the rulings sheet. An ambiguous tier **stops** the
  search — a later, looser tier must not break a tie the stricter one could not.
* **the settlement's 1910 okres wins** over the record's stated okres when the stated okres is in
  the settlement's okres timeline (``okres_all``) — P4, flagged ``birth_okres_corrected`` with the
  stated id kept. Greater Prague (P3) moves a suburb to its own 1910 okres the same way; since 0.3.0
  a P3 move that passes only on a post-1910 ``Praha-venkov/-západ/…`` token, or on the
  agglomeration pool alone, is refused (``prague_later_okres_only`` / ``prague_pool_only``; the
  first can be accepted as a block with ``accept_prague_later_okres=True``).
* **rulings the author has not confirmed do not drive the links** (0.3.0): :func:`load_gazetteer`
  applies only ``ruled_by = author`` rulings unless ``include_unconfirmed=True``; :func:`build`
  writes the confirmed-only links and reports the *with evidence rulings* counts beside them.
* **institutions join at the municipality total, the exact part is kept** (``birth_settlement_id``
  is the part, ``birth_municipality_settlement_id`` the municipality).
* **the register's court is the 1910 court**; the polygon court of ``settlements_1910`` only as a
  flagged fallback (``birth_court_source``).
* **Aš**: a two-letter name; matched like any other here (no length guard), and the register
  anchors it through ``anchor_overrides`` (``as:1``).

Passes, each inside the record's 1910 okres, first match wins, the tier recorded
(``birth_settlement_match``):

======  =================================================================================
P0      clean the string: placeholders → missing; ``též`` alternates, orphan ``)``, ``díl``,
        parentheticals and ``?`` split off as alternates
P1      ``p1_register`` (printed names of the primary edition: ``cz`` for Bohemia,
        ``de-moravia``, ``de-silesia``), then ``p1_lexikon`` (headword / 1910 name / German
        name, healed forms included — :func:`utils.parsing.place_names.name_index`)
P3      Prague (run before P2, so ``Praha-Smíchov`` is never split to ``Praha``):
        ``Praha <Roman>.-X``; quarters I–VIII → their ``praha:1`` part; post-1949 ``Praha 1–10``
        refused; a 1910 suburb (Nusle, Vršovice, …) → its own municipality and okres;
        the Libeň trap (``liben:3`` is a village of okres Vinohrady, Praha VIII Libeň is
        ``liben:2``, a part of ``praha:1``); a name two ring settlements share goes to the one
        that joined Prague in 1922 (the clerk who wrote "Praha" wrote the 1922 city); a 1923
        district number with a name is read by the name (``Praha VIII.-Troja`` is Troja)
P2      variants: alternates and the VÚA German exonym through P1; ``p2_register_alt``
        (the ``de-bohemia`` printed forms); ``p2_nospace``; ``p2_alias`` (ČSÚ ``viz`` alias,
        the target's **1910** okres must equal the record's — ``viz_okres`` is modern);
        ``p2_split`` (``parent-part``: right piece first, the left must be its parent, its
        municipality or the okres seat; else the left piece alone); ``p2_qualifier``
        (``u/nad/pod/na/v/ve/při`` tails stripped on both sides)
P4      ``p4_okres_timeline``: the name is nowhere in the okres, and exactly one settlement of
        that name has the record's stated okres in ``okres_all``
P5      roll-up: register part → its municipality row ``(edition, court_key, muni_seq)``; not in
        the register → the lexicon ``parent_1910`` resolved in the okres; statutory city →
        ``birth_link_unit = statutory_okres``; a settlement two register municipalities hold
        (outside cross-references) is refused
======  =================================================================================

Columns added (prefix ``birth_``): ``settlement_clean``, ``settlement_id``, ``settlement_id_refused``,
``settlement_status``, ``settlement_match``, ``settlement_candidates``, ``municipality_settlement_id``,
``municipality_source`` (``self`` / ``register_part`` / ``lexikon_parent`` / ``statutory_okres``),
``register_row_key``, ``register_key``, ``register_owner_differs``, ``in_register_municipalities``,
``court_id_1910``, ``court_source`` (``register`` / ``polygon``), ``link_unit`` (``municipality`` /
``statutory_okres`` / ``none``), ``link_refusal``, ``okres_id_1910``, ``okres_id_stated``,
``okres_corrected``, ``okres_correction_rule`` (``p4_timeline`` / ``p3_prague_1910_okres`` /
``p3_prague_later_okres``, the block accepted since 0.4.0), ``prague_quarter``,
``greater_prague_1922``, ``settlement_is_okres_name``, ``settlement_qmark``,
``settlement_piece_tier``, ``vua_uncertain``, ``vua_raw_qmark``, ``settlement_owner_mismatch``,
``okres_inferred``, ``obec_over_part`` (0.4.0), ``pool_tie_break`` (0.5.0), ``settlement_uncertain``.

Checks added in 0.2.0:

* **owner sanity** (P5): the register row that owns the matched settlement must print the name the
  record was matched on (``settlement_owner_mismatch`` otherwise); when the settlement's own lexicon
  names and the owner row's printed forms share **no** form *and* the row prints the name of another
  settlement of its okres, the anchor is wrong and the roll-up is refused ``owner_name_conflict``
  (the settlement id is kept, the municipality is not). Disjoint names alone only set the mismatch
  flag: they are mostly German-only cells, 1910 spellings and OCR damage (:func:`owner_check`).
* **Greater Prague 1922 from the settlement only**: a hamlet joins only when its parent, resolved
  *inside the hamlet's own 1910 okres*, is a joiner; the flag reads the settlement, never its
  municipality, so :data:`GREATER_PRAGUE_EXCLUDED` (Háje, Milíčov of Hostivař) stays out.
* **okres corrections carry their rule** (``okres_correction_rule``): ``p4_timeline``; a P3 move to a
  settlement with a Prague-named okres (``Praha …``) or the stated okres in its ``okres_all``
  timeline is ``p3_prague_1910_okres``; one without is ``p3_prague_pool_only`` (the record writer's
  generic *Praha* for the agglomeration; flagged for the author, never dropped here).
* **stated okres outside the agglomeration**: P1 runs there before P3 (``Kyje, Praha`` with okres
  Lomnice nad Popelkou is that okres's Kyje, not Prague's); a P3 reading that would move such a
  record to a ring okres not in the settlement's timeline is refused ``prague_okres_conflict``; a
  Prague city reading with alternates (``Praha? Hrubý Jeseník``) is refused
  ``praha_city_with_alternate``.
* **timeline keys space-free** (the lexicon's ``okres_all`` carries OCR splits: ``usti nad orl ici``).
* ``settlement_uncertain``: the raw string has a ``?``, the match came off an alternate, split or
  qualifier tier, or the VÚA reading was uncertain.

Changes in 0.3.0 (three independent reviews):

* **the register join compares keys, not set membership.** ``register_rechecked/register_municipalities``
  still carries the frozen anchoring, while the gazetteer carries the overrides (and, on request, the
  rulings). ``in_register_municipalities`` is True only where the municipality's row in that table
  has the **same** register key (``edition|court_key|muni_seq``, ``register_key``) as the row that
  owns the link in the gazetteer; ``register_owner_differs`` marks a row that exists under another
  key (0.2.0 counted Kostomlaty's births as reachable through the frozen *Kostomlátky* row). A
  ``register_key`` or ``court_key`` column in the table, once the register hook adds one, is used
  as is (:func:`municipality_keys`).
* **P3 okres moves split** (above); the refused candidate is kept in ``settlement_id_refused``.
* **qualifiers**: ``za`` / ``před`` / ``mezi`` added; a qualified name whose okres holds the same head
  under a *different* qualifier is refused ``qualifier_conflict`` (unless P4 finds the name exactly
  as written), and P4 never strips a qualifier when the stated okres holds that bare head
  (*Lhota u Červeného Kostelce*, okres Náchod, was *Lhota* of okres Nové Město).
* **numbered siblings**: a form without the Roman numeral the register prints for its settlement
  (``Großaupa I, Velká Úpa``) is ambiguous across the numbered siblings the register prints,
  never the first of them (the ČSÚ lexicon's own numerals, *NOVÁ VES I*, do not count).
* **owner check pools** the printed forms of every register row holding the settlement (both
  editions, municipality and part rows; ``Novosady Blatiny`` split into its two names).
* **contradicted rows**: so that pooling does not hide a wrong frozen anchor in one edition, a
  municipality whose rows print none of the settlement's names while another municipality row
  holding it prints one **and** gives another 1910 population no longer holds the settlement in the
  gazetteer (:func:`contradicted_keys`: only the Czech *Kostomlátky* row for
  ``kostomlaty-nad-labem:1`` today); the register join then reports the table's row as differing.
* **Prague pool tie-breaks** (*Sedlec*, *Lipany*, *Libeň*) keep the ids chosen among in
  ``settlement_candidates`` and are listed in the rulings queue at any count.
* ``Praha, X`` with okres ``Praha, Y`` is a parallel two-value list: X is matched in Y as
  ``p2_alternate`` and flagged uncertain, never silently.
* every refusal empties ``settlement_id`` (the candidate goes to ``settlement_id_refused``) and
  leaves the stated okres in place.
* ``settlement_uncertain`` = ``settlement_qmark`` | ``settlement_piece_tier`` | ``vua_uncertain``,
  each also its own column; ``vua_uncertain`` reads ``locations`` 1.2.2 ``candidates_agree_place``
  (candidates naming different places in one okres are uncertain); the VÚA raw cell's ``?``
  (``vua_raw_qmark``) is reported but no longer counted.

Changes in 0.4.0 (the author's decisions of 2026-11-16 and the third review):

* **the later-okres Prague block is accepted** (:data:`ACCEPT_PRAGUE_LATER_OKRES` = True): such a
  record links with its okres moved to the 1910 ring okres and ``okres_correction_rule =
  p3_prague_later_okres``, so the analysis can drop the block; a pool tie-break inside it
  (*Čakovice*, *Lipany*) stays refused ``prague_later_okres_tie_break`` and in the queue;
  ``prague_pool_only`` stays refused.
* **the seat rule**: a name that is the stated okres's own name town, answered by several
  settlements, goes to the one in the okres's seat court (*Podbořany*: ``podborany:1``, not
  ``podboranky:1``); tier ``p1_okres_seat``.
* **an okres inferred from the name** (``{prefix}_okres_match = muni`` with no okres string) links
  only when the name has exactly one settlement in the whole gazetteer or is that okres's seat;
  otherwise ``okres_from_name_ambiguous``; when linked, the component ``okres_inferred``.
* **owner check**: the conflict test reads the split printed forms (*Neustift, Novosady Blatiny*
  holds ``blatiny:1``: ``lhota:36`` on that row is ``owner_name_conflict``), and a part of such a
  municipality row is refused the same way (*Samotín* would roll up to ``lhota:36``); the
  contradicted-row rule never frees a settlement from ``two_owners``
  (:attr:`Gazetteer.contradicted_freed`).
* **Praha-X**: an unknown X never falls back to ``praha:1`` (``praha_name_unknown``), and a piece of
  a string (alternate, German form, split piece) never resolves to ``praha:1`` unless the whole
  string is the city; ``hl. město Praha`` is the capital's title.
* **the VÚA readings**: ``vua_uncertain`` reads ``locations`` 1.2.3 ``n_readings`` (the written head
  counted); a German cell of 2+ forms is decided on the union of their settlements — ambiguous when
  they give two, never D-144's one obec among them (:func:`german_verdict`) — and the
  numbered-sibling guard runs on ``p2_german``; a reading taken from VÚA's first candidate links only
  when every candidate gives the same settlement (``ambiguous:vua_candidates``).
* **P4 in the other direction**: a name the stated okres holds inside a longer name (*Lhota* |
  Tábor: *Balkova Lhota* …; *Ouběnice 1. díl*) is not sent elsewhere (``ambiguous:p4_in_okres``);
  P4's bare-head refusal is ``qualifier_conflict`` on a qualified form, ``head_in_okres`` on the bare
  head.
* **cross-references on both rows**: when every row holding a settlement is a ``viz`` row, the
  municipality row owns it and a part row of 10 % or less of its population is dropped (*Pivoň*).
* **refused rows carry no row key, owner flag, piece tier or uncertainty component**;
  ``rulings_dependence`` counts linked rows only; the component ``obec_over_part`` marks a D-144
  choice of a register municipality over a register part printing the same name (no link change).

Changes in 0.5.0 (the author's decisions of 2026-11-16, D1–D4):

* **D1, the first-candidate rule**: a reading taken from VÚA's first candidate is refused
  (``ambiguous:vua_candidates``) only when another candidate gives a **different** settlement, or
  is itself ambiguous (:func:`candidate_verdicts`). A candidate that gives nothing — its okres does
  not resolve (*Kralupy*, *Hlučín*, a Slovak or Subcarpathian okres), it names no okres or no
  municipality, or it matches nothing in its okres — is no evidence against the main reading; such
  a link keeps ``vua_uncertain = True``. A candidate okres string naming a statutory city and its
  rural okres (*Opava*, *Liberec*) is read as the rural member unless the municipality is the city
  itself (records_geo's twin rule, D-17): the city okres answers any name with the city, which made
  0.4.1 count *Tábor, okres Opava* (``tabor:1``, an osada of Loděnice) as giving nothing.
* **D2, an okres inferred from the name**: linked when D-144 across all okresy (``global_any``;
  one id, else the one obec or town — a register municipality row, a lexikon obec, or a namesake
  whose 1910 status the lexikon does not give) is exactly the settlement the match found in the
  inferred okres, or (0.4.0) the name is that okres's own; refused ``okres_from_name_conflict``
  when that one lies in another okres, else ``okres_from_name_ambiguous``
  (:func:`okres_inferred_refusal`).
* **D3**: ``locations`` 1.2.x is accepted for ``data/final`` (nothing to code here).
* **D4a, head_in_okres**: a qualified name whose stated okres holds exactly one settlement with the
  bare key and no qualified form of it links to that settlement, tier ``p2_qualifier`` (*Klášter nad
  Jizerou* | Mnichovo Hradiště, *Novosedla nad Nežárkou* | Třeboň).
* **D4b**: ``locations`` 1.2.4 counts a parenthetical holding only an okres and a ``?`` as a second
  reading (*Bakov, okr. Náchod? (okr. Slaný?)*): ``vua_uncertain``.
* **D4c, Prague pool tie-breaks** outside the later-okres block — the okres moves of rule
  ``p3_prague_1910_okres`` a pool preference picked (*Záběhlice*, *Podbaba*, *Sedlec*) — link as
  before and carry the new component ``pool_tie_break``; inside the block they stay refused. A
  quarter read in okres Praha itself (*Libeň* → quarter VIII, the Libeň trap) moves nothing and is
  not flagged.
* **D4d**: the VÚA German form breaks a P1 D-144 status tie it can decide: *Oldřichov (Ulgersdorf),
  okres Děčín* is ``oldrichov:1`` (1910 *Ulgersdorf*, part 5 of *Franzenthal-Ulgersdorf*), not the
  obec ``oldrichov:2`` (printed *Ullgersdorf*, court Děčín) — tier ``p2_german``
  (:func:`german_tie_break`). Záblatí and Ulgersdorf get evidence rulings in ``anchor_rulings.csv``.

Changes in 0.6.0 (the author's decisions of 2026-11-16, T1–T4, after the 0.5.0 checkers found
about 10–20 % wrong links among what D1 and D2 restored):

* **T1, D1 tightened** — a VÚA candidate that "gives nothing" must not hide a real conflict
  (:func:`candidate_verdicts`). Its okres is read off the candidate's own text with the typos
  normalised (``okrese``/``okrs``/``okes``/``ores``/``okrr`` … → ``okres``, ``na Nisou`` →
  ``nad Nisou``, ``/…/`` tails dropped, the **last** ``okres X`` taken: :func:`candidate_okres`),
  then resolved (:func:`resolve_okres`): a backbone name; a post-1910 okres onto its 1910 okres
  (:data:`LATER_OKRES_1910`: *Český Těšín* → Těšín, *Frýdek-Místek* → Frýdek/Místek, *Kralupy* →
  the town's 1910 okres) and any other later okres through the lexikon timeline (P4 on the token);
  a Slovak, Hungarian, Subcarpathian or Hlučín okres is **foreign** (no evidence); else a close
  match (difflib >= 0.85) to one Czech-lands okres name (*Nové Město na Morava*). A candidate
  whose item names a land or country outside the Czech lands (*Zwickau, Sasko*; *Vídeň, Dolní
  Rakousy*) is foreign too. **Global-name fallback**: a candidate that still matches nothing — no
  okres, an okres that does not resolve, or nothing of the name in its okres — counts as a
  **conflict** when its name (as written, qualifier kept, or the right piece of a compound)
  answers in ``global_any`` to a Czech-lands 1910 settlement other than the link (kind ``global``;
  :data:`LATER_TOWN_1910`: *Český Těšín* is ``tesin:2``, Teschen), or, in the okres it names, is
  a close spelling (difflib >= 0.9) of another settlement (*Weisbach, okres Frýdland* =
  *Weissbach*, :func:`close_names`). The candidate that is the
  record's own reading is not checked against itself. An ambiguous candidate still refuses (the
  0.4.0 extension, conservative: 11 records in 0.5.0).
* **T2, D2 tightened** (:func:`okres_inferred_refusal`): a link whose okres records_geo inferred
  from the name is refused ``okres_from_name_foreign`` when the raw cell names a land, country or
  district outside the Czech lands (:func:`foreign_token`: *Jaroslav, Halič*; *Steinbach, Gmünd*),
  ``okres_from_name_conflict`` when an okres token of the cell (``okr``/``okres``/``okes``/``ores``
  …), or a bare Czech okres or court name after a comma, names an okres that is neither the
  settlement's nor in its timeline (:func:`raw_okres_refusal`), and
  ``okres_from_name_home_conflict`` when the soldier's home okres or home municipality
  (``home_okres_id`` / ``home_municipality``) holds **another** namesake (:func:`home_conflict`:
  legion *Bukovka*, *Střížkov*, *Hodkov*). D-144 across okresy (:func:`d2_decide`): a namesake of
  unknown 1910 status may refuse but never wins (legion *Dolní Lhotka*), and an **unanchored**
  register municipality row printing the name counts as one more possible obec (*Chudeřice*,
  *Milíčov*).
* **T3, the census key follows the corrected okres** (:func:`correct_census_okres_id`, notebook 02
  §4a): where ``birth_okres_corrected``, ``birth_census_okres_id`` is the pooled census unit
  (:func:`utils.parsing.census.okres_census_crosswalk`, D-17/D-18) of ``birth_okres_id_1910``; the
  stated one is kept in ``birth_census_okres_id_stated``.
* **T4**: ``pool_tie_break`` is set wherever P3 broke a pool tie at ``p3_prague_suburb`` outside
  the later-okres block, okres moved or not; :func:`coverage`'s first-candidate counts are on the
  scope, as the headline; ``locations`` 1.2.5 (an okres-only parenthetical naming the head's own
  okres is no second reading).

Changes in 0.7.0 (the 0.6.0 checkers' findings and the author's answers A1–A3, 2026-11-16; each rule
can be switched off for measurement, :func:`rules_off`, :data:`RULES_070`):

* **F1, a silent candidate the gazetteer holds under a later name** (:func:`global_names`,
  :func:`candidate_verdicts`): a lexikon row with no 1910 okres whose earliest ``okres_all`` okres is
  a Czech-lands one (not Hlučín, Valticko, Vitorazsko: :func:`unplaced_czech`) counts in the
  global-name fallback (*Nový Bohumín*, *Ruda nad Moravou*); in the okres a candidate names, such a
  row of the name or of its qualifier-stripped head counts when its timeline holds that okres
  (*Louky nad Dřevnicí* → ``louky:2``); an **unanchored** register municipality printing the name
  counts (kind ``unanchored``: *Horní Líštná*, ``de-silesia|303009022|28``);
  :data:`LATER_TOWN_1910` adds *Nový Bohumín* → ``sunychl:1`` (Šunychl, 1910). When the candidates
  disagree (a link standing beside silent candidates) the record's own **head** — the written text
  before the first parenthesis — goes through the same global check when it is not the linked
  candidate's own name (*Eisenberg* → ``ruda:4`` beside ``jezeri:1``; kind ``head_global``).
* **F2, the head contradicts the link** (:func:`head_verdict`, same scope): it names a land,
  country or district outside the Czech lands (:func:`foreign_token`, a Hungarian okres: *Jeníkov,
  Nitra*), a Czech land the link is not in (Bohemia against Moravia/Silesia; Moravia against Silesia
  tolerated: *Markovice, Morava* → Chrudim), it is the name of a candidate VÚA placed outside the
  Czech lands and not the linked one's (*Inzersdorf*, Hietzing), or it carries a distinguishing
  word (*Něm.*, *Horní*, *Nový* …) that only another namesake's 1910 / German names carry (*Něm.
  Kravaře* = *Deutsch Krawarn*, ``kravare:2``) — kinds ``head_foreign`` / ``head_land`` /
  ``head_namesake``.
* **F3, D2's home and the post-1910 name** (:func:`okres_inferred_refusal`): a home outside the
  Czech lands (``home_land`` other than *Czech lands*, ``home_megye_id`` / ``home_jaras_id`` set,
  a home municipality that only a Hungarian name answers to; and, where the name answers to more
  than one Czech-lands settlement and is not the okres's own, a home whose municipality and okres
  strings both resolve to nothing in the Czech lands: *Bielik, Bielik*) refuses an inferred okres,
  ``okres_from_name_home_foreign``; a match that came only through a post-1910 lexikon name — the
  register holds the settlement but prints no such form, nor does the lexikon's 1910 name — may not
  win an inferred okres where D-144 had to choose among namesakes, ``okres_from_name_later_name``
  (*Dvorek*, printed only *Höflas*; a unique modern name such as *Český Krumlov* still links).
* **F4, a land word in the cell** (:func:`lands_named`): the raw cell outside parentheses names
  *Čechy* against a Moravian or Silesian link, or *Morava* / *Slezsko* against a Bohemian one →
  ``okres_from_name_land_conflict``; *Horní* / *Pruské Slezsko* (Upper, Prussian Silesia) is foreign.
* **F5, okres alternatives in parentheses** (:func:`paren_okres_alternatives`): an okres named inside
  a parenthesis after an okres word (*Domoradice, okr. Vysoké Mýto? (Český Krumlov?)*) is an
  alternative; when one alternative holds **another** namesake of the key the link is refused
  ``okres_from_name_ambiguous``; when the link fits one alternative and no other alternative holds
  the name it stands (*Javornice*, *Jiřetín* the same way).
* **F6, an okres string that resolves to nothing is no evidence** (:func:`_okres_fits` →
  ``unknown``, the link kept, flagged by ``okres_inferred``); the close match takes the single best
  okres when its ratio beats the runner-up's by :data:`OKRES_FUZZY_MARGIN` (*Valšské Meziříčí*) and
  never reaches or starts from a key of 4 letters or fewer (*Plzań* is not *Plan*); later okres and
  court forms (:data:`OKRES_NAME_ALIASES`: *Zábřeh na Moravě*, *Rokytnice*, *Horní Litvínov*,
  *Vrbno*) and the Austrian districts of :data:`FOREIGN_DISTRICTS` resolve.
* **A1** (the author): a home okres equal to the link's own okres is no conflict — kept from 0.6.0.
* **A2** (the author): where ``birth_okres_id`` is missing but the link supplies
  ``birth_okres_id_1910``, ``birth_census_okres_id`` is that okres's census unit (the stated key stays
  missing); :func:`correct_census_okres_id` is idempotent (F7: the stated key always from
  ``birth_okres_id``).
* **A3** (the author): a written okres conflicting with a key that answers to exactly one Czech-lands
  settlement is refused ``okres_from_name_conflict_unique``; such refusals are their own block of the
  rulings queue with whether the written okres borders the settlement's (MPIDR outlines), and the
  conservative refusals *Rudolice* and *Kienberg* are listed as the block ``conservative``.

Changes in 0.8.0 (the author's answers A4–A6 of 2026-11-16 and the 0.7.0 checkers' defects D-a…D-h; each
switchable, :data:`RULES_080`):

* **A4, a foreign home narrowed**: a home refuses an inferred okres only when it lies in Hungary /
  Slovakia, Galicia or Bukovina (``home_land`` *Slovakia*, *Hungary*, *Galicia* — the records file
  Bukovina under Galicia — a Hungarian county or járás, a home only a Hungarian name answers to); a
  home in Austria (Vienna), overseas or Russia, or in any other land, never refuses; ``home_unresolved``
  keeps its contested-name restriction and does not fire on a home recognisably elsewhere
  (:data:`HOME_ELSEWHERE_WORDS`: *Chicago, Illinois*); and no home refuses when the raw cell writes the
  link's own okres (*Habry, okr. Čáslav*).
* **A6, the Habsburg regiment as refuse-only evidence** (:func:`regiment_region`): the soldier's
  infantry regiment (VÚA ``ah_unit_*``; csol.cz ``habsburg_unit_peacetime`` / ``_capture``) is looked
  up in Ehnl's Tabelle I (``reference/units/ehnl_tabelle1_{infantry,landwehr,honved}.csv``) and its
  recruiting district placed in a region (:func:`regiment_regions`). A regiment raised outside the
  Czech lands refuses a link that VÚA read off its first candidate when another candidate lies in
  that region (``vua_regiment_conflict``: *Žabokriek*, IR 71 Trenčín; *Prislop*, IR 85 Máramaros), and
  an inferred okres when the name is a Slovak obec's and the regiment Hungarian
  (``okres_from_name_regiment_conflict``). The regiment never picks or creates a link.
* **D-a**: F5 reaches a stated okres (an okres word followed by okres alternatives in parentheses: a
  namesake in another alternative refuses ``okres_from_name_ambiguous``), and F6 reaches an okres
  string records_geo left unresolved: :func:`resolve_okres` first, then — for a Czech-looking string —
  the okres inferred from the name as the as-is run does, the string no evidence
  (:func:`unresolved_okres_link`).
* **D-b**: :func:`close_okres` scores the foreign district names too, and a foreign name at least as
  close wins (*Turňa*, *Senice*, *Sečany*).
* **D-c**: the later-name rule does not fire on a cell whose parenthesis prints a 1910 form of the link
  (*Prameny (Sangaberg)*) nor where the home okres is the link's (*Ludvíkov*, home *Einsidl*).
* **D-d**: ``head_global`` takes only namesakes in the land the head names (*Benešov, Slezsko*).
* **D-e**: ``okres_from_name_conflict_unique`` counts the unplaced Czech namesakes (F1's
  :func:`_czech_1910`), and a written okres holding a near spelling of the name or of the link is a
  plain ``okres_from_name_conflict`` (*Libavá*, *Lobeč*, *Dobrová*, *Bernatice*).
* **D-f**: a candidate link stands (flagged) when the head is a printed 1910 form of it and the only
  other candidates are unplaced Czech rows the register does not print (*Modlan*).
* **D-g**: the head refusals (F2) are ``vua_head_conflict``, not ``ambiguous:vua_candidates``.
* **D-h**: a link is refused ``home_name_conflict`` when the home municipality is a Czech-lands name of
  another okres and the written head matches it better than the link (*Krupka, Kutná Hora*); a home
  namesake in a land the head's own land word contradicts does not count (*Držkov, Morava*).

Changes in 0.9.0 (the 0.8.0 checkers' defects E1–E13, 2026-11-17; E1–E12 each switchable, :data:`RULES_090`):

* **E1**: a match through an unresolved okres string that does not link sets no okres — ``okres_id_1910``
  and so the census key (A2) stay empty on every refused row with no stated okres; the okres the string
  gave is only in the diagnostic ``refusal_okres_ids`` (``refusal_detail`` ``okres_string_unlinked`` /
  ``okres_name_unlinked`` / ``okres_timeline_unlinked``).
* **E2**: the regiment refuses only through a candidate in its own recruiting county or a county next to
  it (:func:`regiment_area`, :data:`COUNTY_NEIGHBOURS` from the GISta 1910 county outlines), never through
  a ``dříve:`` former-name reading, and not where the VÚA home cell (not a copy of the head) names the link.
* **E3**: in a VÚA cell, a D-a reading that is not the written head under 2+ ``?`` candidates is refused
  ``ambiguous:vua_candidates`` (*Záběhlice ?* is not Zbraslav).
* **E4**: VÚA's ``Obec-Část``: two distinct 1910 settlements, the left not the right's parent — the right
  piece (*Kralupy nad Vltavou-Míkovice* → ``mikovice:1``), in the record and in VÚA's candidates.
* **E5**: a single German form that is the German name of the okres town the cell names is dropped
  (*Rochlice, okres Jilemncie (Starkenbach)*).
* **E6**: an okres string naming 2+ okresy that hold different namesakes refuses
  ``okres_from_name_ambiguous`` (*? (Nové město nad Metují, Kaplice)*), csol.cz included; and an alternate
  under a doubted okres the home okres contradicts.
* **E7**: Prussian-Silesian towns, Hungarian names as written and *Uherská X* are foreign before any
  later-okres prefix or close Czech spelling (*Uherská Skalice*, *Holíč*, *Ratibor*).
* **E8**: ``n.`` / ``p.`` before a capitalised word is ``nad`` / ``pod`` in :func:`key` (*Ústí n.Orlicí*).
* **E9**: a later okres over several 1910 okresy (*Kralupy*, *Frýdek-Místek*, *Český Těšín*) and the
  capital's countryside (*Praha-venkov*) are timeline okresy searched across the 1910 okresy that formed
  them (:func:`timeline_okres_link`), never one okres nor the city okres Praha.
* **E10**: ``okres_fuzzy``, a new component of ``settlement_uncertain`` (the link's okres came from an
  unresolved string by close spelling), and the diagnostic ``okres_source``.
* **E11**: VÚA readings in separate parentheses are candidates (*Stodůlky … (Praha venkov) (Sušice)*); an
  okres name after a comma locates the place and is no piece of it (*Stupno - Břasy, Plzeň*).
* **E12**: the D-h refusals say whether the home okres was written or inferred; the rulings queue lists them
  as the block ``home_name_conflict`` with their shape — which rows D-h refuses is unchanged.
* **E13**: the checkers' case lists moved to ``utils/reference_tools/places/measure_birth_settlement.py``.

Changes in 0.10.0 (the 0.9.0 checkers' findings F1–F13, 2026-11-17; the behavioural ones switchable as
G1–G7, :data:`RULES_100` — G<n> is the checkers' F<n>, renamed because F1–F6 name the 0.7.0 switches):

* **G1** (F1): VÚA's ``Obec-Část`` names the part *under* the obec — of the right piece's namesakes in the okres
  the one whose 1910 parent or register owner is the left piece (:func:`right_under_left`; *Střechov-Dubovka* →
  ``dubovka:2``, osada of Střechov, not D-144's ``dubovka:1`` of Neveklov); with 2+ namesakes and none under the
  left, the left obec as in 0.8.0. VÚA's candidate readings go through the same split, so two candidates no
  longer agree through a wrong namesake (*Černožice-Čáslavky*).
* **G2** (F2): E6 does not refuse when exactly one settlement is held by every okres piece that holds the name
  (it links, moved as P4 moves where the stated okres is in its timeline, :func:`okres_common_switch`), nor when
  the home municipality is the link or the link's 1910 parent (:func:`home_names_link_or_parent`).
* **G3** (F3): a comma piece is an okres locator only when it is a big city or names the record's own okres
  without resolving to another settlement there (:func:`okres_locator`; *Jablunkov, Piosek, Písek*).
* **G4** (F4): E11's separate parentheses read at depth 1 (:func:`top_level_groups`), and a home cell naming
  the first reading (E2's :func:`home_names_link`) keeps the link. The as-is run uses these candidates too:
  it is the comparison run of the same cells, and a coin flip VÚA wrote is one in either run.
* **G5** (F5): *Uherská X* is read as Hungary only on the first comma piece, written out (*Uh.* is the
  Moravian forms) and not close to a Moravian *Uhersk…* okres (:func:`uhersky_rest`).
* **G6** (F6): E5 keeps the German form when VÚA's own candidate reading is the okres town
  (:func:`okres_town_read`; *Aisič … (Ústí nad Labem, okres Ústí nad Labem ?) (Aussig - ?)*).
* **G7** (F7): E3 also on the stated-okres path.
* F8: :func:`timeline_okres_link`'s docstring on Letky corrected (no behaviour change); F9: ``CONSERVATIVE_CASES``
  moved to the measurement script and the queue's ``conservative`` block dropped (a queue block lists only
  refused rows); F10: the ``okres_fuzzy`` description says what the flag covers.

Changes in 0.11.0 (the 0.10.0 checkers' findings, 2026-11-17; switchable as :data:`RULES_110`):

* **H1**: where no namesake of the right piece lies under the left by 1910 parent, register owner or sibling,
  the modern municipality decides (:attr:`Gazetteer.modern_obec`, from ``settlements_1910_geo``): a namesake
  whose modern obec is the left piece is under it (:func:`right_under_left`; *Jesenice-Martinice* → ``martinice:6``,
  osada of Nedrahovice in 1910, part of Jesenice today — not D-144's ``martinice:1``, part of Votice); in the E4
  shape a left piece whose modern obec is the right piece, and which is not the right piece's own settlement, is
  the place (:func:`left_in_right_modern`; *Mezná-Hřensko* → ``mezna:1``, *Polanka-Chotoviny* → ``polanka:6``);
  and D-144's obec pick no longer stands where modern evidence names another namesake. VÚA's candidate readings
  go through the same split (*Martinice ? (Martinice …; Jesenice-Martinice …)* no longer agrees).
* **H3**: E6's refusal stands where the okres pieces agree on one settlement and the link is another
  (:func:`okres_common_switch` declined to move it).
* H2 is records_geo 1.11.0 (the Praha-countryside veto reads the other pieces of the string); H4 (a fresh VÚA
  re-parse in the build) and H5 (measurement hygiene) change no rule here.

Changes in 0.12.0 (the 0.11.0 checkers' findings, 2026-11-17; switchable as :data:`RULES_120`):

* **I1**: in a VÚA cell a ``?`` between pieces separates alternatives (*Podbořany ? Mukoděly*, *Kamenice nad Lipou ?
  Žďár*, *Benešov) ?Divišov*: VÚA's reading after a lost ``(``). A piece that is the record's own okres or its seat
  or a big city (G3's :func:`okres_locator`) locates the place and is dropped; one piece left is matched alone,
  several that give different settlements (or an ambiguous one) are refused ``ambiguous:qmark_readings``
  (:func:`qmark_readings`, :func:`match_birthplace`). Only with a stated okres, and only in a VÚA cell: a csol.cz
  clerk's *Vrchlabí? Háje nad Jizerou?* is two doubted birthplaces, not a locator and a reading.
* **I2**: ``p2_qualifier``'s stripped head links only where the name **as written** is no other 1910 settlement
  outside the record's okres (:func:`qualified_elsewhere`: *Lipník nad Bečvou (čp. 286)* | Moravský Krumlov is not
  the 95-house ``lipnik:2``); else ``qualifier_conflict`` — unless the soldier's home municipality lies in the
  okres (:func:`home_muni_in_okres`: *Police nad Metují* | Zábřeh, home Drozdov, stays ``police:1``).
* **I5**: :func:`load_gazetteer` raises ``FileNotFoundError`` without ``settlements_1910_geo`` (H1's evidence no
  longer turns off silently) and the report's ``gazetteer`` block counts :attr:`Gazetteer.modern_obec`.
* I3 and I4 are records_geo 1.12.0 (land of an all-Czech Praha-countryside string; the plain-Praha keep for the
  home only), I6 data_checks 1.32.0 (the Praha-countryside block says 'not run').

Changes in 0.13.0 (the 0.12.0 checkers' findings, 2026-11-17; switchable as :data:`RULES_130`):

* **J1**: a **bare** name that P1 does not find (*Lhota*, *Újezd*, *Hradiště*, *Rybná*) is no longer sent to the one
  qualified namesake D-144 picks (*Lhota u Dubu*) when the okres holds other settlements with the name as a word of
  their head — adjective forms (*Horažďovická Lhota*, *Svijanský Újezd*, *Stará Lysá*) and qualified ones alike
  (:func:`bare_namesakes`). Where those namesakes hold more than one obec, or an obec besides the settlement the
  qualifier tier would take, the record is refused ``ambiguous:p2_bare_namesakes`` — unless the soldier's home
  municipality names, parents, owns or shares a modern municipality with exactly one of them (or, failing that, lies
  next to exactly one: RÚIAN adjacency of the modern municipalities), :func:`home_namesake`. A home that repeats the
  written name is no evidence; one that repeats it and then names a municipality (*Újezd, Dubí*) is read at that
  municipality.
* **J2**: :func:`qualified_elsewhere` also matches the written name **abbreviated** — each written word equal to, or
  a shorter beginning of, the name's word, the qualifier's preposition equal (*Újezd u Sv. Kříže* is *Újezd u
  Svatého Kříže*): I2 then refuses the stripped head (*ujezd:14* of okres Kralovice).
* **J3**: a ``qualifier_conflict`` refusal (P2's or P4's) whose written name is within Levenshtein distance 2 of
  exactly **one** qualified settlement of the record's okres with the same head, and is no settlement elsewhere as
  written (exactly or abbreviated), links that settlement at tier ``p2_qualifier_fuzzy``, flagged by its own
  uncertainty component ``qualifier_fuzzy`` (:func:`qualifier_fuzzy`: *Bystřice nad Perštejnem* →
  ``bystrice-nad-pernstejnem:1``, *Ronov na Doubravou* → ``ronov-nad-doubravou:1``).
* **J4**: I1 runs only on the okres the record **stated** (:func:`match_birthplace`'s *stated*, passed by
  :func:`link_one`), not on an okres the D-a, timeline or candidate paths supply; and those paths pass the soldier's
  home, so I2's and J1's home exceptions reach the same rows.
* J5 is data_checks 1.33.0 (the járás halves say 'not run'); J6 is records_geo 1.13.0 (a Praha-countryside piece
  naming a foreign city with a Czech-village namesake — *Krakov*, *Lvov* — is not Czech).

Changes in 0.14.0 (the 0.13.0 checkers' findings, 2026-11-17; switchable as :data:`RULES_140`):

* **K1**: J1's guard reaches the variant tiers. A **bare** name that an alternate, the VÚA German form or a ČSÚ
  ``viz`` alias sends to a settlement none of whose names is the written one (``p2_alternate``, ``p2_german``,
  ``p2_alias``) passes :func:`bare_namesake_verdict` as ``p2_qualifier``'s bare branch does
  (:func:`bare_variant_verdict`): *Lhota* | Náchod is no longer ``lhotky:4`` (1910 *Lhotka*) while the okres holds
  Lhota pod Hořičkami, Lhota za Červeným Kostelcem and Řešetova Lhota. The alias table keeps each row's modern
  okres (:attr:`Gazetteer.alias_okres`), and an alias target is taken only where that okres is in the
  settlement's ``okres_all`` timeline or is its modern okres (:attr:`Gazetteer.modern_okres`), where the row names
  no okres, or where the okres holds no other namesake of the name (:func:`alias_in_okres`: *LHOTA viz Lhotka
  (Benešov / Ústí n. O.)* is not Náchod's Lhotka). A bare name's parenthesised alternate that says where it lies
  is read so (:func:`locator_alternates`): a preposition and its object is the name's qualifier (*Lhota (u
  Č.Kostelce)* is *Lhota u Č.Kostelce*), and the record's own okres or court, where the okres holds a namesake of
  the name, is dropped (*Jeseník (Nymburk)* | Poděbrady is not the court town Nymburk). Those records read the
  home column too.
* **K2**: a qualified name written **abbreviated** (each word equal to the name's or a shorter beginning of it, as
  :func:`abbreviated_names`) that holds exactly one settlement of the record's okres links it at tier
  ``p2_qualifier`` (flagged uncertain through ``settlement_piece_tier``) instead of being refused
  (:func:`qualifier_abbreviated`: *Újezd u Sv. Kříže* | Rokycany → ``ujezd-u-svateho-krize:1``, *Týniště n.Orl* |
  Rychnov → ``tyniste-nad-orlici:1``); inside the okres a written ``u`` (*near*) also meets another preposition
  (*Lhota u Č.Kostelce* → ``lhota-za-cervenym-kostelcem:1``). The unresolved-okres path (D-a) reads a name the
  1910 settlements do not hold through the same abbreviation, where it names exactly one (*Brandýs n. L.*).
* **K3**: J3's bound is relative to the qualifier: a misspelt qualifier may be up to a quarter of the written
  qualifier's length away (never less than :data:`QUALIFIER_FUZZY_DISTANCE`), still to exactly one settlement of the
  okres and only where the written name is no settlement anywhere (:func:`qualifier_fuzzy_bound`: *Veselí na
  Moravě* → ``veseli-nad-moravou:1``, *Bystřice nad Perštýnem* → ``bystrice-nad-pernstejnem:1``).
* **K4**: :func:`home_namesake` also reads the home without its qualifier (its hyphen pieces too): home
  *Trojanovice pod Radhoštěm* is *Trojanovice*, whose modern municipality borders Kunčice pod Ondřejníkem.

Changes in 0.15.0 (the 0.14.0 checkers' findings, 2026-11-17; switchable as :data:`RULES_150`):

* **L1**: K1's exact-name test compares the written name with the target's **full** names only — its lexicon
  names, its 1910 name and the printed forms of its owner row — not the single words :attr:`Gazetteer.pool_forms`
  splits a two-word printed form into (``Chocenická Lhota`` carries ``lhota`` there): *Lhota ?* | Plzeň is no longer
  ``chocenicka-lhota:1`` through the alias while Hradišťská Lhotka is an obec of the okres too, *Málkovice* | Vyškov
  no longer ``moravske-malkovice:1`` beside Bohaté (1910 Německé) Málkovice. A 1910 **town** whose name is the
  written one plus *Město* / *Městys* / *Městečko* (or *Stadt* / *Markt*), or a statutory city, still stands over
  the namesake villages (:func:`town_over_village`: *Libavá* | Moravský Beroun stays ``mesto-libava:1``).
* **L2**: the alias's "no other namesake in the okres" fallback (:func:`alias_in_okres`) holds only where the alias
  row's okres agrees, or the written name is a **spelling** of one of the target's own names (best
  :class:`difflib.SequenceMatcher` ratio at least :data:`ALIAS_SPELLING_RATIO`, :func:`alias_spelling`), or a
  qualified name whose head is the target's. A renaming tied to another okres (*ŠUMVALD viz Podlesí (Opava)*) is set
  aside; if no later tier matches, the record is refused ``alias_other_okres`` (:func:`alias_other_okres`), not
  linked to a settlement that merely shares the target's name (*Šumvald* | Šumperk is not 1910 Krumperky).
* **L3**: the alias's namesakes (:func:`alias_rivals`) leave out those in the target's **own** 1910 municipality
  (its register parts, or the other parts of the municipality it is a part of), so only obce and the parts of other
  municipalities stand against it: *Bezděkov* | Kladno is ``horni-bezdekov:2`` again (Dolní Bezděkov is its part),
  read as J1 reads one candidate, tier ``p2_qualifier``, flagged uncertain; *Oujezd* | Mladá Boleslav is ``ujezd:9``
  (Velký Oujezd) beside Malý Oujezd, both parts of Bratronice, flagged so. A part of another municipality still
  counts (*Hutě* | Kutná Hora: Stará Huť 1. and 2. díl lie in Lošiny and Sudějov; *Lhotka* | Čáslav: Žlebská
  Lhotka against Sovoluská Lhota) — narrower than "only obce", which would turn those into municipal coin flips.
* **L4**: a bare name's locator alternate that resolves to nothing joined (*Lhota (u Nákla)*), while the bare name
  is a P1 settlement, is read by its **object**: the settlements of the okres whose name the object writes in
  another case (:func:`stem_agrees`) are read as :func:`home_namesake` reads a home, over P1's ids and the name's
  namesakes (:func:`locator_object_verdict`). One pick other than P1's links at ``p2_qualifier`` (flagged
  uncertain): ``lhota-nad-moravou:1``, whose modern municipality is Náklo. None, while P1's pick has a qualified
  name of another object (*Lhota u Konice*): refused ``ambiguous:p2_bare_namesakes``.
* **L5**: a qualifier written in another grammatical case or with another preposition reaches the one settlement of
  the okres with the head whose qualifier's object words agree by stem (:func:`qualifier_stem`, :func:`stem_agrees`:
  Czech case endings dropped, a common beginning of at least the shorter stem's length less three and never under
  four letters), where the written name is no settlement anywhere: *Lhota u Červeného Kostelce* | Náchod →
  ``lhota-za-cervenym-kostelcem:1``, *Ostrov n. Macochou* | Boskovice → ``ostrov-u-macochy:1``; tier
  ``p2_qualifier_fuzzy``, component ``qualifier_fuzzy``.
* **L6**: ``alias_namesake_refusal``'s ``ambiguous:p2_bare_namesakes`` lists the alias target(s) it set aside beside
  the namesakes, so the refusal names both readings (*Lhotka* | Čáslav: ``sovoluska-lhota:1`` and
  ``zlebska-lhotka:1``).
* **L7**: K2's :func:`qualifier_abbreviated` takes K3's guard: nothing where the written name is a settlement
  anywhere (:attr:`Gazetteer.global_name`, :attr:`Gazetteer.global_any`) or its abbreviated reading names a
  settlement outside the okres.

Nothing here writes ``data/final``: :func:`build` writes ``output/places/birth_settlement_*`` and
``output/places/birthplace_rulings_queue.csv``.

Usage
-----
    from utils.parsing import birth_settlement as bs
    gaz = bs.load_gazetteer()                       # register + lexikon + overrides + rulings + heals
    legion = bs.add_birth_settlement_columns(legion, gaz)   # the one notebook-02 entry point
    legion = bs.correct_census_okres_id(legion, districts)  # 0.6.0 (T3): the census key, before §4b
    result = bs.build()                             # both datasets, report, rulings queue

                   rivals (:func:`alias_rivals`); L4 a locator's object read as a
                   home (:func:`locator_object_verdict`); L5 a qualifier in another case or with another preposition
                   (:func:`qualifier_stem`); L6 the set-aside alias target listed in the refusal; L7 K2's guard;
                   :data:`RULES_150`. (The 0.14.0 report said *Lhota ?* | Plzeň linked because Hradišťská Lhotka had
                   no obec status; it is an obec: the link came through the word pieces L1 removes.)

#: the rules of the current round (what the measurement switches)

_RULES_OFF: set[str] = set()


@contextmanager
def rules_off(rules=RULES):
    """Inside the block the given *rules* (of :data:`RULES_070`, :data:`RULES_080`, :data:`RULES_090`,
    :data:`RULES_100`, :data:`RULES_110`, :data:`RULES_120`, :data:`RULES_130`, :data:`RULES_140` or
    :data:`RULES_150`) do not apply (measurement only; with every 0.15.0 rule off the module gives the 0.14.0 links,
    with the 0.14.0 ones off as well the 0.13.0 links, and so on)."""
    unknown = (set(rules) - set(RULES_070) - set(RULES_080) - set(RULES_090) - set(RULES_100)
               - set(RULES_110) - set(RULES_120) - set(RULES_130) - set(RULES_140) - set(RULES_150))
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"no such rule: {sorted(unknown)}")
    before = set(_RULES_OFF)
    _RULES_OFF.update(rules)
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        _RULES_OFF.clear()
        _RULES_OFF.update(before)


def _on(rule: str) -> bool:
    return rule not in _RULES_OFF

# ── P0: the string ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def key(text) -> str:
    """Match key: :func:`records_geo._norm` (unaccented, lower, ``-`` → space, ``n.`` → ``nad``),
    then every other punctuation mark dropped.

    0.9.0 (E8): an interior ``n.`` / ``p.`` right before a capital letter is ``nad`` / ``pod`` also when
    no space follows it (*Ústí n.Orlicí* → ``usti nad orlici``, *Frenštát p.Radhoštěm* → ``frenstat pod
    radhostem``); :func:`records_geo._norm` expands only a free-standing ``n.``. No gazetteer name carries
    the shape (checked 2026-11-17), so the indexes are unchanged."""
    if _on("E8") and isinstance(text, str) and ("n." in text or "p." in text):
        text = _ABBREV_NP_RE.sub(lambda m: " nad " if m.group(1) == "n" else " pod ", text)
    k = _norm(text)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", re.sub(r"[^\w\s]", " ", k)).strip()


#: E8 (0.9.0): ``n.`` / ``p.`` after a word and before a capitalised word of 3+ letters (space optional): a
#: river or mountain written out (*n.Labem*), never a one-letter one (*Kamenice n.L.* stays unexpanded,
#: as :func:`records_geo._norm` leaves a trailing ``n.``: the river is ambiguous)
_ABBREV_NP_RE = re.compile(r"(?<=\S)\s+([np])\.\s*(?=[A-ZÁČĎÉĚÍŇÓŘŠŤÚŮÝŽ][^\W\d_]{2})")


def nospace(k: str) -> str:
    return k.replace(" ", "")


# 0.6.0: the curated foreign okresy (Subcarpathia, Hlučín) as keys — checked before the later-okres timeline
_FOREIGN_OKRES_KEYS = frozenset(key(n) for n in FOREIGN_OKRES)


def strip_qualifier(k: str) -> str:
    """``kostelec nad orlici`` → ``kostelec``; unchanged when there is no qualifier."""
    return _QUALIFIER_RE.sub("", k).strip()


def okres_token(text) -> str:
    """An okres name as a timeline token: :func:`key`, ``)`` dropped, then space-free
    (``Ústí nad Orl ici`` and ``Ústí nad Orlicí`` are one token)."""
    return nospace(key(str(text).replace(")", ""))) if text is not None else ""


def form_set(keys) -> set[str]:
    """Comparison forms of name keys: each space-free, as written and without its qualifier, ``ß``
    folded to ``ss`` (the register prints *Roßbach*, the lexicon *Rossbach*)."""
    out = set()
    for k in keys:
        if k:
            k = k.replace("ß", "ss")
            out |= {nospace(k), nospace(strip_qualifier(k))}
    out.discard("")
    return out


def clean_birthplace(raw) -> tuple[str | None, tuple[str, ...]]:
    """``(name, alternates)`` from a birthplace cell; ``(None, ())`` for a placeholder.

    ``též Ronšperk`` → ``Ronšperk``; ``Mirošov (též Nedašov)`` → ``Mirošov`` + ``Nedašov``;
    ``Vrajt)`` → ``Vrajt``; ``Lučice-Janovec 1. díl`` → ``Lučice-Janovec``;
    ``Krásná Lípa ? Krásná Lípa`` → ``Krásná Lípa``; ``(Velké) Jirny`` → ``Velké Jirny`` + ``Jirny``.
    """
    if raw is None or (isinstance(raw, float) and pd.isna(raw)) or raw is pd.NA:
        return None, ()
    s = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", str(raw)).replace("+", " ")
    s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()
    if _PLACEHOLDER_RE.match(s):
        return None, ()
    alts: list[str] = []
    lead = re.match(r"^\(([^()]+)\)\s*(\S.*)$", s)              # "(Velké) Jirny"
    if lead:
        alts.append(lead.group(2))
        s = f"{lead.group(1)} {lead.group(2)}"
    alts += [a for a in re.findall(r"\(([^()]*)\)", s)]
    s = re.sub(r"\([^()]*\)", " ", s)
    s = s.replace("(", " ").replace(")", " ")
    s = _DIL_RE.sub(" ", s)
    pieces = [p for p in re.split(r"\s+\?\s*|\?\s+|,\s*též\b|\btéž\b", s) if p and p.strip()]
    pieces = [_TEZ_RE.sub("", p).strip(" ?,.;:-–") for p in pieces]
    pieces = [re.sub(r"\s+", " ", p.replace("?", " ")).strip() for p in pieces]
    pieces = [p for p in pieces if p and not _PLACEHOLDER_RE.match(p)]
    alts = [re.sub(r"\s+", " ", _TEZ_RE.sub("", a).replace("?", " ")).strip(" ,.;:-–")
            for a in alts]
    alts = [a for a in alts if a and not _PLACEHOLDER_RE.match(a)]
    if not pieces:
        return (alts[0], tuple(alts[1:])) if alts else (None, ())
    out = list(dict.fromkeys([*pieces[1:], *alts]))
    return pieces[0], tuple(a for a in out if key(a) != key(pieces[0]))


def german_form(value) -> str | None:
    """The VÚA German exonym's first usable form (``-; Biela-Tscheche`` debris skipped)."""
    if value is None or (isinstance(value, float) and pd.isna(value)) or value is pd.NA:
        return None
    for item in str(value).split(";"):
        item = re.sub(r"[-–]\s*\?\s*$", "", item).strip(" -–?()")
        if item and not _PLACEHOLDER_RE.match(item):
            return item
    return None


# ── the gazetteer ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
@dataclass
class Gazetteer:
    """Every index the passes read, built once by :func:`build_gazetteer`."""
    reg: dict = field(default_factory=dict)          # (key, okres) -> {sid}   primary editions
    reg_alt: dict = field(default_factory=dict)      # (key, okres) -> {sid}   de-bohemia forms
    lex: dict = field(default_factory=dict)          # (key, okres) -> {sid}
    nospace: dict = field(default_factory=dict)      # (nospace key, okres) -> {sid}
    qualifier: dict = field(default_factory=dict)    # (stripped key, okres) -> {sid}
    alias: dict = field(default_factory=dict)        # alias key -> {target key}
    global_name: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # key -> {sid}
    prague: dict = field(default_factory=dict)       # key -> {sid}  agglomeration + quarters
    status: dict = field(default_factory=dict)       # sid -> healed status_1910 ("" if none)
    reg_municipal: set = field(default_factory=set)  # sids a register municipality row holds
    okres_of: dict = field(default_factory=dict)     # sid -> 1910 okres_id (lexikon)
    parent_key: dict = field(default_factory=dict)   # sid -> key of healed parent_1910
    timeline: dict = field(default_factory=dict)     # sid -> {space-free okres tokens, okres_all}
    forms_of: dict = field(default_factory=dict)     # sid -> form_set of its lexicon names
    court_polygon: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # sid -> court_id (settlements_1910)
    cs_name: dict = field(default_factory=dict)      # sid -> cs_name
    owner: dict = field(default_factory=dict)        # sid -> register owner dict
    two_owners: set = field(default_factory=set)
    quarters: dict = field(default_factory=dict)     # Roman number (1..8) -> sid
    quarter_sids: set = field(default_factory=set)
    statutory: dict = field(default_factory=dict)    # city okres_id -> city sid
    statutory_sids: set = field(default_factory=set)
    city_pieces: set = field(default_factory=set)    # keys of big-city / land names
    greater_prague: set = field(default_factory=set)
    register_munis: set = field(default_factory=set)
    # 0.3.0: register_municipalities by key — sid -> "edition|court_key|muni_seq" and back
    register_muni_key: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    register_key_sid: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    muni_keys: dict = field(default_factory=dict)    # sid -> {keys of municipality rows holding it}
    muni_keys_contradicted: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # sid -> {keys left out, see contradicted_keys}
    okres_names: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # okres_id -> {keys of its okres/seat names}
    numbered: dict = field(default_factory=dict)     # (base key, okres) -> {sid: {numerals}}
    reg_rows: dict = field(default_factory=dict)     # okres -> [(form key, printed, sid, row key)]
    pool_forms: dict = field(default_factory=dict)   # sid -> forms of every register row holding it
    rulings_refused: list = field(default_factory=list)      # anchor rulings apply() skipped
    rulings_unconfirmed: list = field(default_factory=list)  # valid rulings left out (unconfirmed)
    rulings_applied: list = field(default_factory=list)      # ruling keys applied
    include_unconfirmed: bool = False
    # 0.4.0
    seat_court: dict = field(default_factory=dict)   # okres_id -> court_id of the okres seat
    global_any: dict = field(default_factory=dict)   # key -> {sid}: lexikon names + register forms, all okresy
    okres_keys: dict = field(default_factory=dict)   # okres_id -> {key: {sid}} (lexikon + register)
    okres_by_name: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # okres name key (and space-free) -> {okres_id}
    contradicted_freed: list = field(default_factory=list)  # sids the contradicted rule would free from two_owners
    xref_both: list = field(default_factory=list)    # (sid, edition, kept row, dropped rows) viz on every row
    # 0.6.0
    foreign_okres: set = field(default_factory=set)  # keys of okres/district names outside the Czech lands
    later_okres: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # later okres key -> {1910 okres ids} (LATER_OKRES_1910)
    later_town: dict = field(default_factory=dict)   # later town key -> its 1910 sid (LATER_TOWN_1910)
    timeline_tokens: set = field(default_factory=set)  # every space-free okres_all token
    unanchored_munis: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # key -> [okres_id] of unanchored municipality rows
    # 0.7.0
    first_okres: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # sid -> the earliest okres of okres_all (as printed)
    forms_1910: dict = field(default_factory=dict)   # sid -> form_set of the lexikon's 1910 name
    okres_alias: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # OKRES_NAME_ALIASES key -> {okres_id}
    # 0.8.0
    hu_obce: set = field(default_factory=set)        # keys of every Slovak obec name (settlements_hu_1910), A6
    # 0.9.0
    later_token: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # later okres key -> its okres_all token when it spans 2+ 1910 okresy (E9)
    hu_county: dict = field(default_factory=dict)    # key of a Hungarian district / obec / Subcarpathian okres -> {county} (E2)
    # 0.11.0
    modern_obec: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # sid -> key of its modern (RÚIAN) obec, settlements_1910_geo (H1)
    # 0.13.0
    modern_obec_kod: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # sid -> RÚIAN obec_kod of its modern obec (J1)
    obec_neighbours: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # obec_kod -> {neighbouring obec_kod}, ruian_obce_adjacency (J1)
    # 0.14.0
    alias_okres: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # alias key -> {(target key, okres_token(viz_okres) or "")} (K1)
    modern_okres: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # sid -> okres_token of its modern okres, settlements_1910_geo (K1)


def _add(index: dict, k, value) -> None:
    if k and (not isinstance(k, tuple) or k[0]):
        index.setdefault(k, set()).add(value)


def _okres_id(code: str) -> int:
    r, d = str(code).split("-")
    return int(r) * 1000 + int(d)


def _okres_names(districts: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[int, set[str]]:
    out: dict[int, set[str]] = {}
    for r in districts.itertuples(index=False):
        oid = _okres_id(r.okres_code)
        names = out.setdefault(oid, set())
        for v in (r.okres_cs, r.okres_de, getattr(r, "okres_cs_modern", None)):
            if isinstance(v, str) and v.strip():
                names.add(key(re.sub(r"\(město\)", "", v)))
        if getattr(r, "is_okres_seat", False):
            names.add(key(r.gerichtsbezirk_cs))
    return out


def _seat_courts(districts: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[int, int]:
    """``{okres_id: court_id}`` of each okres's seat court (``is_okres_seat``, 0.4.0)."""
    out: dict[int, int] = {}
    for r in districts.itertuples(index=False):
        if bool(getattr(r, "is_okres_seat", False)) and pd.notna(r.court_id):
            out.setdefault(_okres_id(r.okres_code), int(r.court_id))
    return out


def _global_indexes(g: Gazetteer) -> None:
    """0.4.0: every name (lexikon and register, both editions) across all okresy (``global_any``),
    the names of each okres (``okres_keys``, for P4's in-okres guard) and the okres names back to
    their ids (``okres_by_name``, for VÚA's candidate readings)."""
    for table in (g.lex, g.reg, g.reg_alt):
        for (k, oid), sids in table.items():
            g.global_any.setdefault(k, set()).update(sids)
            g.okres_keys.setdefault(oid, {}).setdefault(k, set()).update(sids)
    for k, sids in g.global_name.items():
        g.global_any.setdefault(k, set()).update(sids)
    for oid, names in g.okres_names.items():
        for n in names:
            for kk in (n, nospace(n)):
                g.okres_by_name.setdefault(kk, set()).add(oid)


def _lexikon_indexes(g: Gazetteer, attrs: pd.DataFrame, forms: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    for r in attrs.itertuples(index=False):
        sid = r.settlement_id
        g.status[sid] = str(r.status_1910) if isinstance(r.status_1910, str) else ""
        g.okres_of[sid] = int(r.okres_id) if pd.notna(r.okres_id) else None
        g.parent_key[sid] = key(r.parent_1910) if isinstance(r.parent_1910, str) else ""
        okres_all = r.okres_all if isinstance(r.okres_all, str) else ""
        g.timeline[sid] = ({okres_token(o) for o in okres_all.split("|") if o.strip()}
                           | ({okres_token(r.okres_1910)} if isinstance(r.okres_1910, str) else set()))
        g.timeline[sid].discard("")
        g.court_polygon[sid] = int(r.court_id) if pd.notna(r.court_id) else None
        g.cs_name[sid] = r.cs_name
        # 0.7.0 (F1, F3): the earliest okres of the timeline, the 1910 name's forms
        first = next((o.strip() for o in okres_all.split("|") if o.strip()), "")
        if first:
            g.first_okres[sid] = first
        n1910 = getattr(r, "name_1910", None)
        if isinstance(n1910, str) and n1910.strip():
            g.forms_1910[sid] = form_set(key(f) for f in pn.cell_forms(n1910))
    for sid, form in zip(forms["settlement_id"], forms["form"]):
        k, oid = key(form), g.okres_of.get(sid)
        g.forms_of.setdefault(sid, set()).update(form_set([k]))
        _add(g.global_name, k, sid)
        if oid is not None:
            _add(g.lex, (k, oid), sid)
            _add(g.nospace, (nospace(k), oid), sid)
            if strip_qualifier(k) != k:                  # only qualified forms (see p2_qualifier)
                _add(g.qualifier, (strip_qualifier(k), oid), sid)


def _note_numbered(g: Gazetteer, k: str, oid: int, sid: str) -> None:
    """Record a **printed** register form ending in a Roman numeral (``velka upa ii``) under its base
    (``velka upa``). Only the register's forms: the ČSÚ lexicon's numerals (``NOVÁ VES I``,
    ``PETROVICE II``) are its own disambiguators of places that were all *Nová Ves* in 1910, and
    D-144 already decides those."""
    m = _KEY_NUMERAL_RE.match(k)
    if m:
        g.numbered.setdefault((m.group(1), oid), {}).setdefault(sid, set()).add(m.group(2))


def _register_indexes(g: Gazetteer, places: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    has = places[places["settlement_id"].notna() & places["okres_id"].notna()]
    for r in has.itertuples(index=False):
        target = g.reg if r.edition in PRIMARY_EDITIONS else g.reg_alt
        oid = int(r.okres_id)
        for form in pn.cell_forms(r.printed_name):
            k = key(form)
            _add(target, (k, oid), r.settlement_id)
            _add(g.nospace, (nospace(k), oid), r.settlement_id)
            _note_numbered(g, k, oid, r.settlement_id)
            if strip_qualifier(k) != k:
                _add(g.qualifier, (strip_qualifier(k), oid), r.settlement_id)
        if r.place_level == "municipality":
            g.reg_municipal.add(r.settlement_id)
    # every row of an okres, anchored or not, for the rulings queue (0.3.0)
    for r in places[places["okres_id"].notna()].itertuples(index=False):
        row_key = f"{r.edition}|{r.court_key}|{int(r.muni_seq)}|{int(r.settlement_seq)}"
        sid = r.settlement_id if pd.notna(r.settlement_id) else None
        for form in pn.cell_forms(r.printed_name):
            g.reg_rows.setdefault(int(r.okres_id), []).append((key(form), str(r.printed_name), sid, row_key))


#: viz on every row (0.4.0): a part row at most this share of the municipality row's population is
#: the cross-reference, not a second owner
XREF_PART_SHARE = 0.10


def _row_pop(r) -> float | None:
    v = getattr(r, "pop_total", None)
    return None if v is None or pd.isna(v) else float(v)


def xref_both_owner(use: list) -> tuple[object, list]:
    """``(kept row, dropped rows)`` when every row holding a settlement in one edition prints the
    ``viz`` / ``siehe`` marker (0.4.0): the text sits on both the real row and the cross-reference
    (*Pivoň, Stockau . odd. viz*: municipality 345, part 1), so :data:`_XREF_RE` cannot tell them
    apart. The one municipality-level row is kept when it is the most populous; a part row whose
    population is :data:`XREF_PART_SHARE` (10 %) of it or less is dropped. ``(None, [])`` when
    that does not leave one municipality (two municipality rows, a population missing, a part row
    above 10 %: *Záblatí* part 64 of 312 stays two owners)."""
    munis = [r for r in use if r.place_level == "municipality"]
    if len(munis) != 1 or _row_pop(munis[0]) is None:
        return None, []
    keep = munis[0]
    others = [r for r in use if (str(r.court_key), int(r.muni_seq)) != (str(keep.court_key), int(keep.muni_seq))]
    if any(_row_pop(r) is None or r.place_level != "part"
           or _row_pop(r) > XREF_PART_SHARE * _row_pop(keep) for r in others):
        return None, []
    return keep, others


def register_owners(places: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[dict, set, list]:
    """``({sid: owner}, {sids two municipalities hold}, [viz-on-every-row decisions])`` from the
    land's first edition holding it.

    A cross-reference row (``… odd. viz X``) names a detached piece filed elsewhere and owns nothing
    unless it is the only row holding the settlement; when **every** row is one, see
    :func:`xref_both_owner`. ``owner`` carries the row's register key, level, court, okres and the
    settlement_id of its municipality row (``None`` if unanchored).
    """
    muni_sid = {(e, str(c), int(m)): s for e, c, m, q, s in
                zip(places["edition"], places["court_key"], places["muni_seq"],
                    places["settlement_seq"], places["settlement_id"]) if q == 0 and pd.notna(s)}
    rows_by_sid: dict[str, list] = {}
    for r in places[places["settlement_id"].notna() & places["okres_id"].notna()].itertuples(index=False):
        xref = bool(_XREF_RE.search(str(r.printed_name)))
        rows_by_sid.setdefault(r.settlement_id, []).append((r, xref))
    owners, two, xref_both = {}, set(), []
    for sid, rows in rows_by_sid.items():
        land = int(rows[0][0].okres_id) // 1000
        for ed in EDITION_ORDER.get(land, ()):
            ed_rows = [(r, x) for r, x in rows if r.edition == ed]
            if not ed_rows:
                continue
            use = [r for r, x in ed_rows if not x] or [r for r, _x in ed_rows]
            if len({(str(r.court_key), int(r.muni_seq)) for r in use}) > 1:
                keep, dropped = (xref_both_owner(use) if all(x for _r, x in ed_rows) else (None, []))
                if keep is None:
                    two.add(sid)
                    break
                xref_both.append({"settlement_id": sid, "edition": ed,
                                  "kept": f"{ed}|{keep.court_key}|{int(keep.muni_seq)}|{int(keep.settlement_seq)}",
                                  "kept_pop": _row_pop(keep),
                                  "dropped": [f"{ed}|{r.court_key}|{int(r.muni_seq)}|{int(r.settlement_seq)}"
                                              f" ({_row_pop(r):g})" for r in dropped]})
                use = [keep]
            r = min(use, key=lambda r: int(r.settlement_seq))
            owners[sid] = {"edition": ed, "court_key": str(r.court_key), "muni_seq": int(r.muni_seq),
                           "settlement_seq": int(r.settlement_seq), "level": r.place_level,
                           "court_id": int(r.court_id) if pd.notna(r.court_id) else None,
                           "okres_id": int(r.okres_id),
                           "muni_sid": muni_sid.get((ed, str(r.court_key), int(r.muni_seq))),
                           "printed_name": str(r.printed_name),
                           "printed_keys": tuple(dict.fromkeys(
                               k for f in pn.cell_forms(r.printed_name)
                               for k in (key(f), key(f).replace("ß", "ss")))),
                           "printed_forms": form_set(key(f) for f in pn.cell_forms(r.printed_name))}
            break
    return owners, two, xref_both


def printed_split(form: str) -> list[str]:
    """A printed form and, when it is two capitalised names run together without a comma
    (``Novosady Blatiny``: the Moravian edition's *Novosady t. Blatiny*), each name as well.
    Each name must be 3+ letters (``Velká Úpa I`` and ``Lhota u Brna`` stay whole)."""
    form = str(form).strip()
    words = form.split()
    if (len(words) == 2 and all(len(w) >= 3 and w[0].isupper() and w.isalpha() for w in words)):
        return [form, *words]
    return [form]


def pooled_forms(places: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[str, set]:
    """``{sid: form_set}`` of the printed forms of **every** register row holding the settlement —
    both editions, municipality and part rows, cross-references included (0.3.0). The owner check
    refuses only when none of them shares a form with the settlement's own names: the Czech cell
    of *Doubravička* prints *Doubravice, Kleindoubra- witz*, the German cell *Doubravička*."""
    out: dict[str, set] = {}
    has = places[places["settlement_id"].notna()]
    for sid, cell in zip(has["settlement_id"], has["printed_name"]):
        out.setdefault(sid, set()).update(
            form_set(key(p) for f in pn.cell_forms(cell) for p in printed_split(f)))
    return out


def _prague_indexes(g: Gazetteer, attrs: pd.DataFrame, forms: pd.DataFrame,
                    places: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    for r in attrs.itertuples(index=False):
        m = _QUARTER_NAME_RE.match(str(r.name_1910 or ""))
        if m and m.group(1) in _ROMAN:
            g.quarters[_ROMAN[m.group(1)]] = r.settlement_id
            name = m.group(2)
            for f in [name, *re.split(r"\s*-\s*", name)]:
                _add(g.prague, key(f), r.settlement_id)
                _add(g.prague, nospace(key(f)), r.settlement_id)
    if LIBEN_VIII_SID in g.status and g.okres_of.get(LIBEN_VIII_SID) is None:
        g.quarters[8] = LIBEN_VIII_SID
    g.quarter_sids = set(g.quarters.values())
    for sid, form in zip(forms["settlement_id"], forms["form"]):
        no_okres_ring = (g.okres_of.get(sid) is None and bool(g.timeline.get(sid))
                         and g.timeline[sid] <= _RING_OKRES_NAMES)     # e.g. strasnice:1
        if g.okres_of.get(sid) in PRAGUE_AGGLOMERATION or sid in g.quarter_sids or no_okres_ring:
            _add(g.prague, key(form), sid)
    ring = places[places["okres_id"].isin(PRAGUE_AGGLOMERATION) & places["settlement_id"].notna()]
    for cell, sid in zip(ring["printed_name"], ring["settlement_id"]):
        for f in pn.cell_forms(cell):
            _add(g.prague, key(f), sid)


def _statutory(g: Gazetteer, districts: pd.DataFrame, attrs: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    ok = districts.drop_duplicates("okres_code")
    city_ids = {_okres_id(c) for c, cs in zip(ok["okres_code"], ok["okres_cs"])
                if "(město)" in str(cs)} | {PRAHA_OKRES_ID}
    for cid in city_ids:
        rows = attrs[attrs["okres_id"] == cid]
        if len(rows) == 1:
            g.statutory[cid] = rows["settlement_id"].iloc[0]
    g.statutory_sids = set(g.statutory.values())
    for cid in city_ids:
        g.city_pieces |= g.okres_names.get(cid, set())
    for oid in PRAGUE_AGGLOMERATION:
        g.city_pieces |= g.okres_names.get(oid, set())
    for sid in g.quarter_sids:
        g.city_pieces.add(key(g.cs_name.get(sid)))
    g.city_pieces |= LAND_WORDS
    g.city_pieces.discard("")


def greater_prague_sids(g: Gazetteer) -> tuple[set, dict]:
    """``(sids inside the 1922 annexation, {law name: sid or None})``.

    Each name of :data:`GREATER_PRAGUE_1922` is resolved inside the okres the law files it under
    (D-144: one id, else the one obec); a part or hamlet joins too (Pankrác of Nusle) when its
    parent, resolved **inside the hamlet's own 1910 okres** (register, then lexikon), is a joined
    obec — never by the parent's name alone across the five agglomeration okresy (0.1.0 put
    Bořanovice and Pakoměřice, hamlets of Karlín's Sedlec, under Smíchov's joined Sedlec, and
    Žabovřesky, of Smíchov's Záběhlice, under Vinohrady's). So does every register part of a joined
    municipality row. :data:`GREATER_PRAGUE_EXCLUDED` stays out either way.
    """
    resolved = {}
    for oid, names in GREATER_PRAGUE_1922.items():
        for name in names:
            ids = {s for s in g.prague.get(key(name), set())
                   if g.okres_of.get(s) == oid and s not in g.quarter_sids}
            v, val = decide(ids, _lex_status(g))
            resolved[name] = val if v == "ok" else None
    excluded = {key(n) for n in GREATER_PRAGUE_EXCLUDED}
    joiners = {s for n, s in resolved.items() if s and n not in GREATER_PRAGUE_PARTS_ONLY}
    out = {s for s in resolved.values() if s}
    for sid, pk in g.parent_key.items():
        oid = g.okres_of.get(sid)
        if not pk or oid not in PRAGUE_AGGLOMERATION or sid in out:
            continue
        if key(g.cs_name.get(sid)) in excluded:
            continue
        v, _t, parent = _lookup(pk, oid, g)
        if v == "ok" and parent != sid and parent in joiners:
            out.add(sid)
    out |= {sid for sid, o in g.owner.items() if o.get("muni_sid") in joiners
            and key(g.cs_name.get(sid)) not in excluded}
    return out, resolved


def greater_prague_check(g: Gazetteer) -> dict:
    """The lexikon's own view: ring obce whose timeline names no okres after the ring okresy."""
    lex = {sid for sid, oid in g.okres_of.items()
           if oid in PRAGUE_AGGLOMERATION - {PRAHA_OKRES_ID} and g.status.get(sid) == "obec"
           and g.timeline.get(sid) and g.timeline[sid] <= _RING_OKRES_NAMES}
    law, resolved = greater_prague_sids(g)
    law_obce = {s for s in resolved.values() if s}
    law_okres = {n: oid for oid, names in GREATER_PRAGUE_1922.items() for n in names}
    unresolved = sorted(n for n, s in resolved.items() if s is None)
    # documented exclusions (0.3.0): a law name with no settlements_1910 row in its okres is left
    # out of the resolution, with every settlement of that name elsewhere (Zátiší of Modřany)
    detail = {n: {"okres_id": law_okres[n],
                  "settlements_of_the_name": [f"{s} {g.cs_name.get(s)} (okres {g.okres_of.get(s)})"
                                              for s in sorted(g.global_name.get(key(n), set()))],
                  "note": "no settlements_1910 row of this name in the okres the law names: "
                          "excluded from the 1922 resolution"} for n in unresolved}
    return {"law_names": sum(len(v) for v in GREATER_PRAGUE_1922.values()),
            "law_resolved": len(law_obce),
            "law_unresolved": unresolved,
            "law_unresolved_detail": detail,
            "lexikon_timeline_obce": len(lex),
            "in_law_not_timeline": sorted(g.cs_name[s] for s in law_obce - lex),
            "in_timeline_not_law": sorted(g.cs_name[s] for s in lex - law_obce),
            "settlements_flagged": len(law)}


def build_gazetteer(settlements: pd.DataFrame, places: pd.DataFrame, districts: pd.DataFrame,
                    aliases: pd.DataFrame | None, municipalities: pd.DataFrame,
                    heals: pd.DataFrame | None = None, foreign_names=None) -> Gazetteer:
    """All indexes from the frames (``places`` already carrying the anchor overrides).

    Since 0.3.0 the rows of a municipality that :func:`contradicted_keys` finds contradicted for a
    settlement do not hold that settlement in the gazetteer (they are neither indexed nor an owner):
    an automatic *refusal* of a frozen anchor, never a new one (the cz row *Kostomlátky* no longer
    answers to ``kostomlaty-nad-labem:1``; the register join then reports the table's row as
    differing).

    *foreign_names* (0.6.0): okres and district names outside the Czech lands — a set, or
    :func:`foreign_name_keys`'s ``{"districts", "obce"}`` (an obec name a Czech-lands settlement also
    carries is dropped); :data:`FOREIGN_OKRES` is always added, a Czech okres or court name never."""
    heals = heals if heals is not None else pn.heal_frame(settlements)
    attrs = pn.healed_attributes(settlements, heals)
    forms = pn.name_index(settlements, heals)
    g = Gazetteer(okres_names=_okres_names(districts), seat_court=_seat_courts(districts))
    _lexikon_indexes(g, attrs, forms)
    g.muni_keys_contradicted = contradicted_keys(places, g.forms_of)
    _owners_before, two_before, _x = register_owners(places)
    places = drop_contradicted(places, g.muni_keys_contradicted)
    _register_indexes(g, places)
    g.owner, g.two_owners, g.xref_both = register_owners(places)
    # 0.4.0: dropping a contradicted row is a refusal, never a new link — a settlement it would take
    # out of two_owners stays there (reported in contradicted_freed)
    g.contradicted_freed = sorted(two_before - g.two_owners)
    g.two_owners |= set(g.contradicted_freed)
    _global_indexes(g)
    for r in districts.itertuples(index=False):          # court names name their okres too
        for v in (getattr(r, "gerichtsbezirk_cs", None), getattr(r, "gerichtsbezirk_de", None)):
            if isinstance(v, str) and key(v):
                for kk in (key(v), nospace(key(v))):
                    g.okres_by_name.setdefault(kk, set()).add(_okres_id(r.okres_code))
    _prague_indexes(g, attrs, forms, places)
    _statutory(g, districts, attrs)
    g.greater_prague, _ = greater_prague_sids(g)
    g.pool_forms = pooled_forms(places)
    g.muni_keys = municipality_row_keys(places)
    g.register_munis = set(municipalities["settlement_id"].dropna())
    g.register_muni_key = municipality_keys(municipalities)
    if g.register_munis and not g.register_muni_key:
        raise ValueError("register_municipalities carries no key columns (edition, court_key or "
                         "court_id, muni_seq; or register_key): the join compares keys since 0.3.0")
    g.register_key_sid = {k: s for s, k in g.register_muni_key.items()}
    if aliases is not None:
        viz_okres = aliases["viz_okres"] if "viz_okres" in aliases.columns else [None] * len(aliases)
        for a, t, o in zip(aliases["cs_name"], aliases["viz_target"], viz_okres):
            if isinstance(a, str) and isinstance(t, str):
                _add(g.alias, key(a), key(t))
                # 0.14.0 (K1): the row's modern okres with it ("" where the row names none)
                _add(g.alias_okres, key(a), (key(t), okres_token(o) if isinstance(o, str) else ""))
    _later_indexes(g, places, foreign_names)
    return g


def foreign_name_keys(districts_hu: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
                      settlements_hu: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
    """Keys of the Hungarian frame's names (0.6.0): ``districts`` — every district and county name
    (``districts_hu_1910``: Slovak, Magyar and modern names of each járás and vármegye;
    ``settlements_hu_1910``: each obec's 1910 okres) — and ``obce`` — every Slovak obec name (an
    interwar okres was named after its seat: *Modrý Kameň*, *Bánovce nad Bebravou*). What a VÚA okres
    string names when it is not a Czech-lands okres; an obec name some Czech-lands settlement also
    carries (*Vysočany*) is left out by :func:`build_gazetteer`."""
    out: dict[str, set[str]] = {"districts": set(), "obce": set()}
    for part, frame, cols in (("districts", districts_hu, ("name_sk", "name_sk_alt", "name_sk_modern", "name_hu",
