            return "ambiguous", "p4_okres_timeline", tuple(sorted(ids))
    return "none", "", None


def names_inside(k: str, oid, g: Gazetteer, limit: int = 12) -> set:
    """Settlements of okres *oid* whose name holds *k* as a whole word inside a longer name (0.4.0):
    *Lhota* in okres Tábor (*Balkova Lhota*, *Dlouhá Lhota* …), *Ouběnice* in okres Benešov
    (*Ouběnice 1. díl*). P4 must not send such a bare name to a namesake elsewhere. At most
    *limit* ids are returned (the refusal's candidate list)."""
    if oid is None or not k:
        return set()
    pat = re.compile(rf"(?<!\S){re.escape(k)}(?!\S)")
    out: set = set()
    for kk, sids in g.okres_keys.get(oid, {}).items():
        if kk != k and pat.search(kk):
            out |= sids
    return set(sorted(out)[:limit])


# ── the record ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def german_verdict(forms, clean: str, oid, g: Gazetteer, okres_named: bool = False,
                   keep_okres_town: bool = False) -> tuple[str, object]:
    """The VÚA German cell (0.4.0): every form looked up in the okres and the **union** of their
    settlements taken, so *Nieder-Ebersdorf; Ober-Ebersdorf* (Dolní and Horní Habartice) or
    *Königreich I.; II.; III.* come out ambiguous instead of the first form's settlement; then the
    numbered-sibling guard on the record's own name (*Království* is not ``kralovstvi-i:1``).

    On the union the obec-first rule of D-144 is **not** applied: it settles one name several
    settlements answer to, while the forms of VÚA's list name the places of its candidate list, so
    two settlements are ambiguous (*Lochčitz-Hottowitz; Hottowies*: Otovice and Hostovice). One
    settlement is taken only when **every** form gives it; when some forms give nothing and the rest
    one settlement, the cell decides nothing (``("partial", ids)``): the later P2 tiers and P4 run as
    before 0.4.0, and only if none of them matches is the record refused ``ambiguous:p2_german`` with
    those ids (*Hradiště*, okres Znojmo, *Znaim-Pöltenberg; Erdberg*: only *Erdberg* = Hrádek
    resolves, and Hrádek is VÚA's second candidate; *Albeřice* (*Nieder-Albendorf; Ober-Albendorf*):
    only Dolní Albeřice resolves). A form naming the record's own okres (*Javorník, okres Frývaldov
    (Jauernig; Freiwaldau)*) is dropped unless the record's name is the okres's (a cell of 2+ forms
    only; one form is read as before 0.4.0).

    0.9.0 (E5): where the cell names the okres (*okres_named*), a single German form that is a name of
    that okres's town (``okres_names``: *Starkenbach* for okres Jilemnice) is VÚA's German name of the
    okres, not of the place, and is dropped too — unless the Czech head is a spelling of the town
    (difflib ratio >= :data:`GERMAN_OKRES_TOWN_RATIO`): *Rochlice, okres Jilemncie (Starkenbach)* is not
    Jilemnice, *Pessinkau ?, okres Domažlice (Taus)* not Domažlice.

    0.10.0 (G6): not when VÚA's own candidate reading of the cell is the okres town itself
    (*keep_okres_town*, :func:`okres_town_read`: *Aisič, okres Ústí nad Labem ? (Ústí nad Labem, okres Ústí nad
    Labem ?) (Aussig - ?)* — *Aussig* is the German of that reading, the head a garbled *Aussig*)."""
    k = key(clean)
    if len(forms) >= 2 and oid is not None and k not in g.okres_names.get(oid, set()):
        forms = tuple(f for f in forms if key(f) not in g.okres_names.get(oid, set()))
    if (_on("E5") and okres_named and len(forms) == 1 and oid is not None and not keep_okres_town
            and key(forms[0]) in g.okres_names.get(oid, set())
            and not any(difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, k, n).ratio() >= GERMAN_OKRES_TOWN_RATIO
                        for n in g.okres_names.get(oid, set()))):
        forms = ()
    if not forms:
        return "none", None
    if len(forms) == 1:                          # one form: as before 0.4.0
        v, _t, val = _lookup(key(forms[0]), oid, g, alt=True)
    else:
        ids: set = set()
        silent = False
        for f in forms:
            fv, _t, fval = _lookup(key(f), oid, g, alt=True)
            if fv == "ok":
                ids.add(fval)
            elif fv == "ambiguous":
                ids |= set(fval)
            else:
                silent = True
        v, val = (("ambiguous", tuple(sorted(ids))) if len(ids) > 1
                  else ("ok", next(iter(ids))) if ids and not silent
                  else ("partial", tuple(sorted(ids))) if ids else ("none", None))
        if v == "partial":                  # decided by the caller after the later tiers
            return v, val
    if v == "none":
        return v, val
    return numbered_guard(k, oid, v, val, g)


def _variants(clean: str, alts, german, oid, g, uncertain, vua: bool = False, home=None):
    """P2 in order; yields ``(verdict, tier, value)`` until one is not ``none``. *german* is the
    German cell's verdict (0.4.0, :func:`german_verdict`; a ``partial`` one is left to the caller).
    No alternate or German form resolves to ``praha:1`` unless the string itself is the city
    (:func:`_piece_lookup`'s rule). *home* (0.12.0, I2): the soldier's home values, for :func:`p2_qualifier`.
    0.14.0 (K1): a bare name sent by an alternate, the German form or an alias to a settlement not of its name is
    held against the name's namesakes in the okres (:func:`bare_variant_verdict`)."""
    city = (prague_shape(clean) or ("",))[0] == "city"
    k = key(clean)
    for alt in alts:
        v, t, val = _lookup(key(alt), oid, g, alt=True)
        if v == "ok" and val == PRAHA_SID and not city:
            continue
        if v != "none":
            yield bare_variant_verdict(k, oid, v, "p2_alternate", val, g, home)     # 0.14.0 (K1)
            return
    v, val = german or ("none", None)
    if v in ("ok", "ambiguous") and not (v == "ok" and val == PRAHA_SID and not city):
        yield bare_variant_verdict(k, oid, v, "p2_german", val, g, home)           # 0.14.0 (K1)
        return
    for step in (lambda: _lookup(k, oid, g, alt=True),
                 lambda: _variant_tables(k, oid, g),
                 lambda: p2_split(clean, oid, g, uncertain, vua),
                 lambda: p2_qualifier(k, oid, g, home)):
        res = step()
        if res[0] != "none":
            if res[1] == "p2_alias":
                res = bare_variant_verdict(k, oid, res[0], res[1], res[2], g, home)  # 0.14.0 (K1)
            yield res
            return


def _german_tuple(german, german_forms=None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """The German forms the matcher tries: every form of the raw cell when it holds 2+ (0.4.0,
    ``locations.german_forms``), else the first usable form of the German column."""
    forms = tuple(f for f in (german_forms or ()) if f)
    if len(forms) >= 2:
        return forms
    one = german_form(german)
    return (one,) if one else ()


def qmark_readings(text, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> tuple[str, ...] | None:
    """I1 (0.12.0): the pieces of a VÚA cell written around a ``?`` (a ``?`` with a space on either side, as
    :func:`clean_birthplace` splits) that remain once a piece naming the record's own okres *oid*, its seat or a big
    city (:func:`okres_locator`) is dropped — *Podbořany ? Mukoděly* | Podbořany → ``("Mukoděly",)``, *Benešov)
    ?Divišov* → ``("Divišov",)``, the cell having lost the ``(`` of VÚA's ``(? Reading, okres X ?)``. ``None`` when
    the cell has no such ``?``, no piece is a locator or every piece is one, or the record has no okres."""
    if oid is None or not isinstance(text, str) or "?" not in text:
        return None
    pieces = [p for p in re.split(r"\s+\?\s*|\?\s+", unicodedata.normalize("NFC", text))
              if clean_birthplace(p)[0]]
    if len(pieces) < 2:
        return None
    locator = [okres_locator(clean_birthplace(p)[0], oid, g) for p in pieces]
    if not any(locator) or all(locator):
        return None
    return tuple(p for p, loc in zip(pieces, locator) if not loc)


def _qmark_match(readings, okres_id, stated_okres, german, uncertain, g: Gazetteer, german_forms, vua,
                 keep_okres_town, home) -> dict:
    """I1 (0.12.0): :func:`match_birthplace` on each reading :func:`qmark_readings` left. One reading: its result.
    Several: the settlement they all give, else (two settlements, or a reading D-144 could not decide) refused
    ``ambiguous:qmark_readings`` with every settlement as candidates; none resolving: the first reading's result."""
    found = [match_birthplace(r, okres_id, stated_okres, german, uncertain, g, german_forms=german_forms, vua=vua,
                              keep_okres_town=keep_okres_town, home=home, stated=True) for r in readings]
    if len(found) == 1:
        return found[0]
    sids = {f["sid"] for f in found if f["sid"] is not None}
    amb = {c for f in found if (f["refusal"] or "").startswith("ambiguous") for c in (f["candidates"] or ())}
    if len(sids) == 1 and not amb:
        return next(f for f in found if f["sid"] is not None)
    if sids or amb:
        return {**found[0], "sid": None, "tier": "qmark_readings", "refusal": "ambiguous:qmark_readings",
                "candidates": tuple(sorted(sids | amb)), "okres_1910": int(okres_id), "quarter": None, "tie": None}
    return found[0]


def match_birthplace(text, okres_id, stated_okres=None, german=None, uncertain=False,
                     g: Gazetteer | None = None, german_forms=None, vua: bool = False,
                     keep_okres_town: bool = False, home=None, stated: bool | None = None) -> dict:
    """One birthplace → ``{clean, sid, tier, refusal, candidates, okres_1910, quarter}``.
    *german_forms* (0.4.0): every form of the VÚA German cell (:func:`_german_tuple`); *keep_okres_town*
    (0.10.0, G6): :func:`german_verdict` keeps a German form naming the okres town. *home* (0.12.0, I2): the
    soldier's home values (:func:`home_muni_in_okres`). 0.12.0 (I1): a VÚA cell (*vua*) whose ``?`` pieces include an
    okres locator is matched on the other pieces (:func:`qmark_readings`, :func:`_qmark_match`). 0.13.0 (J4): only
    where *okres_id* is the okres the record **stated** — *stated* ``True`` (:func:`link_one`'s stated-okres path);
    ``False`` from the D-a, timeline and candidate paths, which match in an okres the string, the name or a
    candidate supplied; ``None`` (a direct call) reads *okres_id* as stated, as 0.12.0 did."""
    oid = int(okres_id) if okres_id is not None and pd.notna(okres_id) else None
    if vua and _on("I1") and not (stated is False and _on("J4")):
        readings = qmark_readings(text, oid, g)
        if readings is not None:
            return _qmark_match(readings, okres_id, stated_okres, german, uncertain, g, german_forms, vua,
                                keep_okres_town, home)
    clean, alts = clean_birthplace(text)
    if _on("K1") and clean is not None:             # 0.14.0 (K1): an alternate saying where the place lies
        clean, alts = locator_alternates(clean, alts, oid, g)
    gforms = _german_tuple(german, german_forms)
    out = {"clean": clean, "sid": None, "tier": None, "refusal": None, "candidates": None,
           "okres_1910": oid, "quarter": None, "alternates": bool(alts), "tie": None,
           "name_keys": None if clean is None else name_keys(clean, alts, gforms, g)}
    if clean is None:
        out["refusal"] = "no_municipality"
        return out
    if oid is not None and oid in g.statutory and oid != PRAHA_OKRES_ID:
        return {**out, "sid": g.statutory[oid], "tier": "statutory_city"}
    parallel = praha_parallel(text, stated_okres)
    located = (locator_object_verdict(clean, alts, oid, g) if parallel is None and _on("K1") and _on("L4")
               else None)          # 0.15.0 (L4): an unjoined locator read by its object
    if parallel is not None:
        x_clean, x_alts = clean_birthplace(parallel)
        out["name_keys"] = name_keys(x_clean, x_alts, gforms, g) if x_clean else out["name_keys"]
        res = _parallel_verdict(x_clean, oid, g)
    elif located is not None:
        res = (*located, None, ())
    else:
        res = _first_verdict(clean, alts, oid, stated_okres, gforms, uncertain, g, vua, keep_okres_town, home)
    v, tier, val, quarter, tie = res
    out.update(tier=tier or None, quarter=quarter, tie=tie or None)
    if v == "ok":
        out["sid"] = val
        out["okres_1910"] = _okres_1910(val, oid, tier, g)
    elif v == "ambiguous":
        out["refusal"], out["candidates"] = f"ambiguous:{tier}", val
    elif v == "refused":
        out["refusal"] = val
    else:
        out["refusal"] = "no_okres_1910" if oid is None else "unmatched"
    return out


def name_keys(clean: str, alts=(), german=None, g: Gazetteer | None = None) -> frozenset:
    """Every name the record could have been matched on, as :func:`form_set` forms: the string, its
    alternates, the VÚA German form, its split pieces, the name a Prague form carries, and the
    ``viz`` alias targets of each. P5 compares these with the owner row's printed forms. *german*
    is the German column's value or (0.4.0) a tuple of its forms."""
    ks = {key(clean), *(key(a) for a in alts)}
    gfs = german if isinstance(german, tuple) else ((german_form(german),) if german_form(german) else ())
    ks |= {key(f) for f in gfs if f}
    ks |= {key(p) for p in re.split(r"\s*[-–/]\s*|\s*,\s*", clean) if p.strip()}
    shape = prague_shape(clean)
    if shape is not None and shape[2]:
        ks.add(key(shape[2]))
    if g is not None:
        ks |= {t for k in list(ks) for t in g.alias.get(k, ())}
    return frozenset(form_set(ks))


def _stated_tokens(stated, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> set[str]:
    """The record's stated okres as timeline tokens: the string and the backbone's names of its id."""
    toks = {okres_token(stated)} if stated else set()
    toks |= {nospace(n) for n in g.okres_names.get(oid, set())} if oid is not None else set()
    toks.discard("")
    return toks


def move_allowed(sid: str, stated, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """The decision on okres corrections: the settlement's 1910 okres may replace the stated one only
    when the stated okres is in the settlement's ``okres_all`` timeline."""
    return bool(_stated_tokens(stated, oid, g) & g.timeline.get(sid, set()))


def _first_verdict(clean, alts, oid, stated, german, uncertain, g, vua: bool = False,
                   keep_okres_town: bool = False, home=None) -> tuple:
    """P1, P3, P2, P4 in that order; ``(verdict, tier, value, quarter, tie)``.

    A Prague-shaped string (``Praha-…``, ``… Praha``) skips P1 and P2 in the agglomeration or with
    no okres at all: if P3 cannot place the name it is refused, never split down to ``praha:1``.
    With a stated okres **outside** the agglomeration P1 runs there first, on the string and on the
    name a Prague form carries (``Kyje, Praha``, okres Semily → Semily's Kyje); a P3 reading that
    would then move the record to an okres not in the settlement's timeline is refused
    ``prague_okres_conflict``.
    """
    shape = prague_shape(clean)
    in_prague = oid is None or oid in PRAGUE_AGGLOMERATION
    outside = oid is not None and oid not in PRAGUE_AGGLOMERATION
    if oid is not None and (shape is None or outside):
        # the name of a "X, Praha" / "Praha-X" form only; a district number (Praha XI.-Žižkov) is
        # Prague itself and goes to P3 (and its conflict check), never to a namesake hamlet
        named = [key(shape[2])] if shape and shape[0] == "named" and shape[2] else []
        for k in dict.fromkeys([key(clean), *named]):
            v, t, val = _lookup(k, oid, g)
            if v != "none":
                tie = german_tie_break(k, oid, t, val, german, clean, g) if v == "ok" else None
                if tie is not None:                  # 0.5.0 (D4d)
                    return "ok", "p2_german", tie, None, ()
                return v, t, val, None, ()
    if shape is not None or (oid is not None and oid in PRAGUE_AGGLOMERATION):
        res = p3_prague(clean, oid, g, alts)
        if (res[0] == "ok" and outside and _okres_1910(res[2], oid, res[1], g) != oid
                and not move_allowed(res[2], stated, oid, g)):
            return "refused", "p3_prague", "prague_okres_conflict", res[3], ()
        if res[0] != "none":
            return res
        if shape is not None and in_prague:
            return "refused", "p3_prague", "praha_name_unknown", None, ()
    stated_key = key(stated) if stated else ""
    if oid is None:
        v, t, val = p4_timeline(key(clean), stated_key, None, g)
        return v, t, val, None, ()
    german = german if isinstance(german, tuple) else _german_tuple(german)
    gv = (german_verdict(german, clean, oid, g, okres_named=bool(stated), keep_okres_town=keep_okres_town)
          if german else ("none", None))
    for v, t, val in _variants(clean, alts, gv, oid, g, uncertain, vua, home):
        if v == "refused" and val in ("qualifier_conflict", "head_in_okres"):
            # the okres holds the head under another qualifier: only the exact name elsewhere
            v4, t4, val4 = p4_timeline(key(clean), stated_key, oid, g, exact_only=True)
            if v4 == "ok":
                return v4, t4, val4, None, ()
        if v == "refused" and val == "qualifier_conflict" and _on("J3"):
            fuzzy = qualifier_fuzzy(key(clean), oid, g)          # 0.13.0 (J3): a misspelt qualifier
            if fuzzy is None and _on("L5"):
                fuzzy = qualifier_stem(key(clean), oid, g)       # 0.15.0 (L5): another case or preposition
            if fuzzy is not None:
                return "ok", "p2_qualifier_fuzzy", fuzzy, None, ()
        return v, t, val, None, ()
    v, t, val = p4_timeline(key(clean), stated_key, oid, g)
    if v == "refused" and val == "qualifier_conflict" and _on("J3"):
        fuzzy = qualifier_fuzzy(key(clean), oid, g)              # 0.13.0 (J3): P4's refusal, the same reading
        if fuzzy is None and _on("L5"):
            fuzzy = qualifier_stem(key(clean), oid, g)           # 0.15.0 (L5)
        if fuzzy is not None:
            return "ok", "p2_qualifier_fuzzy", fuzzy, None, ()
    if v == "none" and gv[0] == "partial":
        # 0.4.0: VÚA's German list names several places, some resolve, nothing else matched
        return "ambiguous", "p2_german", gv[1], None, ()
    if v == "none" and _on("K1"):       # 0.14.0 (K1): an alias set aside answers with the namesakes, not unmatched
        res = alias_namesake_refusal(key(clean), oid, g, home)
        if res is not None:
            return (*res, None, ())
    if v == "none" and _on("K1") and _on("L2") and alias_other_okres(key(clean), oid, g):
        return "refused", "p2_alias", "alias_other_okres", None, ()    # 0.15.0 (L2): a renaming of another okres
    return v, t, val, None, ()


def german_tie_break(k: str, oid, tier: str, val, german, clean, g: Gazetteer):
    """0.5.0 (D4d): the settlement the record's VÚA German form names, when P1's D-144 chose *val*
    among several settlements of the name *k* by status alone and the German form resolves in the
    okres to exactly one **other** of them; else ``None``. *Oldřichov (Ulgersdorf), okres Děčín*:
    ``oldrichov`` answers to the obec ``oldrichov:2`` (printed *Ullgersdorf*, court Děčín, 2,188)
    and the osada ``oldrichov:1`` (1910 *Ulgersdorf*, part 5 of *Franzenthal-Ulgersdorf*, 456);
    the German form is the osada's 1910 name, the register's spelling of it and its lexikon German
    name, and nothing else in the okres. D-144's obec preference settles a name with nothing else
    to go on; here the record says more. One VÚA record in 0.4.1."""
    table = {"p1_register": g.reg, "p1_lexikon": g.lex}.get(tier or "")
    forms = german if isinstance(german, tuple) else _german_tuple(german)
    if table is None or not forms:
        return None
    ids = set(table.get((k, oid)) or ())
    if len(ids) < 2 or val not in ids:
        return None
    gv, gval = german_verdict(forms, clean, oid, g)
    return gval if gv == "ok" and gval in ids and gval != val else None


def praha_parallel(text, stated) -> str | None:
    """*X* of ``Praha, X`` when the stated okres is ``Praha, Y`` / ``Praha; Y``: two parallel
    two-value lists (Praha in Praha, or X in Y), so X is only an alternate (0.3.0)."""
    if not isinstance(text, str) or not isinstance(stated, str):
        return None
    m, s = _PRAHA_LIST_RE.match(text), _PRAHA_LIST_RE.match(stated)
    if not (m and s) or prague_shape(text) is None:
        return None
    return m.group(1).strip()


def _parallel_verdict(x_clean, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> tuple:
    """X of a parallel ``Praha, X`` / ``Praha, Y`` list inside the record's okres (resolved from Y
    by :mod:`records_geo`): P1, the de-bohemia forms, the space-free and alias tables, tier
    ``p2_alternate`` (the link is flagged uncertain); else refused ``praha_parallel_unmatched``."""
    if not x_clean or oid is None:
        return "refused", "p2_alternate", "praha_parallel_unmatched", None, ()
    v, _t, val = _lookup_any(key(x_clean), oid, g)
    if v == "none":
        return "refused", "p2_alternate", "praha_parallel_unmatched", None, ()
    return v, "p2_alternate", val, None, ()


def _okres_1910(sid: str, oid, tier: str, g: Gazetteer):
    """The settlement's own 1910 okres where the tier may move it (P3, P4); else the record's."""
    if sid in g.quarter_sids or sid == PRAHA_SID:
        return PRAHA_OKRES_ID
    if tier.startswith(("p3", "p4")):
        return g.okres_of.get(sid) or (g.owner.get(sid) or {}).get("okres_id") or oid
    return oid


# ── P5: roll-up ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def owner_check(sid: str, keys, g: Gazetteer) -> tuple[object, bool, bool]:
    """``(mismatch, disjoint, conflict)`` for a settlement's register owner row.

    *mismatch*: none of the record's name *keys* (:func:`name_keys`) is a form the owner row prints
    (``None`` when no keys are given or the row prints nothing). *disjoint*: the settlement's own
    lexicon names and the owner row's printed forms share no form. *conflict*: disjoint, **and** a
    form the row prints is the lexicon name of another settlement of the row's okres — the anchor
    puts the settlement on a row that prints a different place (0.1.0's Kostomlaty:
    ``kostomlaty-nad-labem:1`` on the row printing *Kostomlátky*, which is ``kostomlatky:2``).

    Disjoint alone is not evidence of a wrong anchor (the build reports the births it covers as
    ``owner_disjoint_unrefused``); nearly all are genuine — the Czech edition printing only the German name
    (*Tannwald*, *Gabel*), a 1910 spelling (*Horní Cerekew*, *Labská Týnice*), OCR damage
    (*Černoš n*), two forms without a comma. P5 refuses on *conflict* only and flags the rest
    through *mismatch*.

    Since 0.3.0 *mismatch* and *disjoint* read the printed forms of **every** register row holding
    the settlement (:func:`pooled_forms`): the Czech row of *Hněvětice* is OCR-damaged (*Rvasice,
    Rwasitz*, pop. 19) while the German row and the Czech part row print *Hněvětice*.
    """
    own = g.owner.get(sid) or {}
    printed = (own.get("printed_forms") or set()) | (g.pool_forms.get(sid) or set())
    if not printed:
        return None, False, False
    mismatch = None if keys is None else not (set(keys) & printed)
    own_forms = g.forms_of.get(sid) or set()
    disjoint = bool(own_forms) and not (own_forms & printed)
    conflict = disjoint and any(s != sid for k in conflict_keys(own)
                                for s in g.lex.get((k, own.get("okres_id")), ()))
    return mismatch, disjoint, conflict


def conflict_keys(own: dict) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """The owner row's printed keys for the conflict test, split as :func:`pooled_forms` splits them
    (0.4.0): *Neustift, Novosady Blatiny* → ``neustift``, ``novosady blatiny``, ``novosady``,
    ``blatiny`` — 0.3.0 tested the unsplit keys, so ``lhota:36`` on Blatiny's row was not refused."""
    printed = own.get("printed_name")
    if not printed:
        return tuple(own.get("printed_keys", ()))
    return tuple(dict.fromkeys(k for f in pn.cell_forms(printed) for p in printed_split(f)
                               for k in (key(p), key(p).replace("ß", "ss"))))


def roll_up(sid: str | None, okres_1910, g: Gazetteer, keys=None) -> dict:
    """The municipality, court and link unit of a matched settlement; *keys* (:func:`name_keys`)
    feed the owner check (:func:`owner_check`)."""
    out = {"municipality_settlement_id": None, "municipality_source": None, "register_row_key": None,
           "register_key": None, "court_id_1910": None, "court_source": None, "link_unit": "none",
           "rollup_refusal": None, "owner_mismatch": None}
    if sid is None:
        return out
    if sid in g.statutory_sids or sid in g.quarter_sids:
        city = PRAHA_SID if sid in g.quarter_sids else sid
        court = g.court_polygon.get(city)
        return {**out, "municipality_settlement_id": city, "municipality_source": "statutory_okres",
                "register_key": owner_muni_key(city, g),
                "court_id_1910": court, "court_source": "polygon" if court else None,
                "link_unit": "statutory_okres"}
    if sid in g.two_owners:
        return {**out, "rollup_refusal": "two_owners"}
    own = g.owner.get(sid)
    if own:
        mismatch, disjoint, conflict = owner_check(sid, keys, g)
        out.update(register_row_key=f"{own['edition']}|{own['court_key']}|{own['muni_seq']}|{own['settlement_seq']}",
                   owner_mismatch=True if disjoint else mismatch)
        if conflict:
            return {**out, "rollup_refusal": "owner_name_conflict"}
        out.update(court_id_1910=own["court_id"], court_source="register")
        if own["level"] == "municipality":
            out.update(municipality_settlement_id=sid, municipality_source="self",
                       register_key=f"{own['edition']}|{own['court_key']}|{own['muni_seq']}")
        elif own["muni_sid"]:
            # 0.4.0: a part of a municipality row whose own anchor conflicts with its printed name
            # (Samotín, a part of the Neustift/Novosady Blatiny row anchored to lhota:36) is refused
            if owner_check(own["muni_sid"], None, g)[2]:
                return {**out, "rollup_refusal": "owner_name_conflict"}
            out.update(municipality_settlement_id=own["muni_sid"], municipality_source="register_part",
                       register_key=f"{own['edition']}|{own['court_key']}|{own['muni_seq']}")
    if out["municipality_settlement_id"] is None:
        muni, source = _lexikon_municipality(sid, okres_1910, g)
        out.update(municipality_settlement_id=muni, municipality_source=source,
                   register_key=owner_muni_key(muni, g) if muni else None)
    if out["court_id_1910"] is None and g.court_polygon.get(sid):
        out.update(court_id_1910=g.court_polygon[sid], court_source="polygon")
    if out["municipality_settlement_id"] is None:
        out["rollup_refusal"] = "no_municipality_1910"
    else:
        out["link_unit"] = "municipality"
    return out


def owner_muni_key(muni_sid, g: Gazetteer) -> str | None:
    """``edition|court_key|muni_seq`` of the register municipality row that holds *muni_sid* in the
    gazetteer (overrides and applied rulings included); ``None`` when no municipality row does."""
    own = g.owner.get(muni_sid) if muni_sid else None
    if not own or own.get("level") != "municipality":
        return None
    return f"{own['edition']}|{own['court_key']}|{own['muni_seq']}"


def municipality_row_keys(places: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[str, set]:
    """``{sid: {"edition|court_key|muni_seq", …}}`` of every register **municipality** row holding
    the settlement in the gazetteer's register (overrides and applied rulings included), in either
    Bohemian edition: the Czech and German rows of one municipality carry different ``muni_seq``
    (*Dolní Kralovice* is cz 10 and de-bohemia 40), and ``register_municipalities`` keys Bohemia on
    the Czech row except where only the German edition prints a municipality."""
    m = places[(places["place_level"] == "municipality") & places["settlement_id"].notna()]
    out: dict[str, set] = {}
    for sid, ed, ck, ms in zip(m["settlement_id"], m["edition"], m["court_key"], m["muni_seq"]):
        out.setdefault(str(sid), set()).add(f"{ed}|{ck}|{int(ms)}")
    return out


def contradicted_keys(places: pd.DataFrame, forms_of: dict) -> dict[str, set]:
    """``{sid: {keys}}`` of municipality rows holding a settlement that the other rows holding it
    contradict on **both** name and population (0.3.0): the row's municipality (the row and every
    part row of it holding the settlement) prints none of the settlement's names, while another
    municipality row holding it prints one and gives another 1910 population.

    This keeps the 0.2.0 Kostomlaty refusal alive after the owner check started pooling the forms of
    both editions: ``kostomlaty-nad-labem:1`` is held by the Czech row *Kostomlátky* (pop. 566) and
    the German row *Großkostomlat, Kostomlaty* (816), so the Czech row is not its municipality — while
    *Doubravička* (Czech *Doubravice, Kleindoubra- witz* 270, German *… Doubravička …* 270) and
    *Hněvětice* (the Czech municipality prints the name on its part row) are not contradicted."""
    held = places[places["settlement_id"].notna()]
    forms_at: dict[tuple, set] = {}
    for sid, ed, ck, ms, cell in zip(held["settlement_id"], held["edition"], held["court_key"],
                                     held["muni_seq"], held["printed_name"]):
        forms_at.setdefault((str(sid), f"{ed}|{ck}|{int(ms)}"), set()).update(
            form_set(key(p) for f in pn.cell_forms(cell) for p in printed_split(f)))
    m = held[held["place_level"] == "municipality"]
    pop = {(str(s), f"{e}|{c}|{int(q)}"): (int(v) if pd.notna(v) else None)
           for s, e, c, q, v in zip(m["settlement_id"], m["edition"], m["court_key"], m["muni_seq"],
                                    m["pop_total"] if "pop_total" in m.columns else [None] * len(m))}
    by_sid: dict[str, list] = {}
    for (sid, k) in pop:
        by_sid.setdefault(sid, []).append(k)
    out: dict[str, set] = {}
    for sid, keys in by_sid.items():
        if len(keys) < 2:
            continue
        own = forms_of.get(sid) or set()
        named = {k for k in keys if forms_at.get((sid, k), set()) & own}
        for k in set(keys) - named:
            pk = pop[(sid, k)]
            if pk is not None and any(pop[(sid, n)] is not None and pop[(sid, n)] != pk for n in named):
                out.setdefault(sid, set()).add(k)
    return out


def drop_contradicted(places: pd.DataFrame, contradicted: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """*places* with the settlement emptied on every row (municipality and part) of a municipality
    :func:`contradicted_keys` found contradicted for that settlement; a copy, input untouched."""
    if not contradicted:
        return places
    bad = {(s, k) for s, ks in contradicted.items() for k in ks}
    hit = [(str(s), f"{e}|{c}|{int(m)}") in bad if pd.notna(s) else False
           for s, e, c, m in zip(places["settlement_id"], places["edition"], places["court_key"],
                                 places["muni_seq"])]
    out = places.copy()
    sid = out["settlement_id"].astype("string")
    out["settlement_id"] = sid.mask(pd.Series(hit, index=out.index))
    return out


def register_join(muni_sid, owner_key, g: Gazetteer) -> tuple[bool, object, object]:
    """``(in_register_municipalities, register_owner_differs, register_key)`` for one link (0.3.0).

    The link reaches the municipality's institutions only when ``register_municipalities`` holds
    *muni_sid* on a key at which the gazetteer's register (overrides and applied rulings) also
    holds it as a municipality (:func:`municipality_row_keys`), a row the other edition does not
    contradict on name and population (:func:`contradicted_keys`) — never on membership alone.
    *differs* is True where the table holds it on a key the gazetteer does not (the frozen anchoring
    an override or ruling moved, e.g. Kostomlaty on the *Kostomlátky* row), False where they agree,
    ``pd.NA`` where the table lacks the settlement (Aš until the register hook) or there is no
    municipality. *register_key* is the table's key where they agree, else the owner row's
    (*owner_key*)."""
    if not muni_sid:
        return False, pd.NA, owner_key
    table_key = g.register_muni_key.get(muni_sid)
    if table_key is None:
        return False, pd.NA, owner_key
    if table_key in g.muni_keys.get(muni_sid, set()):
        return True, False, table_key
    return False, True, owner_key


def _lexikon_municipality(sid: str, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    if g.status.get(sid) == "obec":
        return sid, "self"
    pk = g.parent_key.get(sid)
    okres = g.okres_of.get(sid) or oid
    if not pk or okres is None:
        return None, None
    v, _t, val = _lookup(pk, okres, g)
    if v == "ok" and val != sid:
        return val, "lexikon_parent"
    return None, None


# ── the frame ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def _col(df: pd.DataFrame, name: str):
    return df[name] if name in df.columns else pd.Series(pd.NA, index=df.index)


def vua_uncertain(df: pd.DataFrame, prefix: str = "birth") -> pd.Series:
    """A VÚA place read off 2+ readings that do not name one place: ``locations`` 1.2.2
    ``candidates_agree_place`` (same okres **and** same place; 0.3.0 — *Velká Úpa I./II./III.*
    agree on the okres only), counted on ``locations`` 1.2.3 ``n_readings`` (0.4.0: the written head
    counts, so *Dražov, okres Karlovy Vary ? (Dražov, okres Teplá ?)* is two readings that differ)
    and, without it, on ``n_candidates``; without ``candidates_agree_place`` the 1.2.x
    ``candidates_agree`` (okres only); without either, the v1.1 ``loc_uncertain`` flag; without any
    (the legionnaire frame), False."""
    n = pd.to_numeric(_col(df, f"{prefix}_n_readings"), errors="coerce")
    if n.isna().all():
        n = pd.to_numeric(_col(df, f"{prefix}_n_candidates"), errors="coerce")
    for col in (f"{prefix}_candidates_agree_place", f"{prefix}_candidates_agree"):
        agree = _col(df, col)
        if agree.notna().any():
            return (agree.eq(False) & n.ge(2)).fillna(False).astype(bool)
    return _col(df, f"{prefix}_loc_uncertain").fillna(False).astype(bool)


def _has_question_mark(df: pd.DataFrame, prefix: str, cols=("municipality", "okres")) -> pd.Series:
    """A ``?`` in the recorded municipality / okres (``settlement_qmark``); with
    ``cols=("raw",)`` in the raw VÚA cell, whose ``?`` follows a doubtful okres and every entry of
    its candidate list (``Písek ? (Písek, okres Písek ?; …)``) — reported, not counted (0.3.0)."""
    hit = pd.Series(False, index=df.index)
    for c in (f"{prefix}_{c}" for c in cols):
        if c in df.columns:
            hit |= df[c].astype("string").str.contains("?", regex=False).fillna(False).astype(bool)
    return hit


def piece_tier(tier, parallel: bool = False) -> object:
    """``alternate`` / ``split`` / ``qualifier`` for a tier that read a piece of the string;
    ``praha_parallel`` for X of a ``Praha, X`` / ``Praha, Y`` list; else ``pd.NA``."""
    if parallel:
        return "praha_parallel"
    if not isinstance(tier, str) or tier not in UNCERTAIN_TIERS:
        return pd.NA
    return "alternate" if tier == "p2_alternate" else "qualifier" if tier == "p2_qualifier" else "split"


_ROMAN_ONLY_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*([IVX]+)\s*\.?\s*$")


def quarter_number(value) -> object:
    """A ``locations`` 1.2 ``quarter_no`` (``XI``) as an int; ``pd.NA`` when it is not one."""
    if value is None or (not isinstance(value, str) and pd.isna(value)):
        return pd.NA
    m = _ROMAN_ONLY_RE.match(str(value).upper())
    return _ROMAN.get(m.group(1), pd.NA) if m else pd.NA


def correction_rule(sid, tier, stated, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> str | None:
    """The rule a corrected okres moved under (``okres_correction_rule``).

    ``p4_timeline`` for P4. For P3 (0.3.0):

    * ``p3_prague_1910_okres`` — the settlement joined Prague in 1922 (it or its parent: every
      joined part), is the 1910 city or a quarter, or has the stated okres **literally** in its
      ``okres_all`` timeline: within the standing decision;
    * ``p3_prague_later_okres`` — none of that, and only a post-1910 ``Praha-venkov`` /
      ``-západ`` / ``-sever`` / ``-východ`` / ``-jih`` token in the timeline lets it pass (0.2.0
      counted these as ``p3_prague_1910_okres``): **not** within the decision, refused
      ``prague_later_okres_only`` unless accepted as a block;
    * ``p3_prague_pool_only`` — nothing in the timeline: the move rests on the record writer's
      generic *Praha* for the agglomeration alone; refused ``prague_pool_only``.
    """
    tier = tier or ""
    if tier.startswith("p4"):
        return "p4_timeline"
    if not tier.startswith("p3"):
        return None
    timeline = g.timeline.get(sid, set())
    if (sid in g.greater_prague or sid == PRAHA_SID or sid in g.quarter_sids
            or move_allowed(sid, stated, oid, g)):
        return "p3_prague_1910_okres"
    if any(t.startswith("praha") and t != "praha" for t in timeline):
        return "p3_prague_later_okres"
    return "p3_prague_pool_only"


def okres_from_name(df: pd.DataFrame, prefix: str = "birth") -> pd.Series:
    """True where the record states no okres and :mod:`records_geo` inferred the okres id from the
    municipality name (``{prefix}_okres_match = muni``, 0.4.0); False without the column."""
    match = _col(df, f"{prefix}_okres_match").astype("string")
    stated = _col(df, f"{prefix}_okres").astype("string").str.strip()
    no_string = stated.isna() | stated.eq("")
    return (match.eq(OKRES_FROM_NAME_TIER).fillna(False) & no_string.fillna(True)
            & _col(df, f"{prefix}_okres_id").notna()).astype(bool)


def _raw_cells(df: pd.DataFrame, prefix: str) -> pd.Series | None:
    raw = f"{prefix}_raw"
    if raw not in df.columns:
        return None
    from utils.parsing import clean as cl
    return df[raw].map(lambda v: None if v is None or (not isinstance(v, str) and pd.isna(v))
                       else cl.strip_place_markers(v))


def german_forms_column(df: pd.DataFrame, prefix: str = "birth") -> pd.Series:
    """Every form of the VÚA German cell where it holds 2+ (``locations.german_forms`` on the raw
    cell, 0.4.0), else ``None``. Built as a list, not ``Series.map``: on a ``string``-dtype raw
    column (notebook 02 §4 attaches the cell that way) ``map`` turns each tuple into an array and
    ``None`` into ``<NA>``, which the matcher cannot hash."""
    from utils.parsing import locations as loc
    raw = _raw_cells(df, prefix)
    if raw is None:
        return pd.Series([None] * len(df), index=df.index, dtype=object)
    forms = {v: loc.german_forms(v) for v in raw.dropna().unique()}
    return pd.Series([forms[v] if isinstance(v, str) and v in forms and len(forms[v]) >= 2 else None
                      for v in raw], index=df.index, dtype=object)


def raw_text_column(df: pd.DataFrame, prefix: str = "birth") -> pd.Series:
    """The text the record wrote for the place (0.6.0, T2): the raw VÚA cell (markers stripped) where
    ``{prefix}_raw`` exists, else the municipality string and the okres string (csol.cz writes them
    as two fields); ``None`` where there is none."""
    raw = _raw_cells(df, prefix)
    if raw is not None:
        return pd.Series([v if isinstance(v, str) else None for v in raw], index=df.index, dtype=object)
    m, s = _col(df, f"{prefix}_municipality"), _col(df, f"{prefix}_okres")
    return pd.Series([", ".join(str(x) for x in (a, b) if isinstance(x, str) and x.strip()) or None
                      for a, b in zip(m, s)], index=df.index, dtype=object)


def candidates_column(df: pd.DataFrame, prefix: str = "birth") -> pd.Series:
    """VÚA's candidate readings ``((municipality, okres, text), …)`` where the place was read off the
    first of 2+ candidates (``{prefix}_loc_reading = candidate``, 0.4.0; the reading's own text since
    0.6.0, :func:`locations.candidate_readings`), else ``None``."""
    from utils.parsing import locations as loc
    raw = _raw_cells(df, prefix)
    use = first_candidate_mask(df, prefix)
    if raw is None:
        return pd.Series([None] * len(df), index=df.index, dtype=object)
    cells = {v: loc.candidate_readings(v, with_text=True) for v in raw[use].dropna().unique()}
    out = [cells.get(v) if u else None for v, u in zip(raw, use)]
    if _on("E11"):       # 0.9.0: readings in separate parentheses (Stodůlky … Praha venkov / … Sušice)
        muni = _col(df, f"{prefix}_municipality").astype(object)
        sep = {v: separate_paren_candidates(v) for v in raw[~use].dropna().unique() if v.count("(") >= 2}
        out = [c if c is not None else (_own_first(sep.get(v), mm) if isinstance(v, str) else None)
               for c, v, mm in zip(out, raw, muni)]
    return pd.Series(out, index=df.index, dtype=object)


def first_candidate_mask(df: pd.DataFrame, prefix: str = "birth") -> pd.Series:
    """True where VÚA read the place off the first of 2+ candidates (``{prefix}_loc_reading = candidate``,
    ``{prefix}_n_candidates`` >= 2): the rows :func:`candidates_column` reads with
    :func:`locations.candidate_readings`; the others may take E11's separate parentheses."""
    reading = _col(df, f"{prefix}_loc_reading").astype("string")
    n = pd.to_numeric(_col(df, f"{prefix}_n_candidates"), errors="coerce")
    return (reading.eq("candidate") & n.ge(2)).fillna(False).astype(bool)


def top_level_groups(raw) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """G4 (0.10.0): the depth-1 parentheses of *raw*, each as ``(whole content, own text)`` — the own text
    with every nested parenthesis removed — scanned with a depth counter (an unclosed group runs to the end)."""
    if not isinstance(raw, str):
        return []
    out, depth, start = [], 0, None
    for i, ch in enumerate(raw):
        if ch == "(":
            depth += 1
            if depth == 1:
                start = i + 1
        elif ch == ")" and depth:
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0 and start is not None:
                out.append(raw[start:i])
                start = None
    if depth and start is not None:
        out.append(raw[start:])
    own = []
    for x in out:
        prev = None
        while prev != x:
            prev, x2 = x, re.sub(r"\([^()]*\)", " ", x)
            x = x2
        own.append(re.sub(r"[()]", " ", x))
    return list(zip(out, own))


def separate_paren_candidates(raw) -> tuple | None:
    """E11 (0.9.0): VÚA's candidate readings when the cell gives each in its **own** parenthesis — two or
    more top-level parentheses that each hold an okres word and a ``?`` (*Stodůlky ?, (Stodůlky, okres
    Praha venkov - ?), (Stodůlky, okres Sušice - ?)*), which :func:`locations.candidate_readings` reads as
    one reading; ``((municipality, okres, text), …)`` from each parenthesis's first reading, else ``None``.

    0.10.0 (G4): only **depth-1** parentheses (:func:`top_level_groups`), the okres word and the ``?`` in the
    group's own text, nested groups set aside — 0.9.0's innermost-group regex took *(Hamry, okres Klatovy ?)*
    from inside a second segment of the cell (as-is 124183) as a top-level reading."""
    from utils.parsing import locations as loc
    if not isinstance(raw, str):
        return None
    if _on("G4"):
        groups = [own for _whole, own in top_level_groups(raw)]
    else:
        groups = [m.group(1) for m in re.finditer(r"\(([^()]*)\)", raw)]
    groups = [x for x in groups if _OKRES_WORD_RE.search(x) and "?" in x]
    if len(groups) < 2:
        return None
    out = []
    for x in groups:
        rd = loc.candidate_readings(f"x ({x})", with_text=True) or ()
        if rd and isinstance(rd[0][0], str):
            out.append(rd[0])
    return tuple(out) if len(out) >= 2 else None


def _own_first(cands, muni) -> tuple | None:
    """E11: the separate-parenthesis readings only where the record's reading is the first of them."""
    if not cands or not isinstance(muni, str) or not isinstance(cands[0][0], str):
        return None
    return cands if key(cands[0][0]) == key(muni) else None


def okres_string_unresolved(df: pd.DataFrame, prefix: str = "birth") -> pd.Series:
    """D-a (0.8.0): True where the record writes an okres string records_geo left unresolved (no
    ``{prefix}_okres_id``) beside a municipality, and its land is the Czech lands or unknown (a
    ``{prefix}_land`` outside them — *Vídeň*, *Slovensko* — is never read as a Czech okres)."""
    s = _col(df, f"{prefix}_okres").astype("string").str.strip()
    m = _col(df, f"{prefix}_municipality").astype("string").str.strip()
    land = _col(df, f"{prefix}_land").astype("string")
    ok_land = land.isna() | land.eq("Czech lands")
    return (s.notna() & s.ne("") & m.notna() & m.ne("") & _col(df, f"{prefix}_okres_id").isna()
            & ok_land).fillna(False).astype(bool)


def has_paren_okres(raw) -> bool:
    """D-a (0.8.0): the raw cell's head (before its first parenthesis) has an okres word and a parenthesis
    follows — the shape whose okres alternatives :func:`stated_okres_alternatives` reads (a cheap filter
    on the distinct inputs)."""
    if not isinstance(raw, str) or "(" not in raw:
        return False
    return bool(_OKRES_WORD_RE.search(raw.split("(", 1)[0]))


def okres_only_alternatives(raw, g: Gazetteer, sid=None) -> list[str]:
    """D-a (0.8.0): the okres alternatives of a cell that writes an okres word in its head and then, as its
    **first** parenthesis, one holding **only** okres names (*Domoradice, okr. Vysoké Mýto? (Český
    Krumlov?)*; *Javornice, okr. Lomnice nad Popelkou? (Rychnov nad Kněžnou?, Vodňany?)*): every piece, ``?``
    and ``+`` dropped, names a Czech-lands okres or court as written (no close spelling). A piece that is a
    name of the linked settlement *sid* itself — VÚA's German form after a verified okres, *Falknov, okres
    Česká Lípa+ (Falkenau)*, *Nejdek, okres Mikulov+ (Neudek)*, which happen to be okres or court names
    too — is no alternative; a parenthesis with an okres word inside is VÚA's candidate list (*Planá, Čechy ?
    (Planá, okres Planá ?; …)*), and a later parenthesis VÚA's German forms of the candidates."""
    if not has_paren_okres(raw):
        return []
    grp = re.search(r"\(([^()]*)\)", raw)
    if not grp or _OKRES_WORD_RE.search(grp.group(1)):
        return []
    own = (g.forms_of.get(sid, set()) | g.pool_forms.get(sid, set()) | g.forms_1910.get(sid, set())) if sid else set()
    pieces = [re.sub(r"\s+", " ", re.sub(r"[?+]", " ", x)).strip(" -–.") for x in re.split(r"[,;]", grp.group(1))]
    pieces = [x for x in pieces if x]
    if not pieces or not all(resolve_okres(x, None, None, g, fuzzy=False)[0] in ("czech", "later", "timeline")
                             for x in pieces):
        return []
    return list(dict.fromkeys(x for x in pieces if not (form_set([key(x)]) & own)))


def home_name_conflict(head, sid, home_m, home_o, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """D-h (0.8.0): the soldier's home municipality *home_m* is exactly the name of a Czech-lands
    settlement of his home okres *home_o* (``home_okres_id``; for VÚA records_geo infers it from the home
    name), another okres than the link's; the link itself does not answer to that name; and the written
    *head* is closer to it (difflib, space-free) than to any name of the link *sid*: VÚA 143950 *Krupka,
    Kutná Hora ?* → ``krupa:3`` (Krupá, Kutná Hora), home *Krupka*, okres Teplice — the town Krupka. No
    home okres, no conflict; :func:`home_name_pass` calls it only where VÚA read the place off another
    name than the one written. A home settlement in a land the head's own land word contradicts
    (:func:`lands_named`, :func:`land_conflict`) is no rival: *Držkov, Morava ?* → ``drzkova:1`` (Holešov)
    stands although a Bohemian Držkov (Semily) carries the home name (0.8.0 round, the reader's
    narrowing of D-h)."""
    name = clean_birthplace(re.split(r"[,;]", head)[0])[0] if isinstance(head, str) else None
    hname = clean_birthplace(str(home_m).split(",")[0])[0] if isinstance(home_m, str) else None
    hk, mk = (nospace(key(name)) if name else ""), (key(hname) if hname else "")
    if not hk or not mk or sid is None or home_o is None:
        return False
    namesakes = set(g.global_any.get(mk, ()))
    if sid in namesakes:
        return False
    link_okres = _okres_any(sid, g)
    lands = lands_named(head)
    homes = [s for s in _czech(namesakes, g) if _okres_any(s, g) == home_o != link_okres
             and not land_conflict(lands, _land_of(s, g))]
    if not homes:
        return False
    link_forms = _name_forms(sid, g) | g.forms_1910.get(sid, set())
    to_home = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, hk, nospace(mk)).ratio()
    to_link = max((difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, hk, f).ratio() for f in link_forms), default=0.0)
    return to_home > to_link


def home_name_pass(rows: list, raw_all: pd.Series, df: pd.DataFrame, g: Gazetteer,
                   home_prefix: str = "home", prefix: str = "birth") -> list:
    """D-h (0.8.0): every linked VÚA result (a record with the raw cell ``{prefix}_raw``) whose written
    head (the raw cell's :func:`head_text`, its first comma piece) is **not** the name VÚA read the place
    off (``{prefix}_municipality``: VÚA took a candidate or corrected the spelling — *Krupka* written,
    *Krupá* read) and is within :data:`HOME_HEAD_RATIO` of the home municipality goes through
    :func:`home_name_conflict`; a conflict refuses the link ``home_name_conflict`` (the row's result is
    copied, never the shared one). Where the head is the reading, the link was read off what was
    written and a home copied from it is no evidence against it (*Vesec, okres Liberec+*, home *Vesec*);
    csol.cz writes municipality and okres as fields, with no such reading.

    0.9.0 (E12, a diagnostic; which rows are refused does not change): ``refusal_detail`` says whether the
    home okres was written (``home_name:home_okres_written``) or inferred by records_geo from the home name
    (``home_name:home_okres_inferred`` — then a home cell that copies the head is no independent
    evidence: the coin flips the rulings queue lists as the block ``home_name_conflict``)."""
    if f"{prefix}_raw" not in df.columns:
        return list(rows)
    hm = _col(df, f"{home_prefix}_municipality").astype(object).tolist()
    ho = _col(df, f"{home_prefix}_okres_id").astype(object).tolist()
    hok = _col(df, f"{home_prefix}_okres").astype(object).tolist()
    hmatch = _col(df, f"{home_prefix}_okres_match").astype(object).tolist()
    reading = _col(df, f"{prefix}_municipality").astype(object).tolist()
    out, seen = list(rows), {}
    for i, (res, raw, m, o, rd) in enumerate(zip(rows, raw_all, hm, ho, reading)):
        if res["sid"] is None or not isinstance(m, str) or not isinstance(raw, str) or not isinstance(rd, str):
            continue
        head = head_text(raw)
        if not head:
            continue
        o = int(o) if o is not None and not pd.isna(o) else None
        k = (head, m, o, rd, res["sid"])
        if k not in seen:
            hname = clean_birthplace(re.split(r"[,;]", head)[0])[0]
            mname = clean_birthplace(m.split(",")[0])[0]
            rname = clean_birthplace(rd)[0]
            close = (bool(hname) and bool(mname) and bool(rname) and key(hname) != key(rname)
                     and difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, key(hname), key(mname)).ratio() >= HOME_HEAD_RATIO)
            seen[k] = close and home_name_conflict(head, res["sid"], m, o, g)
        if seen[k]:
            r = _refuse(res, "home_name_conflict", res.get("stated_id"))
            in_reg, differs, reg_key = register_join(None, None, g)
            detail = "home_name"
            if _on("E12"):
                detail += ":home_okres_written" if home_okres_written(hok[i], hmatch[i]) else ":home_okres_inferred"
            r.update(refusal_detail=detail, refusal_okres_ids=(), in_register=in_reg, owner_differs=differs,
                     register_key=reg_key)
            out[i] = r
    return out


def home_okres_written(okres, match) -> bool:
    """E12 (0.9.0): the home okres id comes from an okres the home cell writes, not from records_geo's
    inference from the home name (``home_okres_match = muni``, or no okres string)."""
    written = isinstance(okres, str) and bool(okres.strip(" -?+"))
    return written and not (isinstance(match, str) and match == OKRES_FROM_NAME_TIER)


def add_birth_settlement_columns(df: pd.DataFrame, g: Gazetteer, prefix: str = "birth",
                                 dataset: str | None = None,
                                 accept_prague_later_okres: bool | None = None,
                                 home_prefix: str = "home", diagnostics: bool = False) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The ``{prefix}_*`` settlement columns on a copy of *df* (see the module docstring) — the one
    entry point notebook 02 calls, for either dataset.

    Reads ``{prefix}_municipality``, ``{prefix}_okres``, ``{prefix}_okres_id`` and, where present,
    ``{prefix}_okres_match``, ``{prefix}_german``, ``{prefix}_raw``, the VÚA candidate columns
    (``n_candidates``, ``n_readings``, ``loc_reading``, ``candidates_agree_place``) and
    ``{prefix}_quarter_no``. Each distinct input is matched once. *dataset* is accepted for
    backward compatibility and ignored: every flag reads the columns present.
    *accept_prague_later_okres* (default :data:`ACCEPT_PRAGUE_LATER_OKRES`, True since 0.4.0) is the
    author's single switch for the ``p3_prague_later_okres`` block. Since 0.6.0 (T2) a record whose
    okres was inferred from the name also passes its raw text (:func:`raw_text_column`) and its home
    place (``{home_prefix}_municipality``, ``{home_prefix}_okres_id``) to :func:`okres_inferred_refusal`;
    since 0.7.0 also ``{home_prefix}_land``, ``_megye_id``, ``_jaras_id`` and ``_okres`` (F3), and a
    record read off VÚA's first candidate passes its raw text too (the head, F1/F2). Since 0.8.0 the
    soldier's regiment region (:func:`regiment_region_column`, A6) reaches those records and the ones
    whose okres string records_geo left unresolved (:func:`okres_string_unresolved`, D-a), and a linked
    record is checked against its home municipality (:func:`home_name_pass`, D-h).
    *diagnostics* (0.7.0, :func:`build` only — notebook 02 leaves it off, so ``data/final`` carries
    no such column) adds ``{prefix}_refusal_detail`` (the kinds or sub-rule behind a refusal) and
    ``{prefix}_refusal_okres_ids`` (the okresy a written okres named, A3).
    """
    accept = ACCEPT_PRAGUE_LATER_OKRES if accept_prague_later_okres is None else accept_prague_later_okres
    out = df.copy()
    unc = vua_uncertain(out, prefix)
    inputs = pd.DataFrame({"m": _col(out, f"{prefix}_municipality"), "o": _col(out, f"{prefix}_okres_id"),
                           "s": _col(out, f"{prefix}_okres"), "g": _col(out, f"{prefix}_german"),
                           "u": unc}).astype(object).where(lambda x: x.notna(), None)
    inputs["i"] = okres_from_name(out, prefix).to_numpy()
    inputs["gf"] = german_forms_column(out, prefix).to_numpy()
    inputs["c"] = candidates_column(out, prefix).to_numpy()
    # 0.6.0 (T2): the raw text and the home place, only where the okres was inferred (keeps the
    # distinct inputs few); 0.7.0: the raw text also where the reading came off VÚA's candidates;
    # 0.8.0: the raw text, home and regiment also where the okres string is unresolved (D-a, F6), the
    # raw text where it gives okres alternatives in parentheses (D-a, F5)
    inf = inputs["i"].astype(bool)
    unresolved = okres_string_unresolved(out, prefix).to_numpy()
    raw_all = raw_text_column(out, prefix)
    alternatives = pd.Series([has_paren_okres(v) for v in raw_all], index=out.index, dtype=bool).to_numpy()
    regiment = regiment_region_column(out)                                  # 0.8.0 (A6)
    with_home = inf.to_numpy() | unresolved
    if _on("E2"):        # 0.9.0: a candidate reading whose regiment may refuse it reads the home cell (E2)
        with_home = with_home | (inputs["c"].notna().to_numpy()
                                 & regiment.isin(list(REGIMENT_EVIDENCE_REGIONS)).to_numpy())
    if _on("E6"):        # 0.9.0: an alternate under a doubted okres string reads the home okres (E6)
        doubted = inputs["s"].map(lambda v: isinstance(v, str) and "?" in v).astype(bool).to_numpy()
        with_home = with_home | doubted
    with_raw = with_home | inputs["c"].notna().to_numpy() | alternatives
    # 0.10.0 (G4): the candidates read off E11's separate parentheses (not VÚA's own first-candidate reading)
    separate = (inputs["c"].notna() & ~first_candidate_mask(out, prefix).to_numpy()).to_numpy() if _on("E11") \
        else np.zeros(len(out), dtype=bool)
    if (_on("G7") or _on("G6")) and f"{prefix}_raw" in out.columns:
        # 0.10.0 (G7): a VÚA cell listing 2+ candidates with a '?' reaches the stated-okres E3 test (and G6)
        with_raw = with_raw | np.array([isinstance(v, str) and "(" in v and v.count("?") >= 2 for v in raw_all])
    inputs["r"] = raw_all.where(with_raw, None).to_numpy()
    # the home columns: where the rules above read them, and (0.10.0) for an okres string naming several okresy
    # (G2: the home settles E6's coin flip) and for E11's separate-parenthesis candidates (G4)
    home_rows = with_home.copy()
    if _on("G2"):
        home_rows = home_rows | inputs["s"].map(lambda v: isinstance(v, str) and bool(re.search(r"[/?,;()]", v))
                                                ).astype(bool).to_numpy()
    if _on("G4"):
        home_rows = home_rows | separate
    if _on("G7") and f"{prefix}_raw" in out.columns:     # G7: VÚA's pick off the head reads the home (as G4)
        home_rows = home_rows | np.array([isinstance(v, str) and "(" in v and v.count("?") >= 2 for v in raw_all])
    for col, src in (("hm", f"{home_prefix}_municipality"), ("ho", f"{home_prefix}_okres_id"),
                     ("hl", f"{home_prefix}_land"), ("hmg", f"{home_prefix}_megye_id"),
                     ("hj", f"{home_prefix}_jaras_id"), ("hok", f"{home_prefix}_okres")):
        vals = [v if (f and v is not None and not (not isinstance(v, str) and pd.isna(v))) else None
                for v, f in zip(_col(out, src).astype(object), home_rows)]
        if col == "ho":
            vals = [int(v) if v is not None else None for v in vals]
        elif col != "hm":
            vals = [str(v) if v is not None else None for v in vals]
        inputs[col] = pd.Series(vals, index=inputs.index, dtype=object)
    with_regiment = with_home | inputs["c"].notna().to_numpy()
    inputs["rg"] = pd.Series([v if f else None for v, f in zip(regiment, with_regiment)], index=inputs.index,
                             dtype=object)
    # 1: an unresolved okres field (csol.cz), 2: the same in a VÚA cell (D-a's repeated-name reading)
    inputs["un"] = [(2 if f"{prefix}_raw" in out.columns else 1) if u else 0 for u in unresolved]
    # 0.9.0 (E2): the regiment's recruiting area, where the regiment reaches the rules
    area = regiment_area_column(out) if _on("E2") else pd.Series([None] * len(out), index=out.index, dtype=object)
    inputs["ra"] = pd.Series([v if f and r in REGIMENT_EVIDENCE_REGIONS else None
                              for v, f, r in zip(area, with_regiment, regiment)], index=inputs.index, dtype=object)
    inputs["vc"] = 1 if f"{prefix}_raw" in out.columns else 0                # 0.9.0 (E4): a VÚA cell
    inputs["sp"] = [1 if f and _on("G4") else 0 for f in separate]           # 0.10.0 (G4)
    # 0.12.0 (I2): a qualified name's home municipality, read only by p2_qualifier (its own column, so the other
    # home rules see exactly the rows they saw before)
    qualified = inputs["m"].map(lambda v: isinstance(v, str) and bool(_QUALIFIER_RE.search(key(v)))).astype(bool)
    qualified = qualified & _on("I2")
    if _on("J1"):        # 0.13.0 (J1): also a bare name some qualified settlement carries as its head (home_namesake)
        heads = _qualified_heads(g)
        qualified = qualified | inputs["m"].map(
            lambda v: isinstance(v, str) and bool(clean_birthplace(v)[0])
            and key(clean_birthplace(v)[0]) in heads).astype(bool)
    if _on("J4"):        # 0.13.0 (J4): a VÚA candidate list, matched with the home (candidate_verdicts)
        qualified = qualified | inputs["c"].notna()
    if _on("K1"):        # 0.14.0 (K1): a bare name an alias, an alternate or a German form may send elsewhere
        qualified = qualified | pd.Series([_variant_home_needed(m, ger, g) for m, ger in zip(inputs["m"], inputs["g"])],
                                          index=inputs.index, dtype=bool)
    inputs["hq"] = pd.Series([v if f and isinstance(v, str) else None
                              for v, f in zip(_col(out, f"{home_prefix}_municipality").astype(object), qualified)],
                             index=inputs.index, dtype=object)
    tuples = [tuple(t) for t in inputs.itertuples(index=False, name=None)]
    results = {tup: link_one(tup, g, accept) for tup in set(tuples)}
    rows = [results[t] for t in tuples]
    if _on("Dh"):                                                           # 0.8.0 (D-h)
        rows = home_name_pass(rows, raw_all, out, g, home_prefix, prefix)
    res = pd.DataFrame(rows, index=out.index)
    out.attrs["accept_prague_later_okres"] = bool(accept)
    out = _assemble(out, res, inputs, unc, g, prefix)
    # 0.8.0 (D-a): links through an okres string records_geo left unresolved, by reading
    linked_rule = res["okres_string_rule"].where(res["link_unit"].ne("none"))
    out.attrs["okres_string_rule"] = {str(k): int(v) for k, v in linked_rule.value_counts().items()}
    if diagnostics:
        out[f"{prefix}_refusal_detail"] = pd.array([d or pd.NA for d in res["refusal_detail"]], dtype="string")
        out[f"{prefix}_refusal_okres_ids"] = pd.array(["|".join(str(o) for o in sorted(x)) if x else pd.NA
                                                      for x in res["refusal_okres_ids"]], dtype="string")
        if _on("E10"):   # 0.9.0 (E10): where the okres the match ran in came from (okres_source)
            out[f"{prefix}_okres_source"] = pd.array([v or pd.NA for v in res["okres_source"]], dtype="string")
    return out


def okres_inferred_refusal(clean, sid, oid, g: Gazetteer, raw=None, home=None, tier=None) -> str | None:
    """The refusal of :func:`okres_inferred_verdict` (its first element)."""
    return okres_inferred_verdict(clean, sid, oid, g, raw=raw, home=home, tier=tier)[0]


def okres_inferred_verdict(clean, sid, oid, g: Gazetteer, raw=None, home=None,
                           tier=None, regiment=None, area=None) -> tuple[str | None, str | None, tuple]:
    """``(refusal, detail, written okres ids)``; ``(None, None, ())`` when a name whose okres
    :mod:`records_geo` inferred from the name (no okres string)
    may link to *sid*, the settlement the match found in that okres *oid*; else the refusal.

    0.4.0: the name is the inferred okres's own (its seat or okres name) → link. 0.5.0 (D2): D-144
    across **all** okresy on every name the gazetteer knows (``global_any``: lexikon names and
    register forms) — one id, else the one obec or town (:func:`_obec_or_unknown`: a register
    municipality row, a lexikon obec, or a namesake whose 1910 status the lexikon does not give) —
    and that one is *sid* → link (*Brtnice*, *Netolice*, *Choltice*, *Loket*: one obec among hamlets
    of the name); that one lies in **another** okres → ``okres_from_name_conflict``; no one (*Nové
    Město*: one obec, four namesakes of unknown status among the 13; *Nový Dvůr*; *Pečky*: the
    register prints the Kolín obec Červené Pečky as *Pečky* too) or one in this okres that the match
    did not find → ``okres_from_name_ambiguous``.

    0.6.0 (T2), in this order: the record's *raw* text names a land, country or district outside the
    Czech lands → ``okres_from_name_foreign`` (:func:`foreign_token`), or an okres the settlement does
    not lie in → ``okres_from_name_conflict`` (:func:`raw_okres_refusal`); the okres's own name links
    as before; D-144 across okresy is :func:`d2_decide` (a namesake of unknown 1910 status refuses
    but never wins; an unanchored register municipality printing the name is one more possible
    obec); a link the soldier's *home* ``(municipality, okres_id)`` contradicts →
    ``okres_from_name_home_conflict`` (:func:`home_conflict`).

    0.7.0: the raw cell's land word (F4, ``okres_from_name_land_conflict``), okres alternatives in
    parentheses (F5), an unresolved okres string as no evidence (F6) and the unique name's own
    conflict (A3, ``okres_from_name_conflict_unique``), all in :func:`raw_okres_verdict`; after D-144
    across okresy, a match through a post-1910 name only (F3, :func:`later_name_only`, *tier* the
    match tier: ``okres_from_name_later_name``) and a home outside the Czech lands (F3,
    :func:`home_foreign`: ``okres_from_name_home_foreign``), before the home namesake test. The
    *detail* names the sub-rule; the okres ids are those a conflicting written okres names (A3).

    0.8.0: A4 narrows the foreign home (:func:`home_refuses`); A6 refuses
    ``okres_from_name_regiment_conflict`` where the soldier's *regiment* (:func:`regiment_region`)
    recruited in Hungary and a Slovak obec carries the name (:attr:`Gazetteer.hu_obce`); D-c reaches
    :func:`later_name_only` through *raw* and *home*."""
    k = key(clean) if clean else ""
    if not k:
        return "okres_from_name_ambiguous", "no_name", ()
    if raw:
        why, detail, ids = raw_okres_verdict(raw, clean, sid, g)
        if why:
            return why, detail, ids
    if not (oid is not None and k in g.okres_names.get(oid, set())):
        v, one = d2_decide(k, g)
        if v != "ok":
            return "okres_from_name_ambiguous", "d2_no_single_settlement", ()
        if one != sid:
            if _okres_any(one, g) != oid:
                return "okres_from_name_conflict", "d2_other_okres", ()
            return "okres_from_name_ambiguous", "d2_other_settlement", ()
    # F3's later-name rule and its home_unresolved reading apply only where the name answers to more
    # than one Czech-lands settlement and is not the okres's own — where D-144 had to choose, which is
    # what "may not win" means: VÚA and csol.cz write today's names (Český Krumlov, Bruntál, Jeseník),
    # and a unique name or the okres town (Brno, home Brixton) is the place
    own_name = oid is not None and k in g.okres_names.get(oid, set())
    contested = not own_name and len(_czech_1910(g.global_any.get(k, ()), g)) > 1
    if _on("F3") and contested and later_name_only(k, sid, tier, g, raw=raw, home=home):
        return "okres_from_name_later_name", "later_name", ()
    # 0.8.0 (A6): a Hungarian regiment and a Slovak obec of the name — refuse only, never a link; not on
    # the okres's own name town (Praha: a Slovak village Praha is no rival to the capital)
    if (_on("A6") and regiment == "hungary" and k in g.hu_obce and not own_name
            and not (_on("E2") and not in_area(g.hu_county.get(k, ()), area))):   # 0.9.0 (E2): its county
        return "okres_from_name_regiment_conflict", "regiment_hu_obec", ()
    if home is not None:
        if _on("F3"):
            why = home_foreign(home, g)
            if why == "home_unresolved" and not contested:
                why = None
            if why and _on("A4") and not home_refuses(why, home, raw, sid, g):
                why = None
            if why:
                return "okres_from_name_home_foreign", why, ()
        # A1 (the author, 2026-11-16): a home okres equal to the link's own okres is no conflict —
        # it corroborates the inferred okres (0.6.0's reading, kept; see home_conflict)
        if home_conflict(k, sid, home, g):
            return "okres_from_name_home_conflict", "home_namesake", ()
    return None, None, ()


#: 0.7.0 (F3): a lexikon name counts as a 1910 one when a register form of the settlement is this
#: close to it (difflib ratio): an OCR-damaged printed form (*Markovise*) is not a later name
LATER_NAME_PRINTED_RATIO = 0.8


def later_name_only(k: str, sid, tier, g: Gazetteer, raw=None, home=None) -> bool:
    """F3 (0.7.0): the match reached *sid* only through a post-1910 lexikon name — tier
    ``p1_lexikon``, the register holds the settlement (``pool_forms``) but prints no form of the
    name *k* nor one within :data:`LATER_NAME_PRINTED_RATIO` of it, and the lexikon's 1910 name is
    not *k* either: legion 86003 *Dvorek* → ``dvorek:1``, which the register prints only as
    *Höflas* (the Czech name is post-1945). Such a match may not win an inferred okres — applied by
    :func:`okres_inferred_verdict` only where the name answers to more than one Czech-lands
    settlement and is not the okres's own (a unique modern name, *Český Krumlov*, is the place).

    0.8.0 (D-c): not when a form the raw cell prints in parentheses is a printed 1910 form of the link
    (key, or within :data:`LATER_NAME_PRINTED_RATIO` of a register or 1910 lexikon form: VÚA 91000
    *Prameny (Sangaberg)*, printed *Sangerberg*), nor when the soldier's home lies in the link's okres
    (:func:`home_in_okres`: 171464 *Ludvíkov*, home *Einsidl* = Einsiedel of Bruntál)."""
    if tier != "p1_lexikon" or not k or sid is None:
        return False
    printed = g.pool_forms.get(sid) or set()
    if not printed:
        return False
    mine = form_set([k])
    if mine & (printed | g.forms_1910.get(sid, set())):
        return False
    if any(difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, a, b).ratio() >= LATER_NAME_PRINTED_RATIO
           for a in mine for b in printed):
        return False
    if _on("Dc"):
        forms_1910 = printed | g.forms_1910.get(sid, set())
        parens = [p for grp in re.findall(r"\(([^()]*)\)", raw) for p in re.split(r"[,;]", grp)] \
            if isinstance(raw, str) else []
        for p in parens:
            pc = clean_birthplace(p)[0]
            pf = form_set([key(pc)]) if pc else set()
            if pf & forms_1910 or any(difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, a, b).ratio() >= LATER_NAME_PRINTED_RATIO
                                      for a in pf for b in forms_1910):
                return False
        if home is not None and home_in_okres(home, _okres_any(sid, g), g):
            return False
    return True


def home_in_okres(home, oid, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """D-c (0.8.0): the soldier's home lies in okres *oid*: its stated okres (``home_okres_id``) is
    *oid*, or — with none stated — its municipality answers (D-144 across the Czech-lands namesakes) to
    a settlement of *oid*, or is a close spelling (:data:`HOME_OKRES_NAME_RATIO`) of a settlement name
    of *oid* (*Einsidl* / *Einsiedel*)."""
    if oid is None:
        return False
    hm, ho = (tuple(home) + (None, None))[:2]
    if ho is not None:
        return int(ho) == int(oid)
    first = str(hm).split(",")[0] if isinstance(hm, str) else None
    hclean = clean_birthplace(first)[0] if first else None
    hk = key(hclean) if hclean else ""
    if not hk:
        return False
    v, s = decide(_czech(g.global_any.get(hk, ()), g), _reg_status(g))
    if v == "ok" and _okres_any(s, g) == oid:
        return True
    names = [nospace(n) for n in g.okres_keys.get(oid, {})]
    return bool(difflib.get_close_matches(nospace(hk), names, n=1, cutoff=HOME_OKRES_NAME_RATIO))


def home_foreign(home, g: Gazetteer) -> str | None:
    """F3 (0.7.0): why the soldier's home lies outside the Czech lands, else ``None``. *home* is
    ``(municipality, okres_id, land, megye_id, jaras_id, okres)``: ``home_land`` set and not *Czech
    lands* (``home_land``; legion 54336's is empty), a Hungarian county or járás (``home_hungary``:
    legion 26367, home Ipolské Šiahy, Hont), and — only where no Czech okres was resolved — a home
    municipality that only a Hungarian okres or obec name answers to (``home_name_foreign``), or one no
    Czech-lands settlement answers to whose okres string names no Czech-lands okres either
    (``home_unresolved``: legion 54336 *Bielik, Bielik*; *Chicago, Illinois* — a reading beyond the
    author's text, so :func:`okres_inferred_verdict` applies it only to a contested name)."""
    hm, ho, hl, hmg, hj, hok = (tuple(home) + (None,) * 6)[:6]
    if isinstance(hl, str) and hl.strip() and hl.strip() != "Czech lands":
        return "home_land"
    if (isinstance(hmg, str) and hmg.strip()) or (isinstance(hj, str) and hj.strip()):
        return "home_hungary"
    if ho is not None:
        return None
    first = str(hm).split(",")[0] if isinstance(hm, str) else None
    hclean = clean_birthplace(first)[0] if first else None
    hk = key(hclean) if hclean else ""
    if not hk or _czech_1910(g.global_any.get(hk, ()), g) or hk in g.later_town:
        return None
    if hk in g.foreign_okres:
        return "home_name_foreign"
    ok_first = str(hok).split(",")[0] if isinstance(hok, str) else ""
    if key(ok_first) and resolve_okres(ok_first, None, None, g)[0] in ("none", "foreign"):
        return "home_unresolved"
    return None


def _elsewhere_words() -> frozenset:
    """A4: :data:`HOME_ELSEWHERE_WORDS` and the city keys of :data:`utils.parsing.theater.CITY_THEATER`."""
    from utils.parsing.theater import CITY_THEATER
    return HOME_ELSEWHERE_WORDS | frozenset(key(c) for c in CITY_THEATER)


def home_elsewhere(home) -> bool:
    """A4 (0.8.0): the home cell (municipality and okres strings) places the home outside the refusing
    lands although ``home_land`` is empty — a word of :func:`_elsewhere_words` (*Chicago*, *Illinois*,
    *Ohio*, *Peking*) or a :mod:`records_geo` land marker of another land (*Vídeň*, *Rusko*, *USA*)."""
    from utils.parsing import records_geo as rg
    hm, _ho, _hl, _hmg, _hj, hok = (tuple(home) + (None,) * 6)[:6]
    text = " ".join(str(x) for x in (hm, hok) if isinstance(x, str))
    k = key(text)
    if not k:
        return False
    words = _elsewhere_words()
    padded = f" {k} "
    if any(f" {w} " in padded for w in words):
        return True
    return any(pat.search(k) and land not in HOME_REFUSING_LANDS for pat, land in rg._LAND_MARKER_RES)


def raw_names_link_okres(raw, sid, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """A4 (0.8.0): the raw cell writes the link's own okres — an okres word's name, a bare comma piece
    naming exactly an okres or court, or VÚA's capital-city okres (*Hlavní město Praha*, *Zemské hlavní
    město Brno*: the title dropped) — that fits the settlement (:func:`_okres_fits`: *Habry, okr.
    Čáslav*; *Praha, Hlavní město Praha+*)."""
    if not isinstance(raw, str):
        return False
    named = [(n, False) for n in okres_names_in(raw)] + [(n, True) for n in _bare_qualifiers(raw)]
    top = re.sub(r"\([^()]*\)", " ", raw)
    for piece in re.split(r"[,;]", top)[1:]:
        piece = re.sub(r"[?+]", " ", piece).strip(" -–.")
        if _CAPITAL_RE.match(piece):
            named.append((_CAPITAL_RE.sub("", piece).strip(), True))
    return any(okres_token(n) and _okres_fits(n, sid, g, exact_only=e) is None for n, e in named)


def home_refuses(why: str, home, raw, sid, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """A4 (the author, 2026-11-16): whether the F3 home reason *why* (:func:`home_foreign`) refuses. A
    home refuses only where a same-named foreign birthplace is plausible — ``home_land`` one of
    :data:`HOME_REFUSING_LANDS`, a Hungarian county or járás (``home_hungary``), a home only a Hungarian
    name answers to (``home_name_foreign``) — or (``home_unresolved``, kept for a contested name) a home
    no Czech-lands name answers to that is not recognisably elsewhere (:func:`home_elsewhere`: legion
    54336 *Bielik*, not *Chicago, Illinois*); never when the raw cell writes the link's own okres
    (:func:`raw_names_link_okres`)."""
    if raw_names_link_okres(raw, sid, g):
        return False
    if why == "home_land":
        hl = (tuple(home) + (None,) * 6)[2]
        return isinstance(hl, str) and hl.strip() in HOME_REFUSING_LANDS
    if why == "home_unresolved":
        return not home_elsewhere(home)
    return why in ("home_hungary", "home_name_foreign")


def _okres_any(sid, g: Gazetteer):
    """A settlement's 1910 okres: the lexikon's, else its register owner row's."""
    return g.okres_of.get(sid) or (g.owner.get(sid) or {}).get("okres_id")


def _czech(ids, g: Gazetteer) -> set:
    """The ids of *ids* that are Czech-lands 1910 settlements (a 1910 okres in the lexikon or the
    register): a lexikon row with none (*Český Těšín*, created 1920; the Hlučín villages, Prussian in
    1910) is left out (0.6.0)."""
    return {s for s in (ids or ()) if _okres_any(s, g) is not None}


#: 0.7.0 (F1): the earliest ``okres_all`` okres of the lexikon rows (all present-day Czech Republic)
#: that lay outside the Czech lands in 1910 — the Hlučín villages (Prussian Kreis *Ratibor*), Valticko
#: and Vitorazsko (Lower Austria: *Mistelbach*, *Waidhofen an der Thaya*, *Zwettl*, *Gmünd*)
_FOREIGN_FIRST_OKRES = frozenset({"ratibor", "hlucin"}) | FOREIGN_DISTRICTS_LOWER_AUSTRIA


def unplaced_czech(sid, g: Gazetteer) -> bool:
    """F1 (0.7.0): a lexikon row with no 1910 okres (neither the lexikon's nor a register row's)
    whose **earliest** ``okres_all`` okres is not one of :data:`_FOREIGN_FIRST_OKRES`: a 1910
    settlement of the Czech lands the lexikon knows only under a later name or without its 1910
    clause (*Nový Bohumín*, Fryštát; *Ruda nad Moravou*, Šumperk; *Louky nad Dřevnicí*, Uherské
    Hradiště; *Domoradice*, Krumlov). The lexikon covers today's Czech Republic, so the earliest okres
    outside it is what separates the Hlučín villages, Valticko and Vitorazsko. A row with no timeline
    at all is not counted."""
    if _okres_any(sid, g) is not None:
        return False
    first = g.first_okres.get(sid)
    if not first:
        return False
    k = key(first)
    return k not in _FOREIGN_FIRST_OKRES and _RURAL_WORD_RE.sub("", k).strip() not in _FOREIGN_FIRST_OKRES


def _czech_1910(ids, g: Gazetteer) -> set:
    """F1 (0.7.0): :func:`_czech` plus the Czech-lands settlements with no 1910 okres
    (:func:`unplaced_czech`)."""
    return {s for s in (ids or ()) if _okres_any(s, g) is not None or unplaced_czech(s, g)}


def _land_of(sid, g: Gazetteer):
    """301 Bohemia / 302 Moravia / 303 Silesia of a settlement's 1910 okres, else ``None``."""
    o = _okres_any(sid, g)
    return int(o) // 1000 if o else None


def lands_named(text) -> set:
    """F2/F4 (0.7.0): the lands a text names outside parentheses, in the comma pieces after the
    name (:data:`LAND_PIECES`: ``Morava`` → 302, ``Čechy`` → 301, ``Rakouské Slezsko`` → 303,
    ``Horní Slezsko`` → ``"foreign"``); an okres name holding a land word (*Moravská Třebová*,
    *Nové Město na Moravě*) is no land."""
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        return set()
    top = re.sub(r"\([^()]*\)", " ", text)
    out: set = set()
    for piece in re.split(r"[,;]", top)[1:]:
        k = re.sub(r"^(?:okres|okr|o)\s+", "", key(re.sub(r"[?+]", " ", piece)))
        for phrase, land in LAND_PIECES:
            if k == phrase or k.startswith(phrase + " "):
                out.add(land)
                break
    return out


def land_conflict(lands, land) -> bool:
    """F2/F4 (0.7.0): the named *lands* contradict a settlement's *land*: Bohemia against Moravia or
    Silesia; Moravia and Silesia, which the records confuse, never contradict each other."""
